ar: وَإِن مِّنكُمْ إِلَّا وَارِدُهَا ۚ كَانَ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ حَتْمًۭا مَّقْضِيًّۭا
en: There is none of you who will not pass over it. ˹This is˺ a decree your Lord must fulfil.
t1: And there is none of you but will pass over Hell. This (promise,) which will certainly be fulfilled, is absolutely with your Lord.
t2: Not one of you there is, but he shall go down to it; that for thy Lord is a thing decreed, determined.
t3: There is not one of you but shall approach it. That is a fixed ordinance of thy Lord.

ar: ثُمَّ نُنَجِّى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوا۟ وَّنَذَرُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ فِيهَا جِثِيًّۭا
en: Then We will deliver those who were devout, leaving the wrongdoers there on their knees.
t1: Then We shall deliver the Godfearing, and shall leave the wrongdoers in it (Hell) down on their knees.
t2: Then We shall deliver those that were godfearing; and the evildoers We shall leave there, hobbling on their knees.
t3: Then We shall rescue those who kept from evil, and leave the evil- doers crouching there.

ar: وَإِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتُنَا بَيِّنَٰتٍۢ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ أَىُّ ٱلْفَرِيقَيْنِ خَيْرٌۭ مَّقَامًۭا وَأَحْسَنُ نَدِيًّۭا
en: When Our clear revelations are recited to them, the disbelievers ask the believers ˹mockingly˺, “Which of the two of us is better in status and superior in assembly?”
t1: And when Our enlightening Verses are recited to them, the disbelievers say to the believers: ‘(See in the selfsame world) which of us two groups has better housing and a more influential social circle.’
t2: When Our signs are recited to them as clear signs, the unbelievers say to the believers, ’Which of the two parties is better in station, fairer in assembly?’
t3: And when Our clear revelations are recited unto them, those who disbelieve say unto those who believe: Which of the two parties (yours or ours) is better in position, and more imposing as an army ?

ar: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْنٍ هُمْ أَحْسَنُ أَثَٰثًۭا وَرِءْيًۭا
en: ˹Imagine, O  Prophet˺ how many peoples We have destroyed before them, who were far better in luxury and splendour!
t1: And how many a people have We destroyed before them who were better off (than these) in worldly assets and pomp and show!
t2: And how many a generation We destroyed before them, who were fairer in furnishing and outward show!
t3: How many a generation have We destroyed before them, who were more imposing in respect of gear and outward seeming!

ar: قُلْ مَن كَانَ فِى ٱلضَّلَٰلَةِ فَلْيَمْدُدْ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ مَدًّا ۚ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا رَأَوْا۟ مَا يُوعَدُونَ إِمَّا ٱلْعَذَابَ وَإِمَّا ٱلسَّاعَةَ فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ هُوَ شَرٌّۭ مَّكَانًۭا وَأَضْعَفُ جُندًۭا
en: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Whoever is ˹entrenched˺ in misguidance, the Most Compassionate will allow them plenty of time, until—behold!—they face what they are threatened with: either the torment or the Hour. Only then will they realize who is worse in position and inferior in manpower.”
t1: Say: ‘The Most Kind (Lord also) grants respite in age and luxury to the one who is lost in error until, when they see what they have been promised—the torment or the Day of Rising—then they will come to know him who is worse in respect of dwelling and (also) weaker in respect of troops.’
t2: Say: ’Whosoever is in error, let the All-merciful prolong his term for him! Till, when they see that they were threatened, whether the chastisement, or the Hour, then they shall surely know who is worse in place, and who is weaker in hosts.’
t3: Say: As for him who is in error, the Beneficent will verily prolong his span of life until, when they behold that which they were promised, whether it be punishment (in the world), or the Hour (of doom), they will know who is worse in position and who is weaker as an army.

ar: وَيَزِيدُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱهْتَدَوْا۟ هُدًۭى ۗ وَٱلْبَٰقِيَٰتُ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ خَيْرٌ عِندَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَابًۭا وَخَيْرٌۭ مَّرَدًّا
en: And Allah increases in guidance those who are ˹rightly˺ guided. And the everlasting good deeds are far better with your Lord in reward and in outcome.
t1: Allah adds to the guidance of those who are guided aright. And in the sight of your Lord, the lasting pious deeds are better in respect of reward and (also) more valuable in terms of end result.
t2: And God shall increase those who were guided in guidance; and the abiding things, the deeds of righteousness, are better with thy Lord in reward, and better in return
t3: Allah increaseth in right guidance those who walk aright, and the good deeds which endure are better in thy Lord’s sight for reward, and better for resort.

ar: أَفَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى كَفَرَ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَقَالَ لَأُوتَيَنَّ مَالًۭا وَوَلَدًا
en: Have you seen ˹O Prophet˺ the one who rejects Our revelations yet boasts, “I will definitely be granted ˹plenty of˺ wealth and children ˹if there is an afterlife˺.”?
t1: Have you seen such a person that rejected Our Signs and said: ‘I shall certainly be given wealth and children (the same way, even on the Day of Resurrection)’?
t2: Hast thou seen him who disbelieves in Our signs and says, ’Assuredly I shall be given wealth and children’?
t3: Hast thou seen him who disbelieveth in Our revelations and saith: Assuredly I shall be given wealth and children ?

ar: أَطَّلَعَ ٱلْغَيْبَ أَمِ ٱتَّخَذَ عِندَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَهْدًۭا
en: Has he looked into the unseen or taken a pledge from the Most Compassionate?
t1: Is he aware of the unseen, or has he taken any promise from the Most Kind (Lord)?
t2: What, has he observed the Unseen, or taken a covenant with the All-merciful?
t3: Hath he perused the Unseen, or hath he made a pact with the Beneficent ?

ar: كَلَّا ۚ سَنَكْتُبُ مَا يَقُولُ وَنَمُدُّ لَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ مَدًّۭا
en: Not at all! We certainly record whatever he claims and will increase his punishment extensively.
t1: No way! We shall keep writing down what he says, and shall keep increasing for him torment (upon torment).
t2: No, indeed! We shall assuredly write down all that he says, and We shall prolong for him the chastisement;
t3: Nay, but We shall record that which he saith and prolong for him a span of torment.

ar: وَنَرِثُهُۥ مَا يَقُولُ وَيَأْتِينَا فَرْدًۭا
en: And We will inherit what he boasts of, and he will come before Us all by himself.
t1: And (after his death) We shall inherit from him what he proclaims, and he will come to Us all alone (without wealth and children).
t2: and We shall inherit from him that he says, and he shall come to Us alone.
t3: And We shall inherit from him that whereof he spake, and he will come unto Us, alone (without his wealth and children).

ar: وَٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ ءَالِهَةًۭ لِّيَكُونُوا۟ لَهُمْ عِزًّۭا
en: They have taken other gods, instead of Allah, seeking strength ˹and protection˺ through them.
t1: And they have taken (many other) gods apart from Allah so that they may be a source of honour for them.
t2: And they have taken to them other gods apart from God, that they might be for them a might.
t3: And they have chosen (other) gods beside Allah that they may be a power for them.

ar: كَلَّا ۚ سَيَكْفُرُونَ بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ وَيَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضِدًّا
en: But no! Those ˹gods˺ will deny their worship and turn against them.
t1: By no means! Soon will these (false gods themselves) reject their worship and become their enemies.
t2: No, indeed! They shall deny their service, and they shall be against them pitted.
t3: Nay, but they will deny their worship of them, and become opponents unto them.

ar: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا ٱلشَّيَٰطِينَ عَلَى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ تَؤُزُّهُمْ أَزًّۭا
en: Do you ˹O Prophet˺ not see that We have sent the devils against the disbelievers, constantly inciting them?
t1: Have you not seen that We have sent satans upon the disbelievers? They keep rousing them (against Islam) all the time.
t2: Hast thou not seen how We sent the Satans against the unbelievers, to prick them?
t3: Seest thou not that We have set the devils on the disbelievers to confound them with confusion ?

ar: فَلَا تَعْجَلْ عَلَيْهِمْ ۖ إِنَّمَا نَعُدُّ لَهُمْ عَدًّۭا
en: So do not be in haste against them, for indeed We are ˹closely˺ counting down their days.
t1: So do not make haste against them (for torment). We Ourselves keep counting the days (for their impending catastrophe).
t2: So hasten thou not against them; We are only numbering for them a number.
t3: So make no haste against them (O Muhammad). We do but number unto them a sum (of days).

ar: يَوْمَ نَحْشُرُ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ إِلَى ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ وَفْدًۭا
en: ˹Watch for˺ the Day We will gather the righteous before the Most Compassionate as an honoured delegation,
t1: On the Day, when We shall assemble the Godfearing, and take them (as guests of honour) to the presence of the Most Kind (Lord) on carriages;
t2: On the day that We shall muster the godfearing to the All-merciful with pomp
t3: On the day when We shall gather the righteous unto the Beneficent, a goodly company.

ar: وَنَسُوقُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ وِرْدًۭا
en: and drive the wicked to Hell like a thirsty herd.
t1: And We shall drive the sinners thirsty towards Hell;
t2: and drive the evildoers into Gehenna herding,
t3: And drive the guilty unto hell, a weary herd,

ar: لَّا يَمْلِكُونَ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةَ إِلَّا مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ عِندَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَهْدًۭا
en: None will have the right to intercede, except those who have taken a covenant from the Most Compassionate.
t1: (On that Day,) people will not possess the authority to intercede, except those who have taken a promise (of intercession) from the Most Kind (Lord).
t2: having no power of intercession, save those who have taken with the All-merciful covenant.
t3: They will have no power of intercession, save him who hath made a covenant with his Lord.

ar: وَقَالُوا۟ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وَلَدًۭا
en: They say, “The Most Compassionate has offspring.”
t1: And (the disbelievers) say: ‘The Most Kind (Lord) has taken (to Himself) a son.’
t2: And they say, ’The All-merciful has taken unto Himself a son.
t3: And they say: The Beneficent hath taken unto Himself a son.

ar: لَّقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْـًٔا إِدًّۭا
en: You have certainly made an outrageous claim,
t1: (O disbelievers!) You have indeed brought most horrible and unusual evil (on your tongues).
t2: You have indeed advanced something hideous!
t3: Assuredly ye utter a disastrous thing

ar: تَكَادُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْهُ وَتَنشَقُّ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَتَخِرُّ ٱلْجِبَالُ هَدًّا
en: by which the heavens are about to burst, the earth to split apart, and the mountains to crumble to pieces
t1: The heavens may just burst at this (fabricated lie) and the earth split asunder and the mountains fall down to pieces,
t2: The heavens are wellnigh rent of it and the earth split asunder, and the mountains wellnigh fall down crashing for
t3: Whereby almost the heavens are torn, and the earth is split asunder and the mountains fall in ruins,

ar: أَن دَعَوْا۟ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ وَلَدًۭا
en: in protest of attributing children to the Most Compassionate.
t1: That they have attributed a son to the Most Kind (Lord).
t2: that they have attributed to the All-merciful a son;
t3: That ye ascribe unto the Beneficent a son,

ar: وَمَا يَنۢبَغِى لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدًا
en: It does not befit ˹the majesty of˺ the Most Compassionate to have children.
t1: And it is not befitting the Glory of the Most Kind (Lord) to take (someone as) a son.
t2: and it behoves not the All-merciful to take a son.
t3: When it is not meet for (the Majesty of) the Beneficent that He should choose a son.

ar: إِن كُلُّ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّآ ءَاتِى ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَبْدًۭا
en: There is none in the heavens or the earth who will not return to the Most Compassionate in full submission.
t1: Whoever is (dwelling) in the heavens and the earth (whether an angel, a jinn or a human being) will appear just as a servant before the Most Kind (Lord).
t2: None is there in the heavens and earth but he comes to the All-merciful as a servant;
t3: There is none in the heavens and the earth but cometh unto the Beneficent as a slave.

ar: لَّقَدْ أَحْصَىٰهُمْ وَعَدَّهُمْ عَدًّۭا
en: Indeed, He fully knows them and has counted them precisely.
t1: (Allah) has surely encompassed them with His (knowledge) and has counted them thoroughly (i.e., numbering them one by one).
t2: He has indeed counted them, and He has numbered them exactly.
t3: Verily He knoweth them and numbereth them with (right) numbering.

ar: وَكُلُّهُمْ ءَاتِيهِ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فَرْدًا
en: And each of them will return to Him on the Day of Judgment all alone.
t1: And each one of them has to appear before His presence alone on the Day of Resurrection.
t2: Every one of them shall come to Him upon the Day of Resurrection, all alone.
t3: And each one of them will come unto Him on the Day of Resurrection, alone.

ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ سَيَجْعَلُ لَهُمُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وُدًّۭا
en: As for those who believe and do good, the Most Compassionate will ˹certainly˺ bless them with ˹genuine˺ love.
t1: Surely, those who believed and did pious deeds, the Most Kind (Lord) will create love for them in the hearts (of the people).
t2: Surely those who believe and do deeds of righteousness -- unto them the All-merciful shall assign love.
t3: Lo! those who believe and do good works, the Beneficent will appoint for them love.

ar: فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَٰهُ بِلِسَانِكَ لِتُبَشِّرَ بِهِ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ وَتُنذِرَ بِهِۦ قَوْمًۭا لُّدًّۭا
en: Indeed, We have made this ˹Quran˺ easy in your own language ˹O Prophet˺ so with it you may give good news to the righteous and warn those who are contentious.
t1: So We have indeed made this (Qur’an) easy in your own tongue so that, by means of it, you may communicate good news to the Godfearing and may warn thereby the contentious people.
t2: Now We have made it easy by thy tongue that thou mayest bear good tidings thereby to the godfearing, and warn a people stubborn.
t3: And We make (this Scripture) easy in thy tongue, (O Muhammad) only that thou mayst bear good tidings therewith unto those who ward off (evil), and warn therewith the froward folk.

ar: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْنٍ هَلْ تُحِسُّ مِنْهُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَوْ تَسْمَعُ لَهُمْ رِكْزًۢا
en: ˹Imagine˺ how many peoples We have destroyed before them! Do you ˹still˺ see any of them, or ˹even˺ hear from them the slightest sound?
t1: And how many a community have We destroyed before them! Do you perceive even a trace or hear even the faintest fizzle of any of them?
t2: And how many a generation We destroyed before them! Dost thou perceive so much as one of them, or hear of them a whisper?
t3: And how many a generation before them have We destroyed! Canst thou (Muhammad) see a single man of them, or hear from them the slightest sound ?

ar: طه
en: Ṭa-Ha.
t1: Ta-Ha. (Only Allah and the Messenger [blessings and peace be upon him] know the real meaning.)
t2: Ta Ha
t3: Ta. Ha.

ar: مَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِتَشْقَىٰٓ
en: We have not revealed the Quran to you ˹O Prophet˺ to cause you distress,
t1: (O My Esteemed Beloved!) We have not revealed the Qur’an to you that you land in distress.
t2: We have not sent down the Koran upon thee for thee to be unprosperous,
t3: We have not revealed unto thee (Muhammad) this Qur’an that thou shouldst be distressed,

ar: إِلَّا تَذْكِرَةًۭ لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ
en: but as a reminder to those in awe ˹of Allah˺.
t1: But (it) is (revealed as) admonition for him who fears (his Lord).
t2: but only as a reminder to him who tears,
t3: But as a reminder unto him who feareth,

ar: تَنزِيلًۭا مِّمَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلْأَرْضَ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ ٱلْعُلَى
en: ˹It is˺ a revelation from the One Who created the earth and the high heavens—
t1: (This) has been revealed by (Allah) Who created the earth and the lofty heavens.
t2: a revelation from Him who created the earth and the high heavens;
t3: A revelation from Him Who created the earth and the high heavens,

ar: ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱسْتَوَىٰ
en: the Most Compassionate, ˹Who is˺ established on the Throne.
t1: (He is) Most Kind (Lord) Who established (His sovereignty) on the Throne (of power and supreme authority over all the systems of the universe, befitting His Glory).
t2: the All-compassionate sat Himself upon the Throne; to Him belongs
t3: The Beneficent One, Who is established on the Throne.

ar: لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَمَا تَحْتَ ٱلثَّرَىٰ
en: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is in between and whatever is underground.
t1: (So) whatever is in the heavens (i.e., the upper divine and celestial spheres and spatial terrestrial spheres) and whatever is in the earth and whatever is in between (i.e., the atmospheric spheres) and whatever is beneath the soil to its bed, all are (functioning in compliance with) His (command and control system).
t2: all that is in the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, and all that is underneath the soil.
t3: Unto Him belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth, and whatsoever is between them, and whatsoever is beneath the sod.

ar: وَإِن تَجْهَرْ بِٱلْقَوْلِ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَعْلَمُ ٱلسِّرَّ وَأَخْفَى
en: Whether you speak openly ˹or not˺, He certainly knows what is secret and what is even more hidden.
t1: And (there is no harm) if, in remembrance and Prayer, you raise (your voice). He knows the secrets (of hearts) and also the most hidden mysteries. (Then how He will not hear the loud supplications!)
t2: Be thou loud in thy speech, yet surely He knows the secret and that yet more hidden.
t3: And if thou speakest aloud, then lo! He knoweth the secret (thought) and (that which is yet) more hidden.

ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ لَهُ ٱلْأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ
en: Allah—there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. He has the Most Beautiful Names.
t1: Allah is (His Self-Name) besides Whom there is no God (i.e., believe in Him alone and deny all other false gods). There are (also) many other Beautiful Names for Him (that speak of His most beautiful attributes).
t2: God -- there is no god but He. To Him belong the Names Most Beautiful.
t3: Allah! There is no God save Him. His are the most beautiful names.

ar: وَهَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَىٰٓ
en: Has the story of Moses reached you ˹O Prophet˺?
t1: And has the account of Musa (Moses) reached you?
t2: Hast thou received the story of Moses?
t3: Hath there come unto thee the story of Moses ?

ar: إِذْ رَءَا نَارًۭا فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ ٱمْكُثُوٓا۟ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًۭا لَّعَلِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدًۭى
en: When he saw a fire, he said to his family, “Wait here, ˹for˺ I have spotted a fire. Perhaps I can bring you a torch from it, or find some guidance at the fire.”
t1: When Musa (Moses) saw a fire (on his way back to Egypt from Madyan), he said to his family: ‘Stay here. I have seen a fire (or I have perceived a flash of love and cordiality in a fire). Perhaps I may bring a brand from it for you (also), or I find at that fire the guidance (which I am searching for).’
t2: When he saw a tire, and said to his family, ’Tarry you here; I observe a fire. Perhaps I shall bring you a brand from it, or I shall find at the fire guidance.’
t3: When he saw a fire and said unto his folk: Lo! Wait! I see a fire afar off. Peradventure I may bring you a brand therefrom or may find guidance at the fire.

ar: فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِىَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ
en: But when he approached it, he was called, “O Moses!
t1: So when he reached that (fire), a call was made: ‘O Musa (Moses)!
t2: When he came to it, a voice cried, ’Moses,
t3: And when he reached it, he was called by name: O Moses!

ar: إِنِّىٓ أَنَا۠ رَبُّكَ فَٱخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ ۖ إِنَّكَ بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًۭى
en: It is truly I. I am your Lord! So take off your sandals, for you are in the sacred valley of Ṭuwa.
t1: Certainly, I am your Lord, so take off your shoes. Verily, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
t2: I am thy Lord; put off thy shoes; thou art in the holy valley, Towa.
t3: Lo! I, even I, am thy Lord, So take off thy shoes, for lo! thou art in the holy valley of Tuwa.

ar: وَأَنَا ٱخْتَرْتُكَ فَٱسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَىٰٓ
en: I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed:
t1: And I have chosen you (for My Messengership), so listen to what is being revealed to you with absolute attentiveness.
t2: I Myself have chosen thee; therefore give thou ear to this revelation.
t3: And I have chosen thee, so hearken unto that which is inspired.

ar: إِنَّنِىٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعْبُدْنِى وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكْرِىٓ
en: ‘It is truly I. I am Allah! There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Me. So worship Me ˹alone˺, and establish prayer for My remembrance.
t1: Verily, I am Allah. There is no God other than Me. So always worship Me, and establish Prayer for the sake of My remembrance.
t2: Verily I am God; there is no god but I; therefore serve Me, and perform the prayer of My remembrance.
t3: Lo! I, even I, am Allah, There is no God save Me. So serve Me and establish worship for My remembrance.

ar: إِنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌ أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا لِتُجْزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفْسٍۭ بِمَا تَسْعَىٰ
en: The Hour is sure to come. My Will is to keep it hidden, so that every soul may be rewarded according to their efforts.
t1: Certainly, the Last Hour is about to come. I want to keep it secret so that every soul may be rewarded for that (deed) for which it is exerting.
t2: The Hour is coming; I would conceal it that every soul may be recompensed for its labours.
t3: Lo! the Hour is surely coming. But I will to keep it hidden, that every soul may be rewarded for that which it striveth (to achieve).

ar: فَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا مَن لَّا يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُ فَتَرْدَىٰ
en: So do not let those who disbelieve in it and follow their desires distract you from it, or you will be doomed.’”
t1: So let not someone who (himself) does not believe in it and follows his own lust (of the lower self) prevent you from (focusing on) it, otherwise you (too) will perish.
t2: Let none bar thee from it, that believes not in it but follows after his own caprice, or thou wilt perish.
t3: Therefor, let not him turn thee aside from (the thought of) it who believeth not therein but followeth his own desire, lest thou perish.

ar: وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
en: ˹Allah added,˺ “And what is that in your right hand, O  Moses?”
t1: And what is this in your right hand, O Musa (Moses)?’
t2: What is that, Moses, thou hast in thy right hand?’
t3: And what is that in thy right hand, O Moses ?

ar: قَالَ هِىَ عَصَاىَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا۟ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِى وَلِىَ فِيهَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخْرَىٰ
en: He replied, “It is my staff! I lean on it, and with it I beat down ˹branches˺ for my sheep, and have other uses for it.”
t1: He submitted: ‘This is my staff. I lean on it, and beat down leaves with it for my goats, and in it there are also many other benefits for me.’
t2: ’Why, it is my staff,’ said Moses. ’I lean upon it, and with it I beat down leaves to feed my sheep; other uses also I find in it.
t3: He said: This is my staff whereon I lean, and wherewith I bear down branches for my sheep, and He said: This is my staff whereon I lean, and wherewith I bear down branches for my sheep, and wherein I find other uses.

ar: قَالَ أَلْقِهَا يَٰمُوسَىٰ
en: Allah said, “Throw it down, O  Moses!”
t1: (Allah) said: ‘O Musa (Moses), cast it down (on the ground).’
t2: Said He, ’Cast it down, Moses!’
t3: He said: Cast it down, O Moses!

ar: فَأَلْقَىٰهَا فَإِذَا هِىَ حَيَّةٌۭ تَسْعَىٰ
en: So he did, then—behold!—it became a serpent, slithering.
t1: So he cast it down (on the ground), and suddenly it became a serpent slithering (here and there).
t2: and he cast it down, and behold it was a serpent sliding.
t3: So he cast it down, and lo! it was a serpent, gliding.

ar: قَالَ خُذْهَا وَلَا تَخَفْ ۖ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا ٱلْأُولَىٰ
en: Allah said, “Take it, and have no fear. We will return it to its former state.
t1: Allah said: ‘Catch it and do not fear. We shall transform it to its former state just now.’
t2: Said He, ’Take it, and fear not; We will restore it to its first state.
t3: He said: Grasp it and fear not. We shall return it to its former state.

ar: وَٱضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَىٰ جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ ءَايَةً أُخْرَىٰ
en: And put your hand under your armpit, it will come out ˹shining˺ white, unblemished, as another sign,
t1: And (it was commanded:) ‘Press your hand in your armpit. It will come out radiant white without any disease. (This) is another sign.
t2: Now clasp thy hand to thy arm-pit; it shall come forth white, without evil. That is a second sign.
t3: And thrust thy hand within thine armpit, it will come forth white without hurt. (That will be) another token.

ar: لِنُرِيَكَ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَا ٱلْكُبْرَى
en: so that We may show you some of Our greatest signs.
t1: (We are doing) this so that We show you greater signs of Our (might).
t2: So We would show thee some of Our greatest signs.
t3: That We may show thee (some) of Our greater portents,

ar: ٱذْهَبْ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُۥ طَغَىٰ
en: Go to Pharaoh, for he has truly transgressed ˹all bounds˺.”
t1: Go to Pharaoh. He has exceeded limits (in defiance and rebellion).’
t2: Go to Pharaoh; he has waxed insolent.’
t3: Go thou unto Pharaoh! Lo! he hath transgressed (the bounds).

ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى
en: Moses prayed, “My Lord! Uplift my heart for me,
t1: Musa (Moses) prayed: ‘O my Lord, expand my breast for me.
t2: ’Lord, open my breast,’ said Moses,
t3: (Moses) said: My Lord! relieve my mind

ar: وَيَسِّرْ لِىٓ أَمْرِى
en: and make my task easy,
t1: And make my task (as a Messenger) easy for me.
t2: ’and do Thou ease for me my task.
t3: And ease my task for me;

ar: وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةًۭ مِّن لِّسَانِى
en: and remove the impediment from my tongue
t1: And untie the knot from my tongue,
t2: Unloose the knot upon my tongue, t
t3: And loose a knot from my tongue,

ar: يَفْقَهُوا۟ قَوْلِى
en: so people may understand my speech,
t1: That people may understand (easily) what I say.
t2: hat they may understand my words.
t3: That they may understand my saying.

ar: وَٱجْعَل لِّى وَزِيرًۭا مِّنْ أَهْلِى
en: and grant me a helper from my family,
t1: And appoint for me a minister from my family.
t2: Appoint for me of my folk a familiar,
t3: Appoint for me a henchman from my folk,

ar: هَٰرُونَ أَخِى
en: Aaron, my brother.
t1: (That) is Harun (Aaron), my brother.
t2: Aaron, my brother;
t3: Aaron, my brother.

ar: ٱشْدُدْ بِهِۦٓ أَزْرِى
en: Strengthen me through him,
t1: Provide me strength and backup with him.
t2: by him confirm my strength,
t3: Confirm my strength with him

ar: وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِىٓ أَمْرِى
en: and let him share my task,
t1: And make him share my task (of Messengership),
t2: and associate him with me in my task.
t3: And let him share my task,

ar: كَىْ نُسَبِّحَكَ كَثِيرًۭا
en: so that we may glorify You much
t1: So that we (both) may amply glorify You,
t2: So shall we glorify Thee,
t3: That we may glorify Thee much

ar: وَنَذْكُرَكَ كَثِيرًا
en: and remember You much,
t1: And amply remember You.
t2: and remember Thee abundantly.
t3: And much remember Thee.

ar: إِنَّكَ كُنتَ بِنَا بَصِيرًۭا
en: for truly You have ˹always˺ been overseeing us.”
t1: Surely, You see us well (in the perspective of total scenario).’
t2: Surely Thou seest into us.’
t3: Lo! Thou art ever Seeing us.

ar: قَالَ قَدْ أُوتِيتَ سُؤْلَكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
en: Allah responded, “All that you requested has been granted, O  Moses!
t1: (Allah) said: ‘O Musa (Moses), you are granted your every prayer.
t2: Said He, ’Thou art granted, Moses, thy petition.
t3: He said: Thou art granted thy request, O Moses.

ar: وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَيْكَ مَرَّةً أُخْرَىٰٓ
en: And surely We had shown You favour before,
t1: And surely, We graciously favoured you once (earlier as well),
t2: Already another time We favoured thee,
t3: And indeed, another time, already We have shown thee favour,

ar: إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ
en: when We inspired your mother with this:
t1: When We revealed to your mother’s heart what was revealed—
t2: when We revealed what was revealed unto thy mother:
t3: When we inspired in thy mother that which is inspired,

ar: أَنِ ٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ ٱلْيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّۭ لِّى وَعَدُوٌّۭ لَّهُۥ ۚ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةًۭ مِّنِّى وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيْنِىٓ
en: ‘Put him into a chest, then put it into the river. The river will wash it ashore, and he will be taken by ˹Pharaoh,˺ an enemy of Mine and his.’ And I blessed you with lovability from Me ˹O Moses˺ so that you would be brought up under My ˹watchful˺ Eye.
t1: To put him (Musa [Moses]) into a box and place that (box) into the river. Then the river will drift it to the bank. My enemy and his enemy will pick him up. And I cast on you from My presence a reflection of My (exceptional) love (i.e., We have made you so lovely and charismatic that whoever glances at you will be fascinated). And (this was done) so that you might be brought up before My eyes.
t2: "Cast him into the ark, and cast him into the river, and let the river throw him up on the shore. An enemy of Mine and his shall take him." And I loaded on thee love from Me, and to be formed in My sight,
t3: Saying: Throw him into the ark, and throw it into the river, then the river shall throw it on to the bank, and there an enemy to Me and an enemy to him shall take him. And I endued thee with love from Me that thou mightest be trained according to My will,

ar: إِذْ تَمْشِىٓ أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ مَن يَكْفُلُهُۥ ۖ فَرَجَعْنَٰكَ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ ۚ وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًۭا فَنَجَّيْنَٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّٰكَ فُتُونًۭا ۚ فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ فِىٓ أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَىٰ قَدَرٍۢ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
en: ˹Remember˺ when your sister came along and proposed, ‘Shall I direct you to someone who will nurse him?’ So We reunited you with your mother so that her heart would be put at ease, and she would not grieve. ˹Later˺ you killed a man ˹by mistake˺, but We saved you from sorrow, as well as other tests We put you through. Then you stayed for a number of years among the people of Midian. Then you came here as pre-destined, O  Moses!
t1: (And) when your sister, (posing as a stranger,) walking along, said (to Pharaoh’s family): Shall I point out to you (a woman) who will nurse this (infant)? Then We brought you back to your mother (on the pretext of nursing) so that she might cool her eyes and might not feel aggrieved as well. And you killed a man (a disbeliever of Pharaoh’s people). Then We delivered you from (that) agony (too), and tested and assessed you through many trials. Then you stayed amongst the people of Madyan for many years. Musa (Moses)! Then you came (here) at the time fixed (by Allah. He was then exactly forty years old).
t2: when thy sister went out, saying, "Shall I point you to one to have charge of him?" So We returned thee to thy mother that she might rejoice, and not sorrow. Then thou slewest; a living soul, and We delivered thee out of grief, and We tried thee with many trials. Many years among the people of Midian thou didst sojourn, then camest hither, Moses, according to a decree.
t3: When thy sister went and said: Shall I show you one who will nurse him ? and we restored thee to thy mother that her eyes might be refreshed and might not sorrow. And thou didst kill a man and We delivered thee from great distress, and tried thee with a heavy trial. And thou didst tarry years among the folk of Midian. Then camest thou (hither) by (My) providence, O Moses,

ar: وَٱصْطَنَعْتُكَ لِنَفْسِى
en: And I have selected you for My service.
t1: And (now) I have chosen you for Myself (for the task of Messengership and the exceptional favour).
t2: I have chosen thee for My service;
t3: And I have attached thee to Myself.

ar: ٱذْهَبْ أَنتَ وَأَخُوكَ بِـَٔايَٰتِى وَلَا تَنِيَا فِى ذِكْرِى
en: Go forth, you and your brother, with My signs and never falter in remembering Me.
t1: Go, you and your brother (Harun [Aaron]), with My signs and do not slacken in remembering Me.
t2: go therefore, thou and thy brother; with My signs, and neglect not to remember Me.
t3: Go, thou and thy brother, with My tokens, and be not faint in remembrance of Me.

ar: ٱذْهَبَآ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُۥ طَغَىٰ
en: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh, for he has truly transgressed ˹all bounds˺.
t1: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh; surely, he has transgressed all bounds in rebellion.
t2: Go to Pharaoh, for he has waxed insolent;
t3: Go, both of you, unto Pharaoh. Lo! he hath transgressed (the bounds).

ar: فَقُولَا لَهُۥ قَوْلًۭا لَّيِّنًۭا لَّعَلَّهُۥ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشَىٰ
en: Speak to him gently, so perhaps he may be mindful ˹of Me˺ or fearful ˹of My punishment˺.”
t1: So talk to him politely. He may perhaps accept admonition or fear (My wrath).’
t2: yet speak gently to him, that haply he may be mindful, or perchance fear.’
t3: And speak unto him a gentle word, that peradventure he may heed or fear.

ar: قَالَا رَبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا نَخَافُ أَن يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنَآ أَوْ أَن يَطْغَىٰ
en: They both pleaded, “Our Lord! We fear that he may be quick to harm us or act tyrannically.”
t1: Both of them submitted: ‘O our Lord, we fear lest he should commit some excess against us, or become (more) rebellious.’
t2: ’O our Lord,’ said Moses and Aaron, ’truly we fear he may exceed against us, or wax insolent.’
t3: They said: Our Lord! Lo! we fear that he may be beforehand with us or that he may play the tyrant.

ar: قَالَ لَا تَخَافَآ ۖ إِنَّنِى مَعَكُمَآ أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ
en: Allah reassured ˹them˺, “Have no fear! I am with you, hearing and seeing.
t1: (Allah) said: ‘Do not fear. I am indeed with you both. I hear and see (all).
t2: ’Fear not,’ said He. ’Surely I shall be with you, hearing and seeing.
t3: He said: Fear not. Lo! I am with you twain, Hearing and Seeing.

ar: فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ ۖ قَدْ جِئْنَٰكَ بِـَٔايَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّكَ ۖ وَٱلسَّلَٰمُ عَلَىٰ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ
en: So go to him and say, ‘Indeed we are both messengers from your Lord, so let the Children of Israel go with us, and do not oppress them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And salvation will be for whoever follows the ˹right˺ guidance.
t1: So, go you both to him and say: We are (the Messengers) sent by your Lord. So (set free) the Children of Israel (from your slavery and) send them with us. And do not persecute them (anymore). Surely, we have brought you a sign from your Lord. And peace be upon him who follows guidance!
t2: So go you both to Pharaoh, and say, "We are the Messengers of thy Lord, so send forth with us the Children of Israel and chastise them not; we have brought thee a sign from thy Lord; and peace be upon him who follows the guidance!
t3: So go ye unto him and say: Lo! we are two messengers of thy Lord. So let the children of Israel go with us, and torment them not. We bring thee a token from thy Lord. And peace will be for him who followeth right guidance.

ar: إِنَّا قَدْ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْنَآ أَنَّ ٱلْعَذَابَ عَلَىٰ مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
en: It has indeed been revealed to us that the punishment will be upon whoever denies ˹the truth˺ and turns away.’”
t1: Verily, it has been revealed to us that the torment will come upon (every) such person that rejects (the Messenger) and turns away from him.’
t2: It has been revealed to us that chastisement shall light upon him who cries lies and turns his back."
t3: Lo! it hath been revealed unto us that the doom will be for him who denieth and turneth away.

ar: قَالَ فَمَن رَّبُّكُمَا يَٰمُوسَىٰ
en: Pharaoh asked, “Who then is the Lord of you two, O  Moses?”
t1: (Pharaoh) said: ‘O Musa (Moses)! Who is the Lord of you both?’
t2: Pharaoh said, ’Who is your Lord, Moses?’
t3: (Pharaoh) said: Who then is the Lord of you twain, O Moses ?

ar: قَالَ رَبُّنَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلْقَهُۥ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ
en: He answered, “Our Lord is the One Who has given everything its ˹distinctive˺ form, then guided ˹it˺.”
t1: Musa (Moses) said: ‘Our Lord is He Who brought everything into being (as most suitable), then guided it (according to its potential).’
t2: He said, ’Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation, then guided it.’
t3: He said: Our Lord is He Who gave unto everything its nature, then guided it aright.

ar: قَالَ فَمَا بَالُ ٱلْقُرُونِ ٱلْأُولَىٰ
en: Pharaoh asked, “And what about previous peoples?”
t1: (Pharaoh) said: ‘So, what was the fate of former people (who did not believe in your Lord)?’
t2: Pharaoh said, ’And what of the former generations?’
t3: He said: What then is the state of the generations of old ?

ar: قَالَ عِلْمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّى فِى كِتَٰبٍۢ ۖ لَّا يَضِلُّ رَبِّى وَلَا يَنسَى
en: He replied, “That knowledge is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord neither falters nor forgets ˹anything˺.”
t1: (Musa [Moses]) said: ‘The knowledge about them is recorded (and saved) in a Book with My Lord. My Lord does not go wrong, nor does He forget.’
t2: Said Moses, ’The knowledge of them is with my Lord, in a Book; my Lord goes not astray, nor forgets --
t3: He said: The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord neither erreth nor forgetteth,

ar: ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ مَهْدًۭا وَسَلَكَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلًۭا وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِۦٓ أَزْوَٰجًۭا مِّن نَّبَاتٍۢ شَتَّىٰ
en: ˹He is the One˺ Who has laid out the earth for ˹all of˺ you, and set in it pathways for you, and sends down rain from the sky, causing various types of plants to grow,
t1: He is the One Who made the earth habitable for you and provided therein paths for you (to travel) and sent down water from the sky. Then by means of that (water) We bring forth (from the earth) pairs of various kinds of vegetation.
t2: He who appointed the earth to be a cradle for you, and therein threaded roads for you, and sent down water out of heaven, and therewith We have brought forth divers kinds of plants.
t3: Who hath appointed the earth as a bed and hath threaded roads for you therein and hath sent down water from the sky and thereby We have brought forth divers kinds of vegetation,

ar: كُلُوا۟ وَٱرْعَوْا۟ أَنْعَٰمَكُمْ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلنُّهَىٰ
en: ˹so˺ eat and graze your cattle. Surely in this are signs for people of sound judgment.
t1: Eat and pasture your cattle. Surely, there are signs in it for the wise.
t2: Do you eat, and pasture your cattle! Surely in that are signs for men possessing reason.
t3: (Saying): Eat ye and feed your cattle. Lo! herein verily are portents for men of thought.

ar: ۞ مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ تَارَةً أُخْرَىٰ
en: From the earth We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you back again.
t1: We created you from this (very soil of the earth), and We shall return you into the same, and shall bring you forth from the very same once more.
t2: Out of the earth We created you, and We shall restore you into it, and bring you forth from it a second time.’
t3: Thereof We created you, and thereunto We return you, and thence We bring you forth a second time.

ar: وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتِنَا كُلَّهَا فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبَىٰ
en: And We certainly showed Pharaoh all of Our signs, but he denied them and refused ˹to believe˺.
t1: And surely We showed him (Pharaoh) all Our signs (bestowed upon Musa [Moses] and Harun [Aaron]), but he belied and refused to believe.
t2: So We showed Pharaoh all Our signs, but he cried lies, and refused.
t3: And We verily did show him all Our tokens, but he denied them and refused.

ar: قَالَ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتُخْرِجَنَا مِنْ أَرْضِنَا بِسِحْرِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
en: He said, “Have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic, O  Moses?
t1: He said: ‘Musa (Moses), have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic?
t2: ’Hast thou come, Moses,’ he said, ’to expel us out of our land
t3: He said: Hast come to drive us out from our land by thy magic, O Moses ?

ar: فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍۢ مِّثْلِهِۦ فَٱجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِدًۭا لَّا نُخْلِفُهُۥ نَحْنُ وَلَآ أَنتَ مَكَانًۭا سُوًۭى
en: We can surely meet you with similar magic. So set for us an appointment that neither of us will fail to keep, in a central place.”
t1: So we shall also bring you magic resembling it. Therefore, settle an appointment between us and yourself (for the contest) which neither we nor you shall violate. (The place of contest) is to be an open and smooth ground.’
t2: by thy sorcery? We shall assuredly bring thee sorcery the like of it; therefore appoint a tryst between us and thee, a place mutually agreeable, and we shall not fail it, neither thou.’
t3: But we surely can produce for thee magic the like thereof; so appoint a tryst between us and you, which neither we nor thou shall fail to keep, at a place convenient (to us both).

ar: قَالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ ٱلزِّينَةِ وَأَن يُحْشَرَ ٱلنَّاسُ ضُحًۭى
en: Moses said, “Your appointment is on the Day of the Festival, and let the people be gathered mid-morning.”
t1: (Musa [Moses]) said: ‘The day of your promise is the Eid (‘Id) Day (the day of Annual Festival), and that (on that day) all the people are to assemble there early in the forenoon.’
t2: ’Your tryst shall be upon the Feast Day.’ said Moses. ’Let the people be mustered at the high noon.’
t3: (Moses) said: Your tryst shall be the day of the feast, and let the people assemble when the sun hath risen high.

ar: فَتَوَلَّىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُۥ ثُمَّ أَتَىٰ
en: Pharaoh then withdrew, orchestrated his scheme, then returned.
t1: Then Pharaoh went back (from the meeting), put together his (schemes of) pretension and deception and then came back (at the appointed time).
t2: Pharaoh then withdrew, and gathered his guile. Thereafter he came again,
t3: Then Pharaoh went and gathered his strength, then came (to the appointed tryst).

ar: قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰ وَيْلَكُمْ لَا تَفْتَرُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًۭا فَيُسْحِتَكُم بِعَذَابٍۢ ۖ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ
en: Moses warned the magicians, “Woe to you! Do not fabricate a lie against Allah, or He will wipe you out with a torment. Whoever fabricates ˹lies˺ is bound to fail.”
t1: Musa (Moses) said to them(the sorcerers): ‘Woe to you! (Beware!) Do not invent a lie against Allah lest He should eliminate you by torment. And surely, he who fabricates a lie (against Allah) is a failure.’
t2: and Moses said to them, ’O beware! Forge not a lie against God, lest He destroy you with a chastisement. Whoso forges has ever failed.’
t3: Moses said unto them: Woe unto you! Invent not a lie against Allah, lest He extirpate you by some punishment. He who lieth faileth miserably.

ar: فَتَنَٰزَعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُم بَيْنَهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا۟ ٱلنَّجْوَىٰ
en: So the magicians disputed the matter among themselves, conversing privately.
t1: Thereupon, they (the sorcerers) disputed amongst themselves about their affair and started whispering inaudibly.
t2: And they disputed upon their plan between them, and communed secretly
t3: Then they debated one with another what they must do, and they kept their counsel secret.

ar: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنْ هَٰذَٰنِ لَسَٰحِرَٰنِ يُرِيدَانِ أَن يُخْرِجَاكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِمَا وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ ٱلْمُثْلَىٰ
en: They concluded, “These two are only magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic, and do away with your most cherished traditions.
t1: They said: ‘These two are really magicians who have the intention to drive you out of your land with sorcery, and put an end to your exemplary culture and religion.
t2: saying, ’These two men are sorcerers and their purpose is to expel you out of your land by their sorcery, and to extirpate your justest way.
t3: They said: Lo! these are two wizards who would drive you out from your country by their magic, and destroy your best traditions;

ar: فَأَجْمِعُوا۟ كَيْدَكُمْ ثُمَّ ٱئْتُوا۟ صَفًّۭا ۚ وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مَنِ ٱسْتَعْلَىٰ
en: So orchestrate your plan, then come forward in ˹perfect˺ ranks. And whoever prevails today will certainly be successful.”
t1: (They mutually decided.) So, collect all your tricks (of magic), and come into the arena (together) in a queue, and the one who prevails today will be victorious.’
t2: So gather your guile; then come in battle-line. Whoever today gains the upper hand shall surely prosper.
t3: So arrange your plan, and come in battle line. Whoso is uppermost this day will be indeed successful.

ar: قَالُوا۟ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِمَّآ أَن تُلْقِىَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَىٰ
en: They said, “O Moses! Either you cast, or let us be the first to cast.”
t1: (The magicians) said: ‘O Musa (Moses), either you cast (your thing) or we become the first ones to cast.’
t2: They said, ’Moses, either thou wilt cast, or we shall be the first to cast.’
t3: They said: O Moses! Either throw first, or let us be the first to throw ?

ar: قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوا۟ ۖ فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَىٰ
en: Moses responded, “No, you go first.” And suddenly their ropes and staffs appeared to him—by their magic—to be slithering.
t1: (Musa [Moses]) said: ‘Rather you cast down.’ Then the sight was that suddenly their cords and rods, by the effect of their magic, seemed to Musa (Moses) as if they were slithering (on the ground).
t2: ’No,’ said Moses. ’Do you cast!’ And lo, it seemed to him, by their sorcery, their ropes and their staffs were sliding;
t3: He said: Nay, do ye throw! Then lo! their cords and their staves, by their magic, appeared to him as though they ran.

ar: فَأَوْجَسَ فِى نَفْسِهِۦ خِيفَةًۭ مُّوسَىٰ
en: So Moses concealed fear within himself.
t1: Now Musa (Moses) felt a sort of hidden fear in his heart.
t2: and Moses conceived a fear within him.
t3: And Moses conceived a fear in his mind.

ar: قُلْنَا لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ
en: We reassured ˹him˺, “Do not fear! It is certainly you who will prevail.
t1: We said (to Musa [Moses]): ‘Do not fear. Verily, you will have the upper hand.
t2: We said unto him, ’Fear not; surely thou art the uppermost.
t3: We said: Fear not! Lo! thou art the higher.

ar: وَأَلْقِ مَا فِى يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوٓا۟ ۖ إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا۟ كَيْدُ سَٰحِرٍۢ ۖ وَلَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ
en: Cast what is in your right hand, and it will swallow up what they have made, for what they have made is no more than a magic trick. And magicians can never succeed wherever they go.”
t1: And cast down (this staff) that is in your right hand (on the ground). It will swallow up that (craft) which they have contrived (artificially). Whatever they have wrought is but a deceitful trick of a sorcerer, and wherever a magician may come, he will not be successful.’
t2: Cast down what is in thy right hand, and it shall swallow what they have fashioned; for they have fashioned only the guile of a sorcerer, and the sorcerer prospers not; wherever he goes.’
t3: Throw that which is in thy right hand! It will eat up that which they have made. Lo! that which they have made is but a wizard’s artifice, and a wizard shall not be successful to whatever point (of skill) he may attain.

ar: فَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدًۭا قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَٰرُونَ وَمُوسَىٰ
en: So the magicians fell down in prostration, declaring, “We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.”
t1: (Then things happened the same way.) So all the sorcerers were made to fall down in prostration (and) said: ‘We embrace faith in the Lord of Harun (Aaron) and Musa (Moses).’
t2: And the sorcerers cast themselves down prostrating. ’We believe,’ they said, ’in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.’
t3: Then the wizards were (all) flung down prostrate, crying: We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.

ar: قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ ۖ فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَٰفٍۢ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِى جُذُوعِ ٱلنَّخْلِ وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَآ أَشَدُّ عَذَابًۭا وَأَبْقَىٰ
en: Pharaoh threatened, “How dare you believe in him before I give you permission? He must be your master who taught you magic. I will certainly cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and crucify you on the trunks of palm trees. You will really see whose punishment is more severe and more lasting.”
t1: (Pharaoh) said: ‘You have embraced faith in Him before I grant you permission. Surely, he (Musa [Moses]) is also your chief (trainer) who has taught you magic. So, (now) I shall certainly cut off your hands and your feet on the opposite sides and shall certainly crucify you on the palm trunks. Then you shall come to know for sure which of us is sterner in inflicting torture and lasts for a longer term.’
t2: Pharaoh said, ’Have you believed him before I gave you leave? Why, he is the chief of you, the same that taught you sorcery; I shall assuredly cut off alternately your hands and feet, then I shall crucify you upon the trunks of palm-trees; you shall know of a certainty which of us is more terrible in chastisement, and more abiding.’
t3: (Pharaoh) said: Ye put faith in him before I give you leave. Lo! he is your chief who taught you magic. Now surely I shall cut off your hands and your feet alternately, and I shall crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and ye shall know for certain which of us hath sterner and more lasting punishment.

ar: قَالُوا۟ لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ وَٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنَا ۖ فَٱقْضِ مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍ ۖ إِنَّمَا تَقْضِى هَٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَآ
en: They responded, “By the One Who created us! We will never prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us. So do whatever you want! Your authority only covers the ˹fleeting˺ life of this world.
t1: (The magicians) said: ‘We shall not at all prefer you to the clear signs that have come to us. By that (Lord) Who has created us, decide whatever you want to do, for you can decide merely about (this few days’) worldly life.
t2: They said, ’We will not prefer thee over the clear signs that have come to us, nor over Him who originated us. Decide then what thou wilt decide; thou canst only decide touching this present life.
t3: They said: We choose thee not above the clear proofs that have come unto us, and above Him Who created us. So decree what thou wilt decree. Thou wilt end for us only this life of the world.

ar: إِنَّآ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَا وَمَآ أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلسِّحْرِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰٓ
en: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord so He may forgive our sins and that magic you have forced us to practice. And Allah is far superior ˹in reward˺ and more lasting ˹in punishment˺.”
t1: We have indeed believed in our Lord in order that He forgives us our sins, and also (forgives) that sorcery to which you forced us, and Allah is the Best and Ever-Abiding.’
t2: We believe in our Lord, that He may pardon us our offences, and the sorcery thou hast constrained us to practise; God is better, and more abiding.’
t3: Lo! we believe in our Lord, that He may forgive us our sins and the magic unto which thou didst force us. Allah is better and more lasting.

ar: إِنَّهُۥ مَن يَأْتِ رَبَّهُۥ مُجْرِمًۭا فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ جَهَنَّمَ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ
en: Whoever comes to their Lord as an evildoer will certainly have Hell, where they can neither live nor die.
t1: Surely, whoever comes to his Lord as an evildoer, certainly for him is Hell. (And it is such a torment) wherein he will neither die nor survive.
t2: Whosoever comes unto his Lord a sinner, for him awaits Gehenna wherein he shall neither die nor live.
t3: Lo! whoso cometh guilty unto his Lord, verily for him is hell. There he will neither die nor live.

ar: وَمَن يَأْتِهِۦ مُؤْمِنًۭا قَدْ عَمِلَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمُ ٱلدَّرَجَٰتُ ٱلْعُلَىٰ
en: But whoever comes to Him as a believer, having done good, they will have the highest ranks:
t1: And whoever comes to His presence as a believer (and) has (also) done good deeds, it is they for whom are high ranks.
t2: And whoso comes unto Him a believer having done deeds of righteousness, those -- for them await the most sublime degrees;
t3: But whoso cometh unto Him a believer, having done good works, for such are the high stations;

ar: جَنَّٰتُ عَدْنٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا ۚ وَذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ
en: the Gardens of Eternity, under which rivers flow, where they will stay forever. That is the reward of those who purify themselves.
t1: (Those) are evergreen gardens beneath which streams flow. (They) will dwell therein forever. And that is the reward for the one who purifies himself (of the impurity and indecency of disbelief and immorality).
t2: Gardens of Eden, underneath which rivers flow, therein dwelling forever; that is the recompense of the self-purified.
t3: Gardens of Eden underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide for ever. That is the reward of him who groweth.

ar: وَلَقَدْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِى فَٱضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقًۭا فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ يَبَسًۭا لَّا تَخَٰفُ دَرَكًۭا وَلَا تَخْشَىٰ
en: And We surely inspired Moses, ˹saying,˺ “Leave with My servants ˹at night˺ and strike a dry passage for them across the sea. Have no fear of being overtaken, nor be concerned ˹of drowning˺.”
t1: And certainly We sent Revelation to Musa (Moses): ‘Move out at night taking My servants with you. So, make a dry path in the river (by striking your staff). Have no fear to be overtaken (by Pharaoh), nor be afraid (of drowning).’
t2: Also We revealed unto Moses, ’Go with My servants by night; strike for them a dry path in the sea, fearing not overtaking, neither afraid.’
t3: And verily We inspired Moses, saying: Take away My slaves by night and strike for them a dry path in the sea, fearing not to be overtaken, neither being afraid (of the sea).

ar: فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِۦ فَغَشِيَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ
en: Then Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers—but how overwhelming were the waters that submerged them!
t1: Then Pharaoh chased them with his troops. So, the (waves of the) river swept over them as much as they covered them up.
t2: Pharaoh followed them with his hosts, but they were overwhelmed by the sea;
t3: Then Pharaoh followed them with his hosts and there covered them that which did cover them of the sea.

ar: وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُۥ وَمَا هَدَىٰ
en: And ˹so˺ Pharaoh led his people astray, and did not guide ˹them rightly˺.
t1: And Pharaoh led his people astray, and did not guide them to the right path.
t2: so Pharaoh had led his people astray, and was no guide to them.
t3: And Pharaoh led his folk astray, he did not guide them.

ar: يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ قَدْ أَنجَيْنَٰكُم مِّنْ عَدُوِّكُمْ وَوَٰعَدْنَٰكُمْ جَانِبَ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلْأَيْمَنَ وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلْوَىٰ
en: O Children of Israel! We saved you from your enemy, and made an appointment with you
t1: O Children of Israel! (Realize!) Certainly, We delivered you from your enemy, and gave you the promise of (coming to) the right of (Mount) Tur, and (there) We sent down to you the manna and the quails.
t2: Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy; and We made covenant with you upon the right side of the Mount, and sent down on you manna and quails:
t3: O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and we made a covenant with you on the holy mountain’s side, and sent down on you the manna and the quails,

ar: كُلُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقْنَٰكُمْ وَلَا تَطْغَوْا۟ فِيهِ فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِى ۖ وَمَن يَحْلِلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِى فَقَدْ هَوَىٰ
en: ˹saying,˺ “Eat from the good things We have provided for you, but do not transgress in them, or My wrath will befall you. And whoever My wrath befalls is certainly doomed.
t1: (And He said to you:) ‘Eat of the pure things that We have provided for you, and do not exceed limits in that, or My wrath will become inevitable for you. And he on whom My wrath comes due is in truth destroyed.’
t2: ’Eat of the good things wherewith We have provided you; but exceed not therein, or My anger shall alight on you; and on whomsoever My anger alights, that man is hurled to ruin.
t3: (Saying): Eat of the good things wherewith We have provided you, and transgress not in respect thereof lest My wrath come upon you: and he on whom My wrath cometh, he is lost indeed.

ar: وَإِنِّى لَغَفَّارٌۭ لِّمَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا ثُمَّ ٱهْتَدَىٰ
en: But I am truly Most Forgiving to whoever repents, believes, and does good, then persists on ˹true˺ guidance.”
t1: And I am surely Most Forgiving to him who repents and affirms faith and behaves piously, then sticks to guidance (firmly).
t2: Yet I am All-forgiving to him who repents and believes, and does righteousness, and at last is guided.’
t3: And lo! verily I am Forgiving toward him who repenteth and believeth and doeth good, and afterward walketh aright.

ar: ۞ وَمَآ أَعْجَلَكَ عَن قَوْمِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
en: ˹Allah asked,˺ “Why have you come with such haste ahead of your people, O  Moses?”
t1: And, O Musa (Moses), why did you hasten (in coming to Tur ahead of) your people?
t2: ’What has sped thee far from thy people, Moses?’
t3: And (it was said): What hath made thee hasten from thy folk, O Moses ?

ar: قَالَ هُمْ أُو۟لَآءِ عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِى وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضَىٰ
en: He replied, “They are close on my tracks. And I have hastened to You, my Lord, so You will be pleased.”
t1: (Musa [Moses]) submitted: ‘They too are coming behind me, and I have hastened to appear before Your presence (possessed by love and ecstasy) in order that You may be pleased, O my Lord!’
t2: ’They are upon my tracks,’ Moses said. ’I have hastened, Lord, only that I may please Thee.’
t3: He said: They are close upon my track. I hastened unto Thee, my Lord, that Thou mightest be well pleased.

ar: قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدْ فَتَنَّا قَوْمَكَ مِنۢ بَعْدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ
en: Allah responded, “We have indeed tested your people in your absence, and the Samiri has led them astray.”
t1: (Allah) said: ‘We have indeed put your people to trial after you (came away) and Samiri has led them astray.’
t2: Said He, ’We have tempted thy people since thou didst leave them. The Samaritan has misled them into error.’
t3: He said: Lo! We have tried thy folk in thine absence, and As- Samiri hath misled them.

ar: فَرَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ غَضْبَٰنَ أَسِفًۭا ۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ أَلَمْ يَعِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ وَعْدًا حَسَنًا ۚ أَفَطَالَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْعَهْدُ أَمْ أَرَدتُّمْ أَن يَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُم مَّوْعِدِى
en: So Moses returned to his people, furious and sorrowful. He said, “O my people! Had your Lord not made you a good promise?
t1: So, Musa (Moses) returned to his people, angered and grieved, (and) said: ‘O my people, did your Lord not give you a fair promise? Had a long time lapsed on you in (the fulfilment of) the promise? (Or) did you wish that the wrath of your Lord should come due (and befall) you? So you have violated (your) promise to me.’
t2: Then Moses returned very angry and sorrowful to his people, saying, ’My people, did your Lord not promise a fair promise to you? Did the time of the covenant seem so long to you, or did you desire that anger should alight on you from your Lord, so that you failed in your tryst with me?’
t3: Then Moses went back unto his folk, angry and sad. He said: O my people! Hath not your Lord promised you a fair promise ? Did the time appointed then appear too long for you, or did ye wish that wrath from your Lord should come upon you, that ye broke tryst with me ?

ar: قَالُوا۟ مَآ أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا وَلَٰكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَآ أَوْزَارًۭا مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْنَٰهَا فَكَذَٰلِكَ أَلْقَى ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ
en: They argued, “We did not break our promise to you of our own free will, but we were made to carry the burden of the people’s ˹golden˺ jewellery, then we threw it ˹into the fire˺, and so did the Samiri.”
t1: They said: ‘We have not violated our promise to you of our own will, but (what happened is that) we were loaded with the heavy burden of the ornaments of the people, so we cast them (into the fire); then similarly, Samiri (too) cast them away.’
t2: ’We have not failed in our tryst with thee,’ they said, ’of our volition; but we were loaded with fardels, even the ornaments of the people, and we cast them, as the Samaritan also threw them, into the fire.’
t3: They said: We broke not tryst with thee of our own will, but we were laden with burdens of ornaments of the folk, then cast them (in the fire), for thus As-Samiri proposed.

ar: فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًۭا جَسَدًۭا لَّهُۥ خُوَارٌۭ فَقَالُوا۟ هَٰذَآ إِلَٰهُكُمْ وَإِلَٰهُ مُوسَىٰ فَنَسِىَ
en: Then he moulded for them an idol of a calf that made a lowing sound. They said, “This is your god and the god of Moses, but Moses forgot ˹where it was˺!”
t1: Then he (Samiri) moulded (out of the molten ornaments) a statue of a calf for them which produced a sound like that of a cow. Then they said: ‘This is your Lord and the Lord of Musa (Moses too). So he (Samiri) forgot (at this point).’
t2: (Then he brought out for them a Calf, a mere body that lowed; and they said, ’This is your god, and the god of Moses, whom he has forgotten.’
t3: Then he produced for them a calf, of saffron hue, which gave forth a lowing sound. And they cried: This is your god and the god of Moses, but he hath forgotten.

ar: أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًۭا وَلَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ ضَرًّۭا وَلَا نَفْعًۭا
en: Did they not see that it did not respond to them, nor could it protect or benefit them?
t1: Well, did they not see (even this much) that this (calf) could not answer them a word, nor had it any power to cause them any loss or profit?
t2: What? Did they not see that thing returned no speech unto them, neither had any power to hurt or profit them?
t3: See they not, then, that it returneth no saying unto them and possesseth for them neither hurt nor use ?

ar: وَلَقَدْ قَالَ لَهُمْ هَٰرُونُ مِن قَبْلُ يَٰقَوْمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنتُم بِهِۦ ۖ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ فَٱتَّبِعُونِى وَأَطِيعُوٓا۟ أَمْرِى
en: Aaron had already warned them beforehand, “O my people! You are only being tested by this, for indeed your ˹one true˺ Lord is the Most Compassionate. So follow me and obey my orders.”
t1: Earlier, Harun (Aaron also) had said to them, (warning): ‘O people, you have undergone a trial by virtue of this (calf), whilst your Lord is (not this,) but surely (He) the Most Kind One. So follow me and obey my command.’
t2: Yet Aaron had aforetime said to them, ’My people, you have been tempted by this thing, no more; surety your Lord is the All-merciful; therefore follow me, and obey my commandment!’
t3: And Aaron indeed had told them beforehand: O my people! Ye are but being seduced therewith, for lo! your Lord is the Beneficent, so follow me and obey my order.

ar: قَالُوا۟ لَن نَّبْرَحَ عَلَيْهِ عَٰكِفِينَ حَتَّىٰ يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ
en: They replied, “We will not cease to worship it until Moses returns to us.”
t1: They said: ‘We shall hold fast to its (worship) until Musa (Moses) comes back to us.’
t2: ’We will not cease,’ they said, ’to cleave to it, until Moses returns to us.’)
t3: They said: We shall by no means cease to be its votaries till Moses return unto us.

ar: قَالَ يَٰهَٰرُونُ مَا مَنَعَكَ إِذْ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ضَلُّوٓا۟
en: Moses scolded ˹his brother˺, “O Aaron! What prevented you, when you saw them going astray,
t1: Musa (Moses) said: ‘O Harun (Aaron), when you saw them erring, what stopped you,
t2: Moses said, ’What prevented thee, Aaron, when thou sawest them in error,
t3: He (Moses) said: O Aaron! What held thee back when thou didst see them gone astray,

ar: أَلَّا تَتَّبِعَنِ ۖ أَفَعَصَيْتَ أَمْرِى
en: from following after me? How could you disobey my orders?”
t1: (Moreover, who prohibited you) from following my way (in forbidding them fiercely)? Did you disobey me?’
t2: so that thou didst not follow after me? Didst thou then disobey my commandment?’
t3: That thou followedst me not ? Hast thou then disobeyed my order ?

ar: قَالَ يَبْنَؤُمَّ لَا تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِى وَلَا بِرَأْسِىٓ ۖ إِنِّى خَشِيتُ أَن تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَمْ تَرْقُبْ قَوْلِى
en: Aaron pleaded, “O son of my mother! Do not seize me by my beard or ˹the hair of˺ my head. I really feared that you would say, ‘You have caused division among the Children of Israel, and did not observe my word.’”
t1: (Harun [Aaron]) said: ‘O son of my mother, seize me not by my beard or my head. (In being harsh) I feared you would say: You have created division amongst the Children of Israel and have not safeguarded my word.’
t2: ’Son of my mother,’ Aaron said, ’take me not by the beard, or the head! I was fearful that thou wouldst say, "Thou hast divided the Children of Israel, and thou hast not observed my word."
t3: He said: O son of my mother! Clutch not my beard nor my head! I feared lest thou shouldst say: Thou hast caused division among the Children of Israel, and hast not waited for my word.

ar: قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكَ يَٰسَٰمِرِىُّ
en: Moses then asked, “What did you think you were doing, O  Samiri?”
t1: (Musa [Moses]) said: ‘Samiri, (tell me,) what is the matter with you?’
t2: Moses said, ’And thou, Samaritan, what was thy business?’
t3: (Moses) said: And what hast thou to say, O Samiri ?

ar: قَالَ بَصُرْتُ بِمَا لَمْ يَبْصُرُوا۟ بِهِۦ فَقَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةًۭ مِّنْ أَثَرِ ٱلرَّسُولِ فَنَبَذْتُهَا وَكَذَٰلِكَ سَوَّلَتْ لِى نَفْسِى
en: He said, “I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful ˹of dust˺ from the hoof-prints of ˹the horse of˺ the messenger-angel ˹Gabriel˺ then cast it ˹on the moulded calf˺. This is what my lower-self tempted me into.”
t1: He said: ‘I saw what these people had not seen. I took a handful (of dust) from the footstep of the angel (that visited you); then I cast it (into the model of the calf), and this way my (lower) self made (it) attractive to me.’
t2: ’I beheld what they beheld not,’ he said, ’and I seized a handful of dust from the messenger’s track, and cast it into the thing. So my soul prompted me.’
t3: He said: I perceived what they perceive not, so I seized a handful from the footsteps of the messenger, and then threw it in. Thus my soul commended to me.

ar: قَالَ فَٱذْهَبْ فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ أَن تَقُولَ لَا مِسَاسَ ۖ وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًۭا لَّن تُخْلَفَهُۥ ۖ وَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِكَ ٱلَّذِى ظَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًۭا ۖ لَّنُحَرِّقَنَّهُۥ ثُمَّ لَنَنسِفَنَّهُۥ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ نَسْفًا
en: Moses said, “Go away then! And for ˹the rest of your˺ life you will surely be crying, ‘Do not touch ˹me˺!’ that you cannot escape. Now look at your god to which you have been devoted: we will burn it up, then scatter it in the sea completely.”
t1: Musa (Moses) said: ‘So (get out from here and) go away. There is for you a lifelong (punishment) that you will keep saying (to everyone): Touch (me) not, (touch me not). And there is yet another promise (of punishment) for you which will not be averted at all. And look at this (self-made) god of yours to which you held fast (in worship). We will surely burn it and scatter (its dust) well over the river.
t2: ’Depart!’ said Moses. ’It shall be thine all this life to cry "Untouchable!" And thereafter a tryst awaits thee thou canst not fail to keep Behold thy god, to whom all the day thou wast cleaving! We will surely burn it and scatter its ashes into the sea.
t3: (Moses) said: Then go! and lo! in this life it is for thee to say: Touch me not! and lo! there is for thee a tryst thou canst not break. Now look upon thy god of which thou hast remained a votary. Verily we will burn it and will scatter its dust over the sea.

ar: إِنَّمَآ إِلَٰهُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ عِلْمًۭا
en: ˹Then Moses addressed his people,˺ “Your only god is Allah, there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. He encompasses everything in ˹His˺ knowledge.”
t1: (O my people! He) Allah alone is your God apart from Whom there is no God. He has encompassed everything in (His) knowledge.’
t2: Your God is only the One God; there is no god, but He alone who in His knowledge embraces everything.’
t3: Your God is only Allah, than Whom there is no other God. He embraceth all things in His knowledge.

ar: كَذَٰلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ مَا قَدْ سَبَقَ ۚ وَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَٰكَ مِن لَّدُنَّا ذِكْرًۭا
en: This is how We relate to you ˹O Prophet˺ some of the stories of the past. And We have certainly granted you a Reminder from Us.
t1: (O Esteemed Beloved!) Thus We communicate to you news about the (communities) who have passed away, and We have surely given you from Our exclusive presence the Reminder (i.e., an Admonishing Book).
t2: So We relate to thee stories of what has gone before, and We have given thee a remembrance from Us.
t3: Thus relate We unto thee (Muhammad) some tidings of that which happened of old, and We have given thee from Our presence a reminder.

ar: مَّنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَحْمِلُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ وِزْرًا
en: Whoever turns away from it will surely bear the burden ˹of sin˺ on the Day of Judgment,
t1: Whoever turns away from it will certainly carry an unmanageable burden on the Day of Rising.
t2: Whosoever turns away from it, upon the Day of Resurrection He shall bear a fardel,
t3: Whoso turneth away from it, he verily will bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection,

ar: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهِ ۖ وَسَآءَ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ حِمْلًۭا
en: suffering its consequences forever. What an evil burden they will carry on Judgment Day!
t1: They will (remain) in this (torment) forever, and it will be a very evil burden for them on the Day of Rising.
t2: therein abiding forever; how evil upon the Day of Resurrection that burden for them!
t3: Abiding under it - an evil burden for them on the Day of Resurrection,

ar: يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِى ٱلصُّورِ ۚ وَنَحْشُرُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ زُرْقًۭا
en: ˹Beware of˺ the Day the Trumpet will be blown,
t1: The Day when the trumpet will be blown, We shall assemble the evildoers with their bodies and eyes turned blue (due to intense fear and loss of sight),
t2: On the day the Trumpet is blown; and We shall muster the sinners upon that day with eyes staring,
t3: The day when the Trumpet is blown. On that day we assemble the guilty white-eyed (with terror),

ar: يَتَخَٰفَتُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا عَشْرًۭا
en: They will whisper among themselves, “You stayed no more than ten days ˹on the earth˺.”
t1: Inaudibly whispering to one another: ‘You stayed in the world hardly for ten days.’
t2: whispering one to another, ’You have tarried only ten nights.’
t3: Murmuring among themselves: Ye have tarried but ten (days).

ar: نَّحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذْ يَقُولُ أَمْثَلُهُمْ طَرِيقَةً إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا يَوْمًۭا
en: We know best what they will say—the most reasonable of them will say, “You stayed no more than a day.”
t1: We know best what they will be saying, whilst one of them better in wisdom and deeds will say: ‘You have not stayed (in the world) for more than a day.’
t2: We know very well what they will say, when the justest of them in the way will say, ’You have tarried only a day.’
t3: We are Best Aware of what they utter when their best in conduct say: Ye have tarried but a day.

ar: وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْجِبَالِ فَقُلْ يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّى نَسْفًۭا
en: And ˹if˺ they ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about the mountains, ˹then˺ say, “My Lord will wipe them out completely,
t1: And they ask you concerning mountains. So say: ‘My Lord will blow them off as dust particles,
t2: They will question thee concerning the mountains. Say: ’My Lord will scatter them as ashes;
t3: They will ask thee of the mountains (on that day). Say: My Lord will break them into scattered dust.

ar: فَيَذَرُهَا قَاعًۭا صَفْصَفًۭا
en: leaving the earth level and bare,
t1: Then will change it into a levelled, barren land,
t2: then He will leave them a level hollow
t3: And leave it as an empty plain,

ar: لَّا تَرَىٰ فِيهَا عِوَجًۭا وَلَآ أَمْتًۭا
en: with neither depressions nor elevations to be seen.”
t1: In which you will find neither any depression nor any elevation.’
t2: wherein thou wilt see no crookedness neither any curving.’
t3: Wherein thou seest neither curve nor ruggedness.

ar: يَوْمَئِذٍۢ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلدَّاعِىَ لَا عِوَجَ لَهُۥ ۖ وَخَشَعَتِ ٱلْأَصْوَاتُ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ فَلَا تَسْمَعُ إِلَّا هَمْسًۭا
en: On that Day all will follow the caller ˹for assembly˺, ˹and˺ none will dare to deviate. All voices will be hushed before the Most Compassionate. Only whispers will be heard.
t1: On that Day, people will tread on behind the caller, and there will be no deviation in (following) him. And all voices will be hushed due to the Majesty of the Most Kind (Lord). So you will not hear anything except a faint sound of a stir.
t2: On that day they will follow the Summoner in whom is no crookedness; voices will be hushed to the All-merciful, so that thou hearest naught but a murmuring.
t3: On that day they follow the summoner who deceiveth not, and voices are hushed for the Beneficent, and thou hearest but a faint murmur.

ar: يَوْمَئِذٍۢ لَّا تَنفَعُ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةُ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وَرَضِىَ لَهُۥ قَوْلًۭا
en: On that Day no intercession will be of any benefit, except by those granted permission by the Most Compassionate and whose words are agreeable to Him.
t1: On that Day, no intercession shall be fruitful except his (intercession) whom the Most Kind (Lord) has granted leave (and permission) and with whose word He is pleased (such as Prophets and Messengers, Allah’s chosen and pious servants, Godwary slaves, innocent children, and many other devoted servants of Allah whose intercession is validated).
t2: Upon that day the intercession will not profit, save for him to whom the All-merciful gives leave, and whose speech He approves.
t3: On that day no intercession availeth save (that of) him unto whom the Beneficent hath given leave and whose word He accepteth.

ar: يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِۦ عِلْمًۭا
en: He ˹fully˺ knows what is ahead of them and what is behind them,
t1: He knows all those (things) which are ahead of them and which are behind them, and they cannot encompass His (knowledge) with (their) knowledge.
t2: He knows what is before them and behind them, and they comprehend Him not in knowledge.
t3: He knoweth (all) that is before them and (all) that is behind them, while they cannot compass it in knowledge.

ar: ۞ وَعَنَتِ ٱلْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَىِّ ٱلْقَيُّومِ ۖ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًۭا
en: And all faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, All-Sustaining. And those burdened with wrongdoing will be in loss.
t1: And (all) faces will bow down before the holy presence of the Ever-Living (and) Self-Subsisting (Lord), and surely he who bears the burden of wrongdoing will crumble to failure.
t2: And faces shall be humbled unto the Living, the Eternal. He will have failed whose burden is of evildoing;
t3: And faces humble themselves before the Living, the Eternal. And he who beareth (a burden of) wrongdoing is indeed a failure (on that day).

ar: وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌۭ فَلَا يَخَافُ ظُلْمًۭا وَلَا هَضْمًۭا
en: But whoever does good and is a believer will have no fear of being wronged or denied ˹their reward˺.
t1: And whoever does righteous deeds and is also blessed with faith will fear neither any injustice nor any harm.
t2: but whosoever does deeds of righteousness, being a believer, shall fear neither wrong nor injustice.
t3: And he who hath done some good works, being a believer, he feareth not injustice nor begrudging (of his wage).

ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ قُرْءَانًا عَرَبِيًّۭا وَصَرَّفْنَا فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلْوَعِيدِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ أَوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهُمْ ذِكْرًۭا
en: And so We have sent it down as an Arabic Quran and varied the warnings in it, so perhaps they will shun evil or it may cause them to be mindful.
t1: And in this way have We sent down (this last Revealed Book) in the Arabic tongue (in the shape of) the Qur’an, and have explained in it more often than not matters inspiring fear (of torment, in diverse ways,) so that they may become Godfearing, or this (Qur’an) may inculcate in their (hearts a passion for the acceptance of admonition, or) the remembrance (of the Last Day).
t2: Even so We have sent it down as an Arabic Koran, and We have turned about in it something of threats, that haply they may be godfearing, or it may arouse in them remembrance.
t3: Thus we have revealed it as a Lecture in Arabic, and have displayed therein certain threats, that peradventure they may keep from evil or that it may cause them to take heed.

ar: فَتَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱلْحَقُّ ۗ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ ۖ وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدْنِى عِلْمًۭا
en: Exalted is Allah, the True King! Do not rush to recite ˹a revelation of˺ the Quran ˹O Prophet˺ before it is ˹properly˺ conveyed to you, and pray, “My Lord! Increase me in knowledge.”
t1: So Most High and Exalted is Allah. He alone is the True Sovereign. And do not hasten in (reciting) the Qur’an before its revelation is fully accomplished to you. And always submit (before the holy presence of your Lord): ‘O my Lord, increase me further in knowledge.’
t2: So high exalted be God, the true King! And hasten not with the Koran ere its revelation is accomplished unto thee; and say, ’O my Lord, increase me in knowledge.’
t3: Then exalted be Allah, the True King! And hasten not (O Muhammad) with the Qur’an ere its revelation hath been perfected unto thee, and say: My Lord! Increase me in knowledge.

ar: وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ مِن قَبْلُ فَنَسِىَ وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُۥ عَزْمًۭا
en: And indeed, We once made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot, and ˹so˺ We did not find determination in him.
t1: And truly, (far) earlier than this, We had given a strict command to Adam but he forgot. And We did not observe in him any intention (to disobey) at all (it was just an omission).
t2: And We made covenant with Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no constancy.
t3: And verily We made a covenant of old with Adam, but he forgot, and We found no constancy in him.

ar: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ
en: And ˹remember˺ when We said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam,” so they all did—but not Iblis, who refused ˹arrogantly˺.
t1: And (recall the time) when We commanded the angels: ‘Prostrate yourselves before Adam,’ they fell down in prostration except Iblis. He refused.
t2: And when We said to the angels, ’Bow yourselves to Adam’; so they bowed themselves, save Iblis; he refused.
t3: And when We said unto the angels: Fall prostrate before Adam, they fell prostrate (all) save Iblis; he refused.

ar: فَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ إِنَّ هَٰذَا عَدُوٌّۭ لَّكَ وَلِزَوْجِكَ فَلَا يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَىٰٓ
en: So We cautioned, “O Adam! This is surely an enemy to you and to your wife. So do not let him drive you both out of Paradise, for you ˹O Adam˺ would then suffer ˹hardship˺.
t1: Then We said: ‘O Adam, verily, this (Satan) is an enemy to you and your wife. So let him not get you both ousted from Paradise; then you shall be put to toil.
t2: Then We said, ’Adam, surely this is an enemy to thee and thy wife. So let him not expel you both from the Garden, so that thou art unprosperous.
