t1: He had nearly turned us away from our gods, had we not held fast to their (worship).’ And when they see the torment, they will soon realize who was astray.
t2: Wellnigh he had led us astray from our gods, but that we kept steadfast to them.’ Assuredly they shall know, when they see the chastisement, who is further astray from the way.
t3: He would have led us far away from our gods if we had not been staunch to them. They will know, when they behold the doom, who is more astray as to the road.

ar: أَرَءَيْتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ أَفَأَنتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ وَكِيلًا
en: Have you seen ˹O Prophet˺ the one who has taken their own desires as their god? Will you then be a keeper over them?
t1: Have you seen him who has taken the desire of his lower self as god? Would you then become a guardian over him?
t2: Hast thou seen him who has taken his caprice to be his god? Wilt thou be a guardian over them?
t3: Hast thou seen him who chooseth for his god his own lust ? Wouldst thou then be guardian over him ?

ar: أَمْ تَحْسَبُ أَنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ أَوْ يَعْقِلُونَ ۚ إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا كَٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ ۖ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا
en: Or do you think that most of them listen or understand?
t1: Do you think that most of them hear or understand? (Nay,) they have become like cattle, rather worse in error than they are.
t2: Or deemest thou that most of them hear or understand? They are but as the cattle; nay, they are further astray from the way.
t3: Or deemest thou that most of them hear or understand ? They are but as the cattle - nay, but they are farther astray ?

ar: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ وَلَوْ شَآءَ لَجَعَلَهُۥ سَاكِنًۭا ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا ٱلشَّمْسَ عَلَيْهِ دَلِيلًۭا
en: Have you not seen how your Lord extends the shade—He could have simply made it ˹remain˺ still if He so willed—then We make the sun its guide,
t1: Have you not had a glance of (the Might of) your Lord, how He lengthens the shadow (till noon)? And had He willed, He could certainly have made it stationary. Then We have made the sun a proof of this (shadow).
t2: Hast thou not regarded thy Lord, how He has stretched out the shadow? Had He willed, He would have made it still. Then We appointed the sun, to be a guide to it;
t3: Hast thou not seen how thy Lord hath spread the shade - And if He willed He could have made it still - then We have made the sun its pilot;

ar: ثُمَّ قَبَضْنَٰهُ إِلَيْنَا قَبْضًۭا يَسِيرًۭا
en: causing the shade to retreat gradually?
t1: Then, drawing this (shadow) little by little towards Ourselves, We roll it up.
t2: thereafter We seize it to Ourselves, drawing it gently.
t3: Then We withdraw it unto Us, a gradual withdrawal ?

ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيْلَ لِبَاسًۭا وَٱلنَّوْمَ سُبَاتًۭا وَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ نُشُورًۭا
en: He is the One Who has made the night for you as a cover, and ˹made˺ sleep for resting, and the day for rising.
t1: And He is the One Who has made the night a (wrapper-like) covering for you and made sleep (a means of) rest (for you) and the day a time to get up (for work).
t2: It is He who appointed the night for you to be a garment and sleep for a rest, and day He appointed for a rising.
t3: And He it is Who maketh night a covering for you, and sleep repose, and maketh day a resurrection.

ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَرْسَلَ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ بُشْرًۢا بَيْنَ يَدَىْ رَحْمَتِهِۦ ۚ وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ طَهُورًۭا
en: And He is the One Who sends the winds ushering in His mercy, and We send down pure rain from the sky,
t1: And He is the One Who sends the breezes as good news before (the rain of) His mercy. And it is We Who send down pure (and cleansing) water from the sky,
t2: And it is He who has loosed the winds, bearing good tidings before His mercy; and We sent down from heaven pure water
t3: And He it is Who sendeth the winds, glad tidings heralding His mercy, and We send down purifying water from the sky,

ar: لِّنُحْۦِىَ بِهِۦ بَلْدَةًۭ مَّيْتًۭا وَنُسْقِيَهُۥ مِمَّا خَلَقْنَآ أَنْعَٰمًۭا وَأَنَاسِىَّ كَثِيرًۭا
en: giving life to a lifeless land, and providing water for countless animals and humans of Our Own creation.
t1: So that We may give life with that to (any) dead city, and (furthermore) We provide this (water) for drink to many cattle and (nomadic) people that We have created.
t2: so that We might revive a dead land, and give to drink of it, of that We created, cattle and men a many.
t3: That We may give life thereby to a dead land, and We give many beasts and men that We have created to drink thereof.

ar: وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَٰهُ بَيْنَهُمْ لِيَذَّكَّرُوا۟ فَأَبَىٰٓ أَكْثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ إِلَّا كُفُورًۭا
en: We certainly disperse it among them so they may be mindful, but most people persist in ungratefulness.
t1: And surely, We keep distributing this (rain) amongst them (on the scale of different times and cities) so that they may contemplate. Even then most people did not accept (anything) except ingratitude.
t2: We have indeed turned it about amongst them, so that they may remember; yet most men refuse all but unbelief.
t3: And verily We have repeated it among them that they may remember, but most of mankind begrudge aught save ingratitude.

ar: وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَبَعَثْنَا فِى كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍۢ نَّذِيرًۭا
en: Had We willed, We could have easily sent a warner to every society.
t1: And had We willed, We would have sent a Warner in every town.
t2: If We had willed, We would have raised up in every city a warner.
t3: If We willed, We could raise up a warner in every village.

ar: فَلَا تُطِعِ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ وَجَٰهِدْهُم بِهِۦ جِهَادًۭا كَبِيرًۭا
en: So do not yield to the disbelievers, but strive diligently against them with this ˹Quran˺.
t1: So, (O man of faith,) do not follow the disbelievers, and launch a large-scale struggle against them by means of (logic and preaching of the Qur’an).
t2: So obey not the unbelievers, but struggle with them thereby mightily.
t3: So obey not the disbelievers, but strive against them herewith with a great endeavour.

ar: ۞ وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى مَرَجَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ هَٰذَا عَذْبٌۭ فُرَاتٌۭ وَهَٰذَا مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌۭ وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخًۭا وَحِجْرًۭا مَّحْجُورًۭا
en: And He is the One Who merges the two bodies of water: one fresh and palatable and the other salty and bitter, placing between them a barrier they cannot cross.
t1: And He is the One Who joined two rivers, this (one) very sweet and freshening and that (other one) very salty and bitter. And He set a barrier and a strong partition between them.
t2: And it is He who let forth the two seas, this one Sweet, grateful to taste, and this salt, bitter to the tongue, and He set between them a barrier, and a ban forbidden.
t3: And He it is Who hath given independence to the two seas (though they meet); one palatable, sweet, and the other saltish, bitter; and hath set a bar and a forbidding ban between them.

ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ بَشَرًۭا فَجَعَلَهُۥ نَسَبًۭا وَصِهْرًۭا ۗ وَكَانَ رَبُّكَ قَدِيرًۭا
en: And He is the One Who creates human beings from a ˹humble˺ liquid, then establishes for them bonds of kinship and marriage. For your Lord is Most Capable.
t1: And He is the One Who created man from (a sperm drop resembling) water, and made for him (kinship by) lineage and in-laws. And your Lord is All-Powerful.
t2: And it is He who created of water a mortal, and made him kindred of blood and marriage; thy Lord is All-powerful.
t3: And He it is Who hath created man from water, and hath appointed for him kindred by blood and kindred by marriage; for thy Lord is ever Powerful.

ar: وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُهُمْ وَلَا يَضُرُّهُمْ ۗ وَكَانَ ٱلْكَافِرُ عَلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ ظَهِيرًۭا
en: Yet they worship besides Allah what can neither benefit nor harm them. And the disbeliever always collaborates against their Lord.
t1: And they (disbelievers) worship besides Allah those (idols) that can neither bring them any profit, nor do them any harm. And the disbeliever is (always) a helper (of Satan) in (disobeying) his Lord.
t2: And they serve, apart from God, what neither profits them nor hurts them; and the unbeliever is ever a partisan against his Lord.
t3: Yet they worship instead of Allah that which can neither benefit them nor hurt them. The disbeliever was ever a partisan against his Lord.

ar: وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَٰكَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرًۭا وَنَذِيرًۭا
en: And We have sent you ˹O Prophet˺ only as a deliverer of good news and a warner.
t1: And We have not sent you but as a Bearer of good news (for the obedient servants of Allah) and as a Warner (to the rebels).
t2: We have sent thee not, except good tidings to bear, and warning.
t3: And We have sent thee (O Muhammad) only as a bearer of good tidings and a warner.

ar: قُلْ مَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِلَّا مَن شَآءَ أَن يَتَّخِذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ سَبِيلًۭا
en: Say, “I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺, but whoever wishes, let them pursue the Way to their Lord.”
t1: Say: ‘I do not ask you for any compensation for this (preaching), but that whoever desires to take a path to (reach) his Lord (may step in).’
t2: Say: ’I do not ask of you a wage for this, except for him who wishes to take to his Lord a way.’
t3: Say: I ask of you no reward for this, save that whoso will may choose a way unto his Lord.

ar: وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱلْحَىِّ ٱلَّذِى لَا يَمُوتُ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِهِۦ ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِهِۦ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِۦ خَبِيرًا
en: Put your trust in the Ever-Living, Who never dies, and glorify His praises. Sufficient is He as All-Aware of the sins of His servants.
t1: And put your trust in the Ever-Living (Lord) Who will never die, and glorify Him with His praise, and Sufficient is His awareness of the sins of His servants,
t2: Put thy trust in the Living God, the Undying, and proclaim His praise. Sufficiently is He aware of His servants sins
t3: And trust thou in the Living One Who dieth not, and hymn His praise. He sufficeth as the Knower of His bondmen’s sins,

ar: ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِى سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍۢ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ۚ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ فَسْـَٔلْ بِهِۦ خَبِيرًۭا
en: ˹He is˺ the One Who created the heavens and the earth and everything in between in six Days, then established Himself on the Throne. ˹He is˺ the Most Compassionate! Ask ˹none other than˺ the All-Knowledgeable about Himself.
t1: He Who created the heavenly spheres and the earth and this (universe) in between in six periods.* Then He established (His authority) on the Throne (befitting His Majesty. He) is Most Kind. (O aspirant to His gnosis!) Ask of Him someone who has attained to His awareness. (The unaware do not have any gnosis of Him.)
t2: who created the heavens and the earth, and what between them is, in six days, then sat Himself upon the Throne, the All-compassionate: ask any informed of Him!
t3: Who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six Days, then He mounted the Throne. The Beneficent! Ask anyone informed concerning Him!

ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ قَالُوا۟ وَمَا ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ أَنَسْجُدُ لِمَا تَأْمُرُنَا وَزَادَهُمْ نُفُورًۭا ۩
en: When it is said to them, “Prostrate to the Most Compassionate,” they ask ˹in disgust˺, “What is ‘the Most Compassionate’? Will we prostrate to whatever you order us to?” And it only drives them farther away.
t1: And when it is said to them: ‘Prostrate yourselves before the Most Kind (Lord),’ the (deniers of the truth) say: ‘What is the Most Kind Lord? Shall we prostrate ourselves before whatever you command us?’ And this (command) increased only hatred in them.
t2: But when they are told, ’Bow yourselves to the All-merciful,’ they say, ’And what is the All-merciful? Shall we bow ourselves to what thou biddest us?’ And it increases them in aversion.
t3: And when it is said unto them: Adore the Beneficent! they say: And what is the Beneficent ? Are we to adore whatever thou (Muhammad) biddest us ? And it increaseth aversion in them.

ar: تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ بُرُوجًۭا وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سِرَٰجًۭا وَقَمَرًۭا مُّنِيرًۭا
en: Blessed is the One Who has placed constellations in the sky, as well as a ˹radiant˺ lamp and a luminous moon.
t1: Most Blessed and Most Glorified is He Who made vast mansions of heavenly spheres (in the form of galaxies) in the heavenly cosmos and made (the sun) in it a (light-generating and heat-emitting) lamp and a shining moon (in the solar system).
t2: Blessed be He who has set in heaven constellations, and has set among them a lamp, and an illuminating moon.
t3: Blessed be He Who hath placed in the heaven mansions of the stars, and hath placed therein a great lamp and a moon giving light!

ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ خِلْفَةًۭ لِّمَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَذَّكَّرَ أَوْ أَرَادَ شُكُورًۭا
en: And He is the One Who causes the day and the night to alternate, ˹as a sign˺ for whoever desires to be mindful or to be grateful.
t1: And He is the One Who made the day and the night rotate after each other for him who desires to contemplate or intends to be grateful. (There is direction and guidance in these creative powers.)
t2: And it is He who made the night and day a succession for whom He desires to remember or He desires to be thankful.
t3: And He it is Who hath appointed night and day in succession, for him who desireth to remember, or desireth thankfulness.

ar: وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ هَوْنًۭا وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ ٱلْجَٰهِلُونَ قَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًۭا
en: The ˹true˺ servants of the Most Compassionate are those who walk on the earth humbly, and when the foolish address them ˹improperly˺, they only respond with peace.
t1: And the (favourite) servants of the Most Kind (Lord) are those who walk gently on the earth, and when the ignorant (i.e., impolite) people say to them something (unlikable), they (get aside), saying: ‘Peace.’
t2: The servants of the All-merciful are those who walk in the earth modestly and who, when the ignorant address them, say, ’Peace’;
t3: The (faithful) slaves of the Beneficent are they who walk upon the earth modestly, and when the foolish ones address them answer: Peace;

ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًۭا وَقِيَٰمًۭا
en: ˹They are˺ those who spend ˹a good portion of˺ the night, prostrating themselves and standing before their Lord.
t1: And (these) are the ones who spend their nights prostrating themselves and standing before their Lord (cloaked in submissiveness).
t2: who pass the night prostrate to their Lord and standing;
t3: And who spend the night before their Lord, prostrate and standing,

ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا ٱصْرِفْ عَنَّا عَذَابَ جَهَنَّمَ ۖ إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَامًا
en: ˹They are˺ those who pray, “Our Lord! Keep the punishment of Hell away from us, for its punishment is indeed unrelenting.
t1: And (these) are the people who pray (all the time before the presence of Allah): ‘O our Lord, turn away from us the torment of Hell. Surely, its torment is most injurious (and everlasting).
t2: who say, ’Our Lord, turn Thou from us the chastisement of Gehenna; surely its chastisement is torment most terrible;
t3: And who say: Our Lord! Avert from us the doom of hell; lo! the doom thereof is anguish;

ar: إِنَّهَا سَآءَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّۭا وَمُقَامًۭا
en: It is certainly an evil place to settle and reside.”
t1: Surely, that is an evil lodging (for temporary lodgers) and an evil abode (for permanent dwellers).’
t2: evil it is as a lodging-place and an abode’;
t3: Lo! it is wretched as abode and station;

ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَنفَقُوا۟ لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا۟ وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا۟ وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ قَوَامًۭا
en: ˹They are˺ those who spend neither wastefully nor stingily, but moderately in between.
t1: And (these) are the people who are neither extravagant nor miserly when they spend. And their spending is (based on) a balance between the two extremes (of extravagance and miserliness).
t2: who, when they expend, are neither prodigal nor parsimonious, but between that is a just stand;
t3: And those who, when they spend, are neither prodigal nor grudging; and there is ever a firm station between the two;

ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ وَلَا يَقْتُلُونَ ٱلنَّفْسَ ٱلَّتِى حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَا يَزْنُونَ ۚ وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثَامًۭا
en: ˹They are˺ those who do not invoke any other god besides Allah, nor take a ˹human˺ life—made sacred by Allah—except with ˹legal˺ right, nor commit fornication. And whoever does ˹any of˺ this will face the penalty.
t1: And these are the people who do not worship any other god apart from Allah, nor do they kill the soul whose killing without any lawful cause Allah has forbidden, nor do they commit adultery. And whoever does this will receive the punishment due for the sin.
t2: who call not upon another god with God, nor slay the soul God has forbidden except by right, neither fornicate, for whosoever does that shall meet the price
t3: And those who cry not unto any other god along with Allah, nor take the life which Allah hath forbidden save in (course of) justice, nor commit adultery - and whoso doeth this shall pay the penalty;

ar: يُضَٰعَفْ لَهُ ٱلْعَذَابُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِۦ مُهَانًا
en: Their punishment will be multiplied on the Day of Judgment, and they will remain in it forever, in disgrace.
t1: His punishment will be doubled on the Day of Rising and, disgraced and humiliated, he will live in it forever.
t2: of sin-doubled shall be the chastisement for him on the Resurrection Day, and he shall dwell therein humbled,
t3: The doom will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein disdained for ever;

ar: إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًۭا صَٰلِحًۭا فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمْ حَسَنَٰتٍۢ ۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورًۭا رَّحِيمًۭا
en: As for those who repent, believe, and do good deeds, they are the ones whose evil deeds Allah will change into good deeds. For Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
t1: But whoever repents and believes and does good deeds, so these are the people whose evil deeds Allah will change into good ones. And Allah is Most Forgiving, Ever-Merciful.
t2: save him who repents, and believes, and does righteous work -- those, God will change their evil deeds into good deeds, for God is ever All-forgiving, All-compassionate;
t3: Save him who repenteth and believeth and doth righteous work; as for such, Allah will change their evil deeds to good deeds. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.

ar: وَمَن تَابَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا فَإِنَّهُۥ يَتُوبُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَتَابًۭا
en: And whoever repents and does good has truly turned to Allah properly.
t1: And whoever repents and executes good, so he returns to Allah (the way) returning is due.
t2: and whosoever repents, and does righteousness, he truly turns to God in repentance.
t3: And whosoever repenteth and doeth good, he verily repenteth toward Allah with true repentance -

ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَشْهَدُونَ ٱلزُّورَ وَإِذَا مَرُّوا۟ بِٱللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا۟ كِرَامًۭا
en: ˹They are˺ those who do not bear false witness, and when they come across falsehood, they pass ˹it˺ by with dignity.
t1: And these are the people who do not attend (both verbally and practically) the false and untruthful matters, and when they pass by evil activities, they pass on (observing caution) with utmost nobility and dignity.
t2: And those who bear not false witness and, when they pass by idle talk, pass by with dignity;
t3: And those who will not witness vanity, but when they pass near senseless play, pass by with dignity.

ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ لَمْ يَخِرُّوا۟ عَلَيْهَا صُمًّۭا وَعُمْيَانًۭا
en: ˹They are˺ those who, when reminded of the revelation of their Lord, do not turn a blind eye or a deaf ear to it.
t1: And these are the people who, when they are directed and guided by means of Revelations of their Lord, do not fall at them deaf and blind (but reflect on them).
t2: who, when they are reminded of the signs of their Lord, fall not down thereat deaf and blind;
t3: And those who, when they are reminded of the revelations of their Lord, fall not deaf and blind thereat.

ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَٰجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّٰتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍۢ وَٱجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا
en: ˹They are˺ those who pray, “Our Lord! Bless us with ˹pious˺ spouses and offspring who will be the joy of our hearts, and make us models for the righteous.”
t1: And these are the people who submit (before the presence of Allah): ‘O our Lord, grant us coolness of eyes in our wives and our children, and make us leaders of the Godfearing people.’
t2: who say, ’Our Lord, give us refreshment of our wives and seed, and make us a model to the godfearing.’
t3: And who say: Our Lord! Vouchsafe us comfort of our wives and of our offspring, and make us patterns for (all) those who ward off (evil).

ar: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ ٱلْغُرْفَةَ بِمَا صَبَرُوا۟ وَيُلَقَّوْنَ فِيهَا تَحِيَّةًۭ وَسَلَٰمًا
en: It is they who will be rewarded with ˹elevated˺ mansions ˹in Paradise˺ for their perseverance, and will be received with salutations and ˹greetings of˺ peace,
t1: They will be rewarded with lofty palaces (in Paradise) as recompense for their patience and steadfastness and will be welcomed therein with greetings and salutations of peace.
t2: Those shall be recompensed with the highest heaven, for that they endured patiently, and they shall receive therein a greeting and --’ Peace!’
t3: They will be awarded the high place forasmuch as they were steadfast, and they will meet therein with welcome and the ward of peace,

ar: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا ۚ حَسُنَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّۭا وَمُقَامًۭا
en: staying there forever. What an excellent place to settle and reside!
t1: They will live therein forever. Those (lofty palaces in Paradise) are the most excellent lodgings and (decent) abodes.
t2: Therein they shall dwell forever; fair it is as a lodging-place and an abode.
t3: Abiding there for ever. Happy is it as abode and station!

ar: قُلْ مَا يَعْبَؤُا۟ بِكُمْ رَبِّى لَوْلَا دُعَآؤُكُمْ ۖ فَقَدْ كَذَّبْتُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزَامًۢا
en: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “You ˹all˺ would not ˹even˺ matter to my Lord were it not for your faith ˹in Him˺. But now you ˹disbelievers˺ have denied ˹the truth˺, so the torment is bound to come.”
t1: Say: ‘My Lord cares little for you if you do not worship (Him). But you have indeed rejected (Him). So now this (denial) will ever endure as a permanent torment (for you).’
t2: Say: ’My Lord esteems you not at all were it not for your prayer, for you have cried lies, and it shall surely be fastened.’
t3: Say (O Muhammad, unto the disbelievers): My Lord would not concern Himself with you but for your prayer. But now ye have denied (the Truth), therefor there will be judgment.

ar: طسٓمٓ
en: Ṭa-Sĩn-Mĩm.
t1: Ta, Sin, Mim. (Only Allah and the Messenger [blessings and peace be upon him] know the real meaning.)
t2: Ta Sin Mim
t3: Ta. Sin. Mim.

ar: تِلْكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ ٱلْمُبِينِ
en: These are the verses of the clear Book.
t1: These are the Verses of the Book that makes clear (the truth).
t2: Those are the signs of the Manifest Book.
t3: These are revelations of the Scripture that maketh plain.

ar: لَعَلَّكَ بَٰخِعٌۭ نَّفْسَكَ أَلَّا يَكُونُوا۟ مُؤْمِنِينَ
en: Perhaps you ˹O Prophet˺ will grieve yourself to death over their disbelief.
t1: (O Esteemed Beloved!) You will perhaps risk your (dearest) life, (grieving) that they do not accept faith.
t2: Perchance thou consumest thyself that they are not believers.
t3: It may be that thou tormentest thyself (O Muhammad) because they believe not.

ar: إِن نَّشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ ءَايَةًۭ فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَٰقُهُمْ لَهَا خَٰضِعِينَ
en: If We willed, We could send down upon them a ˹compelling˺ sign from the heavens, leaving their necks bent in ˹utter˺ submission to it.
t1: If We intend, We should send down upon them (such) a sign from heaven as their necks would not but bow down before it.
t2: If We will, We shall send down on them out of heaven a sign, so their necks will stay humbled to it.
t3: If We will, We can send down on them from the sky a portent so that their necks would remain bowed before it.

ar: وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ مُحْدَثٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا۟ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضِينَ
en: Whatever new reminder comes to them from the Most Compassionate, they always turn away from it.
t1: And there does not come to them any new admonition from the Most Kind (Lord) but they turn away from it.
t2: But never fresh remembrance comes to them from the All-merciful, except they turn away from it.
t3: Never cometh there unto them a fresh reminder from the Beneficent One, but they turn away from it.

ar: فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوا۟ فَسَيَأْتِيهِمْ أَنۢبَٰٓؤُا۟ مَا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ
en: They have certainly denied ˹the truth˺, so they will soon face the consequences of their ridicule.
t1: Thus they have indeed denied (the truth), so the news of what they used to make fun of will reach them soon.
t2: So they have cried lies; therefore assuredly tidings will come to them of that they mocked at.
t3: Now they have denied (the Truth); but there will come unto them tidings of that whereat they used to scoff.

ar: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ كَمْ أَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍۢ كَرِيمٍ
en: Have they failed to look at the earth, ˹to see˺ how many types of fine plants We have caused to grow in it?
t1: And have they not discerned the earth—what a variety of excellent vegetation We have caused to grow in it?
t2: What, have they not regarded the earth, how many therein We have caused to grow of every generous kind?
t3: Have they not seen the earth, how much of every fruitful kind We make to grow therein ?

ar: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
en: Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.
t1: Surely, there is a sign in it (of Allah’s might), but most of them are not the ones to believe.
t2: Surely in that is a sign, yet most of them are not believers.
t3: Lo! herein is indeed a portent; yet most of them are not believers.

ar: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
en: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.
t1: And assuredly, your Lord alone is the Almighty, Ever-Merciful.
t2: Surely thy Lord, He is the All-mighty, the All-compassionate.
t3: And lo! thy Lord! He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful.

ar: وَإِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبُّكَ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱئْتِ ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
en: ˹Remember˺ when your Lord called out to Moses, “Go to the wrongdoing people—
t1: And (recall) when your Lord called to Musa (Moses): ‘Go to the wrongdoing people;
t2: And when thy Lord called to Moses, ’Go to the people of the evildoers,
t3: And when thy Lord called Moses, saying: Go unto the wrongdoing folk,

ar: قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ ۚ أَلَا يَتَّقُونَ
en: the people of Pharaoh. Will they not fear ˹Allah˺?”
t1: (That is) the people of Pharaoh. Do they not fear (Allah)?’
t2: the people of Pharaoh; will they not be godfearing?’
t3: The folk of Pharaoh. Will they not ward off (evil) ?

ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
en: He replied, “My Lord! I fear that they will reject me.
t1: Musa (Moses) submitted: ‘O my Lord, I fear that they will reject me.
t2: He said, ’My Lord, I fear they will cry me lies,
t3: He said: My Lord! Lo! I fear that they will deny me,

ar: وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ
en: And ˹so˺ my heart will be broken and my tongue will be tied. So send Aaron along ˹as a messenger˺.
t1: And my breast constricts (under such adverse circumstances) and my tongue does not express (fluently), so send (Gabriel with revelation) to Harun ([Aaron] as well so that he becomes my helper).
t2: and my breast will be straitened, and my tongue will not be loosed; so send to Aaron.
t3: And I shall be embarrassed, and my tongue will not speak plainly, therefor send for Aaron (to help me).

ar: وَلَهُمْ عَلَىَّ ذَنۢبٌۭ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ
en: Also, they have a charge against me, so I fear they may kill me.”
t1: And they also have a charge against me (of killing a Copt), so I fear they may kill me.’
t2: They also have a sin against me, and I fear they will slay me.’
t3: And they have a crime against me, so I fear that they will kill me.

ar: قَالَ كَلَّا ۖ فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ ۖ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ
en: Allah responded, “Certainly not! So go, both of you, with Our signs. We will be with you, listening.
t1: (Allah) said: ‘By no means, so go both of you, with Our signs. Surely, We are with you, hearing (everything).
t2: Said He, ’No indeed; but go, both of you, with Our signs, and We assuredly shall be with you, listening.
t3: He said: Nay, verily. So go ye twain with Our tokens. Lo! We shall be with you, Hearing.

ar: فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: Go to Pharaoh and say, ‘We are messengers from the Lord of all worlds,
t1: So go, both of you, to Pharaoh and say: We are the Messengers (sent) by the Lord of all the worlds.
t2: So go you to Pharaoh, and say, "Verily, I am the Messenger of the Lord of all Being;
t3: And come together unto Pharaoh and say: Lo! we bear a message of the Lord of the Worlds,

ar: أَنْ أَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
en: ˹commanded to say:˺ ‘Let the Children of Israel go with us.’’”
t1: (Our aim is that) you send the Children of Israel with us (setting them free).’
t2: so send forth with us the Children of Israel."
t3: (Saying): Let the Children of Israel go with us.

ar: قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًۭا وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ
en: Pharaoh protested, “Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you stayed several years of your life in our care?
t1: Pharaoh said: ‘Did we not bring you up amongst us as a child, and you spent many years of your life with us?’
t2: He said, ’Did we not raise thee amongst us as a child? Didst thou not tarry among us years of thy life?
t3: (Pharaoh) said (unto Moses): Did we not rear thee among us as a child ? And thou didst dwell many years of thy life among us,

ar: وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ ٱلَّتِى فَعَلْتَ وَأَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
en: Then you did what you did, being ˹utterly˺ ungrateful!”
t1: And (then) you committed that deed which you committed (i.e., you killed a Copt), and you are one of the ungrateful (you have forgotten our guardianship and favours).
t2: And thou didst the deed thou didst, being one of the ungrateful!’
t3: And thou didst that thy deed which thou didst, and thou wast one of the ingrates.

ar: قَالَ فَعَلْتُهَآ إِذًۭا وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
en: Moses replied, “I did it then, lacking guidance.
t1: (Musa [Moses]) said: ‘When I did that deed, I was unaware (that even a single blow would take his life).
t2: Said he, ’Indeed I did it then, being one of those that stray;
t3: He said: I did it then, when I was of those who are astray.

ar: فَفَرَرْتُ مِنكُمْ لَمَّا خِفْتُكُمْ فَوَهَبَ لِى رَبِّى حُكْمًۭا وَجَعَلَنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
en: So I fled from you when I feared you. Then my Lord granted me wisdom and made me one of the messengers.
t1: So (at that time), I went out of your (line of control) when I feared your (designs). Then my Lord bestowed on me the commandment (of Prophethood) and (finally) made me one of the Messengers.
t2: so I fled from you, fearing you. But my Lord gave me Judgment and made me one of the Envoys.
t3: Then I fled from you when I feared you, and my Lord vouchsafed me a command and appointed me (of the number) of those sent (by Him).

ar: وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌۭ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَىَّ أَنْ عَبَّدتَّ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
en: How can that be a ‘favour,’ of which you remind me, when ˹it was only because˺ you ˹have˺ enslaved the Children of Israel?”
t1: And is that (any) favour of which you are reminding me? (That happened also because) you had enslaved (all my people) the Children of Israel.’
t2: That is a blessing thou reproachest me with, having enslaved the Children of Israel.’
t3: And this is the past favour wherewith thou reproachest me: that thou hast enslaved the Children of Israel.

ar: قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَا رَبُّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: Pharaoh asked, “And what is ‘the Lord of all worlds’?”
t1: (Pharaoh) said: ‘What is the Lord of all the worlds?’
t2: Pharaoh said, ’And what is the Lord of all Being?’
t3: Pharaoh said: And what is the Lord of the Worlds ?

ar: قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ ۖ إِن كُنتُم مُّوقِنِينَ
en: Moses replied, “˹He is˺ the Lord of the heavens and the earth and everything in between, if only you had sure faith.”
t1: (Musa [Moses]) said: ‘(He) is the Lord of all the heavens and the earth and the (whole universe) between the two if you are a firm believer.’
t2: He said, ’The Lord of the heavens and earth, and what between them is, if you have faith.’
t3: (Moses) said: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, if ye had but sure belief.

ar: قَالَ لِمَنْ حَوْلَهُۥٓ أَلَا تَسْتَمِعُونَ
en: Pharaoh said to those around him, “Did you hear ˹what he said˺?”
t1: He said to those seated around him: ‘Are you not listening?’
t2: Said he to those about him, ’Do you not hear?’
t3: (Pharaoh) said unto those around him: Hear ye not ?

ar: قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ ءَابَآئِكُمُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
en: Moses added, “˹He is˺ your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers.”
t1: (Musa [Moses]) added: ‘(The One Who) is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers (too).’
t2: He said, ’Your Lord and the Lord of your fathers, the ancients.’
t3: He said: Your Lord and the Lord of your fathers.

ar: قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌۭ
en: Pharaoh said ˹mockingly˺, “Your messenger, who has been sent to you, must be insane.”
t1: (Pharaoh) said: ‘Surely, your Messenger that has been sent to you is but insane.’
t2: Said he, ’Surely your Messenger who was sent to you is possessed!’
t3: (Pharaoh) said: Lo! your messenger who hath been sent unto you is indeed a madman!

ar: قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ وَٱلْمَغْرِبِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ ۖ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ
en: Moses responded: “˹He is˺ the Lord of the east and west, and everything in between, if only you had any sense.”
t1: (Musa [Moses]) said: ‘(He) is the Lord of the east and the west, and (the whole universe) between the two if you have (some) sense.’
t2: He said, ’The Lord of the East and West, and what between them is, if you have understanding,’
t3: He said: Lord of the East and the West and all that is between them, if ye did but understand.

ar: قَالَ لَئِنِ ٱتَّخَذْتَ إِلَٰهًا غَيْرِى لَأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمَسْجُونِينَ
en: Pharaoh threatened, “If you take any other god besides me, I will certainly have you imprisoned.”
t1: (Pharaoh) said: ‘(O Musa [Moses,]) if you take a god other than me, I will certainly (arrest and) put you amongst the prisoners.’
t2: Said he, ’If thou takest a god other than me, I shall surely make thee one of the imprisoned.’
t3: (Pharaoh) said: If thou choosest a god other than me, I assuredly shall place thee among the prisoners.

ar: قَالَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكَ بِشَىْءٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
en: Moses responded, “Even if I bring you a clear proof?”
t1: (Musa [Moses]) said: ‘Even if I bring you something manifest (also as a miracle)?’
t2: He said, ’What, even though I brought thee something so manifest?’
t3: He said: Even though I show thee something plain ?

ar: قَالَ فَأْتِ بِهِۦٓ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
en: Pharaoh demanded, “Bring it then, if what you say is true.”
t1: (Pharaoh) said: ‘Bring it if you are truthful.’
t2: Said he, ’Bring it then, if thou art of the truthful.’
t3: (Pharaoh) said: Produce it then, if thou art of the truthful!

ar: فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ ثُعْبَانٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
en: So he threw down his staff and—behold!—it became a real snake.
t1: So Musa (Moses) put his staff down (on the ground) and that, at once, became a serpent, evidently clear.
t2: So he cast his staff, and behold, it was a serpent manifest.
t3: Then he flung down his staff and it became a serpent manifest,

ar: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ
en: Then he drew his hand ˹out of his collar˺ and it was ˹shining˺ white for all to see.
t1: And (Musa [Moses]) brought out his hand (after putting it under his armpit) and there it became radiant white to the viewers.
t2: And he drew forth his hand, and lo, it was white to the beholders.
t3: And he drew forth his hand and lo! it was white to the beholders.

ar: قَالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُۥٓ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌۭ
en: Pharaoh said to the chiefs around him, “He is indeed a skilled magician,
t1: (Pharaoh) said to the chiefs (sitting) around him: ‘Undoubtedly, he is a (highly) learned sorcerer.
t2: Said he to the Council about him, ’Surely this man is a cunning sorcerer
t3: (Pharaoh) said unto the chiefs about him: Lo! this is verily a knowing wizard,

ar: يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِۦ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ
en: who seeks to drive you from your land by his magic. So what do you propose?”
t1: He seeks to drive you out of your land by (the force of) his magic. So what is your opinion (about him now)?’
t2: who desires to expel you from your land by his sorcery; what do you command?’
t3: Who would drive you out of your land by his magic. Now what counsel ye ?

ar: قَالُوٓا۟ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَٱبْعَثْ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ
en: They replied, “Let him and his brother wait and dispatch mobilizers to all cities
t1: They said: ‘Put off (the announcement of sentence for) him and his brother (Harun [Aaron]) and send callers to (all) the cities (to summon the sorcerers).
t2: They said, ’Put him and his brother off a while, and send among the cities musterers,
t3: They said: Put him off, (him) and his brother, and send into the cities summoners

ar: يَأْتُوكَ بِكُلِّ سَحَّارٍ عَلِيمٍۢ
en: to bring you every skilled magician.”
t1: They will bring you every high ranking, expert sorcerer.’
t2: to bring thee every cunning sorcerer.
t3: Who shall bring unto thee every knowing wizard.

ar: فَجُمِعَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ لِمِيقَٰتِ يَوْمٍۢ مَّعْلُومٍۢ
en: So the magicians were assembled at the set time on the appointed day.
t1: So all the sorcerers were assembled at the appointed time on the fixed day.
t2: So the sorcerers were assembled for the appointed time of a fixed day.
t3: So the wizards were gathered together at a set time on a day appointed.

ar: وَقِيلَ لِلنَّاسِ هَلْ أَنتُم مُّجْتَمِعُونَ
en: And the people were asked, “Will you join the gathering,
t1: And it was said to the people (from Pharaoh’s side): ‘You will assemble together (on this occasion),
t2: The people were asked, ’Will you assemble?
t3: And it was said unto the people: Are ye (also) gathering ?

ar: لَعَلَّنَا نَتَّبِعُ ٱلسَّحَرَةَ إِن كَانُوا۟ هُمُ ٱلْغَٰلِبِينَ
en: so that we may follow the magicians if they prevail?”
t1: So that we may follow (the din [religion] of) the sorcerers if they overmaster (Musa [Moses] and Harun [Aaron]).’
t2: Haply we shall follow the sorcerers if it should be they are the victors.’
t3: (They said): Aye, so that we may follow the wizards if they are the winners.

ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ قَالُوا۟ لِفِرْعَوْنَ أَئِنَّ لَنَا لَأَجْرًا إِن كُنَّا نَحْنُ ٱلْغَٰلِبِينَ
en: When the magicians came, they asked Pharaoh, “Shall we have a ˹suitable˺ reward if we prevail?”
t1: Then when the sorcerers arrived, they said to Pharaoh: ‘Is there (also) any reward (fixed) for us if we gain the upper hand (in the contest)?’
t2: Then, when the sorcerers came, they said to Pharaoh, ’Shall we indeed have a wage, if we should be the victors?’
t3: And when the wizards came they said unto Pharaoh: Will there surely be a reward for us if we are the winners ?

ar: قَالَ نَعَمْ وَإِنَّكُمْ إِذًۭا لَّمِنَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ
en: He replied, “Yes, and you will then certainly be among those closest to me.”
t1: (Pharaoh) said: ‘Yes indeed! (Instead of the rewarded ones,) you will straight away join (my) closer circle (and intimate relationship is far higher in grade than reward).’
t2: He said, ’Yes indeed; and you shall then be among the near-stationed.’
t3: He said: Aye, and ye will then surely be of those brought near (to me).

ar: قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰٓ أَلْقُوا۟ مَآ أَنتُم مُّلْقُونَ
en: Moses said to them, “Cast whatever you wish to cast.”
t1: ( Musa [ Moses]) said to those (sorcerers): ‘Throw down the (magic) items which you are about to throw.’
t2: Moses said to them, ’Cast you down what you will cast.’
t3: Moses said unto them: Throw what ye are going to throw!

ar: فَأَلْقَوْا۟ حِبَالَهُمْ وَعِصِيَّهُمْ وَقَالُوا۟ بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ
en: So they cast down their ropes and staffs, saying, “By Pharaoh’s might, it is we who will surely prevail.”
t1: So they cast down their strings and sticks and said: ‘By the honour of Pharaoh, we shall certainly win.’
t2: So they cast their ropes and their staffs, and said, ’By the might of Pharaoh we shall be the victors.’
t3: Then they threw down their cords and their staves and said: By Pharaoh’s might, lo! we verily are the winners.

ar: فَأَلْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ تَلْقَفُ مَا يَأْفِكُونَ
en: Then Moses threw down his staff, and—behold!—it devoured the objects of their illusion!
t1: Then Musa (Moses) cast down his staff which, (changing into a serpent,) began swallowing up those things which they had made look different (from reality) through trickery.
t2: Then Moses cast his staff and lo, it forthwith swallowed up their lying invention;
t3: Then Moses threw his staff and lo! it swallowed that which they did falsely show.

ar: فَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سَٰجِدِينَ
en: So the magicians fell down, prostrating.
t1: So, all the magicians fell down prostrating themselves.
t2: so the sorcerers were cast down, bowing themselves.
t3: And the wizards were flung prostrate,

ar: قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: They declared, “We ˹now˺ believe in the Lord of all worlds—
t1: They said: ‘We believe in the Lord of all the worlds,
t2: They said, ’We believe in the Lord of all Being,
t3: Crying: We believe in the Lord of the Worlds,

ar: رَبِّ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ
en: the Lord of Moses and Aaron.”
t1: The Lord of Musa (Moses) and Harun (Aaron).’
t2: the Lord of Moses and Aaron.’
t3: The Lord of Moses and Aaron.

ar: قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ ۚ لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَٰفٍۢ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
en: Pharaoh threatened, “How dare you believe in him before I give you permission? He must be your master who taught you magic, but soon you will see. I will certainly cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, then crucify you all.”
t1: (Pharaoh) said: ‘You have believed in Him before I granted you permission. Surely, it is he (Musa [Moses]) who is your chief (coach) and who has taught you magic. You will soon come to know (your end). I will definitely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides and will surely crucify you all.’
t2: Said Pharaoh, ’You have believed him before I gave you leave. Why, he is the chief of you, the same that taught you sorcery; now you shall know! I shall assuredly cut off alternately your hands and feet, then I shall crucify you all together.’
t3: (Pharaoh) said: Ye put your faith in him before I give you leave. Lo! he doubtless is your chief who taught you magic! But verily ye shall come to know. Verily I will cut off your hands and your feet alternately, and verily I will crucify you every one.

ar: قَالُوا۟ لَا ضَيْرَ ۖ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا مُنقَلِبُونَ
en: They responded, “˹That would be˺ no harm! Surely to our Lord we will ˹all˺ return.
t1: They said: ‘There is no harm (in it). Surely, we are to return to our Lord.
t2: They said, ’There is no harm; surely unto our Lord we are turning.
t3: They said: It is no hurt, for lo! unto our Lord we shall return.

ar: إِنَّا نَطْمَعُ أَن يَغْفِرَ لَنَا رَبُّنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَآ أَن كُنَّآ أَوَّلَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
en: We really hope that our Lord will forgive our sins, as we are the first to believe.”
t1: We have strong hope that our Lord will forgive our sins since it is we who are the first to believe (now).’
t2: We are eager that our Lord should forgive us our offences, for that we are the first of the believers.’
t3: Lo! we ardently hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins because we are the first of the believers.

ar: ۞ وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِىٓ إِنَّكُم مُّتَّبَعُونَ
en: And We inspired Moses, ˹saying,˺ “Leave with My servants at night, for you will surely be pursued.”
t1: And We revealed to Musa (Moses): ‘Take away My servants (from here) by night; you will certainly be chased.’
t2: Also We revealed unto Moses, ’Go with My servants by night; surely you will be followed.’
t3: And We inspired Moses, saying: Take away My slaves by night, for ye will be pursued.

ar: فَأَرْسَلَ فِرْعَوْنُ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ
en: Then Pharaoh sent mobilizers to all cities,
t1: Then Pharaoh sent callers to the cities.
t2: Then Pharaoh sent among the cities musterers:
t3: Then Pharaoh sent into the cities summoners,

ar: إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ لَشِرْذِمَةٌۭ قَلِيلُونَ
en: ˹and said,˺ “These ˹outcasts˺ are just a handful of people,
t1: (And he conveyed:) ‘Surely, these (Children of Israel) are but a small party.
t2: ’Behold, these are a small troop,
t3: (Who said): Lo! these indeed are but a little troop,

ar: وَإِنَّهُمْ لَنَا لَغَآئِظُونَ
en: who have really enraged us,
t1: And undoubtedly, they are provoking us.
t2: and indeed they are enraging us;
t3: And lo! they are offenders against us.

ar: وَإِنَّا لَجَمِيعٌ حَٰذِرُونَ
en: but we are all on the alert.”
t1: And verily, we all are (also) alert and vigilant.’
t2: and we are a host on our guard.’
t3: And lo! we are a ready host.

ar: فَأَخْرَجْنَٰهُم مِّن جَنَّٰتٍۢ وَعُيُونٍۢ
en: So We lured the tyrants out of ˹their˺ gardens, springs,
t1: Then We drove them (Pharaoh’s people) out of gardens and springs,
t2: So We expelled them from gardens and fountains,
t3: Thus did We take them away from gardens and watersprings,

ar: وَكُنُوزٍۢ وَمَقَامٍۢ كَرِيمٍۢ
en: treasures, and splendid residences.
t1: And (also expelled them) from treasures and refined dwellings.
t2: and treasures and a noble station;
t3: And treasures and a fair estate.

ar: كَذَٰلِكَ وَأَوْرَثْنَٰهَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
en: So it was. And We awarded it ˹all˺ to the Children of Israel.
t1: So (We did) and made the Children of Israel inheritors of all (those bounties).
t2: even so, and We bequeathed them upon the Children of Israel.
t3: Thus (were those things taken from them) and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them.

ar: فَأَتْبَعُوهُم مُّشْرِقِينَ
en: And so they pursued them at sunrise.
t1: Then at sunrise, they (Pharaoh’s people) chased them.
t2: Then they followed them at the sunrise;
t3: And they overtook them at sunrise.

ar: فَلَمَّا تَرَٰٓءَا ٱلْجَمْعَانِ قَالَ أَصْحَٰبُ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ
en: When the two groups came face to face, the companions of Moses cried out, “We are overtaken for sure.”
t1: So when the two parties came face to face, the companions of Musa (Moses) said: ‘(Now) we are sure to be caught.’
t2: and, when the two hosts sighted each other, the companions of Moses said, ’We are overtaken!’
t3: And when the two hosts saw each other, those with Moses said: Lo! we are indeed caught.

ar: قَالَ كَلَّآ ۖ إِنَّ مَعِىَ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ
en: Moses reassured ˹them˺, “Absolutely not! My Lord is certainly with me—He will guide me.”
t1: (Musa [Moses]) said: ‘Never! Surely, my Lord is with me. He will show me the way (to deliverance) just now.’
t2: Said he, ’No indeed; surely my Lord is with me; He will guide me.’
t3: He said: Nay, verily! for lo! my Lord is with me. He will guide me.

ar: فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْبَحْرَ ۖ فَٱنفَلَقَ فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍۢ كَٱلطَّوْدِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
en: So We inspired Moses: “Strike the sea with your staff,” and the sea was split, each part was like a huge mountain.
t1: Then We revealed to Musa (Moses): ‘Strike the sea with your staff.’ So the sea split (into twelve parts) and each part became like a huge mountain.
t2: Then We revealed to Moses, ’Strike with thy staff the sea’; and it clave, and each part was as a mighty mount.
t3: Then We inspired Moses, saying: Smite the sea with thy staff. And it parted, and each part was as a mountain vast.

ar: وَأَزْلَفْنَا ثَمَّ ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ
en: We drew the pursuers to that place,
t1: And We brought the other party (Pharaoh and his companions) closer to that place.
t2: And there We brought the others on,
t3: Then brought We near the others to that place.

ar: وَأَنجَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥٓ أَجْمَعِينَ
en: and delivered Moses and those with him all together.
t1: And We saved Musa (Moses) and (also) all those who were with him.
t2: and We delivered Moses and those with him all together;
t3: And We saved Moses and those with him, every one;

ar: ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ
en: Then We drowned the others.
t1: Then We drowned the others (i.e., Pharaoh and his people).
t2: then We drowned the others.
t3: And We drowned the others.

ar: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
en: Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.
t1: Surely, in this (incident), there is a great sign (of Allah’s Infinite Power). And most of them were not believers.
t2: Surely in that is a sign, yet most of them are not believers.
t3: Lo! herein is indeed a portent, yet most of them are not believers.

ar: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
en: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.
t1: And verily, your Lord alone is Almighty, Ever-Merciful indeed.
t2: Surely thy Lord, He is the All-mighty, the All-compassionate.
t3: And lo, thy Lord! He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful.

ar: وَٱتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
en: Relate to them ˹O Prophet˺ the story of Abraham,
t1: And also recite to them the story of Ibrahim (Abraham).
t2: And recite to them the tiding of Abraham
t3: Recite unto them the story of Abraham:

ar: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ
en: when he questioned his father and his people, “What is that you worship ˹besides Allah˺?”
t1: When he said to his father* and his people: ‘What do you worship?’
t2: when he said to his father and his people, ’What do you serve?’
t3: When he said unto his father and his folk: What worship ye ?

ar: قَالُوا۟ نَعْبُدُ أَصْنَامًۭا فَنَظَلُّ لَهَا عَٰكِفِينَ
en: They replied, “We worship idols, to which we are fully devoted.”
t1: They said: ‘We worship idols and remain stuck to their (worship and care).’
t2: They said, ’We serve idols, and continue cleaving to them.
t3: They said: We worship idols, and are ever devoted unto them.

ar: قَالَ هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ إِذْ تَدْعُونَ
en: Abraham asked, “Can they hear you when you call upon them?
t1: (Ibrahim [Abraham]) said: ‘Do they hear you when you call (them)?
t2: He said, ’Do they hear you when you call,
t3: He said: Do they hear you when ye cry ?

ar: أَوْ يَنفَعُونَكُمْ أَوْ يَضُرُّونَ
en: Or can they benefit or harm you?”
t1: Or do they bring you any profit or loss?’
t2: or do they profit you, or harm?’
t3: Or do they benefit or harm you ?

ar: قَالُوا۟ بَلْ وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا كَذَٰلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ
en: They replied, “No! But we found our forefathers doing the same.”
t1: They said: ‘(We do not know that) but we found our fathers doing the same.’
t2: They said, ’Nay, but we found our fathers so doing.’
t3: They said: Nay, but we found our fathers acting on this wise.

ar: قَالَ أَفَرَءَيْتُم مَّا كُنتُمْ تَعْبُدُونَ
en: Abraham responded, “Have you ˹really˺ considered what you have been worshipping—
t1: (Ibrahim [Abraham]) said: ‘Have you (ever) thought (of their reality) you worship?’
t2: He said, ’And have you considered what you have been serving,
t3: He said: See now that which ye worship,

ar: أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُمُ ٱلْأَقْدَمُونَ
en: you and your ancestors?
t1: (Did) you or (any of) your forefathers (ever realize)?
t2: you and your fathers, the elders?
t3: Ye and your forefathers!

ar: فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّۭ لِّىٓ إِلَّا رَبَّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: They are ˹all˺ enemies to me, except the Lord of all worlds.
t1: So (all) these (idols) are enemies to me except the Lord of all the worlds. (He is the One Who is my God.)
t2: They are an enemy to me, except the Lord of all Being
t3: Lo! they are (all) an enemy unto me, save the Lord of the Worlds,

ar: ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَنِى فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِ
en: ˹He is˺ the One Who created me, and He ˹alone˺ guides me.
t1: He Who created me and He is the One Who guides me.
t2: who created me, and Himself guides me,
t3: Who created me, and He doth guide me,

ar: وَٱلَّذِى هُوَ يُطْعِمُنِى وَيَسْقِينِ
en: ˹He is˺ the One Who provides me with food and drink.
t1: And He is the One Who provides me with food and drink.
t2: and Himself gives me to eat and drink,
t3: And Who feedeth me and watereth me.

ar: وَإِذَا مَرِضْتُ فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ
en: And He ˹alone˺ heals me when I am sick.
t1: And when I fall ill, He is the One Who cures me.
t2: and, whenever I am sick, heals me,
t3: And when I sicken, then He healeth me,

ar: وَٱلَّذِى يُمِيتُنِى ثُمَّ يُحْيِينِ
en: And He ˹is the One Who˺ will cause me to die, and then bring me back to life.
t1: And He is the One Who will cause me to die and then He alone will give me life (again),
t2: who makes me to die, then gives me life,
t3: And Who causeth me to die, then giveth me life (again),

ar: وَٱلَّذِىٓ أَطْمَعُ أَن يَغْفِرَ لِى خَطِيٓـَٔتِى يَوْمَ ٱلدِّينِ
en: And He is ˹the One˺ Who, I hope, will forgive my flaws on Judgment Day.”
t1: And Who, I hope, will forgive me my misdeeds on the Day of Judgment.
t2: and who I am eager shall forgive me my offence on the Day of Doom.
t3: And Who, I ardently hope, will forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment.

ar: رَبِّ هَبْ لِى حُكْمًۭا وَأَلْحِقْنِى بِٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
en: “My Lord! Grant me wisdom, and join me with the righteous.
t1: O my Lord! Bless me with excellence in knowledge and deeds, and include me amongst those who deserve Your exceptional intimacy.
t2: My Lord, give me Judgment, and join me with the righteous,
t3: My Lord! Vouchsafe me wisdom and unite me to the righteous.

ar: وَٱجْعَل لِّى لِسَانَ صِدْقٍۢ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
en: Bless me with honourable mention among later generations.
t1: And ordain for me virtuous remembrance and acceptance amongst the coming generations (too).
t2: and appoint me a tongue of truthfulness among the others.
t3: And give unto me a good report in later generations.

ar: وَٱجْعَلْنِى مِن وَرَثَةِ جَنَّةِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
en: Make me one of those awarded the Garden of Bliss.
t1: And include me amongst the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss.
t2: Make me one of the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss
t3: And place me among the inheritors of the Garden of Delight,

ar: وَٱغْفِرْ لِأَبِىٓ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
en: Forgive my father, for he is certainly one of the misguided.
t1: And forgive my father. Surely, he was of the misguided.
t2: and forgive my father, for he is one of those astray.
t3: And forgive my father. Lo! he is of those who err.

ar: وَلَا تُخْزِنِى يَوْمَ يُبْعَثُونَ
en: And do not disgrace me on the Day all will be resurrected—
t1: And disgrace me not on the Day (when) people will be raised up (from the graves),
t2: Degrade me not upon the day when they are raised up,
t3: And abase me not on the day when they are raised,

ar: يَوْمَ لَا يَنفَعُ مَالٌۭ وَلَا بَنُونَ
en: the Day when neither wealth nor children will be of any benefit.
t1: The Day when neither wealth nor sons will profit.
t2: the day when neither wealth nor sons shall profit
t3: The day when wealth and sons avail not (any man)

ar: إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى ٱللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍۢ سَلِيمٍۢ
en: Only those who come before Allah with a pure heart ˹will be saved˺.”
t1: But he alone (will be the gainer) who appears before the presence of Allah with a heart protected (from) and pure (of all evils).’
t2: except for him who comes to God with a pure heart.
t3: Save him who bringeth unto Allah a whole heart.

ar: وَأُزْلِفَتِ ٱلْجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ
en: ˹On that Day˺ Paradise will be brought near to the God-fearing,
t1: And (on that Day) Paradise will be brought closer to the Godfearing (and self-protecting).
t2: And Paradise shall be brought forward for the godfearing,
t3: And the Garden will be brought nigh for those who ward off (evil).

ar: وَبُرِّزَتِ ٱلْجَحِيمُ لِلْغَاوِينَ
en: and the Hellfire will be displayed to the deviant.
t1: And Hell will be uncovered before the misguided.
t2: and Hell advanced for the perverse.
t3: And hell will appear plainly to the erring.

ar: وَقِيلَ لَهُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْبُدُونَ
en: And it will be said to them, “Where are those you used to worship
t1: And it will be said to them: ‘Where are those (idols) which you used to worship,
t2: It shall be said to them, ’Where is that you were serving
t3: And it will be said unto them: Where is (all) that ye used to worship

ar: مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ هَلْ يَنصُرُونَكُمْ أَوْ يَنتَصِرُونَ
en: besides Allah? Can they help you or even help themselves?”
t1: Besides Allah? Can they help you, or can they help themselves (to protect themselves from Hell)?’
t2: apart from God? Do they help you or help themselves?’
t3: Instead of Allah ? Can they help you or help themselves ?

ar: فَكُبْكِبُوا۟ فِيهَا هُمْ وَٱلْغَاوُۥنَ
en: Then the idols will be hurled headlong into Hell, along with the deviant
t1: So into Hell will be thrown headlong (the idols as well as) the people who lost the straight road.
t2: Then they shall be pitched into it, they and the perverse
t3: Then will they be hurled therein, they and the seducers

ar: وَجُنُودُ إِبْلِيسَ أَجْمَعُونَ
en: and the soldiers of Iblis, all together.
t1: And all the troops of Iblis (too will be hurled into Hell).
t2: and the hosts of Iblis, all together.
t3: And the hosts of Iblis, together.

ar: قَالُوا۟ وَهُمْ فِيهَا يَخْتَصِمُونَ
en: There the deviant will cry while disputing with their idols,
t1: Those (misguided people) will say whilst disputing amongst themselves (in the Hell):
t2: They shall say, as they dispute there one with another,
t3: And they will say, when they are quarrelling therein:

ar: تَٱللَّهِ إِن كُنَّا لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍ
en: “By Allah! We were clearly mistaken,
t1: ‘By Allah, we were in manifest error,
t2: ’By God, we were certainly in manifest error
t3: By Allah, of a truth we were in error manifest

ar: إِذْ نُسَوِّيكُم بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: when we made you equal to the Lord of all worlds.
t1: When we held you equal to the Lord of all the worlds.
t2: when we made you equal with the Lord of all Being.
t3: When we made you equal with the Lord of the Worlds.

ar: وَمَآ أَضَلَّنَآ إِلَّا ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ
en: And none led us astray other than the wicked.
t1: And no other than (these) evildoers led us astray.
t2: It was naught but the sinners that led us astray;
t3: It was but the guilty who misled us.

ar: فَمَا لَنَا مِن شَٰفِعِينَ
en: Now we have none to intercede for us,
t1: So we do not have any intercessor (Today).
t2: so now we have no intercessors,
t3: Now we have no intercessors

ar: وَلَا صَدِيقٍ حَمِيمٍۢ
en: nor a close friend.
t1: Nor do we have any passionate friend.
t2: no loyal friend.
t3: Nor any loving friend.

ar: فَلَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةًۭ فَنَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
en: If only we could have a second chance, then we would be believers.”
t1: Alas! If once we could have (a chance to) return (to the world), we would become believers.’
t2: O that we might return again, and be among the believers!’
t3: Oh, that we had another turn (on earth), that we might be of the believers!

ar: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
en: Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.
t1: Surely, in this (incident), there is a great sign (of Allah’s Infinite Power). And most of them were not the believers.
t2: Surely in that is a sign, yet most of them are not believers.
t3: Lo! herein is indeed a portent, yet most of them are not believers!

ar: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
en: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.
t1: And verily, your Lord alone is Almighty, Ever-Merciful.
t2: Surely thy Lord, He is the All-mighty, the All-compassionate.
t3: And lo, thy Lord! He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful.

ar: كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
en: The people of Noah rejected the messengers
t1: The people of Nuh (Noah also) rejected the Messengers.
t2: The people of Noah cried lies to the Envoys
t3: Noah’s folk denied the messengers (of Allah),

ar: إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ نُوحٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
en: when their brother Noah said to them, “Will you not fear ˹Allah˺?
t1: When their (kinship) brother Nuh (Noah) said to them: ‘Do you not fear (Allah)?
t2: when their brother Noah said to them, ’Will you not be godfearing?
t3: When their brother Noah said unto them: Will ye not ward off (evil) ?

ar: إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌۭ
en: I am truly a trustworthy messenger to you.
t1: Indeed, I (have come as) a trustworthy Messenger to you.
t2: I am for you a faithful Messenger,
t3: Lo! I am a faithful messenger unto you,

ar: فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
en: So fear Allah, and obey me.
t1: So fear Allah and obey me.
t2: so serve you God, and obey you me.
t3: So keep your duty to Allah, and obey me.

ar: وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺. My reward is only from the Lord of all worlds.
t1: And I do not demand of you any wages for this (preaching of the truth). My reward is only with the Lord of all the worlds.
t2: I ask of you no wage for this; my wage falls only upon the Lord of all Being;
t3: And I ask of you no wage therefor; my wage is the concern only of the Lord of the Worlds.

ar: فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
en: So fear Allah, and obey me.”
t1: So fear Allah and obey me.’
t2: so fear you God, and obey you me.’
t3: So keep your duty to Allah, and obey me.

ar: ۞ قَالُوٓا۟ أَنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ وَٱتَّبَعَكَ ٱلْأَرْذَلُونَ
en: They argued, “How can we believe in you, when you are followed ˹only˺ by the lowest of the low?”
t1: They said: ‘Should we believe in you whilst the people of the lowest and most worthless (classes of society) are following you?’
t2: They said, ’Shall we believe thee, whom the vilest follow?’
t3: They said: Shall we put faith in thee, when the lowest (of the people) follow thee ?

ar: قَالَ وَمَا عِلْمِى بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
en: He responded, “And what knowledge do I have of what they do?
t1: (Nuh [Noah]) said: ‘What has my knowledge to do with their (professional) tasks?
t2: He said, ’What knowledge have I of that they have been doing?
t3: He said: And what knowledge have I of what they may have been doing (in the past) ?

ar: إِنْ حِسَابُهُمْ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّى ۖ لَوْ تَشْعُرُونَ
en: Their judgment is with my Lord, if you had any sense!
t1: Their account is only with my Lord. If you could but understand (what the real honour and dishonour is)!
t2: Their account falls only upon my Lord, were you but aware.
t3: Lo! their reckoning is my Lord’s concern, if ye but knew;

ar: وَمَآ أَنَا۠ بِطَارِدِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
en: I am not going to expel the believers.
t1: And I am not the one who casts out the believers.
t2: I would not drive away the believers;
t3: And I am not (here) to repulse believers.

ar: إِنْ أَنَا۠ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
en: I am only sent with a clear warning.”
t1: I am only a clear Warner.’
t2: ’I am naught but a plain warner.’
t3: I am only a plain warner.

ar: قَالُوا۟ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ يَٰنُوحُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمَرْجُومِينَ
en: They threatened, “If you do not desist, O  Noah, you will surely be stoned ˹to death˺.”
t1: They said: ‘O Nuh (Noah), if you do not stop (saying these things), then surely you will be stoned to death.’
t2: They said, ’If thou givest not over, Noah, thou shalt assuredly be one of the stoned.’
t3: They said: If thou cease not, O Noah, thou wilt surely be among those stoned (to death).

ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِى كَذَّبُونِ
en: Noah prayed, “My Lord! My people have truly rejected me.
t1: (Nuh [Noah]) submitted: ‘O my Lord, my people have rejected me.
t2: He said, ’My Lord, my people have cried me lies,
t3: He said: My Lord! Lo! my own folk deny me.

ar: فَٱفْتَحْ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَهُمْ فَتْحًۭا وَنَجِّنِى وَمَن مَّعِىَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
en: So judge between me and them decisively, and save me and the believers with me.”
t1: So judge between me and them, and deliver me and the believers who are in my company.’
t2: so give true deliverance between me and them, and deliver me and the believers that are with me.
t3: Therefor judge Thou between us, a (conclusive) judgment, and save me and those believers who are with me.

ar: فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ
en: So We saved him and those with him in the fully loaded Ark.
t1: So We delivered him and those who were (aboard) with him in the fully loaded Ark.
t2: So We delivered him, and those with him, in the laden ship,
t3: And We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.

ar: ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا بَعْدُ ٱلْبَاقِينَ
en: Then afterwards We drowned the rest.
t1: Then thereafter We drowned all the rest.
t2: then afterwards We drowned the rest.
t3: Then afterward We drowned the others.

ar: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
en: Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.
t1: Surely, in this (incident), there is a great sign (of Allah’s Infinite Power) and most of them were not the believers.
t2: Surely in that is a sign, yet most of them are not believers.
t3: Lo! herein is indeed a portent, yet most of them are not believers.

ar: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
en: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.
t1: And verily, your Lord alone is Almighty, Ever-Merciful.
t2: Surely thy Lord, He is the All-mighty, the All-compassionate.
t3: And lo, thy Lord, He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful.

ar: كَذَّبَتْ عَادٌ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
en: The people of ’ad rejected the messengers
t1: (The people of) ‘Ad (too) rejected the Messengers.
t2: Ad cried lies to the Envoys
t3: (The tribe of) A’ad denied the messengers (of Allah).

ar: إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ هُودٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
en: when their brother Hûd said to them, “Will you not fear ˹Allah˺?
t1: When their (kinship) brother Hud said to them: ‘Do you not fear (Allah)?
t2: when their brother Hood said to them, ’Will you not be godfearing?
t3: When their brother Hud said unto them: Will ye not ward off (evil) ?

ar: إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌۭ
en: I am truly a trustworthy messenger to you.
t1: Verily, I (have come as) a trustworthy Messenger to you.
t2: I am for you a faithful Messenger,
t3: Lo! I am a faithful messenger unto you,

ar: فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
en: So fear Allah, and obey me.
t1: So fear Allah and obey me.
t2: so fear you God, and obey you me.
t3: So keep your duty to Allah and obey me.

ar: وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺. My reward is only from the Lord of all worlds.
t1: And I do not demand of you any wages for this (preaching of the truth). My reward is only with the Lord of all the worlds.
t2: I ask of you no wage for this; my wage falls only upon the Lord of all Being.
t3: And I ask of you no wage therefor; my wage is the concern only of the Lord of the Worlds.

ar: أَتَبْنُونَ بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ ءَايَةًۭ تَعْبَثُونَ
en: ˹Why˺ do you build a landmark on every high place in vanity,
t1: Do you build a monument on every high point (merely) for vanity and vain pursuits?
t2: What, do you build on every prominence a sign, sporting,
t3: Build ye on every high place a monument for vain delight ?

ar: وَتَتَّخِذُونَ مَصَانِعَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَخْلُدُونَ
en: and construct castles, as if you are going to live forever,
t1: And do you erect strongly-built palaces (having pools) with the hope of living (in the world) forever?
t2: and do you take to you castles, haply to dwell forever?
t3: And seek ye out strongholds, that haply ye may last for ever ?

ar: وَإِذَا بَطَشْتُم بَطَشْتُمْ جَبَّارِينَ
en: and act so viciously when you attack ˹others˺?
t1: And when you lay hand on someone, you do it like ruthless tyrants.
t2: When you assault, you assault like tyrants!
t3: And if ye seize by force, seize ye as tyrants ?

ar: فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
en: So fear Allah, and obey me.
t1: So fear Allah and obey me.
t2: So fear you God, and obey you me;
t3: Rather keep your duty to Allah, and obey me.

ar: وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَمَدَّكُم بِمَا تَعْلَمُونَ
en: Fear the One Who has provided you with ˹the good˺ things you know:
t1: And fear Him (Allah) Who has helped you with the things which you know.
t2: and fear Him who has succoured you with what you know,
t3: Keep your duty toward Him Who hath aided you with (the good things) that ye know,

ar: أَمَدَّكُم بِأَنْعَٰمٍۢ وَبَنِينَ
en: He provided you with cattle, and children,
t1: He has helped you with cattle and children,
t2: succoured you with flocks and sons,
t3: Hath aided you with cattle and sons.

ar: وَجَنَّٰتٍۢ وَعُيُونٍ
en: and gardens, and springs.
t1: And (also) with gardens and springs.
t2: gardens and fountains.
t3: And gardens and watersprings.

ar: إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍۢ
en: I truly fear for you the torment of a tremendous day.”
t1: Surely, I fear the torment of a Terrible Day coming upon you.’
t2: ’Indeed, I fear for you the chastisement of a dreadful day.’
t3: Lo! I fear for you the retribution of an awful day.

ar: قَالُوا۟ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْنَآ أَوَعَظْتَ أَمْ لَمْ تَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْوَٰعِظِينَ
en: They responded, “It is all the same to us whether you warn ˹us˺ or not.
t1: They said: ‘It is all the same to us whether you admonish, or do not become of those who admonish (we shall not believe).
t2: They said, ’Alike it is to us, whether thou admonishest, or art not one of the admonishers;
t3: They said: It is all one to us whether thou preachest or art not of those who preach;

ar: إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا خُلُقُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
en: This is simply the tradition of our predecessors.
t1: It is nothing (else) but the habits (and customs) of the ancients (which we cannot abandon).
t2: this is nothing but the habit of the ancients,
t3: This is but a fable of the men of old,

ar: وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ
en: And we will never be punished.”
t1: And we shall not be afflicted with the torment.
t2: and we shall not be chastised.’
t3: And we shall not be doomed.

ar: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَهْلَكْنَٰهُمْ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
en: So they rejected him, and ˹so˺ We destroyed them. Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.
t1: So they rejected him (Hud) and We destroyed them. Surely, in this (incident), there is a great sign (of Allah’s Infinite Power) and most of them were not the believers.
t2: So they cried him lies; then We destroyed them. Surely in that is a sign, yet most of them are not believers.
t3: And they denied him; therefor We destroyed them. Lo! herein is indeed a portent, yet most of them are not believers.

ar: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
en: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.
t1: And verily, your Lord alone is Almighty, Ever-Merciful.
t2: Surely thy Lord, He is the All-mighty, the All-compassionate.
t3: And lo! thy Lord, He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful.

ar: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
en: The people of Thamûd rejected the messengers
t1: (The people of) Thamud (also) rejected the Messengers.
t2: Thamood cried lies to the Envoys
t3: (The tribe of) Thamud denied the messengers (of Allah)

ar: إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ صَٰلِحٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
en: when their brother salih said to them, “Will you not fear ˹Allah˺?
t1: When Salih, their (kinship) brother, said to them: ‘Do you not fear (Allah)?
t2: when their brother Salih said to them, ’Will you not be godfearing?
t3: When their brother Salih said unto them: Will ye not ward off (evil) ?

ar: إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌۭ
en: I am truly a trustworthy messenger to you.
t1: Verily, I (have come as) a trustworthy Messenger to you.
t2: am for you a faithful Messenger,
t3: Lo! I am a faithful messenger unto you,

ar: فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
en: So fear Allah, and obey me.
t1: So fear Allah and obey me.
t2: so fear you God, and obey you me.’
t3: So keep your duty to Allah and obey me.

ar: وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺. My reward is only from the Lord of all worlds.
t1: And I do not demand of you any wages for this (preaching of the truth). My reward is only with the Lord of all the worlds.
t2: ’I ask of you no wage for this; my wage falls only upon the Lord of all Being.
t3: And I ask of you no wage therefor; my wage is the concern only of the Lord of the Worlds.

ar: أَتُتْرَكُونَ فِى مَا هَٰهُنَآ ءَامِنِينَ
en: Do you think you will be ˹forever˺ left secure in what you have here:
t1: Will you be left in peace and contentment (forever) in these (bounties) which are (available to you) here?
t2: Will you be left secure in this here,
t3: Will ye be left secure in that which is here before us,

ar: فِى جَنَّٰتٍۢ وَعُيُونٍۢ
en: amid gardens and springs,
t1: (Here) in the gardens and springs?
t2: among gardens and fountains,
t3: In gardens and watersprings.

ar: وَزُرُوعٍۢ وَنَخْلٍۢ طَلْعُهَا هَضِيمٌۭ
en: and ˹various˺ crops, and palm trees ˹loaded˺ with tender fruit;
t1: And in crops and palm-trees which have soft and fine blossoms?
t2: sown fields, and palms with slender spathes?
t3: And tilled fields and heavy-sheathed palm-trees,

ar: وَتَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًۭا فَٰرِهِينَ
en: to carve homes in the mountains with great skill?
t1: And, skilled (in stone-carving), you carve out houses in the mountains.
t2: Will you still skilfully hew houses out of the mountains?
t3: Though ye hew out dwellings in the mountain, being skilful ?

ar: فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
en: So fear Allah, and obey me.
t1: So fear Allah and obey me.
t2: So fear you God, and obey you me;
t3: Therefor keep your duty to Allah and obey me,

ar: وَلَا تُطِيعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ
en: And do not follow the command of the transgressors,
t1: And do not obey the instructions of those who exceed limits,
t2: and obey not the commandment of the prodigal
t3: And obey not the command of the prodigal,

ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا يُصْلِحُونَ
en: who spread corruption throughout the land, never setting things right.”
t1: Those who spread destructive activities in the land and do not do constructive works (for society).’
t2: who do corruption in the earth, and set not things aright.’
t3: Who spread corruption in the earth, and reform not.

ar: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسَحَّرِينَ
en: They replied, “You are simply bewitched!
t1: They said: ‘You are but of the magic-stricken people.
t2: They said, ’Thou art merely one of those that are bewitched;
t3: They said: Thou art but one of the bewitched;

ar: مَآ أَنتَ إِلَّا بَشَرٌۭ مِّثْلُنَا فَأْتِ بِـَٔايَةٍ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
en: You are only a human being like us, so bring forth a sign if what you say is true.”
t1: You are but a human being like us, so bring some sign if you are truthful.’
t2: thou art naught but a mortal, like us; then produce a sign, if thou art one of the truthful.’
t3: Thou art but a mortal like us. So bring some token if thou art of the truthful.

ar: قَالَ هَٰذِهِۦ نَاقَةٌۭ لَّهَا شِرْبٌۭ وَلَكُمْ شِرْبُ يَوْمٍۢ مَّعْلُومٍۢ
en: salih said, “Here is a camel. She will have her turn to drink as you have yours, each on an appointed day.
t1: (Salih) said: ‘(That sign) is this she-camel. A time for water is (appointed) for her, and on an appointed day is your turn for water.
t2: He said, ’This is a she-camel; to her a draught and to you a draught, on a day appointed,
t3: He said: (Behold) this she-camel. She hath the right to drink (at the well), and ye have the right to drink, (each) on an appointed day.

ar: وَلَا تَمَسُّوهَا بِسُوٓءٍۢ فَيَأْخُذَكُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍۢ
en: And do not ever touch her with harm, or you will be overtaken by the torment of a tremendous day.”
t1: And do not touch her with evil (intention), or the torment of a (gravely) terrible day will seize you.’
t2: and do not touch her with malice so that there seize you the chastisement of a dreadful day.’
t3: And touch her not with ill lest there come on you the retribution of an awful day.

ar: فَعَقَرُوهَا فَأَصْبَحُوا۟ نَٰدِمِينَ
en: But they killed her, becoming regretful.
t1: But they hamstrung her (and killed her). Then they became remorseful (because of what they did).
t2: But they hamstrung her, and in the morning they were remorseful,
t3: But they hamstrung her, and then were penitent.

ar: فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
en: So the punishment overtook them. Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.
t1: So the torment seized them. Surely, in this (incident), there is a great sign and most of them were not the believers.
t2: and the chastisement seized them. Surely in that is a sign, yet most of them are not believers.
t3: So the retribution came on them. Lo! herein is indeed a portent, yet most of them are not believers.

ar: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
en: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.
t1: And verily, your Lord alone is Almighty, Ever-Merciful.
t2: Surely thy Lord, He is the All-mighty, the All-compassionate.
t3: And lo! thy Lord! He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful.

ar: كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
en: The people of Lot rejected the messengers
t1: (The people of) Lut (Lot) also rejected the Messengers,
t2: The people of Lot cried lies to the Envoys
t3: The folk of Lot denied the messengers (of Allah),

ar: إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ لُوطٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
en: when their brother Lot said to them, “Will you not fear ˹Allah˺?
t1: When Lut (Lot), their (kinship) brother, said to them: ‘Do you not fear (Allah)?
t2: when their brother Lot said to them, ’Will you not be godfearing?
t3: When their brother Lot said unto them: Will ye not ward off (evil) ?

ar: إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌۭ
en: I am truly a trustworthy messenger to you.
t1: Verily, I (have come as) a trustworthy Messenger to you.
t2: am for you a faithful Messenger,
t3: Lo! I am a faithful messenger unto you,

ar: فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
en: So fear Allah, and obey me.
t1: So fear Allah and obey me.
t2: so fear you God, and obey you me.
t3: So keep your duty to Allah and obey me.

ar: وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺. My reward is only from the Lord of all worlds.
t1: And I do not demand of you any wages for this (preaching of the truth). My reward is only with the Lord of all the worlds.
t2: I ask of you no wage for this; my wage falls only upon the Lord of all Being.
t3: And I ask of you no wage therefor; my wage is the concern only of the Lord of the Worlds.

ar: أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلذُّكْرَانَ مِنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: Why do you ˹men˺ lust after fellow men,
t1: Do you approach only males (to satisfy your sexual desire) from amongst the people of the world;
t2: What, do you come to male beings,
t3: What! Of all creatures do ye come unto the males,
