ar: وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم ۚ بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ عَادُونَ
en: leaving the wives that your Lord has created for you? In fact, you are a transgressing people.”
t1: And you leave your wives your Lord has created for you? You are rather of those who exceed bounds (in transgression).’
t2: leaving your wives that your Lord created for you? Nay, but you are a people of transgressors.
t3: And leave the wives your Lord created for you ? Nay, but ye are froward folk.

ar: قَالُوا۟ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ يَٰلُوطُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمُخْرَجِينَ
en: They threatened, “If you do not desist, O  Lot, you will surely be expelled.”
t1: They said: ‘O Lut (Lot), if you do not stop (saying these things), you will surely become of the exiled.’
t2: They said, ’If thou givest not over, Lot, thou shalt assuredly be one of the expelled.’
t3: They said: If thou cease not, O Lot, thou wilt soon be of the outcast.

ar: قَالَ إِنِّى لِعَمَلِكُم مِّنَ ٱلْقَالِينَ
en: Lot responded, “I am truly one of those who despise your ˹shameful˺ practice.
t1: (Lut [Lot]) said: ‘No doubt I am of those who are disgusted by your practice.
t2: He said, ’Truly I am a detester of what you do.
t3: He said: I am in truth of those who hate your conduct.

ar: رَبِّ نَجِّنِى وَأَهْلِى مِمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ
en: My Lord! Save me and my family from ˹the consequences of˺ what they do.”
t1: O Lord! Deliver me and my family from (the consequent suffering of) this practice which they are doing.’
t2: My Lord, deliver me and my people from that they do.’
t3: My Lord! Save me and my household from what they do.

ar: فَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ أَجْمَعِينَ
en: So We saved him and all of his family,
t1: So We delivered him and his entire family,
t2: My Lord, deliver me and my people from that they do.’
t3: So We saved him and his household, every one,

ar: إِلَّا عَجُوزًۭا فِى ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ
en: except an old woman, who was one of the doomed.
t1: Except for an old woman who was amongst those who stayed behind.
t2: save an old woman among those that tarried;
t3: Save an old woman among those who stayed behind.

ar: ثُمَّ دَمَّرْنَا ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ
en: Then We utterly destroyed the rest,
t1: Then We destroyed the others.
t2: then We destroyed the others,
t3: Then afterward We destroyed the others.

ar: وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًۭا ۖ فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
en: pouring upon them a rain ˹of brimstone˺. How evil was the rain of those who had been warned!
t1: And We rained on them (stones). So how devastating was that rain on the people who were stressed with horror!
t2: and We rained on them a rain; and evil is the rain of them that are warned.
t3: And We rained on them a rain. And dreadful is the rain of those who have been warned.

ar: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
en: Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.
t1: Surely, in this (incident), there is a great sign and most of them were not believers.
t2: Surely in that is a sign, yet most of them are not believers.
t3: Lo! herein is indeed a portent, yet most of them are not believers.

ar: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
en: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.
t1: And verily, your Lord alone is Almighty, Ever-Merciful.
t2: Surely thy Lord, He is the All-mighty, the All-compassionate.
t3: And lo! thy Lord, He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful.

ar: كَذَّبَ أَصْحَٰبُ لْـَٔيْكَةِ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
en: The residents of the Forest rejected the messengers
t1: The dwellers of al-Ayka (i.e., the People of the Wood also) rejected the Messengers,
t2: The men of the Thicket cried lies to the Envoys
t3: The dwellers in the wood (of Midian) denied the messengers (of Allah),

ar: إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ شُعَيْبٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
en: when Shu’aib said to them, “Will you not fear ˹Allah˺?
t1: When Shu‘ayb said to them: ‘Do you not fear (Allah)?
t2: when Shuaib said to them, ’Will you not be godfearing?
t3: When Shu’eyb said unto them: Will ye not ward off (evil) ?

ar: إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌۭ
en: I am truly a trustworthy messenger to you.
t1: Verily, I (have come as) a trustworthy Messenger to you.
t2: I am for you a faithful Messenger, so fear you God, and obey you me.
t3: Lo! I am a faithful messenger unto you,

ar: فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
en: So fear Allah, and obey me.
t1: So fear Allah and obey me.
t2: I ask of you no wage for this;
t3: So keep your duty to Allah and obey me.

ar: وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺. My reward is only from the Lord of all worlds.
t1: And I do not demand of you any wages for this (preaching of the truth). My reward is only with the Lord of all the worlds.
t2: my wage falls only upon the Lord of all Being.
t3: And I ask of you no wage for it; my wage is the concern only of the Lord of the Worlds.

ar: ۞ أَوْفُوا۟ ٱلْكَيْلَ وَلَا تَكُونُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلْمُخْسِرِينَ
en: Give full measure, and cause no loss ˹to others˺.
t1: Always fill up full measure and do not become injurious (to the rights of the people).
t2: Fill up the measure, and be not cheaters,
t3: Give full measure, and be not of those who give less (than the due).

ar: وَزِنُوا۟ بِٱلْقِسْطَاسِ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمِ
en: Weigh with an even balance,
t1: And weigh with a straight balance.
t2: and weigh with the straight balance,
t3: And weigh with the true balance.

ar: وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا۟ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشْيَآءَهُمْ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ
en: and do not defraud people of their property. Nor go about spreading corruption in the land.
t1: And do not give to the people their things (weighing) less than what is due, nor provoke strife in the land (by such moral, economic and social corruption and fraud).
t2: and diminish not the goods of the people, and do not mischief in the earth, working corruption.
t3: Wrong not mankind in their goods, and do not evil, making mischief, in the earth.

ar: وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُمْ وَٱلْجِبِلَّةَ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
en: And fear the One Who created you and ˹all˺ earlier peoples.”
t1: And fear Him (Allah) Who has created you and the former generations.’
t2: Fear Him who created you, and the generations of the ancients.’
t3: And keep your duty unto Him Who created you and the generations of the men of old.

ar: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسَحَّرِينَ
en: They replied, “You are simply bewitched!
t1: They said: ‘(O Shu‘ayb,) you are but of the magic-stricken people.
t2: They said, ’Thou art merely one of those that are bewitched;
t3: They said: Thou art but one of the bewitched;

ar: وَمَآ أَنتَ إِلَّا بَشَرٌۭ مِّثْلُنَا وَإِن نَّظُنُّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
en: Also, you are only a human being like us, and we think you are indeed a liar.
t1: And you are but a human being like us, and surely we consider you amongst the liars.
t2: thou art naught but a mortal, like us; indeed, we think that thou art one of the liars.
t3: Thou art but a mortal like us, and lo! we deem thee of the liars.

ar: فَأَسْقِطْ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفًۭا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
en: So cause ˹deadly˺ pieces of the sky to fall upon us, if what you say is true.”
t1: So, make a piece of heaven fall on us if you are truthful.’
t2: Then drop down on us lumps from heaven, if thou art one of the truthful.’
t3: Then make fragments of the heaven fall upon us, if thou art of the truthful.

ar: قَالَ رَبِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
en: Shu’aib responded, “My Lord knows best whatever you do.”
t1: (Shu‘ayb) said: ‘My Lord knows best these (frauds) which you are doing.’
t2: He said, ’My Lord knows very well what you are doing.’
t3: He said: My Lord is Best Aware of what ye do.

ar: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَهُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمِ ٱلظُّلَّةِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
en: So they rejected him, and ˹so˺ were overtaken by the torment of the day of the ˹deadly˺ cloud. That was really a torment of a tremendous day.
t1: So they rejected Shu‘ayb, and the torment of the Day of Shadow seized them. No doubt, that was the torment of a terrible day.
t2: But they cried him lies; then there seized them the chastisement of the Day of Shadow; assuredly it was the chastisement of a dreadful day.
t3: But they denied him, so there came on them the retribution of the day of gloom. Lo! it was the retribution of an awful day.

ar: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
en: Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.
t1: Surely, in this (incident), there is a great sign and most of them were not believers.
t2: Surely in that is a sign, yet most of them are not believers.
t3: Lo! herein is indeed a portent; yet most of them are not believers.

ar: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
en: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.
t1: And verily, your Lord alone is Almighty, Ever-Merciful.
t2: Surely thy Lord, He is the All-mighty, the All-compassionate.
t3: And lo! thy Lord! He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful.

ar: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَتَنزِيلُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: This is certainly a revelation from the Lord of all worlds,
t1: And indeed, this Qur’an has been revealed by the Lord of all the worlds.
t2: Truly it is the revelation of the Lord of all Being,
t3: And lo! it is a revelation of the Lord of the Worlds,

ar: نَزَلَ بِهِ ٱلرُّوحُ ٱلْأَمِينُ
en: which the trustworthy spirit ˹Gabriel˺ brought down
t1: The Trusted Spirit (Gabriel) has descended with it,
t2: brought down by the Faithful Spirit
t3: Which the True Spirit hath brought down

ar: عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنذِرِينَ
en: into your heart ˹O Prophet˺—so that you may be one of the warners—
t1: Upon your (most illumined) heart so that you may be a Warner (to the disobedient).
t2: upon thy heart, that thou mayest be one of the warners,
t3: Upon thy heart, that thou mayst be (one) of the warners,

ar: بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِىٍّۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
en: in a clear Arabic tongue.
t1: (It is sent down) in the plain Arabic language.
t2: in a clear, Arabic tongue.
t3: In plain Arabic speech.

ar: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَفِى زُبُرِ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
en: And it has indeed been ˹foretold˺ in the Scriptures of those before.
t1: And verily, it is (also mentioned) in the scriptures of the former communities.
t2: Truly it is in the Scriptures of the ancients.
t3: And lo! it is in the Scriptures of the men of old.

ar: أَوَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُمْ ءَايَةً أَن يَعْلَمَهُۥ عُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
en: Was it not sufficient proof for the deniers that it has been recognized by the knowledgeable among the Children of Israel?
t1: And is it not for them a (sufficient) proof (of the truth of the Qur’an and the truth of Muhammad’s Prophethood [blessings and peace be upon him]) that the learned scholars of the Children of Israel (also) recognize it?
t2: Was it not a sign for them, that it is known to the learned of the Children of Israel?
t3: Is it not a token for them that the doctors of the Children of Israel know it ?

ar: وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنَٰهُ عَلَىٰ بَعْضِ ٱلْأَعْجَمِينَ
en: Had We revealed it to a non-Arab,
t1: And if We had sent it down to any of the non-Arabs,
t2: If We had sent it down on a barbarian
t3: And if We had revealed it unto one of any other nation than the Arabs,

ar: فَقَرَأَهُۥ عَلَيْهِم مَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ مُؤْمِنِينَ
en: who would then recite it to the deniers ˹in fluent Arabic˺, still they would not have believed in it!
t1: And he had recited it to these people, (even then) they would not have believed in it.
t2: and he had recited it to them, they would not have believed in it.
t3: And he had read it unto them, they would not have believed in it.

ar: كَذَٰلِكَ سَلَكْنَٰهُ فِى قُلُوبِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
en: This is how We allow denial ˹to steep˺ into the hearts of the wicked.
t1: Thus have We forced its (denial) firmly into the hearts of the sinners.
t2: Even so We have caused it to enter into the hearts of the sinners,
t3: Thus do We make it traverse the hearts of the guilty.

ar: لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِۦ حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُا۟ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلْأَلِيمَ
en: They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment,
t1: They will not believe in it until they see the painful torment.
t2: who will not believe in it, until they see the painful chastisement
t3: They will not believe in it till they behold the painful doom,

ar: فَيَأْتِيَهُم بَغْتَةًۭ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
en: which will take them by surprise when they least expect ˹it˺.
t1: So that (torment) will come upon them all of a sudden, and they will not (even) perceive it.
t2: so that it will come upon them suddenly, while they are not aware,
t3: So that it will come upon them suddenly, when they perceive not.

ar: فَيَقُولُوا۟ هَلْ نَحْنُ مُنظَرُونَ
en: Then they will cry, “Can we be allowed more time?”
t1: They will then say: ‘Shall we be given respite?’
t2: and they will say, ’Shall we be respited?’
t3: Then they will say: Are we to be reprieved ?

ar: أَفَبِعَذَابِنَا يَسْتَعْجِلُونَ
en: Do they ˹really˺ seek to hasten Our torment?
t1: Do they seek to hasten Our punishment?
t2: What, do they seek to hasten Our chastisement?
t3: Would they (now) hasten on Our doom ?

ar: أَفَرَءَيْتَ إِن مَّتَّعْنَٰهُمْ سِنِينَ
en: Imagine ˹O Prophet˺ if We allowed them enjoyment for years,
t1: Tell Me, if We provide them benefit for years,
t2: What thinkest thou? If We give them enjoyment of days for many years,
t3: Hast thou then seen, if We content them for (long) years,

ar: ثُمَّ جَآءَهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يُوعَدُونَ
en: then there came to them what they had been threatened with:
t1: Then comes to them that (torment) which they are being promised,
t2: then there comes on them that they were promised,
t3: And then cometh that which they were promised,

ar: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يُمَتَّعُونَ
en: would that enjoyment be of any benefit to them ˹at all˺?
t1: Then what will those resources which they were utilizing do (to drive that torment away from them)?
t2: what will it then avail them, the enjoyment of days they were given?
t3: (How) that wherewith they were contented naught availeth them ?

ar: وَمَآ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ إِلَّا لَهَا مُنذِرُونَ
en: We have never destroyed a society without warners
t1: And We have not destroyed any town except those (towns) for which Warners had come,
t2: Never a city We destroyed, but it had warners
t3: And We destroyed no township but it had its warners

ar: ذِكْرَىٰ وَمَا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
en: to remind ˹them˺, for We would never wrong ˹anyone˺.
t1: (And that too) for direction and guidance. And We were not unjust.
t2: for a reminder; and never did We wrong.
t3: For reminder, for We never were oppressors.

ar: وَمَا تَنَزَّلَتْ بِهِ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينُ
en: It was not the devils who brought this ˹Quran˺ down:
t1: And it is not satans who descended with this (Qur’an).
t2: Not by the Satans has it been brought down;
t3: The devils did not bring it down.

ar: وَمَا يَنۢبَغِى لَهُمْ وَمَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ
en: it is not for them ˹to do so˺, nor can they,
t1: They are neither worthy nor capable (of it).
t2: it behoves them not, neither are they able.
t3: It is not meet for them, nor is it in their power,

ar: إِنَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّمْعِ لَمَعْزُولُونَ
en: for they are strictly barred from ˹even˺ overhearing ˹it˺.
t1: Surely, they have been debarred from hearing (this divine communication).
t2: Truly, they are expelled from hearing.
t3: Lo! verily they are banished from the hearing.

ar: فَلَا تَدْعُ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُعَذَّبِينَ
en: So do not ever call upon any other god besides Allah, or you will be one of the punished.
t1: So, (O My servant,) do not call upon any other god besides Allah lest you become of those who are punished.
t2: So call thou not upon another god with God, lest thou shouldst be one of those that are chastised.
t3: Therefor invoke not with Allah another god, lest thou be one of the doomed.

ar: وَأَنذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ ٱلْأَقْرَبِينَ
en: And warn ˹all, starting with˺ your closest relatives,
t1: And, (O Esteemed Beloved,) warn your close relatives (of Our torment).
t2: And warn thy clan, thy nearest kin.
t3: And warn thy tribe of near kindred,

ar: وَٱخْفِضْ جَنَاحَكَ لِمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
en: and be gracious to the believers who follow you.
t1: And extend your (merciful, kind and supporting) hand to those believers who follow you.
t2: Lower thy wing to those who follow thee, being believers;
t3: And lower thy wing (in kindness) unto those believers who follow thee.

ar: فَإِنْ عَصَوْكَ فَقُلْ إِنِّى بَرِىٓءٌۭ مِّمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
en: But if they disobey you, say, “I am certainly free of what you do.”
t1: But, if they disobey you, then say: ‘I am disgusted by these (evil) deeds which you are doing.’
t2: then, if they disobey thee, say, ’I am quit of that you do.’
t3: And if they (thy kinsfolk) disobey thee, say: Lo! I am innocent of what they do.

ar: وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ
en: Put your trust in the Almighty, Most Merciful,
t1: And put your trust in Almighty, Ever-Merciful (Lord),
t2: Put thy trust in the All-mighty, the All-compassionate
t3: And put thy trust in the Mighty, the Merciful.

ar: ٱلَّذِى يَرَىٰكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ
en: Who sees you when you rise ˹for prayer at night˺,
t1: Who sees you when you stand up (for Tahajjud Prayer in the solitary hours at night),
t2: who sees thee when thou standest
t3: Who seeth thee when thou standest up (to pray)

ar: وَتَقَلُّبَكَ فِى ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ
en: as well as your movements ˹in prayer˺ along with ˹fellow˺ worshippers.
t1: And Who (also keeps) seeing your turning movements amongst those who prostrate themselves in Prayer.
t2: and when thou turnest about among those who bow.
t3: And (seeth) thine abasement among those who fall prostrate (in worship).

ar: إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
en: He ˹alone˺ is indeed the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
t1: Verily, He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
t2: Surely He is the All-hearing, the All-knowing.
t3: Lo! He, only He, is the Hearer, the Knower.

ar: هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ عَلَىٰ مَن تَنَزَّلُ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينُ
en: Shall I inform you of whom the devils ˹actually˺ descend upon?
t1: Shall I tell you upon whom the satans descend?
t2: Shall I tell you on whom the Satans come down?
t3: Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend ?

ar: تَنَزَّلُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ أَثِيمٍۢ
en: They descend upon every sinful liar,
t1: They descend on every lying sinner (who weaves false allegations),
t2: They come down on every guilty impostor.
t3: They descend on every sinful, false one.

ar: يُلْقُونَ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ كَٰذِبُونَ
en: who gives an ˹attentive˺ ear ˹to half-truths˺, mostly passing on sheer lies.
t1: Who pour (into their ears) hearsay and most of them are liars.
t2: They give ear, but most of them are liars.
t3: They listen eagerly, but most of them are liars.

ar: وَٱلشُّعَرَآءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ ٱلْغَاوُۥنَ
en: As for poets, they are followed ˹merely˺ by deviants.
t1: And only the digressers follow the poets.
t2: And the poets -- the perverse follow them;
t3: As for poets, the erring follow them.

ar: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِى كُلِّ وَادٍۢ يَهِيمُونَ
en: Do you not see how they rant in every field,
t1: Have you not seen that these (poets) wander distracted (purposelessly) in every valley (of reflections? They take little serious and true interest in reality. They rather remain happy and lost in verbal leaps and imaginative jumps).
t2: hast thou not seen how they wander in every valley
t3: Hast thou not seen how they stray in every valley,

ar: وَأَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ مَا لَا يَفْعَلُونَ
en: only saying what they never do?
t1: And that they say (such things) that they do not (themselves) do,
t2: and how they say that which they do not?
t3: And how they say that which they do not ?

ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَذَكَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرًۭا وَٱنتَصَرُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُوا۟ ۗ وَسَيَعْلَمُ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ أَىَّ مُنقَلَبٍۢ يَنقَلِبُونَ
en: Except those who believe, do good, remember Allah often, and ˹poetically˺ avenge ˹the believers˺ after being wrongfully slandered. The wrongdoers will come to know what ˹evil˺ end they will meet.
t1: Except for those (poets) who believe and do pious deeds persistently and remember Allah abundantly (i.e., they eulogize Allah and the Holy Prophet [blessings and peace be upon him] in their poetry), and avenge themselves after they are wronged (by means of poetic compositions, and defend Islam and the oppressed rather inspire them with zeal through their poetry. This type of poetry is not condemnable.) And those who do wrong will soon come to know to what place of turning they will turn back (after death).
t2: Save those that believe, and do righteous deeds, and remember God oft, and help themselves after being wronged; and those who do wrong shall surely know by what overturning they will he overturned.
t3: Save those who believe and do good works, and remember Allah much, and vindicate themselves after they have been wronged. Those who do wrong will come to know by what a (great) reverse they will be overturned!

ar: طسٓ ۚ تِلْكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱلْقُرْءَانِ وَكِتَابٍۢ مُّبِينٍ
en: Ṭa-Sĩn. These are the verses of the Quran; the clear Book.
t1: Ta, Sin. (Only Allah and the Messenger [blessings and peace be upon him] know the real meaning.) These are the Verses of the (Holy) Qur’an and an enlightening Book—
t2: Ta Sin. Those are the signs of the Koran and a Manifest Book,
t3: Ta. Sin. These are revelations of the Qur’an and a Scripture that maketh plain;

ar: هُدًۭى وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
en: ˹It is˺ a guide and good news for the believers:
t1: A guidance and good news for (those) believers,
t2: a guidance, and good tidings unto the believers
t3: A guidance and good tidings for believers

ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَهُم بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ
en: ˹those˺ who establish prayer, pay alms-tax, and have sure faith in the Hereafter.
t1: Who establish prayer and pay Zakat (the Alms-due), and it is they who believe in the Hereafter (as well).
t2: who perform the prayer, and pay the alms, and have sure faith in the Hereafter.
t3: Who establish worship and pay the poor-due and are sure of the Hereafter.

ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ زَيَّنَّا لَهُمْ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ فَهُمْ يَعْمَهُونَ
en: As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have certainly made their ˹evil˺ deeds appealing to them, so they wander blindly.
t1: Surely, those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have made their (evil) deeds appear fascinating (to them). So they wander distracted (in error).
t2: Those who believe not in the Hereafter, We have decked out fair for them their works, and they wander blindly;
t3: Lo! as for those who believe not in the Hereafter, We have made their works fairseeming unto them so that they are all astray.

ar: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَهُمْ سُوٓءُ ٱلْعَذَابِ وَهُمْ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ هُمُ ٱلْأَخْسَرُونَ
en: It is they who will suffer a dreadful torment, and in the Hereafter they will ˹truly˺ be the greatest losers.
t1: It is they for whom there is an evil punishment, and it is they who are (the greatest) losers in the Hereafter.
t2: those are they whom an evil chastisement awaits, and they will be the greatest losers in the Hereafter.
t3: Those are they for whom is the worst of punishment, and in the Hereafter they will be the greatest losers.

ar: وَإِنَّكَ لَتُلَقَّى ٱلْقُرْءَانَ مِن لَّدُنْ حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍ
en: And indeed, you ˹O Prophet˺ are receiving the Quran from the One ˹Who is˺ All-Wise, All-Knowing.
t1: And surely, you are being taught (this) Qur’an from the All-Wise, All-Knowing (Lord).
t2: Thou receivest the Koran from One All-wise, All-knowing.
t3: Lo! as for thee (Muhammad), thou verily receivest the Qur’an from the presence of One Wise, Aware.

ar: إِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِأَهْلِهِۦٓ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًۭا سَـَٔاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ ءَاتِيكُم بِشِهَابٍۢ قَبَسٍۢ لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ
en: ˹Remember˺ when Moses said to his family, “I have spotted a fire. I will either bring you some directions from there, or a burning torch so you may warm yourselves.”
t1: (Recall that incident) when Musa (Moses) said to his wife: ‘I have seen a fire (or I have perceived a flash of love and liking in the fire). Soon I shall bring you some news from it (for which we have been wandering in deserts and forests since long), or I shall bring (you also from there) some burning brand so that you (too) may feel the burn (of its heat).’
t2: When Moses said to his people ’I observe a fire, and will bring you news of it, or I will bring you a flaming brand, that haply you shall warm yourselves.’
t3: (Remember) when Moses said unto his household: Lo! I spy afar off a fire; I will bring you tidings thence, or bring to you a borrowed flame that ye may warm yourselves.

ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهَا نُودِىَ أَنۢ بُورِكَ مَن فِى ٱلنَّارِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا وَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: But when he came to it, he was called ˹by Allah˺, “Blessed is the one at the fire, and whoever is around it! Glory be to Allah, the Lord of all worlds.
t1: So when he neared it, a call was given: ‘Blessed is He Who is (luminously unveiling His veil of Light) in this fire, and (also) he who is around it (in the reflection of the theophanies of Allah’s Light). And Allah is Holy (and Glorified, High above any resemblance and physical manifestation), the Lord of all the worlds.
t2: So, when he came to it, he was called: ’Blessed is he who is in the fire, and he who is about it. Glory be to God, the Lord of all Being!
t3: But when he reached it, he was called, saying: Blessed is Whosoever is in the fire and Whosoever is round about it! And Glorified be Allah, the Lord of the Worlds!

ar: يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
en: O  Moses! It is truly I. I am Allah—the Almighty, All-Wise.
t1: O Musa (Moses)! It is I, Allah (Unveiling My Light), Almighty, All-Wise.
t2: Moses, behold, it is I, God, the All-mighty, the All-wise.
t3: O Moses! Lo! it is I, Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.

ar: وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ ۚ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّۭ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًۭا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ ۚ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَا تَخَفْ إِنِّى لَا يَخَافُ لَدَىَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
en: Now, throw down your staff!” But when he saw it slithering like a snake, he ran away without looking back. ˹Allah reassured him,˺ “O Moses! Do not be afraid! Messengers should have no fear in My presence.
t1: And, (O Musa [Moses],) cast your staff (on the ground).’ So when (Musa (Moses) after casting the staff on the ground) saw it moving fast as if it were a serpent, he (reacting naturally) turned back running and did not (even) look back. (Allah said:) ‘O Musa (Moses), do not fear. Surely, the Messengers do not fear in My presence.
t2: Cast down thy staff.’ And when he saw it quivering like a serpent he turned about, retreating, and turned not back. ’Moses, fear not; surely the Envoys do not fear in My presence,
t3: And throw down thy staff! But when he saw it writhing as it were a demon, he turned to flee headlong; (but it was said unto him): O Moses! Fear not! the emissaries fear not in My presence,

ar: إِلَّا مَن ظَلَمَ ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسْنًۢا بَعْدَ سُوٓءٍۢ فَإِنِّى غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
en: ˹Fear is˺ only for those who do wrong. But if they later mend ˹their˺ evil ˹ways˺ with good, then I am certainly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
t1: But whoever wrongs, then after doing evil replaces (it) with good, then I am indeed Most Forgiving, Ever-Merciful.
t2: save him who has done evil, then; after evil, has changed into good; All-forgiving am I, All-compassionate.
t3: Save him who hath done wrong and afterward hath changed evil for good. And lo! I am Forgiving, Merciful.

ar: وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍۢ ۖ فِى تِسْعِ ءَايَٰتٍ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِۦٓ ۚ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًۭا فَٰسِقِينَ
en: Now put your hand through ˹the opening of˺ your collar, it will come out ˹shining˺ white, unblemished. They have truly been a rebellious people.”
t1: And put your hand into the opening of your collar. It will come out radiant white without any ill. (Both these are) of the nine signs (of Allah). Go (with them) to Pharaoh and his people. Surely, they are a disobedient people.’
t2: Thrust thy hand in thy bosom and it will come forth white without evil-among nine signs to Pharaoh and his people; they are an ungodly people.’
t3: And put thy hand into the bosom of thy robe, it will come forth white but unhurt. (This will be one) among nine tokens unto Pharaoh and his people Lo! they were ever evil-living folk.

ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْهُمْ ءَايَٰتُنَا مُبْصِرَةًۭ قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا سِحْرٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
en: But when Our enlightening signs came to them, they said, “This is pure magic.”
t1: But when Our clear and sight-giving signs reached them, they said: ‘This is plain magic.’
t2: But when Our signs came to them visibly, they said, ’This is a manifest sorcery’;
t3: But when Our tokens came unto them, plain to see, they said: This is mere magic,

ar: وَجَحَدُوا۟ بِهَا وَٱسْتَيْقَنَتْهَآ أَنفُسُهُمْ ظُلْمًۭا وَعُلُوًّۭا ۚ فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ
en: And, although their hearts were convinced the signs were true, they still denied them wrongfully and arrogantly. See then what was the end of the corruptors!
t1: And out of vanity and wickedness, they rejected them straight away whilst their hearts had accepted these (signs as true). So see how (evil) was the end of the evildoers!
t2: and they denied them, though their souls acknowledged them, wrongfully and out of pride. Behold, how was the end of the workers of corruption!
t3: And they denied them, though their souls acknowledged them, for spite and arrogance. Then see the nature of the consequence for the wrong- doers!

ar: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا دَاوُۥدَ وَسُلَيْمَٰنَ عِلْمًۭا ۖ وَقَالَا ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى فَضَّلَنَا عَلَىٰ كَثِيرٍۢ مِّنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
en: Indeed, We granted knowledge to David and Solomon. And they said ˹in acknowledgment˺, “All praise is for Allah Who has privileged us over many of His faithful servants.”
t1: And indeed, We bestowed upon Dawud (David) and Sulayman ([Solomon] extraordinary knowledge) and both said: ‘All praise be to Allah, Who has exalted us above many of His believing servants.’
t2: And We gave David and Solomon knowledge and they said, ’Praise belongs to God who has preferred us over many of His believing servants.’
t3: And We verily gave knowledge unto David and Solomon, and they said: Praise be to Allah, Who hath preferred us above many of His believing slaves!

ar: وَوَرِثَ سُلَيْمَٰنُ دَاوُۥدَ ۖ وَقَالَ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ عُلِّمْنَا مَنطِقَ ٱلطَّيْرِ وَأُوتِينَا مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍ ۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْفَضْلُ ٱلْمُبِينُ
en: And David was succeeded by Solomon, who said, “O people! We have been taught the language of birds, and been given everything ˹we need˺. This is indeed a great privilege.”
t1: And Sulayman (Solomon) succeeded Dawud (David) and said: ‘O people, we have been taught the speech of birds (as well) and we have been granted everything. No doubt, this is the most obvious Grace (of Allah).’
t2: And Solomon was David’s heir, and he said, ’Men, we have been taught the speech of the birds, and we have been given of everything; surely this is indeed the manifest bounty.’
t3: And Solomon was David’s heir. And he said: O mankind! Lo! we have been taught the language of birds, and have been given (abundance) of all things. This surely is evident favour.

ar: وَحُشِرَ لِسُلَيْمَٰنَ جُنُودُهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلْإِنسِ وَٱلطَّيْرِ فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ
en: Solomon’s forces of jinn, humans, and birds were rallied for him, perfectly organized.
t1: And armies for Sulayman (Solomon) were collected from amongst (all species of) the jinn, human beings and birds. So they were held on (in his service) for discipline and training.
t2: And his hosts were mustered to Solomon, jinn, men and birds, duly disposed;
t3: And there were gathered together unto Solomon his armies of the jinn and humankind, and of the birds, and they were set in battle order;

ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَتَوْا۟ عَلَىٰ وَادِ ٱلنَّمْلِ قَالَتْ نَمْلَةٌۭ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّمْلُ ٱدْخُلُوا۟ مَسَٰكِنَكُمْ لَا يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ سُلَيْمَٰنُ وَجُنُودُهُۥ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
en: And when they came across a valley of ants, an ant warned, “O ants! Go quickly into your homes so Solomon and his armies do not crush you, unknowingly.”
t1: Until when these (troops) reached an open field of ants, one ant said: ‘O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Sulayman (Solomon) and his troops crush you whilst they remain just unaware.’
t2: till, when they came on the Valley of Ants, an ant said, ’Ants, enter your dwelling-places, lest Solomon and his hosts crush you, being unaware!’
t3: Till, when they reached the Valley of the Ants, an ant exclaimed: O ants! Enter your dwellings lest Solomon and his armies crush you, unperceiving.

ar: فَتَبَسَّمَ ضَاحِكًۭا مِّن قَوْلِهَا وَقَالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِىٓ أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَىَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَىَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَٰلِحًۭا تَرْضَىٰهُ وَأَدْخِلْنِى بِرَحْمَتِكَ فِى عِبَادِكَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
en: So Solomon smiled in amusement at her words, and prayed, “My Lord! Inspire me to ˹always˺ be thankful for Your favours which You have blessed me and my parents with, and to do good deeds that please you. Admit me, by Your mercy, into ˹the company of˺ Your righteous servants.”
t1: So he (Sulayman [Solomon]) smiled, feeling amused at the ant’s words, and submitted: ‘O Lord, keep me by Your bestowal firm on it that I remain ever-thankful for Your favour You have conferred on me and on my parents, and I do such pious deeds as You are pleased with, and admit me by Your mercy amongst Your pious slaves enjoying exceptional nearness to You.’
t2: But he smiled, laughing at its words, and he said, ’My Lord, dispose me that I may be thankful for Thy blessing wherewith Thou hast blessed me and my father and mother, and that I may do righteousness well-pleasing to Thee; and do Thou admit me, by Thy mercy, amongst Thy righteous servants.’
t3: And (Solomon) smiled, laughing at her speech, and said: My Lord, arouse me to be thankful for Thy favour wherewith Thou hast favoured me and my parents, and to do good that shall be pleasing unto Thee, and include me in (the number of) Thy righteous slaves.

ar: وَتَفَقَّدَ ٱلطَّيْرَ فَقَالَ مَا لِىَ لَآ أَرَى ٱلْهُدْهُدَ أَمْ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْغَآئِبِينَ
en: ˹One day˺ he inspected the birds, and wondered, “Why is it that I cannot see the hoopoe? Or could he be absent?
t1: And Sulayman (Solomon) inspected the birds and said: ‘How is it that I do not see the hoopoe? Or has he (really) vanished?
t2: And he reviewed the birds; then he said, ’How is it with me, that I do not see the hoopoe? Or is he among the absent?
t3: And he sought among the birds and said: How is it that I see not the hoopoe, or is he among the absent ?

ar: لَأُعَذِّبَنَّهُۥ عَذَابًۭا شَدِيدًا أَوْ لَأَا۟ذْبَحَنَّهُۥٓ أَوْ لَيَأْتِيَنِّى بِسُلْطَٰنٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
en: I will surely subject him to a severe punishment, or ˹even˺ slaughter him, unless he brings me a compelling excuse.”
t1: I will certainly award him severe punishment (for being absent without leave), or will certainly slaughter him, or he will bring me a sound plea (of being not guilty).’
t2: Assuredly I will chastise him with a terrible chastisement, or I will slaughter him, or he bring me a clear authority.’
t3: I verily will punish him with hard punishment or I verily will slay him, or he verily shall bring me a plain excuse.

ar: فَمَكَثَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍۢ فَقَالَ أَحَطتُ بِمَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِۦ وَجِئْتُكَ مِن سَبَإٍۭ بِنَبَإٍۢ يَقِينٍ
en: It was not long before the bird came and said, “I have found out something you do not know. I have just come to you from Sheba with sure news.
t1: It was only for a little while that he stayed (outside), then he (appeared and) said: ‘I have come to know a thing that is (perhaps) not in your knowledge, and I have brought you from (the land of) Saba (Sheba) a sure and true piece of news.
t2: But he tarried not long, and said, ’I have comprehended that which thou hast not comprehended, and I have come from Sheba to thee with a sure tiding.
t3: But he was not long in coming, and he said: I have found out (a thing) that thou apprehendest not, and I come unto thee from Sheba with sure tidings.

ar: إِنِّى وَجَدتُّ ٱمْرَأَةًۭ تَمْلِكُهُمْ وَأُوتِيَتْ مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ وَلَهَا عَرْشٌ عَظِيمٌۭ
en: Indeed, I found a woman ruling over them, who has been given everything ˹she needs˺, and who has a magnificent throne.
t1: I have found (there) a woman who is ruling over them (i.e., the citizens of the land of Saba [Sheba]), and she has been given everything (of possession and authority), and she has a great throne.
t2: I found a woman ruling over them, and she has been given of everything, and she possesses a mighty throne.
t3: Lo! I found a woman ruling over them, and she hath been given (abundance) of all things, and hers is a mighty throne.

ar: وَجَدتُّهَا وَقَوْمَهَا يَسْجُدُونَ لِلشَّمْسِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ فَهُمْ لَا يَهْتَدُونَ
en: I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah. For Satan has made their deeds appealing to them—hindering them from the ˹Right˺ Way and leaving them unguided—
t1: I found her and her people prostrating themselves before the sun instead of Allah. And Satan has made their (evil) deeds highly fascinating to them, and has hindered them from the path (of the Oneness of Allah). So they are not getting guidance.
t2: I found her and her people prostrating to the sun, apart from God; Satan has decked out fair their deeds to them and he has barred them from the way, and therefore they are not guided,
t3: I found her and her people worshipping the sun instead of Allah; and Satan maketh their works fairseeming unto them, and debarreth them from the way (of Truth), so that they go not aright;

ar: أَلَّا يَسْجُدُوا۟ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى يُخْرِجُ ٱلْخَبْءَ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تُخْفُونَ وَمَا تُعْلِنُونَ
en: so they do not prostrate to Allah, Who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, and knows what you ˹all˺ conceal and what you reveal.
t1: (They are hindered) so that they do not fall in prostration before the presence of Allah, Who brings forth (i.e., unveils the realities and forms of matter) hidden in the heavens and the earth and knows (all) those things which you hide and which you disclose.
t2: so that they prostrate not themselves to God, who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and earth; and He knows what you conceal and what you publish.
t3: So that they worship not Allah, Who bringeth forth the hidden in the heavens and the earth, and knoweth what ye hide and what ye proclaim,

ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ رَبُّ ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ ۩
en: ˹He is˺ Allah! There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him, the Lord of the Mighty Throne.”
t1: There is none worthy of worship except Allah. He alone is the Master of the Supreme Throne of Authority.’
t2: God: there is no god but He, the Lord of the Mighty Throne.’
t3: Allah; there is no God save Him, the Lord of the Tremendous Throne.

ar: ۞ قَالَ سَنَنظُرُ أَصَدَقْتَ أَمْ كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
en: Solomon said, “We will see whether you are telling the truth or lying.
t1: (Sulayman [Solomon]) said: ‘We see right now whether you speak the truth or you are of the liars.
t2: Said he, ’Now We will see whether thou hast spoken truly, or whether thou art amongst those that lie.
t3: (Solomon) said: We shall see whether thou speakest truth or whether thou art of the liars.

ar: ٱذْهَب بِّكِتَٰبِى هَٰذَا فَأَلْقِهْ إِلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا يَرْجِعُونَ
en: Go with this letter of mine and deliver it to them, then stand aside and see how they will respond.”
t1: Go with this letter of mine and deliver it to them. Then withdraw from them and see what they turn to.’
t2: Take this letter of mine, and cast it unto them, then turn back from them and see what they shall return ’
t3: Go with this my letter and throw it down unto them; then turn away and see what (answer) they return,

ar: قَالَتْ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ إِنِّىٓ أُلْقِىَ إِلَىَّ كِتَٰبٌۭ كَرِيمٌ
en: The Queen ˹later˺ announced, “O chiefs! Indeed, a noble letter has been delivered to me.
t1: (The Queen) said: ‘O chiefs, a noble letter has been delivered to me.
t2: She said, ’O Council, see, a letter honourable has been cast unto me.
t3: (The Queen of Sheba) said (when she received the letter): O chieftains! Lo! there hath been thrown unto me a noble letter.

ar: إِنَّهُۥ مِن سُلَيْمَٰنَ وَإِنَّهُۥ بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ
en: It is from Solomon, and it reads: ‘In the Name of Allah—the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful.
t1: That (letter) has indeed (come) from Sulayman (Solomon), and that begins with the Name of Allah, Who is Most Kind, Ever-Merciful.
t2: It is from Solomon, and it is "In the Name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.
t3: Lo! it is from Solomon, and lo! it is: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful;

ar: أَلَّا تَعْلُوا۟ عَلَىَّ وَأْتُونِى مُسْلِمِينَ
en: Do not be arrogant with me, but come to me, fully submitting ˹to Allah˺.’”
t1: (Its contents read:) ‘Do not (strive to) rise above me and come to me in submission.’
t2: Rise not up against me, but come to me in surrender." ’
t3: Exalt not yourselves against me, but come unto me as those who surrender.

ar: قَالَتْ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ أَفْتُونِى فِىٓ أَمْرِى مَا كُنتُ قَاطِعَةً أَمْرًا حَتَّىٰ تَشْهَدُونِ
en: She said, “O chiefs! Advise me in this matter of mine, for I would never make any decision without you.”
t1: (The Queen) said: ‘O courtiers, advise me in this matter. I do not make a final decision on any matter until you come to me and state your opinions (for or against the matter).’
t2: She said, ’O Council, pronounce to me concerning my affair; I am not used to decide an affair until you bear me witness.’
t3: She said: O chieftains! Pronounce for me in my case. I decide no case till ye are present with me.

ar: قَالُوا۟ نَحْنُ أُو۟لُوا۟ قُوَّةٍۢ وَأُو۟لُوا۟ بَأْسٍۢ شَدِيدٍۢ وَٱلْأَمْرُ إِلَيْكِ فَٱنظُرِى مَاذَا تَأْمُرِينَ
en: They responded, “We are a people of strength and great ˹military˺ might, but the decision is yours, so decide what you will command.”
t1: They said: ‘We are powerful and great warriors but the command is your prerogative. So consider (yourself) what command you should give.’
t2: They said, ’We possess force and we possess great might. The affair rests with thee; so consider what thou wilt command.’
t3: They said: We are lords of might and lords of great prowess, but it is for thee to command; so consider what thou wilt command.

ar: قَالَتْ إِنَّ ٱلْمُلُوكَ إِذَا دَخَلُوا۟ قَرْيَةً أَفْسَدُوهَا وَجَعَلُوٓا۟ أَعِزَّةَ أَهْلِهَآ أَذِلَّةًۭ ۖ وَكَذَٰلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ
en: She reasoned, “Indeed, when kings invade a land, they ruin it and debase its nobles. They really do so!
t1: (The Queen) said: ‘No doubt when kings enter a town, they destroy it and disgrace and humiliate its elite citizens. And these (people) too will do the same.
t2: She said, ’Kings, when they enter a city, disorder it and make the mighty ones of its inhabitants abased. Even so they too will do.
t3: She said: Lo! kings, when they enter a township, ruin it and make the honour of its people shame. Thus will they do.

ar: وَإِنِّى مُرْسِلَةٌ إِلَيْهِم بِهَدِيَّةٍۢ فَنَاظِرَةٌۢ بِمَ يَرْجِعُ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
en: But I will certainly send him a gift, and see what ˹response˺ my envoys will return with.”
t1: And, surely, I am sending him some gifts and see what reply the messengers bring back.’
t2: Now I will send them a present, and see what the envoys bring back.’
t3: But lo! I am going to send a present unto them, and to see with what (answer) the messengers return.

ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَ سُلَيْمَٰنَ قَالَ أَتُمِدُّونَنِ بِمَالٍۢ فَمَآ ءَاتَىٰنِۦَ ٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌۭ مِّمَّآ ءَاتَىٰكُم بَلْ أَنتُم بِهَدِيَّتِكُمْ تَفْرَحُونَ
en: When the chief-envoy came to him, Solomon said, “Do you offer me wealth? What Allah has granted me is far greater than what He has granted you. No! It is you who rejoice in ˹receiving˺ gifts.
t1: So when that (messenger) came to Sulayman (Solomon, he) said (to him [i.e., the messenger]): ‘Do you want to help me with wealth, whereas what Allah has given me is better than this (wealth) which He has given you? It is rather you who take pleasure (and) pride in your gifts.
t2: But when he came to Solomon he said, ’What, would you succour me with wealth, and what God gave me is better than what He has given you? Nay, but instead you rejoice in your gift!
t3: So when (the envoy) came unto Solomon, (the King) said: What! Would ye help me with wealth ? But that which Allah hath given me is better than that which He hath given you. Nay it is ye (and not I) who exult in your gift.

ar: ٱرْجِعْ إِلَيْهِمْ فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّهُم بِجُنُودٍۢ لَّا قِبَلَ لَهُم بِهَا وَلَنُخْرِجَنَّهُم مِّنْهَآ أَذِلَّةًۭ وَهُمْ صَٰغِرُونَ
en: Go back to them, for we will certainly mobilize against them forces which they can never resist, and we will drive them out from there in disgrace, fully humbled.”
t1: So go back to them (with your gifts). We shall come with such troops (to invade) them that they will not have (the power) to fight back, and, humiliating them, we shall drive them out from there in such a plight that they will be dishonoured (becoming prisoners).’
t2: Return thou to them; we shall assuredly come against them with hosts they have not power to resist, and we shall expel them from there, abased and utterly humbled.’
t3: Return unto them. We verily shall come unto them with hosts that they cannot resist, and we shall drive them out from thence with shame, and they will be abased.

ar: قَالَ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ أَيُّكُمْ يَأْتِينِى بِعَرْشِهَا قَبْلَ أَن يَأْتُونِى مُسْلِمِينَ
en: Solomon asked, “O chiefs! Which of you can bring me her throne before they come to me in ˹full˺ submission?”
t1: Sulayman (Solomon) said: ‘O courtiers, which of you can bring me the throne (of the Queen) before they come to me in submission?’
t2: He said, ’O Council, which one of you will bring me her throne, before they come to me in surrender?’
t3: He said: O chiefs! Which of you will bring me her throne before they come unto me, surrendering ?

ar: قَالَ عِفْرِيتٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْجِنِّ أَنَا۠ ءَاتِيكَ بِهِۦ قَبْلَ أَن تَقُومَ مِن مَّقَامِكَ ۖ وَإِنِّى عَلَيْهِ لَقَوِىٌّ أَمِينٌۭ
en: One mighty jinn responded, “I can bring it to you before you rise from this council of yours. And I am quite strong and trustworthy for this ˹task˺.”
t1: One mighty jinn submitted: ‘I can bring it to you before you rise from your seat. And I am indeed powerful (enough) and trustworthy (to bring it).’
t2: An efreet of the jinns said, ’I will bring it to thee, before thou risest from thy place; I have strength for it
t3: A stalwart of the jinn said: I will bring it thee before thou canst rise from thy place. Lo! I verily am strong and trusty for such work.

ar: قَالَ ٱلَّذِى عِندَهُۥ عِلْمٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ أَنَا۠ ءَاتِيكَ بِهِۦ قَبْلَ أَن يَرْتَدَّ إِلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ ۚ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهُ مُسْتَقِرًّا عِندَهُۥ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِن فَضْلِ رَبِّى لِيَبْلُوَنِىٓ ءَأَشْكُرُ أَمْ أَكْفُرُ ۖ وَمَن شَكَرَ فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ رَبِّى غَنِىٌّۭ كَرِيمٌۭ
en: But the one who had knowledge of the Scripture said, “I can bring it to you in the blink of an eye.” So when Solomon saw it placed before him, he exclaimed, “This is by the grace of my Lord to test me whether I am grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful, it is only for their own good. But whoever is ungrateful, surely my Lord is Self-Sufficient, Most Generous.”
t1: Then the one who had some knowledge of the (heavenly) Book submitted: ‘I can bring it to you before your vision turns back to you (i.e., even before the twinkling of an eye).’ So, when (Sulayman [Solomon]) saw it (the throne) placed before him, he said: ‘This is by the Grace of my Lord so that He may put me to the test whether I thank (Him) or not. And he who thanks (Allah), his gratitude is for the good of his own self, and he who is ungrateful, then surely my Lord is Self-Sufficient, Most Generous.’
t2: and I am trusty.’ Said he who possessed knowledge of the Book, ’I will bring it to thee, before ever thy glance returns to thee.’ Then, when he saw it settled before him, he said, ’This is of my Lord’s bounty that He may try me, whether I am thankful or ungrateful. Whosoever gives thanks gives thanks only for his own soul’s good, and whosoever is ungrateful -- my Lord is surely All-sufficient, All-generous.’
t3: One with whom was knowledge of the Scripture said: I will bring it thee before thy gaze returneth unto thee. And when he saw it set in his presence, (Solomon) said: This is of the bounty of my Lord, that He may try me whether I give thanks or am ungrateful. Whosoever giveth thanks he only giveth thanks for (the good of) his own soul; and whosoever is ungrateful (is ungrateful only to his own soul’s hurt). For lo! my Lord is Absolute in independence, Bountiful.

ar: قَالَ نَكِّرُوا۟ لَهَا عَرْشَهَا نَنظُرْ أَتَهْتَدِىٓ أَمْ تَكُونُ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَهْتَدُونَ
en: ˹Then˺ Solomon said, “Disguise her throne for her so we may see whether she will recognize ˹it˺ or she will not be able to.”
t1: Sulayman (Solomon) said: ‘(To test the Queen) change the display and appearance of her throne. We shall see whether she gets some clue (to recognize it) or proves to be of those who do not have quick reflexes.’
t2: He said, ’Disguise her throne for her, and we shall behold whether she is guided or if she is of those that are not guided.’
t3: He said: Disguise her throne for her that we may see whether she will go aright or be of those not rightly guided.

ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْ قِيلَ أَهَٰكَذَا عَرْشُكِ ۖ قَالَتْ كَأَنَّهُۥ هُوَ ۚ وَأُوتِينَا ٱلْعِلْمَ مِن قَبْلِهَا وَكُنَّا مُسْلِمِينَ
en: So when she arrived, it was said ˹to her˺, “Is your throne like this?” She replied, “It looks to be the same. We have ˹already˺ received knowledge ˹of Solomon’s prophethood˺ and have submitted ˹to Allah˺.”
t1: Then when she (the Queen) came, she was asked: ‘Is your throne like this?’ She said: ‘It looks as if it is the same and we have already known (the truth of Sulayman’s [Solomon’s] Prophethood) and we have become Muslims.’
t2: So, when she came, it was said, ’Is thy throne like this?’ She said, ’It seems the same.’ ’And we were given the knowledge before her, and we were in surrender,
t3: So, when she came, it was said (unto her): Is thy throne like this ? She said: (It is) as though it were the very one. And (Solomon said): We were given the knowledge before her and we had surrendered (to Allah).

ar: وَصَدَّهَا مَا كَانَت تَّعْبُدُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ مِن قَوْمٍۢ كَٰفِرِينَ
en: But she had been hindered by what she used to worship instead of Allah, for she was indeed from a disbelieving people.
t1: And the (false god) she worshipped besides Allah prevented her (the Queen from accepting the truth before this). No doubt, she was of a disbelieving people.
t2: but that she served, apart from God, barred her, for she was of a people of unbelievers.’
t3: And (all) that she was wont to worship instead of Allah hindered her, for she came of disbelieving folk.

ar: قِيلَ لَهَا ٱدْخُلِى ٱلصَّرْحَ ۖ فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ حَسِبَتْهُ لُجَّةًۭ وَكَشَفَتْ عَن سَاقَيْهَا ۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ صَرْحٌۭ مُّمَرَّدٌۭ مِّن قَوَارِيرَ ۗ قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّى ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِى وَأَسْلَمْتُ مَعَ سُلَيْمَٰنَ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: Then she was told, “Enter the palace.” But when she saw the hall, she thought it was a body of water, so she bared her legs. Solomon said. “It is just a palace paved with crystal.” ˹At last˺ she declared, “My Lord! I have certainly wronged my soul. Now I ˹fully˺ submit myself along with Solomon to Allah, the Lord of all worlds.”
t1: It was said to her (the Queen): ‘Enter the compound of the palace (beneath which were flowing waves of bluish water).’ So when the Queen saw that (elegant, crystal floor), she thought it was a deep pool. And (pulling up her skirt) she uncovered her lower legs. Sulayman (Solomon) said: ‘This is the compound of the palace paved with crystal slabs.’ The Queen submitted: ‘O my Lord, (I was deluded in like manner.) Surely, I wronged my soul. And now along with Sulayman (Solomon), I submit to Allah, Who is the Lord of all the worlds.’
t2: It was said to her, ’Enter the pavilion.’ But when she saw it, she supposed it was a spreading water, and she bared her legs. He said, ’It is a pavilion smoothed of crystal. She said, ’My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I surrender with Solomon to God, the Lord of all Being.’
t3: It was said unto her: Enter the hall. And when she saw it she deemed it a pool and bared her legs. (Solomon) said: Lo! it is a hall, made smooth, of glass. She said: My Lord! Lo! I have wronged myself, and I surrender with Solomon unto Allah, the Lord of the Worlds.

ar: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَآ إِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ صَٰلِحًا أَنِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ فَإِذَا هُمْ فَرِيقَانِ يَخْتَصِمُونَ
en: And We certainly sent to the people of Thamûd their brother salih, proclaiming, “Worship Allah,” but they suddenly split into two opposing groups.
t1: And, surely, We sent to the people of Thamud their (kinship) brother Salih (as a Messenger:) ‘Worship Allah.’ Then they became two parties disputing with each other.
t2: And We sent to Thamood their brother Salih: ’Serve you God!’ And behold, they were two parties, that were disputing one with another.
t3: And We verily sent unto Thamud their brother Salih, saying: Worship Allah. And lo! they (then became two parties quarrelling.

ar: قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ لِمَ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ ٱلْحَسَنَةِ ۖ لَوْلَا تَسْتَغْفِرُونَ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ
en: He urged ˹the disbelieving group˺, “O my people! Why do you ˹seek to˺ hasten the torment If only you sought Allah’s forgiveness so you may be shown mercy!”
t1: (Salih) said: ‘O my people, why do you hasten the evil (i.e., torment) before the good (i.e., mercy)? Why do you not ask for forgiveness from Allah so that you are shown mercy?’
t2: He said, ’O my people, why do you seek to hasten evil before good? Why do you not ask forgiveness of God? Haply so you will find mercy.’
t3: He said: O my people! Why will ye hasten on the evil rather than the good ? Why will ye not ask pardon of Allah, that ye may receive mercy.

ar: قَالُوا۟ ٱطَّيَّرْنَا بِكَ وَبِمَن مَّعَكَ ۚ قَالَ طَٰٓئِرُكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ۖ بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌۭ تُفْتَنُونَ
en: They replied, “You and your followers are a bad omen for us.” He responded, “Your omens are destined by Allah. In fact, you are ˹only˺ a people being tested.”
t1: They said: ‘You have caused us misfortune, and so have your companions.’ (Salih) said: ‘(The cause of) your misfortune is (written) with Allah; you people have rather been put to trial.’
t2: They said, ’We augur ill of thee and of those that are with thee.’ He said, ’Your augury is with God; nay, but you are a people being proved.’
t3: They said: We augur evil of thee and those with thee. He said: Your evil augury is with Allah. Nay, but ye are folk that are being tested.

ar: وَكَانَ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ تِسْعَةُ رَهْطٍۢ يُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا يُصْلِحُونَ
en: And there were in the city nine ˹elite˺ men who spread corruption in the land, never doing what is right.
t1: And there were in the city (of the people of Thamud) nine prominent leaders (leading their respective parties) who used to spread destructive activities in the land and would not do constructive works.
t2: Now in the city there were nine persons who did corruption in the land, and put not things right;
t3: And there were in the city nine persons who made mischief in the land and reformed not.

ar: قَالُوا۟ تَقَاسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُۥ وَأَهْلَهُۥ ثُمَّ لَنَقُولَنَّ لِوَلِيِّهِۦ مَا شَهِدْنَا مَهْلِكَ أَهْلِهِۦ وَإِنَّا لَصَٰدِقُونَ
en: They vowed, “Let us swear by Allah that we will take him and his family down by night. Then we will certainly say to his ˹closest˺ heirs, ‘We did not witness the murder of his family. We are definitely telling the truth.’”
t1: (These leaders) said: ‘Vow amongst yourselves by swearing in the Name of Allah that we will certainly launch a murder attack against Salih and his family at night, and will then tell their heirs that we were not present on the occasion of their murder. And surely, we are telling the truth.’
t2: they said, ’Swear you, one to another, by God, "We will attack him and his family by night, then we will tell his protector, We were not witnesses of the destruction of his family; and assuredly we are truthful men."’
t3: They said: Swear one to another by Allah that we verily will attack him and his household by night, and afterward we will surely say unto his friend: We witnessed not the destruction of his household. And lo! we are truthtellers.

ar: وَمَكَرُوا۟ مَكْرًۭا وَمَكَرْنَا مَكْرًۭا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
en: And ˹so˺ they made a plan, but We too made a plan, while they were unaware.
t1: And they worked out a plan in secret, and We (also) devised a secret scheme (to foil that), and they did not get a hint of it.
t2: And they devised a device, and We likewise devised a device, while they were not aware;
t3: So they plotted a plot: and We plotted a plot, while they perceived not.

ar: فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ أَنَّا دَمَّرْنَٰهُمْ وَقَوْمَهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
en: See then what the consequences of their plan were: We ˹utterly˺ destroyed them and their people all together.
t1: See then what was the end of their (wicked) plan! Surely, We destroyed those (leaders) and their entire people altogether.
t2: and behold, how was the end of their device! For We destroyed them and their people all together.
t3: Then see the nature of the consequence of their plotting, for lo! We destroyed them and their people, every one.

ar: فَتِلْكَ بُيُوتُهُمْ خَاوِيَةًۢ بِمَا ظَلَمُوٓا۟ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَعْلَمُونَ
en: So their homes are there, ˹but completely˺ ruined because of their wrongdoing. Surely in this is a lesson for people of knowledge.
t1: So these are their houses lying ruined, for they committed oppression and injustice. No doubt there is a sign (of warning) in it for those who have knowledge.
t2: Those are their houses, all fallen down because of the evil they committed; surely in that is a sign for a people who have knowledge.
t3: See, yonder are their dwellings empty and in ruins because they did wrong. Lo! herein is indeed a portent for a people who have knowledge.

ar: وَأَنجَيْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَكَانُوا۟ يَتَّقُونَ
en: And We delivered those who were faithful and were mindful ˹of Allah˺.
t1: And We delivered those who believed and became Godfearing.
t2: And We delivered those who believed and were godfearing.
t3: And we saved those who believed and used to ward off (evil).

ar: وَلُوطًا إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِۦٓ أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَٰحِشَةَ وَأَنتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ
en: And ˹remember˺ Lot, when he rebuked ˹the men of˺ his people, “Do you commit that shameful deed while you can see ˹one another˺?
t1: And (recall) Lut (Lot) when he said to his people: ‘Do you commit indecency whilst you see (as well)?
t2: And Lot, when he said to his people, ’What, do you commit indecency with your eyes open?
t3: And Lot! when he said unto his folk: Will ye commit abomination knowingly ?

ar: أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ ٱلرِّجَالَ شَهْوَةًۭ مِّن دُونِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ ۚ بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌۭ تَجْهَلُونَ
en: Do you really lust after men instead of women? In fact, you are ˹only˺ a people acting ignorantly.”
t1: Do you approach men rather than women to satisfy your sexual desire? The truth is that you are ignorant people.’
t2: What, do you approach men lustfully instead of women? No, you are a people that are ignorant.’
t3: Must ye needs lust after men instead of women ? Nay, but ye are folk who act senselessly.

ar: ۞ فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوٓا۟ أَخْرِجُوٓا۟ ءَالَ لُوطٍۢ مِّن قَرْيَتِكُمْ ۖ إِنَّهُمْ أُنَاسٌۭ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ
en: But his people’s only response was to say, “Expel Lot’s followers from your land! They are a people who wish to remain chaste!”
t1: The only answer of his people was that they said: ‘Drive out the family of Lut (Lot) from your town; they claim to be very pious!’
t2: And the only answer of his people was that they said, ’Expel the folk of Lot from your city; they are men that keep themselves clean!’
t3: But the answer of his folk was naught save that they said: Expel the household of Lot from your township, for they (forsooth) are folk who would keep clean!

ar: فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَهُۥ قَدَّرْنَٰهَا مِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ
en: So We delivered him and his family, except his wife. We had destined her to be one of the doomed.
t1: So We delivered Lut (Lot) and his family except his wife, for We destined her to be amongst those who stayed behind (for torment).
t2: So We delivered him and his family, except his wife; We decreed she should be of those that tarried.
t3: Then We saved him and his household save his wife; We destined her to be of those who stayed behind.

ar: وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًۭا ۖ فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
en: And We poured upon them a rain ˹of brimstone˺. How evil was the rain of those who had been warned!
t1: And We heavily rained upon them (stones). So evil was the rain (of stones) upon those people who were stressed with horror.
t2: And We rained on them a rain; and evil indeed is the rain of them that are warned.
t3: And We rained a rain upon them. Dreadful is the rain of those who have been warned.

ar: قُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَسَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ عِبَادِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصْطَفَىٰٓ ۗ ءَآللَّهُ خَيْرٌ أَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
en: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Praise be to Allah, and peace be upon the servants He has chosen.” ˹Ask the disbelievers,˺ “Which is better: Allah or whatever ˹gods˺ they associate ˹with Him˺?”
t1: Say: ‘All praise be to Allah, and peace be upon His Servants whom He has chosen (and exalted). Is Allah better or those (false gods) that these people associate (with Him)?’
t2: Say: ’Praise belongs to God, and peace be on His servants whom He has chosen.’ What, is God better, or that they associate?
t3: Say (O Muhammad): Praise be to Allah, and peace be on His slaves whom He hath chosen! Is Allah best, or (all) that ye ascribe as partners (unto Him) ?

ar: أَمَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَأَنزَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ فَأَنۢبَتْنَا بِهِۦ حَدَآئِقَ ذَاتَ بَهْجَةٍۢ مَّا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَن تُنۢبِتُوا۟ شَجَرَهَآ ۗ أَءِلَٰهٌۭ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌۭ يَعْدِلُونَ
en: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who created the heavens and the earth, and sends down rain for you from the sky, by which We cause delightful gardens to grow? You could never cause their trees to grow. Was it another god besides Allah?” Absolutely not! But they are a people who set up equals ˹to Allah˺!
t1: Well, Who has created the heavens and the earth and poured down water for you from the atmosphere in the sky? Then with that (water), We brought forth fresh and beautiful gardens. It was not possible for you to grow plants in these (gardens). Is there any (other) God besides Allah? In fact, they are the people who are turning away (from the path of truth).
t2: He who created the heavens and earth, and sent down for you out of heaven water; and We caused to grow therewith gardens full of loveliness whose trees you could never grow. Is there a god with God? Nay, but they are a people who assign to Him equals!
t3: Is not He (best) Who created the heavens and the earth, and sendeth down for you water from the sky wherewith We cause to spring forth joyous orchards, whose trees it never hath been yours to cause to grow. Is there any God beside Allah ? Nay, but they are folk who ascribe equals (unto Him)!

ar: أَمَّن جَعَلَ ٱلْأَرْضَ قَرَارًۭا وَجَعَلَ خِلَٰلَهَآ أَنْهَٰرًۭا وَجَعَلَ لَهَا رَوَٰسِىَ وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ حَاجِزًا ۗ أَءِلَٰهٌۭ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
en: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who made the earth a place of settlement, caused rivers to flow through it, placed firm mountains upon it, and set a barrier between ˹fresh and salt˺ bodies of water? Was it another god besides Allah?” Absolutely not! But most of them do not know.
t1: Or, Who made the earth a dwelling place and made rivers amid it and made for it huge mountains and put a barrier between the two seas (of salt and sweet waters)? Is there any (other) God besides Allah? But most of these (disbelievers) do not have knowledge.
t2: He who made the earth a fixed place and set amidst it rivers and appointed for it firm mountains and placed a partition between the two seas. Is there a god with God? Nay, but the most of them have no knowledge.
t3: Is not He (best) Who made the earth a fixed abode, and placed rivers in the folds thereof, and placed firm hills therein, and hath set a barrier between the two seas ? Is there any God beside Allah ? Nay, but most of them know not!

ar: أَمَّن يُجِيبُ ٱلْمُضْطَرَّ إِذَا دَعَاهُ وَيَكْشِفُ ٱلسُّوٓءَ وَيَجْعَلُكُمْ خُلَفَآءَ ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ أَءِلَٰهٌۭ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ قَلِيلًۭا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ
en: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who responds to the distressed when they cry to Him, relieving ˹their˺ affliction, and ˹Who˺ makes you successors in the earth? Is it another god besides Allah? Yet you are hardly mindful!”
t1: Or, Who grants the supplication of the anxiety-stricken caller when he calls upon Him, and Who removes the trouble and makes you successors and inheritors (of the predecessors) in the earth? Is there any (other) God besides Allah? You people accept advice but little.
t2: He who answers the constrained, when he calls unto Him, and removes the evil and appoints you to be successors in the earth. Is there a god with God? Little indeed do you remember.
t3: Is not He (best) Who answereth the wronged one when he crieth unto Him and removeth the evil, and hath made you viceroys of the earth ? Is there any God beside Allah ? Little do they reflect!

ar: أَمَّن يَهْدِيكُمْ فِى ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ وَمَن يُرْسِلُ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ بُشْرًۢا بَيْنَ يَدَىْ رَحْمَتِهِۦٓ ۗ أَءِلَٰهٌۭ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ تَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
en: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who guides you in the darkness of the land and sea, Is it another god besides Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate ˹with Him˺!
t1: Or, Who guides you in the darkness of land and sea and sends winds as good news before (the rain of) His mercy? Is there any (other) God besides Allah? Exalted is Allah, High above (the false gods) which they associate with Him.
t2: He who guides you in the shadows of the land and the sea and looses the winds, bearing good tidings before His mercy. Is there a god with God? High exalted be God, above that which they associate!
t3: Is not He (best) Who guideth you in the darkness of the land and the sea, He Who sendeth the winds as heralds of His mercy ? Is there any God beside Allah ? High Exalted be Allah from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him)!

ar: أَمَّن يَبْدَؤُا۟ ٱلْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُۥ وَمَن يَرْزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ أَءِلَٰهٌۭ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ قُلْ هَاتُوا۟ بُرْهَٰنَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
en: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who originates the creation then resurrects it, and gives you provisions from the heavens and the earth? Is it another god besides Allah?” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Show ˹me˺ your proof, if what you say is true.”
t1: Well, Who originates creation and shall repeat the same (process of creation), and Who grants you sustenance from the heavens and the earth? Is there any (other) God besides Allah? Say: ‘(O polytheists,) bring your proof if you are truthful.’
t2: Who originates creation, then brings it back again, and provides you out of heaven and earth. Is there a god with God? Say: ’Produce your proof, if you speak truly.’
t3: Is not He (best) Who produceth creation, then reproduceth it, and Who provideth for you from the heaven and the earth ? Is there any God beside Allah ? Say: Bring your proof, if ye are truthful!

ar: قُل لَّا يَعْلَمُ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْغَيْبَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ ۚ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ
en: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “None in the heavens and the earth has knowledge of the unseen except Allah. Nor do they know when they will be resurrected.
t1: Say: ‘Those who are in the heavens and the earth do not have the knowledge of the unseen (by themselves) except Allah (Who is Self-Knowing), nor do they know when they will be raised up (alive again).’
t2: Say: ’None knows the Unseen in the heavens and earth except God. And they are not aware when they shall be raised;
t3: Say (O Muhammad): None in the heavens and the earth knoweth the Unseen save Allah; and they know not when they will be raised (again).

ar: بَلِ ٱدَّٰرَكَ عِلْمُهُمْ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ ۚ بَلْ هُمْ فِى شَكٍّۢ مِّنْهَا ۖ بَلْ هُم مِّنْهَا عَمُونَ
en: No! Their knowledge of the Hereafter amounts to ignorance. In fact, they are in doubt about it. In truth, they are ˹totally˺ blind to it.
t1: The truth is that their knowledge about the Hereafter terminated after reaching (its) limit, but they are just (caught) in doubt about it. Nay, they are blind to its (exact knowledge).
t2: nay, but their knowledge fails as to the Hereafter; nay, they are in doubt of it; nay, they are blind to it.
t3: Nay, but doth their knowledge reach to the Hereafter ? Nay, for they are in doubt concerning it. Nay, for they cannot see it.

ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَءِذَا كُنَّا تُرَٰبًۭا وَءَابَآؤُنَآ أَئِنَّا لَمُخْرَجُونَ
en: The disbelievers ask, “When we and our fathers are reduced to dust, will we really be brought forth ˹alive˺?
t1: And the disbelievers say: ‘When we and our fathers become dust (after death), shall we be brought forth (from graves alive)?
t2: The unbelievers say, ’What, when we are dust, and our fathers, shall we indeed be brought forth?
t3: Yet those who disbelieve say: When we have become dust like our fathers, shall we verily be brought forth (again) ?

ar: لَقَدْ وُعِدْنَا هَٰذَا نَحْنُ وَءَابَآؤُنَا مِن قَبْلُ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّآ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
en: We have already been promised this, as well as our forefathers earlier. This is nothing but ancient fables!”
t1: In fact, we and, before this, our ancestors (too) have been promised this. These are but stories fabricated by the ancients.’
t2: We have been promised this, and our fathers before; this is naught but the fairy-tales of the ancients.’
t3: We were promised this, forsooth, we and our fathers. (All) this is naught but fables of the men of old.

ar: قُلْ سِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
en: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Travel throughout the land and see the fate of the wicked.”
t1: Say: ‘Travel in the land and see how was the end of the evildoers.’
t2: Say: ’Journey in the land, then behold how was the end of the sinners.’
t3: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Travel in the land and see the nature of the sequel for the guilty!

ar: وَلَا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا تَكُن فِى ضَيْقٍۢ مِّمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ
en: Do not grieve for them, nor be distressed by their schemes.
t1: And, (O Esteemed Beloved,) do not grieve (over what they say), nor (undergo) distress at the deceitful and treacherous activities which they are carrying out.
t2: Do not sorrow for them, nor be thou straitened for what they devise.
t3: And grieve thou not for them, nor be in distress because of what they plot (against thee).

ar: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
en: They ask ˹the believers˺, “When will this threat come to pass, if what you say is true?”
t1: And they say: ‘(Tell us) when this promise (of the Last Day) will come true if you are truthful.’
t2: They say, ’When shall this promise come to pass, if you speak the truth?’
t3: And they say: When (will) this promise (be fulfilled), if ye are truthful ?

ar: قُلْ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ رَدِفَ لَكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِى تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ
en: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Perhaps some of what you seek to hasten is close at hand.”
t1: Say: ‘It is not far from possible that a part of that (torment) which you seek to hasten has nearly reached you.’
t2: Say: ’It may be that riding behind you already is some part of that you seek to hasten on.
t3: Say: It may be that a part of that which ye would hasten on is close behind you.

ar: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ
en: Surely your Lord is ever Bountiful to humanity, but most of them are ungrateful.
t1: And surely, your Lord is Gracious to the people but most of them do not give thanks.
t2: Surely thy Lord is bountiful to men; but most of them are not thankful.
t3: Lo! thy Lord is full of bounty for mankind, but most of them do not give thanks.

ar: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيَعْلَمُ مَا تُكِنُّ صُدُورُهُمْ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ
en: And surely your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they reveal.
t1: And certainly, your Lord knows well what their breasts hide and also what they make known.
t2: Surely thy Lord knows what their hearts conceal, and what they publish.
t3: Lo! thy Lord knoweth surely all that their bosoms hide, and all that they proclaim.

ar: وَمَا مِنْ غَآئِبَةٍۢ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّا فِى كِتَٰبٍۢ مُّبِينٍ
en: For there is nothing hidden in the heavens or the earth without being ˹written˺ in a perfect Record.
t1: And there is nothing hidden in the heavens and the earth but is recorded in a Clear Book (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).
t2: And not a thing is there hidden in heaven and earth but it is in a Manifest Book.
t3: And there is nothing hidden in the heaven or the earth but it is in a clear Record.

ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ يَقُصُّ عَلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ أَكْثَرَ ٱلَّذِى هُمْ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ
en: Indeed, this Quran clarifies for the Children of Israel most of what they differ over.
t1: Surely, this Qur’an expounds to the Children of Israel most of the things in which they differ.
t2: Surely this Koran relates to the Children of Israel most of that concerning which they are at variance;
t3: Lo! this Qur’an narrateth unto the Children of Israel most of that concerning which they differ.

ar: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَهُدًۭى وَرَحْمَةٌۭ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
en: And it is truly a guide and mercy for the believers.
t1: And verily, it is guidance and mercy for the believers.
t2: it is a guidance, and a mercy unto the believers.
t3: And lo! it is a guidance and a mercy for believers.

ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقْضِى بَيْنَهُم بِحُكْمِهِۦ ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
en: Your Lord will certainly judge between them by His justice, for He is the Almighty, All-Knowing.
t1: Verily, your Lord will judge between these (believers and disbelievers) by His command (of justice). And He is Almighty, All-Knowing.
t2: Surely thy Lord will decide between them by His Judgment; He is the All-mighty, the All-knowing.
t3: Lo! thy Lord will judge between them of His wisdom, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.

ar: فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَى ٱلْحَقِّ ٱلْمُبِينِ
en: So put your trust in Allah, for you are surely upon the ˹Path of˺ clear truth.
t1: So put your trust in Allah. Surely, you are (firm and fixed) on the evident truth.
t2: So put thy trust in God; thou art upon the manifest truth.
t3: Therefor (O Muhammad) put thy trust in Allah, for thou (standest) on the plain Truth.

ar: إِنَّكَ لَا تُسْمِعُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَلَا تُسْمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ إِذَا وَلَّوْا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ
en: You certainly cannot make the dead hear ˹the truth˺. Nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn their backs and walk away.
t1: (O Beloved!) Surely, you make neither the dead (i.e., the disbelievers deprived of the vitality of faith) hear your call nor the deaf (i.e., deprived of hearing the call of truth) while they are getting away (from you) turning their backs.*
t2: Thou shalt not make the dead to hear, neither shalt thou make the deaf to hear the call when they turn about, retreating.
t3: Lo! thou canst not make the dead to hear, nor canst thou make the deaf to hear the call when they have turned to flee;

ar: وَمَآ أَنتَ بِهَٰدِى ٱلْعُمْىِ عَن ضَلَٰلَتِهِمْ ۖ إِن تُسْمِعُ إِلَّا مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَهُم مُّسْلِمُونَ
en: Nor can you lead the blind out of their misguidance. You can make none hear ˹the truth˺ except those who believe in Our revelations, ˹fully˺ submitting ˹to Allah˺.
t1: Nor can you guide the blind (of heart, rescuing them) from their wrong path. (In fact) you make only them hear who (accepting your call) believe in Our Revelations. So it is they who are Muslims (and only they deserve to be called alive).
t2: Thou shalt not guide the blind out of their error neither shalt thou make any to hear, save such as believe in Our signs, and so surrender.
t3: Nor canst thou lead the blind out of their error. Thou canst make none to hear, save those who believe Our revelations and who have surrendered.

ar: ۞ وَإِذَا وَقَعَ ٱلْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَخْرَجْنَا لَهُمْ دَآبَّةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ أَنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ كَانُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا لَا يُوقِنُونَ
en: And when the decree ˹of the Hour˺ comes to pass against them, We will bring forth for them a beast from the earth, telling them that the people had no sure faith in Our revelations.
t1: And when the time to execute Our command (of torment) against them comes, We shall bring out for them from the earth a beast who will converse with them because people do not have certitude in Our signs.
t2: When the Word falls on them, We shall bring forth for them out of the earth a beast that shall speak unto them: ’Mankind had no faith in Our signs.’
t3: And when the word is fulfilled concerning them, We shall bring forth a beast of the earth to speak unto them because mankind had not faith in Our revelations.

ar: وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُ مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةٍۢ فَوْجًۭا مِّمَّن يُكَذِّبُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ
en: ˹Watch for˺ the Day We will gather from every faith-community a group of those who denied Our revelations, and they will be driven in ranks.
t1: And the Day when We shall gather out of every community a party of those who used to reject Our Revelations, they will be stopped (from the front in order that they all move together).
t2: Upon the day when We shall muster out of every nation a troop of those that cried lies to Our signs, duly disposed,
t3: And (remind them of) the Day when We shall gather out of every nation a host of those who denied Our revelations, and they will be set in array;

ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُو قَالَ أَكَذَّبْتُم بِـَٔايَٰتِى وَلَمْ تُحِيطُوا۟ بِهَا عِلْمًا أَمَّاذَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
en: When they ˹finally˺ come before their Lord, He will ask ˹them˺, “Did you deny My revelations without ˹even˺ comprehending them? Or what ˹exactly˺ did you do?”
t1: Till, when they all reach (the point of reckoning), it will be said: ‘Did you reject My Revelations (without meditating on them), whereas you could not thoroughly understand them with (your inadequate) knowledge? Or (tell yourselves) what else was (the reason) that you used to (belie the truth).’
t2: till, when they are come, He shall say, ’Did you cry lies to My signs, not comprehending them in knowledge, or what have you been doing?’
t3: Till, when they come (before their Lord), He will say: Did ye deny My revelations when ye could not compass them in knowledge, or what was it that ye did ?

ar: وَوَقَعَ ٱلْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِم بِمَا ظَلَمُوا۟ فَهُمْ لَا يَنطِقُونَ
en: And the decree ˹of torment˺ will be justified against them for their wrongdoing, leaving them speechless.
