t3: If Allah took mankind to task by that which they deserve, He would not leave a living creature on the surface of the earth; but He reprieveth them unto an appointed term, and when their term cometh - then verily (they will know that) Allah is ever Seer of His slaves.

ar: يسٓ
en: Ya-Sĩn.
t1: Ya-Sin. (Only Allah and the Messenger [blessings and peace be upon him] know the real meaning.)
t2: Ya Sin
t3: Ya Sin.

ar: وَٱلْقُرْءَانِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ
en: By the Quran, rich in wisdom!
t1: By the Qur’an, full of wisdom,
t2: By the Wise Koran,
t3: By the wise Qur’an,

ar: إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
en: You ˹O Prophet˺ are truly one of the messengers
t1: You are indeed one of the Messengers,
t2: thou art truly among the Envoys
t3: Lo! thou art of those sent

ar: عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍۢ مُّسْتَقِيمٍۢ
en: upon the Straight Path.
t1: On the straight path.
t2: on a straight path;
t3: On a straight path,

ar: تَنزِيلَ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ
en: ˹This is˺ a revelation from the Almighty, Most Merciful,
t1: This is revealed by the Almighty, Ever-Merciful,
t2: the sending down of the All-mighty, the All-wise,
t3: A revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful,

ar: لِتُنذِرَ قَوْمًۭا مَّآ أُنذِرَ ءَابَآؤُهُمْ فَهُمْ غَٰفِلُونَ
en: so that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, and so are heedless.
t1: That you may warn the people whose fathers were (also) not warned. So they are careless and neglectful.
t2: that thou mayest warn a people whose fathers were never warned, so they are heedless.
t3: That thou mayst warn a folk whose fathers were not warned, so they are heedless.

ar: لَقَدْ حَقَّ ٱلْقَوْلُ عَلَىٰٓ أَكْثَرِهِمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
en: The decree ˹of torment˺ has already been justified against most of them, for they will never believe.
t1: In fact, Our command has proved true against most of them. So they will not believe.
t2: The Word has been realised against most of them, yet they do not believe.
t3: Already hath the judgment, (for their infidelity) proved true of most of them, for they believe not.

ar: إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا فِىٓ أَعْنَٰقِهِمْ أَغْلَٰلًۭا فَهِىَ إِلَى ٱلْأَذْقَانِ فَهُم مُّقْمَحُونَ
en: ˹It is as if˺ We have put shackles around their necks up to their chins, so their heads are forced up,
t1: Surely, We have put iron collars round their necks reaching their chins. So they have raised their heads up.
t2: Surely We have put on their necks fetters up to the chin, so their heads are raised;
t3: Lo! We have put on their necks carcans reaching unto the chins, so that they are made stiff-necked.

ar: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنۢ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّۭا وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّۭا فَأَغْشَيْنَٰهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ
en: and have placed a barrier before them and a barrier behind them and covered them ˹all˺ up, so they fail to see ˹the truth˺.
t1: And We have set a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, and We have cast a veil over their eyes so they do not see anything.
t2: and We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier; and We have covered them, so they do not see.
t3: And We have set a bar before them and a bar behind them, and (thus) have covered them so that they see not.

ar: وَسَوَآءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
en: It is the same whether you warn them or not—they will never believe.
t1: And it is all the same for them whether you warn or do not warn them, they will not believe.
t2: Alike it is to them whether thou hast warned them or thou hast not warned them, they do not believe.
t3: Whether thou warn them or thou warn them not, it is alike for them, for they believe not.

ar: إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلذِّكْرَ وَخَشِىَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ ۖ فَبَشِّرْهُ بِمَغْفِرَةٍۢ وَأَجْرٍۢ كَرِيمٍ
en: You can only warn those who follow the Reminder So give them good news of forgiveness and an honourable reward.
t1: You can only warn the one who follows the direction and guidance and fears the Most Kind (Lord) unseen. So give him the good news of forgiveness and a reward of great honour.
t2: Thou only warnest him who follows the Remembrance and who fears the All-merciful in the Unseen; so give him the good tidings of forgiveness and a generous wage.
t3: Thou warnest only him who followeth the Reminder and feareth the Beneficent in secret. To him bear tidings of forgiveness and a rich reward.

ar: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُوا۟ وَءَاثَٰرَهُمْ ۚ وَكُلَّ شَىْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَٰهُ فِىٓ إِمَامٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
en: It is certainly We Who resurrect the dead, and write what they send forth and what they leave behind. Everything is listed by Us in a perfect Record.
t1: Surely, We alone raise the dead to life. And We are writing down (the deeds) which they have sent forward and their effects (that are left behind). And We have encompassed everything in the illumining Book (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).
t2: Surely it is We who bring the dead to life and write down what they have forwarded and what they have left behind; everything We have numbered in a clear register.
t3: Lo! We it is Who bring the dead to life. We record that which they send before (them, and their footprints. And all things We have kept in a clear Register.

ar: وَٱضْرِبْ لَهُم مَّثَلًا أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ إِذْ جَآءَهَا ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
en: Give them an example ˹O Prophet˺ of the residents of a town, when the messengers came to them.
t1: And narrate to them the (legendary) example of the people of a city (Antioch—an ancient city in Northern Syria) when there came to them some Messengers.
t2: Strike for them a similitude -- the inhabitants of the city, when the Envoys came to it;
t3: Coin for them a similitude: The people of the city when those sent (from Allah) came unto them;

ar: إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَآ إِلَيْهِمُ ٱثْنَيْنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزْنَا بِثَالِثٍۢ فَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّآ إِلَيْكُم مُّرْسَلُونَ
en: We sent them two messengers, but they rejected both. So We reinforced ˹the two˺ with a third, and they declared, “We have indeed been sent to you ˹as messengers˺.”
t1: When (at first) We sent to them two Messengers, they rejected them both. Then We reinforced (them) with a third (Messenger). Then the three of them said: ‘Surely, we have been sent to you.’
t2: when We sent unto them two men, but they cried them lies, so We sent a third as reinforcement. They said, ’We are assuredly Envoys unto you.
t3: When We sent unto them twain, and they denied them both, so We reinforced them with a third, and they said: Lo! we have been sent unto you.

ar: قَالُوا۟ مَآ أَنتُمْ إِلَّا بَشَرٌۭ مِّثْلُنَا وَمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ مِن شَىْءٍ إِنْ أَنتُمْ إِلَّا تَكْذِبُونَ
en: The people replied, “You are only humans like us, and the Most Compassionate has not revealed anything. You are simply lying!”
t1: (The people of the city) said: ‘You are but human beings like us, and the Most Kind (Lord) has not sent down anything. You are only lying.’
t2: They said, ’You are naught but mortals like us; the All-merciful has not sent down anything. You are speaking only lies.’
t3: They said: Ye are but mortals like unto us. The Beneficent hath naught revealed. Ye do but lie!

ar: قَالُوا۟ رَبُّنَا يَعْلَمُ إِنَّآ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمُرْسَلُونَ
en: The messengers responded, “Our Lord knows that we have truly been sent to you.
t1: (The Messengers) said: ‘Surely, our Lord knows that we have been sent to you.
t2: They said, ’Our Lord knows we are Envoys unto you;
t3: They answered: Our Lord knoweth that we are indeed sent unto you,

ar: وَمَا عَلَيْنَآ إِلَّا ٱلْبَلَٰغُ ٱلْمُبِينُ
en: And our duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺ clearly.”
t1: And there is nothing binding upon us except to communicate the message clearly.’
t2: and it is only for us to deliver the Manifest Message.’
t3: And our duty is but plain conveyance (of the message).

ar: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا تَطَيَّرْنَا بِكُمْ ۖ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهُوا۟ لَنَرْجُمَنَّكُمْ وَلَيَمَسَّنَّكُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌۭ
en: The people replied, “We definitely see you as a bad omen for us. If you do not desist, we will certainly stone you ˹to death˺ and you will be touched with a painful punishment from us.”
t1: (The people of the city) said: ‘An evil omen has reached us from you. If you do not desist, we shall certainly stone you, and you will definitely suffer an agonizing punishment at our hands.’
t2: They said, ’We augur ill of you. If you give not over, we will stone you and there shall visit you from us a painful chastisement.’
t3: (The people of the city) said: We augur ill of you. If ye desist not, we shall surely stone you, and grievous torture will befall you at our hands.

ar: قَالُوا۟ طَٰٓئِرُكُم مَّعَكُمْ ۚ أَئِن ذُكِّرْتُم ۚ بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌۭ مُّسْرِفُونَ
en: The messengers said, “Your bad omen lies within yourselves. Are you saying this because you are reminded ˹of the truth˺? In fact, you are a transgressing people.”
t1: (The Messengers) said: ‘Your evil omen is with you. Is it an evil omen that you are admonished? Nay, but you are a people who exceed limits.’
t2: They said, ’Your augury is with you; if you are reminded? But you are a prodigal people.’
t3: They said: Your evil augury be with you! Is it because ye are reminded (of the truth) ? Nay, but ye are froward folk!

ar: وَجَآءَ مِنْ أَقْصَا ٱلْمَدِينَةِ رَجُلٌۭ يَسْعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱتَّبِعُوا۟ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
en: Then from the farthest end of the city a man came, rushing. He advised, “O my people! Follow the messengers.
t1: And a person came running from the farthest end of the city. He said: ‘O my people, follow the Messengers.
t2: Then came a man from the furthest part of the city, running; he said, ’My people, follow the Envoys!
t3: And there came from the uttermost part of the city a man running. He cried: O my people! Follow those who have been sent!

ar: ٱتَّبِعُوا۟ مَن لَّا يَسْـَٔلُكُمْ أَجْرًۭا وَهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ
en: Follow those who ask no reward of you, and are ˹rightly˺ guided.
t1: Follow those who do not ask from you any compensation and who are rightly guided.
t2: Follow such as ask no wage of you, that are right-guided.
t3: Follow those who ask of you no fee, and who are rightly guided.

ar: وَمَا لِىَ لَآ أَعْبُدُ ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنِى وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
en: And why should I not worship the One Who has originated me, and to Whom you will be returned.
t1: And what is the matter with me that I should not worship Him Who has created me and to Him (all of) you will be returned?
t2: And why should I not serve Him who originated me, and unto whom you shall be returned?
t3: For what cause should I not serve Him Who hath created me, and unto Whom ye will be brought back ?

ar: ءَأَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةً إِن يُرِدْنِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ بِضُرٍّۢ لَّا تُغْنِ عَنِّى شَفَٰعَتُهُمْ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَا يُنقِذُونِ
en: How could I take besides Him other gods whose intercession would not be of any benefit to me, nor could they save me if the Most Compassionate intended to harm me?
t1: Should I take such gods apart from Him (Allah) that if the Most Kind (Lord) intends to do me any harm, their intercession would not bring me any benefit, nor would they be able to rescue me?
t2: What, shall I take, apart from Him, gods whose intercession, if the All-merciful desires affliction for me, shall not avail me anything, and who will never deliver me?
t3: Shall I take (other) gods in place of Him when, if the Beneficent should wish me any harm, their intercession will avail me naught, nor can they save ?

ar: إِنِّىٓ إِذًۭا لَّفِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍ
en: Indeed, I would then be clearly astray.
t1: Then, certainly, I would be in open error.
t2: Surely in that case I should be in manifest error.
t3: Then truly I should be in error manifest.

ar: إِنِّىٓ ءَامَنتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ فَٱسْمَعُونِ
en: I do believe in your Lord, so listen to me.”
t1: Surely, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me (attentively).’
t2: Behold, I believe in your Lord; therefore hear me!’
t3: Lo! I have believed in your Lord, so hear me!

ar: قِيلَ ٱدْخُلِ ٱلْجَنَّةَ ۖ قَالَ يَٰلَيْتَ قَوْمِى يَعْلَمُونَ
en: ˹But they killed him, then˺ he was told ˹by the angels˺, “Enter Paradise!” He said, “If only my people knew
t1: (The disbelievers martyred him; then it) was said (to him): ‘(Come,) enter Paradise.’ He said: ‘Alas! Would that my people knew,
t2: It was said, ’Enter Paradise!’ He said, ’Ah, would that my people had knowledge
t3: It was said (unto him): Enter paradise. He said: Would that my people knew

ar: بِمَا غَفَرَ لِى رَبِّى وَجَعَلَنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ
en: of how my Lord has forgiven me, and made me one of the honourable.”
t1: That my Lord has forgiven me, and put me amongst the honoured and near ones.’
t2: that my Lord has forgiven me and that He has placed me among the honoured.’
t3: With what (munificence) my Lord hath pardoned me and made me of the honoured ones!

ar: ۞ وَمَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ مِن جُندٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا كُنَّا مُنزِلِينَ
en: We did not send any soldiers from the heavens against his people after his death, nor did We need to.
t1: And, after him, We did not send any army (of angels) from the heaven to his people, nor were We to send down (angels to destroy them).
t2: And We sent not down upon his people, after him, any host out of heaven; neither would We send any down.
t3: We sent not down against his people after him a host from heaven, nor do We ever send.

ar: إِن كَانَتْ إِلَّا صَيْحَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ فَإِذَا هُمْ خَٰمِدُونَ
en: All it took was one ˹mighty˺ blast, and they were extinguished at once.
t1: (Their torment) was nothing but a Mighty Blast, and there were they extinguished (dead like charred coal).
t2: It was only one Cry and lo, they were silent and still.
t3: It was but one Shout, and lo! they were extinct.

ar: يَٰحَسْرَةً عَلَى ٱلْعِبَادِ ۚ مَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ
en: Oh pity, such beings! No messenger ever came to them without being mocked.
t1: Ah! Woe to (these) servants! Never did a Messenger come to them but they used to mock him.
t2: Ah, woe for those servants! Never comes unto them a Messenger, but they mock at him.
t3: Ah, the anguish for the bondmen! Never came there unto them a messenger but they did mock him!

ar: أَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ
en: Have the deniers not considered how many peoples We destroyed before them who never came back to life again?
t1: Have they not seen how many communities We destroyed before them, and that now they will not return to them,
t2: What, have they not seen how many generations We have destroyed before them, and that it is not unto them that they return?
t3: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, which indeed returned not unto them;

ar: وَإِن كُلٌّۭ لَّمَّا جَمِيعٌۭ لَّدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ
en: Yet they will all be brought before Us.
t1: But that all of them will be brought before Our presence?
t2: They shall every one of them be arraigned before Us.
t3: But all, without exception, will be brought before Us.

ar: وَءَايَةٌۭ لَّهُمُ ٱلْأَرْضُ ٱلْمَيْتَةُ أَحْيَيْنَٰهَا وَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهَا حَبًّۭا فَمِنْهُ يَأْكُلُونَ
en: There is a sign for them in the dead earth: We give it life, producing grain from it for them to eat.
t1: And a sign for them is the dead earth to which We gave life, and We brought forth from it (grain); then they eat of it.
t2: And a sign for them is the dead land, that We quickened and brought forth from it grain, whereof they eat;
t3: A token unto them is the dead earth. We revive it, and We bring forth from it grain so that they eat thereof;

ar: وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا جَنَّٰتٍۢ مِّن نَّخِيلٍۢ وَأَعْنَٰبٍۢ وَفَجَّرْنَا فِيهَا مِنَ ٱلْعُيُونِ
en: And We have placed in it gardens of palm trees and grapevines, and caused springs to gush forth in it,
t1: And We produced in it gardens of date-palms and grapes, and also caused some springs as well to gush forth in it,
t2: and We made therein gardens of palms and vines, and therein We caused fountains to gush forth,
t3: And We have placed therein gardens of the date-palm and grapes, and We have caused springs of water to gush forth therein,

ar: لِيَأْكُلُوا۟ مِن ثَمَرِهِۦ وَمَا عَمِلَتْهُ أَيْدِيهِمْ ۖ أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ
en: so that they may eat from its fruit, which they had no hand in making. Will they not then give thanks?
t1: So that they may eat of its fruits. And it is not their hands that made it. Do they not thank (even) then?
t2: that they might eat of its fruits and their hands’ labour. What, will they not be thankful?
t3: That they may eat of the fruit thereof, and their hands made it not. Will they not, then, give thanks ?

ar: سُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلْأَزْوَٰجَ كُلَّهَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَمِنْ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَمِمَّا لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
en: Glory be to the One Who created all ˹things in˺ pairs—˹be it˺ what the earth produces, their genders, or what they do not know!
t1: Glory be to Him Who created everything in pairs of those the earth grows and of themselves as well and, (moreover,) of the things they do not know.
t2: Glory be to Him, who created all the pairs of what the earth produces, and of themselves, and of what they know not.
t3: Glory be to Him Who created all the sexual pairs, of that which the earth groweth, and of themselves, and of that which they know not!

ar: وَءَايَةٌۭ لَّهُمُ ٱلَّيْلُ نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فَإِذَا هُم مُّظْلِمُونَ
en: There is also a sign for them in the night: We strip from it daylight, then—behold!—they are in darkness.
t1: And (also) a sign for them is the night: (how) We draw the day out from it! So then they are left in darkness!
t2: And a sign for them is the night; We strip it of the day and lo, they are in darkness.
t3: A token unto them is night. We strip it of the day, and lo! they are in darkness.

ar: وَٱلشَّمْسُ تَجْرِى لِمُسْتَقَرٍّۢ لَّهَا ۚ ذَٰلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْعَلِيمِ
en: The sun travels for its fixed term. That is the design of the Almighty, All-Knowing.
t1: And the sun is constantly rotating (non-stop) for its appointed destination. It is a measure fixed by the Almighty, All-Knowing (Lord).
t2: And the sun -- it runs to a fixed resting-place; that is the ordaining of the All-mighty, the All-knowing.
t3: And the sun runneth on unto a resting-place for him. That is the measuring of the Mighty, the Wise.

ar: وَٱلْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْنَٰهُ مَنَازِلَ حَتَّىٰ عَادَ كَٱلْعُرْجُونِ ٱلْقَدِيمِ
en: As for the moon, We have ordained ˹precise˺ phases for it, until it ends up like an old, curved palm stalk.
t1: And We have also appointed stages (of motion and rotation) of the moon till (its appearance to the dwellers of the earth wanes to) the semblance of an old dry branch of a palm-tree.
t2: And the moon -- We have determined it by stations, till it returns like an aged palm-bough.
t3: And for the moon We have appointed mansions till she return like an old shrivelled palm-leaf.

ar: لَا ٱلشَّمْسُ يَنۢبَغِى لَهَآ أَن تُدْرِكَ ٱلْقَمَرَ وَلَا ٱلَّيْلُ سَابِقُ ٱلنَّهَارِ ۚ وَكُلٌّۭ فِى فَلَكٍۢ يَسْبَحُونَ
en: It is not for the sun to catch up with the moon, nor does the night outrun the day. Each is travelling in an orbit of their own.
t1: Neither can the sun (deviate from its orbit and) overtake the moon, nor can the night precede the day, and all (the stars and planets) are moving in their respective orbits.
t2: It behoves not the sun to overtake the moon, neither does the night outstrip the day, each swimming in a sky.
t3: It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor doth the night outstrip the day. They float each in an orbit.

ar: وَءَايَةٌۭ لَّهُمْ أَنَّا حَمَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ
en: Another sign for them is that We carried their ancestors ˹with Noah˺ in the fully loaded Ark,
t1: And a sign for them is (also) that We boarded their fathers (the Children of Adam) into the laden Ark of (Nuh [Noah] and saved them).
t2: And a sign for them is that We carried their seed in the laden ship,
t3: And a token unto them is that We bear their offspring in the laden ship,

ar: وَخَلَقْنَا لَهُم مِّن مِّثْلِهِۦ مَا يَرْكَبُونَ
en: and created for them similar things to ride in.
t1: And like this (Ark) We made for them (many other means of transport) which they ride.
t2: and We have created for them the like of it whereon they ride;
t3: And have created for them of the like thereof whereon they ride.

ar: وَإِن نَّشَأْ نُغْرِقْهُمْ فَلَا صَرِيخَ لَهُمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنقَذُونَ
en: If We willed, We could drown them: then no one would respond to their cries, nor would they be rescued—
t1: And if We intend, We drown them. Then there will not be any to respond to their cry, nor will they be saved anyway,
t2: and if We will, We drown them, then none have they to cry to, neither are they delivered,
t3: And if We will, We drown them, and there is no help for them, neither can they be saved;

ar: إِلَّا رَحْمَةًۭ مِّنَّا وَمَتَٰعًا إِلَىٰ حِينٍۢ
en: except by mercy from Us, allowing them enjoyment for a ˹little˺ while.
t1: Except for Our mercy and (this) provision is for an appointed term.
t2: save as a mercy from Us, and enjoyment for a while.
t3: Unless by mercy from Us and as comfort for a while.

ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّقُوا۟ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَمَا خَلْفَكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ
en: ˹Still they turn away˺ when it is said to them, “Beware of what is ahead of you ˹in the Hereafter˺ and what is behind you ˹of destroyed nations˺ so you may be shown mercy.”
t1: And (recall) when it is said to them: ‘Fear that (torment) which is before you and which is behind you so that you may be shown mercy.’
t2: And when it is said to them, ’Fear what is before you and what is behind you; haply you will find mercy’ --
t3: When it is said unto them: Beware of that which is before you and that which is behind you, that haply ye may find mercy (they are heedless).

ar: وَمَا تَأْتِيهِم مِّنْ ءَايَةٍۢ مِّنْ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَّا كَانُوا۟ عَنْهَا مُعْرِضِينَ
en: Whenever a sign comes to them from their Lord, they turn away from it.
t1: And not a sign of the signs of their Lord comes to them but they turn away from it.
t2: yet never any sign of the signs of their Lord comes to them, but they are turning away from it.
t3: Never came a token of the tokens of their Lord to them, but they did turn away from it!

ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ أَنفِقُوا۟ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ أَنُطْعِمُ مَن لَّوْ يَشَآءُ ٱللَّهُ أَطْعَمَهُۥٓ إِنْ أَنتُمْ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
en: And when it is said to them, “Donate from what Allah has provided for you,” the disbelievers say to the believers, “Why should we feed those whom Allah could have fed if He wanted to? You are clearly astray!”
t1: And when it is said to them: ‘Spend (in the way of Allah) of what Allah has given you,’ the disbelievers say to the believers: ‘Shall we feed that (poor) man whom, if Allah so willed, He would feed (Himself)?’ You are but (caught) in clear error.
t2: And when it is said to them, ’Expend of that God has provided you,’ the unbelievers say to the believers, ’What, shall we feed such a one whom, if God willed, He would feed? You are only in manifest error!’
t3: And when it is said unto them: Spend of that wherewith Allah hath provided you, those who disbelieve say unto those who believe: Shall we feed those whom Allah, if He willed, would feed ? Ye are in naught else than error manifest.

ar: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
en: And they ask ˹the believers˺, “When will this threat come to pass, if what you say is true?”
t1: And they say: ‘When will this promise (of the Last Hour) be fulfilled if you are truthful?’
t2: They also say, ’When shall this promise come to pass, if you speak truly?’
t3: And they say: When will this promise be fulfilled, if ye are truthful ?

ar: مَا يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّا صَيْحَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ تَأْخُذُهُمْ وَهُمْ يَخِصِّمُونَ
en: They must be awaiting a single Blast, which will seize them while they are ˹entrenched˺ in ˹worldly˺ disputes.
t1: They are simply waiting for a Mighty Blast which will seize them (all of a sudden), and they will be disputing amongst themselves.
t2: They are awaiting only for one Cry to seize them while they are yet disputing,
t3: They await but one Shout, which will surprise them while they are disputing.

ar: فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ تَوْصِيَةًۭ وَلَآ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِمْ يَرْجِعُونَ
en: Then they will not be able to make a ˹last˺ will, nor can they return to their own people.
t1: Then they will not be able to make a will or to return to their families.
t2: then they will not be able to make any testament, nor will they return to their people.
t3: Then they cannot make bequest, nor can they return to their own folk.

ar: وَنُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَإِذَا هُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَجْدَاثِ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يَنسِلُونَ
en: The Trumpet will be blown ˹a second time˺, then—behold!—they will rush from the graves to their Lord.
t1: And (when) the Trumpet will be blown (again) they will come out of the graves at once and run towards their Lord.
t2: And the Trumpet shall be blown; then behold, they are sliding down from their tombs unto their Lord.
t3: And the trumpet is blown and lo! from the graves they hie unto their Lord,

ar: قَالُوا۟ يَٰوَيْلَنَا مَنۢ بَعَثَنَا مِن مَّرْقَدِنَا ۜ ۗ هَٰذَا مَا وَعَدَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وَصَدَقَ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
en: They will cry, “Woe to us! Who has raised us up from our place of rest? This must be what the Most Compassionate warned us of; the messengers told the truth!”
t1: (Seeing the horrors of the Hour of Resurrection,) they will say: ‘Ah, woe to us! Who has raised us from our sleeping places? This (coming back to life) is the same that the Most Kind (Lord) promised and the Messengers spoke the truth.’
t2: They say, ’Alas for us! Who roused us out of our sleeping place? This is what the All-merciful promised, and the Envoys spoke truly.’
t3: Crying: Woe upon us! Who hath raised us from our place of sleep ? This is that which the Beneficent did promise, and the messengers spoke truth.

ar: إِن كَانَتْ إِلَّا صَيْحَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ فَإِذَا هُمْ جَمِيعٌۭ لَّدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ
en: It will only take one Blast, then at once they will all be brought before Us.
t1: This will only be a Mighty Blast. Then all of them will be brought to Our presence straight away.
t2: ’It was only one Cry; then behold, they are all arraigned before Us.
t3: It is but one Shout, and behold them brought together before Us!

ar: فَٱلْيَوْمَ لَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌۭ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَا تُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
en: On that Day no soul will be wronged in the least, nor will you be rewarded except for what you used to do.
t1: So Today no soul will be wronged in the least. Nor will you be rewarded except for the deeds you used to do.
t2: So today no soul shall be wronged anything, and you shall not be recompensed, except according to what you have been doing.
t3: This day no soul is wronged in aught; nor are ye requited aught save what ye used to do.

ar: إِنَّ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ٱلْيَوْمَ فِى شُغُلٍۢ فَٰكِهُونَ
en: Indeed, on that Day the residents of Paradise will be busy enjoying themselves.
t1: Surely, the residents of Paradise will be rejoicing Today (in their) favourite pastime pursuits (like spiritual visits, entertainments, sessions of hymns and eulogies).
t2: See, the inhabitants of Paradise today are busy in their rejoicing,
t3: Lo! those who merit paradise this day are happily employed,

ar: هُمْ وَأَزْوَٰجُهُمْ فِى ظِلَٰلٍ عَلَى ٱلْأَرَآئِكِ مُتَّكِـُٔونَ
en: They and their spouses will be in ˹cool˺ shade, reclining on ˹canopied˺ couches.
t1: They and their wives will be reclining on raised couches under the deep, calming shades.
t2: they and their spouses, reclining upon couches in the shade;
t3: They and their wives, in pleasant shade, on thrones reclining;

ar: لَهُمْ فِيهَا فَٰكِهَةٌۭ وَلَهُم مَّا يَدَّعُونَ
en: There they will have fruits and whatever they desire.
t1: There they will be provided with fruits (of every kind) and will find (available) everything they will solicit.
t2: therein they have fruits, and they have all that they call for.
t3: Theirs the fruit (of their good deeds) and theirs (all) that they ask;

ar: سَلَٰمٌۭ قَوْلًۭا مِّن رَّبٍّۢ رَّحِيمٍۢ
en: And “Peace!” will be ˹their˺ greeting from the Merciful Lord.
t1: ‘Peace (be upon you)!’ (This) greeting will be conveyed (to them) from the Ever-Merciful Lord.
t2: ’Peace!’ -- such is the greeting, from a Lord All-compassionate.
t3: The word from a Merciful Lord (for them) is: Peace!

ar: وَٱمْتَٰزُوا۟ ٱلْيَوْمَ أَيُّهَا ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ
en: ˹Then the disbelievers will be told,˺ “Step away ˹from the believers˺ this Day, O  wicked ones!
t1: ‘And, O evildoers, get aside (from the righteous) this Day.
t2: ’Now keep yourselves apart, you sinners, upon this day!
t3: But avaunt ye, O ye guilty, this day!

ar: ۞ أَلَمْ أَعْهَدْ إِلَيْكُمْ يَٰبَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ أَن لَّا تَعْبُدُوا۟ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
en: Did I not command you, O  Children of Adam, not to follow Satan, for he is truly your sworn enemy,
t1: O Children of Adam! Did I not take this covenant from you not to worship Satan; no doubt he is your open enemy;
t2: Made I not covenant with you, Children of Adam, that you should not serve Satan -- surely he is a manifest foe to you --
t3: Did I not charge you, O ye sons of Adam, that ye worship not the devil - Lo! he is your open foe! -

ar: وَأَنِ ٱعْبُدُونِى ۚ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطٌۭ مُّسْتَقِيمٌۭ
en: but to worship Me ˹alone˺? This is the Straight Path.
t1: And that you keep worshipping Me alone? That is the straight path.
t2: and that you should serve Me? This is a straight path.
t3: But that ye worship Me ? That was the right path.

ar: وَلَقَدْ أَضَلَّ مِنكُمْ جِبِلًّۭا كَثِيرًا ۖ أَفَلَمْ تَكُونُوا۟ تَعْقِلُونَ
en: Yet he already misled great multitudes of you. Did you not have any sense?
t1: And surely, he led great many of you astray, so had you not any wisdom?
t2: He led astray many a throng of you; did you not understand?
t3: Yet he hath led astray of you a great multitude. Had ye then no sense ?

ar: هَٰذِهِۦ جَهَنَّمُ ٱلَّتِى كُنتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ
en: This is the Hell you were warned of.
t1: This is the same Hell that was being promised to you.
t2: This is Gehenna, then, the same that you were promised;
t3: This is hell which ye were promised (if ye followed him).

ar: ٱصْلَوْهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ
en: Burn in it Today for your disbelief.”
t1: Enter this Hell Today, for you kept disbelieving.’
t2: roast well in it today, for that you were unbelievers!’
t3: Burn therein this day for that ye disbelieved.

ar: ٱلْيَوْمَ نَخْتِمُ عَلَىٰٓ أَفْوَٰهِهِمْ وَتُكَلِّمُنَآ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَتَشْهَدُ أَرْجُلُهُم بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ
en: On this Day We will seal their mouths, their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify to what they used to commit.
t1: Today We shall seal their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to the deeds which they used to earn.
t2: Today We set a seal on their mouths, and their hands speak to Us, and their feet bear witness as to what they have been earning.
t3: This day We seal up their mouths, and their hands speak out to Us and their feet bear witness as to what they used to earn.

ar: وَلَوْ نَشَآءُ لَطَمَسْنَا عَلَىٰٓ أَعْيُنِهِمْ فَٱسْتَبَقُوا۟ ٱلصِّرَٰطَ فَأَنَّىٰ يُبْصِرُونَ
en: Had We willed, We could have easily blinded their eyes, so they would struggle to find their way. How then could they see?
t1: And if We had so willed, We would have obliterated the very marks of their eyes. Then if they would have run on the path, how could they have seen?
t2: Did We will, We would have obliterated their eyes, then they would race to the path, but how would they see?
t3: And had We willed, We verily could have quenched their eyesight so that they should struggle for the way. Then how could they have seen ?

ar: وَلَوْ نَشَآءُ لَمَسَخْنَٰهُمْ عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِهِمْ فَمَا ٱسْتَطَٰعُوا۟ مُضِيًّۭا وَلَا يَرْجِعُونَ
en: And had We willed, We could have transfigured them on the spot, so they could neither progress forward nor turn back.
t1: And if We had so intended, We would have defaced them in their places. Then they would have power neither to go forward nor to turn back.
t2: Did We will, We would have changed them where they were, then they could not go on, nor could they return.
t3: And had We willed, We verily could have fixed them in their place, making them powerless to go forward or turn back.

ar: وَمَن نُّعَمِّرْهُ نُنَكِّسْهُ فِى ٱلْخَلْقِ ۖ أَفَلَا يَعْقِلُونَ
en: And whoever We grant a long life, We reverse them in development. Will they not then understand?
t1: And someone whom We give long life, We cause him to degenerate (towards childhood and debility) in strength and disposition. So, do they not have sense?
t2: And to whomsoever We give long life, We bend him over in His constitution; what, do they not understand?
t3: He whom we bring unto old age, We reverse him in creation (making him go back to weakness after strength). Have ye then no sense ?

ar: وَمَا عَلَّمْنَٰهُ ٱلشِّعْرَ وَمَا يَنۢبَغِى لَهُۥٓ ۚ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌۭ وَقُرْءَانٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
en: We have not taught him poetry, nor is it fitting for him. This ˹Book˺ is only a Reminder and a clear Quran
t1: And We have not taught him (the Holy Messenger [blessings and peace be upon him]) composing poetry, nor does it befit his dignity. This (Book) is but direction and guidance and the illumining Qur’an,
t2: We have not taught him poetry; it is not seemly for him. It is only a Remembrance and a Clear Koran,
t3: And We have not taught him (Muhammad) poetry, nor is it meet for him. This is naught else than a Reminder and a Lecture making plain,

ar: لِّيُنذِرَ مَن كَانَ حَيًّۭا وَيَحِقَّ ٱلْقَوْلُ عَلَى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
en: to warn whoever is ˹truly˺ alive and fulfil the decree ˹of torment˺ against the disbelievers.
t1: So that it may warn the one who is alive, and the word of judgment may be proved against the disbelievers.
t2: that he may warn whosoever is living, and that the Word may be realized against the unbelievers.
t3: To warn whosoever liveth, and that the word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers.

ar: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَا لَهُم مِّمَّا عَمِلَتْ أَيْدِينَآ أَنْعَٰمًۭا فَهُمْ لَهَا مَٰلِكُونَ
en: Do they not see that We singlehandedly created for them, among other things, cattle which are under their control?
t1: Have they not seen that We created for them cattle out of the (creation) We made with Our Mighty Hand, so they are their owners?
t2: Have they not seen how that We have created for them of that Our hands wrought cattle that they own?
t3: Have they not seen how We have created for them of Our handiwork the cattle, so that they are their owners,

ar: وَذَلَّلْنَٰهَا لَهُمْ فَمِنْهَا رَكُوبُهُمْ وَمِنْهَا يَأْكُلُونَ
en: And We have subjected these ˹animals˺ to them, so they may ride some and eat others.
t1: And We subjected those (cattle) to them. So some of them are their riding animals and they eat some of them.
t2: We have subdued them to them, and some of them they ride, and some they eat;
t3: And have subdued them unto them, so that some of them they have for riding, some for food ?

ar: وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا مَنَٰفِعُ وَمَشَارِبُ ۖ أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ
en: And they derive from them other benefits and drinks. Will they not then give thanks?
t1: And there are other benefits and drinks in them as well for them. Then why do they not give thanks?
t2: other uses also they have in them, and beverages. What, will they not be thankful?
t3: Benefits and (divers) drinks have they from them. Will they not then give thanks ?

ar: وَٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ ءَالِهَةًۭ لَّعَلَّهُمْ يُنصَرُونَ
en: Still they have taken other gods besides Allah, hoping to be helped ˹by them˺.
t1: And they have made idols their gods other than Allah with the hope that they will be helped.
t2: Yet they have taken, apart from God, gods; haply they might be helped.
t3: And they have taken (other) gods beside Allah, in order that they may be helped.

ar: لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَهُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُمْ جُندٌۭ مُّحْضَرُونَ
en: They cannot help the pagans, even though they serve the idols as dedicated guards.
t1: These idols are incapable of helping them. And these (disbelievers and polytheists) will be an army of these (idols) that will be brought (into Hell together).
t2: They cannot help them, though they be hosts made ready for them.
t3: It is not in their power to help them; but they (the worshippers) are unto them a host in arms.

ar: فَلَا يَحْزُنكَ قَوْلُهُمْ ۘ إِنَّا نَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ
en: So do not let their words grieve you ˹O Prophet˺. Indeed, We ˹fully˺ know what they conceal and what they reveal.
t1: So let not what they utter hurt you. Surely, We know whatever they hide and whatever they make public.
t2: So do not let their saying grieve thee; assuredly We know what they keep secret and what they publish.
t3: So let not their speech grieve thee (O Muhammad). Lo! We know what they conceal and what proclaim.

ar: أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَٰهُ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
en: Do people not see that We have created them from a sperm-drop, then—behold!—they openly challenge ˹Us˺?
t1: Has man not seen that We have created him from a sperm drop? Even then, he has become an open adversary.
t2: Has not man regarded how that We created him of a sperm-drop? Then lo, he is a manifest adversary.
t3: Hath not man seen that We have created him from a drop of seed ? Yet lo! he is an open opponent.

ar: وَضَرَبَ لَنَا مَثَلًۭا وَنَسِىَ خَلْقَهُۥ ۖ قَالَ مَن يُحْىِ ٱلْعِظَٰمَ وَهِىَ رَمِيمٌۭ
en: And they argue with Us—forgetting they were created—saying, “Who will give life to decayed bones?”
t1: And he (himself) puts forth examples for Us and has forgotten (the truth of) his creation. He says: ‘Who will give life to bones when they will have been decomposed?’
t2: And he has struck for Us a similitude and forgotten his creation; he says, ’Who shall quicken the bones when they are decayed?’
t3: And he hath coined for Us a similitude, and hath forgotten the fact of his creation, saying: Who will revive these bones when they have rotted away ?

ar: قُلْ يُحْيِيهَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَهَآ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍۢ ۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ خَلْقٍ عَلِيمٌ
en: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “They will be revived by the One Who produced them the first time, for He has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of every created being.
t1: Say: ‘He Who created them the first time will give them life. And He knows best every creation;
t2: Say: ’He shall quicken them, who originated them the first time; He knows all creation,
t3: Say: He will revive them Who produced them at the first, for He is Knower of every creation,

ar: ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّجَرِ ٱلْأَخْضَرِ نَارًۭا فَإِذَآ أَنتُم مِّنْهُ تُوقِدُونَ
en: ˹He is the One˺ Who gives you fire from green trees, and—behold!—you kindle ˹fire˺ from them.
t1: He Who produces fire for you out of the green tree so now you kindle fire with the same!
t2: who has made for you out of the green tree fire and lo, from it you kindle.’
t3: Who hath appointed for you fire from the green tree, and behold! ye kindle from it.

ar: أَوَلَيْسَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ بِقَٰدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُم ۚ بَلَىٰ وَهُوَ ٱلْخَلَّٰقُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
en: Can the One Who created the heavens and the earth not ˹easily˺ resurrect these ˹deniers˺?” Yes ˹He can˺! For He is the Master Creator, All-Knowing.
t1: And does He Who created the heavens and the earth not have the power to create the like of them (again)?’ Yes indeed! And He is the Supreme Creator, the All-Knowing.
t2: Is not He, who created the heavens and earth, able to create the like of them? Yes indeed; He is the All-creator, the All-knowing.
t3: Is not He Who created the heavens and the earth Able to create the like of them ? Aye, that He is! for He is the All-Wise Creator,

ar: إِنَّمَآ أَمْرُهُۥٓ إِذَآ أَرَادَ شَيْـًٔا أَن يَقُولَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
en: All it takes, when He wills something ˹to be˺, is simply to say to it: “Be!” And it is!
t1: His command (of creation) is only that when He intends (to create) something, He says to it: ‘Be,’ so it instantly becomes (existent or visible and continues becoming).
t2: His command, when He desires a thing, is to say to it ’Be,’ and it is.
t3: But His command, when He intendeth a thing, is only that He saith unto it: Be! and it is.

ar: فَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِى بِيَدِهِۦ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
en: So glory be to the One in Whose Hands is the authority over all things, and to Whom ˹alone˺ you will ˹all˺ be returned.
t1: So, Glory be to Him in Whose Hand (i.e., power and control) is the sovereignty over everything and to Him you will be returned.
t2: So glory be to Him, in whose hand is the dominion of everything, and unto whom you shall be returned.
t3: Therefor Glory be to Him in Whose hand is the dominion over all things! Unto Him ye will be brought back.

ar: وَٱلصَّٰٓفَّٰتِ صَفًّۭا
en: By those ˹angels˺ lined up in ranks,
t1: By the parties ranged in close ranks,
t2: By the rangers ranging
t3: By those who set the ranks in battle order

ar: فَٱلزَّٰجِرَٰتِ زَجْرًۭا
en: and those who diligently drive ˹the clouds˺,
t1: And by those who drive away the clouds or by those parties who severely reprimand evils,
t2: and the scarers scaring
t3: And those who drive away (the wicked) with reproof

ar: فَٱلتَّٰلِيَٰتِ ذِكْرًا
en: and those who recite the Reminder!
t1: Then by those parties that remember Allah (or) recite (the Holy Qur’an),
t2: and the reciters of a Remembrance,
t3: And those who read (the Word) for a reminder,

ar: إِنَّ إِلَٰهَكُمْ لَوَٰحِدٌۭ
en: Surely your God is One!
t1: Surely, your God is One,
t2: surely your God is One,
t3: Lo! thy Lord is surely One;

ar: رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَرَبُّ ٱلْمَشَٰرِقِ
en: ˹He is˺ the Lord of the heavens and the earth and everything in between, and the Lord of all points of sunrise.
t1: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever (creation) is between them, and the Lord of every point of sunrise.
t2: Lord of the heavens and the earth, and of what between them is Lord of the Easts.
t3: Lord of the heavens and of the earth and all that is between them, and Lord of the sun’s risings.

ar: إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِزِينَةٍ ٱلْكَوَاكِبِ
en: Indeed, We have adorned the lowest heaven with the stars for decoration
t1: Surely, We have adorned the world’s heaven (the first heavenly sphere) with the adornment of stars and planets,
t2: We have adorned the lower heaven with the adornment of the stars
t3: Lo! We have adorned the lowest heaven with an ornament, the planets;

ar: وَحِفْظًۭا مِّن كُلِّ شَيْطَٰنٍۢ مَّارِدٍۢ
en: and ˹for˺ protection from every rebellious devil.
t1: And made (them) secure from every rebellious satan.
t2: and to preserve against every rebel Satan;
t3: With security from every froward devil.

ar: لَّا يَسَّمَّعُونَ إِلَى ٱلْمَلَإِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ وَيُقْذَفُونَ مِن كُلِّ جَانِبٍۢ
en: They cannot listen to the highest assembly ˹of angels˺ for they are pelted from every side,
t1: They (satans) cannot listen to the celestial world. And (burning brands) are thrown on them from every side,
t2: they listen not to the High Council, for they are pelted from every side,
t3: They cannot listen to the Highest Chiefs for they are pelted from every side,

ar: دُحُورًۭا ۖ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌۭ وَاصِبٌ
en: ˹fiercely˺ driven away. And they will suffer an everlasting torment.
t1: To repulse them. And for them there is eternal torment.
t2: rejected, and theirs is an everlasting chastisement,
t3: Outcast, and theirs is a perpetual torment;

ar: إِلَّا مَنْ خَطِفَ ٱلْخَطْفَةَ فَأَتْبَعَهُۥ شِهَابٌۭ ثَاقِبٌۭ
en: But whoever manages to stealthily eavesdrop is ˹instantly˺ pursued by a piercing flare.
t1: But that (satan) who snatches away (something from angels), a burning brand follows it in chase.
t2: except such as snatches a fragment, and he is pursued by a piercing flame.
t3: Save him who snatcheth a fragment, and there pursueth him a piercing flame

ar: فَٱسْتَفْتِهِمْ أَهُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَم مَّنْ خَلَقْنَآ ۚ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰهُم مِّن طِينٍۢ لَّازِبٍۭ
en: So ask them ˹O Prophet˺, which is harder to create: them or other marvels of Our creation?
t1: Ask them: ‘Are they harder (and more difficult) to create, or those things which We have created (in the heavenly universe)? Surely, We have created them from a sticky clay.’
t2: So ask them for a pronouncement -- Are they stronger in constitution, or those We created? We created them of clinging clay.
t3: Then ask them (O Muhammad): Are they stronger as a creation, or those (others) whom we have created ? Lo! We created them of plastic clay.

ar: بَلْ عَجِبْتَ وَيَسْخَرُونَ
en: In fact, you are astonished ˹by their denial˺, while they ridicule ˹you˺.
t1: But you express your wonder whilst they make fun.
t2: Nay, thou marvellest; and they scoff
t3: Nay, but thou dost marvel when they mock

ar: وَإِذَا ذُكِّرُوا۟ لَا يَذْكُرُونَ
en: When they are reminded, they are never mindful.
t1: And when they are given advice, they do not accept it.
t2: and, when reminded, do not remember
t3: And heed not when they are reminded,

ar: وَإِذَا رَأَوْا۟ ءَايَةًۭ يَسْتَسْخِرُونَ
en: And whenever they see a sign, they make fun of it,
t1: And when they see some sign, they mock it,
t2: and, when they see a sign, would scoff;
t3: And seek to scoff when they behold a portent.

ar: وَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحْرٌۭ مُّبِينٌ
en: saying, “This is nothing but pure magic.
t1: And say: ‘This is but obvious magic.
t2: and they say, ’This is nothing but manifest sorcery.
t3: And they say: Lo! this is mere magic;

ar: أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًۭا وَعِظَٰمًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ
en: When we are dead and reduced to dust and bones, will we really be resurrected?
t1: What! When we are dead and turned to dust and bones, shall we certainly be raised (alive again)?
t2: What, when we are dead and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised up?
t3: When we are dead and have become dust and bones, shall we then, forsooth, be raised (again) ?

ar: أَوَءَابَآؤُنَا ٱلْأَوَّلُونَ
en: And our forefathers as well?”
t1: And shall our forefathers too (be raised)?’
t2: What, and our fathers, the ancients?’
t3: And our forefathers ?

ar: قُلْ نَعَمْ وَأَنتُمْ دَٰخِرُونَ
en: Say, “Yes! And you will be fully humbled.”
t1: Say: ‘Yes, (of course,) and you will be disgraced and humiliated (as well).’
t2: Say: ’Yes, and in all lowliness.’
t3: Say (O Muhammad): Ye, in truth; and ye will be brought low.

ar: فَإِنَّمَا هِىَ زَجْرَةٌۭ وَٰحِدَةٌۭ فَإِذَا هُمْ يَنظُرُونَ
en: It will only take one Blast, then at once they will see ˹it all˺.
t1: So, it will be merely a single dreadful shout (of a stern call). Then all will suddenly (rise and) begin to stare.
t2: For it is only a single scaring, then behold, they are watching
t3: There is but one Shout, and lo! they behold,

ar: وَقَالُوا۟ يَٰوَيْلَنَا هَٰذَا يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ
en: They will cry, “Oh, woe to us! This is the Day of Judgment!”
t1: And they will say: ‘Woe to us! This is the Day of Requital.’
t2: and they say, ’Woe, alas for us! This is the Day of Doom.’
t3: And say: Ah, woe for us! This is the Day of Judgment.

ar: هَٰذَا يَوْمُ ٱلْفَصْلِ ٱلَّذِى كُنتُم بِهِۦ تُكَذِّبُونَ
en: ˹They will be told,˺ “This is the Day of ˹Final˺ Decision which you used to deny.”
t1: (It will be said: ‘Yes,) this is the same Day of Judgment which you used to reject.
t2: ’This is the Day of Decision, even that you cried lies to.
t3: This is the Day of Separation, which ye used to deny.

ar: ۞ ٱحْشُرُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ وَأَزْوَٰجَهُمْ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْبُدُونَ
en: ˹Allah will say to the angels,˺ “Gather ˹all˺ the wrongdoers along with their peers, and whatever they used to worship
t1: Assemble all those who committed injustice as well as their companions and followers and those (false gods) that they used to worship,
t2: Muster those who did evil, their wives, and that they were serving,
t3: (And it is said unto the angels): Assemble those who did wrong, together with their wives and what they used to worship

ar: مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ فَٱهْدُوهُمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
en: instead of Allah, then lead them ˹all˺ to the path of Hell.
t1: Besides Allah. Then take them to the path of Hell.
t2: apart from God, and guide them unto the path of Hell!
t3: Instead of Allah, and lead them to the path to hell;

ar: وَقِفُوهُمْ ۖ إِنَّهُم مَّسْـُٔولُونَ
en: And detain them, for they must be questioned.”
t1: And halt them (near the passage); they shall be interrogated.’
t2: And halt them, to be questioned:
t3: And stop them, for they must be questioned.

ar: مَا لَكُمْ لَا تَنَاصَرُونَ
en: ˹Then they will be asked,˺ “What is the matter with you that you can no longer help each other?”
t1: (It will be said to them:) ‘What has happened to you that you do not help one another?’
t2: "Why help you not one another?"
t3: What aileth you that ye help not one another ?

ar: بَلْ هُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ مُسْتَسْلِمُونَ
en: In fact, on that Day they will be ˹fully˺ submissive.
t1: (What help can they provide?) For, in truth, they will be standing bending their necks Today.
t2: No indeed; but today they resign themselves in submission
t3: Nay, but this day they make full submission.

ar: وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍۢ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
en: They will turn on each other, throwing blame.
t1: And turning to one another, they will mutually question.
t2: and advance one upon another, asking each other questions.
t3: And some of them draw near unto others, mutually questioning.

ar: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّكُمْ كُنتُمْ تَأْتُونَنَا عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ
en: The misled will say, “It was you who deluded us away from what is right.”
t1: They will say: ‘Surely, it is you who used to come to us from the right side (i.e., asserting on oath of being right).’
t2: These say, ’Why, you of old would come to us from the right hand.’
t3: They say: Lo! ye used to come unto us, imposing, (swearing that ye spoke the truth).

ar: قَالُوا۟ بَل لَّمْ تَكُونُوا۟ مُؤْمِنِينَ
en: The misleaders will reply, “No! You disbelieved on your own.
t1: (Their misleading leaders) will say: ‘The truth is that it was you yourselves who did not believe.
t2: Those say, ’No; on the contrary, you were not believers;
t3: They answer: Nay, but ye (yourselves) were not believers.

ar: وَمَا كَانَ لَنَا عَلَيْكُم مِّن سُلْطَٰنٍۭ ۖ بَلْ كُنتُمْ قَوْمًۭا طَٰغِينَ
en: We had no authority over you. In fact, you yourselves were a transgressing people.
t1: Nor did we have any authority (and control) over you. But you yourselves were a rebellious people.
t2: we had no authority over you; no, you were an insolent people.
t3: We had no power over you, but ye were wayward folk.

ar: فَحَقَّ عَلَيْنَا قَوْلُ رَبِّنَآ ۖ إِنَّا لَذَآئِقُونَ
en: The decree of our Lord has come to pass against us ˹all˺: we will certainly taste ˹the punishment˺.
t1: So the command of our Lord has been proved against us. (Now) we are about to taste (the torment).
t2: So our Lord’s Word is realised against us; we are tasting it.
t3: Now the Word of our Lord hath been fulfilled concerning us. Lo! we are about to taste (the doom).

ar: فَأَغْوَيْنَٰكُمْ إِنَّا كُنَّا غَٰوِينَ
en: We caused you to deviate, for we ourselves were deviant.”
t1: So we led you astray. Surely, we ourselves had gone astray.’
t2: Therefore we perverted you, and we ourselves were perverts.’
t3: Thus we misled you. Lo! we were (ourselves) astray.

ar: فَإِنَّهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ فِى ٱلْعَذَابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ
en: Surely on that Day they will ˹all˺ share in the punishment.
t1: So on that Day, they (all) will share the torment.
t2: So all of them on that day are sharers in the chastisement.
t3: Then lo! this day they (both) are sharers in the doom.

ar: إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَفْعَلُ بِٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
en: That is certainly how We deal with the wicked.
t1: No doubt, this is how We deal with the sinners.
t2: Even so We do with the sinners;
t3: Lo! thus deal We with the guilty.

ar: إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوٓا۟ إِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ
en: For whenever it was said to them ˹in the world˺, “There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Allah,” they acted arrogantly
t1: Surely, they were such people that when it was said to them: ‘There is none worthy of worship except Allah,’ they used to show arrogance,
t2: for when it was said to them, ’There is no god but God,’ they were ever waxing proud,
t3: For when it was said unto them, There is no God save Allah, they were scornful

ar: وَيَقُولُونَ أَئِنَّا لَتَارِكُوٓا۟ ءَالِهَتِنَا لِشَاعِرٍۢ مَّجْنُونٍۭ
en: and argued, “Should we really abandon our gods for a mad poet?”
t1: And used to say: ‘Are we going to forsake our gods for the sake of an insane poet?’
t2: saying, ’What, shall we forsake our gods for a poet possessed?’
t3: And said: Shall we forsake our gods for a mad poet ?

ar: بَلْ جَآءَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَصَدَّقَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
en: In fact, he came with the truth, confirming ˹earlier˺ messengers.
t1: (He is neither an insane person nor a poet.) He has rather brought the truth (Din [Religion]) and confirmed the Messengers (of Allah).
t2: ’No indeed; but he brought the truth, and confirmed the Envoys.
t3: Nay, but he brought the Truth, and he confirmed those sent (before him).

ar: إِنَّكُمْ لَذَآئِقُوا۟ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْأَلِيمِ
en: You will certainly taste the painful torment,
t1: Verily, you are about to taste the painful torment.
t2: Now certainly you shall be tasting the painful chastisement,
t3: Lo! (now) verily ye taste the painful doom -

ar: وَمَا تُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
en: and will only be rewarded for what you used to do.
t1: And you will not be given (any) reward but for what you used to do.
t2: and not be recompensed, except according to what you were doing.’
t3: Ye are requited naught save what ye did -

ar: إِلَّا عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
en: But not the chosen servants of Allah.
t1: (Yes,) but those (exalted and chosen) servants of Allah who have divested themselves of (their ill-commanding selves and its pursuits),
t2: Except for God’s sincere servants;
t3: Save single-minded slaves of Allah;

ar: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمْ رِزْقٌۭ مَّعْلُومٌۭ
en: They will have a known provision:
t1: It is they for whom a special provision is appointed (morning and evening),
t2: for them awaits a known provision,
t3: For them there is a known provision,

ar: فَوَٰكِهُ ۖ وَهُم مُّكْرَمُونَ
en: fruits ˹of every type˺. And they will be honoured
t1: Fruits (of every kind). And they will be honoured and venerated,
t2: fruits -- and they high-honoured
t3: Fruits. And they will be honoured

ar: فِى جَنَّٰتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
en: in the Gardens of Bliss,
t1: (Abiding) in Gardens of bliss and bounty,
t2: in the Gardens of Bliss
t3: In the Gardens of delight,

ar: عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍۢ مُّتَقَٰبِلِينَ
en: facing each other on thrones.
t1: (Making spiritual disclosures) face to face on raised couches.
t2: upon couches, set face to face,
t3: On couches facing one another;

ar: يُطَافُ عَلَيْهِم بِكَأْسٍۢ مِّن مَّعِينٍۭ
en: A drink ˹of pure wine˺ will be passed around to them from a flowing stream:
t1: Round them will be passed cups of (sacred) overflowing drink.
t2: cup from a spring being passed round to them,
t3: A cup from a gushing spring is brought round for them,

ar: بَيْضَآءَ لَذَّةٍۢ لِّلشَّٰرِبِينَ
en: crystal-white, delicious to drink.
t1: It will be sparkling white and superbly delicious, a treat for those who drink.
t2: white, a delight to the drinkers,
t3: White, delicious to the drinkers,

ar: لَا فِيهَا غَوْلٌۭ وَلَا هُمْ عَنْهَا يُنزَفُونَ
en: It will neither harm ˹them˺, nor will they be intoxicated by it.
t1: It will not cause any harm or giddiness; nor will they lose balance (after drinking it).
t2: wherein no sickness is, neither intoxication;
t3: Wherein there is no headache nor are they made mad thereby.

ar: وَعِندَهُمْ قَٰصِرَٰتُ ٱلطَّرْفِ عِينٌۭ
en: And with them will be maidens of modest gaze and gorgeous eyes,
t1: And beside them will be (sitting chaste women) with lowered gazes and wide beautiful eyes,
t2: and with them wide-eyed maidens restraining their glances
t3: And with them are those of modest gaze, with lovely eyes,

ar: كَأَنَّهُنَّ بَيْضٌۭ مَّكْنُونٌۭ
en: as if they were pristine pearls.
t1: (Fair, charming complexion, they will look) as if they were eggs protected from dust.
t2: as if they were hidden pearls.
t3: (Pure) as they were hidden eggs (of the ostrich).

ar: فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍۢ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
en: Then they will turn to one another inquisitively.
t1: Then those (residents of Paradise) will turn to one another and mutually inquire (about their well-being).
t2: They advance one upon another, asking each other questions.
t3: And some of them draw near unto others, mutually questioning.

ar: قَالَ قَآئِلٌۭ مِّنْهُمْ إِنِّى كَانَ لِى قَرِينٌۭ
en: One of them will say, “I once had a companion ˹in the world˺
t1: One (of the participants in conversation) will say (to the other): ‘There was an acquaintance of mine (who disbelieved in the Hereafter).
t2: One of them says, ’I had a comrade
t3: A speaker of them saith: Lo! I had a comrade

ar: يَقُولُ أَءِنَّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُصَدِّقِينَ
en: who used to ask ˹me˺, ‘Do you actually believe ˹in resurrection˺?
t1: He used to say (to me): Are you (also) of those who confirm and firmly believe (in these things)?
t2: who would say, "Are you a confirmer?
t3: Who used to say: Art thou in truth of those who put faith (in his words) ?

ar: أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًۭا وَعِظَٰمًا أَءِنَّا لَمَدِينُونَ
en: When we are dead and reduced to dust and bones, will we really be brought to judgment?’”
t1: (That) when we are dead and have become dust and bones, so shall we be requited (in that condition)?’
t2: What, when we are dead and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be requited?"
t3: Can we, when we are dead and have become mere dust and bones - can we (then) verily be brought to book ?

ar: قَالَ هَلْ أَنتُم مُّطَّلِعُونَ
en: He will ˹then˺ ask, “Would you care to see ˹his fate˺?”
t1: Then he (the dweller of Paradise) will say: ‘Will you peer down to see (him in which plight he is)?’
t2: He says, ’Are you looking down?’
t3: He saith: Will ye look ?

ar: فَٱطَّلَعَ فَرَءَاهُ فِى سَوَآءِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
en: Then he ˹and the others˺ will look and spot him in the midst of the Hellfire.
t1: Then on peering down, he will find him (right) in the middle of Hell.
t2: Then he looks, and sees him in the midst of Hell.
t3: Then looketh he and seeth him in the depth of hell.

ar: قَالَ تَٱللَّهِ إِن كِدتَّ لَتُرْدِينِ
en: He will ˹then˺ say, “By Allah! You nearly ruined me.
t1: (He) will say (to him): ‘By my Lord, you had nearly ruined me.
t2: He says, ’By God, wellnigh thou didst destroy me;
t3: He saith: By Allah, thou verily didst all but cause my ruin,

ar: وَلَوْلَا نِعْمَةُ رَبِّى لَكُنتُ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْضَرِينَ
en: Had it not been for the grace of my Lord, I ˹too˺ would have certainly been among those brought ˹to Hell˺.”
t1: And had it not been the favour of my Lord, I (too) would have joined those who are brought (for torment with you).’
t2: But for my Lord’s blessing, I were one of the arraigned.
t3: And had it not been for the favour of my Lord, I too had been of those haled forth (to doom).

ar: أَفَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَيِّتِينَ
en: ˹Then he will ask his fellow believers,˺ “Can you imagine that we will never die,
t1: So (the dwellers of Paradise will gladly ask:) ‘Shall we not die now?
t2: What, do we then not die
t3: Are we then not to die

ar: إِلَّا مَوْتَتَنَا ٱلْأُولَىٰ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ
en: except our first death, nor be punished ˹like the others˺?”
t1: Except for the first death (which we have passed through and have reached here) and shall we not be ever tormented?’
t2: except for our first death, and are we not chastised?
t3: Saving our former death, and are we not to be punished ?

ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
en: This is truly the ultimate triumph.
t1: This is surely the supreme success.
t2: This is indeed the mighty triumph,
t3: Lo! this is the supreme triumph.

ar: لِمِثْلِ هَٰذَا فَلْيَعْمَلِ ٱلْعَٰمِلُونَ
en: For such ˹honour˺ all should strive.
t1: For such (a success) the doers should do work.
t2: for the like of this let the workers work.’
t3: For the like of this, then, let the workers work.

ar: أَذَٰلِكَ خَيْرٌۭ نُّزُلًا أَمْ شَجَرَةُ ٱلزَّقُّومِ
en: Is this ˹bliss˺ a better accommodation or the tree of Zaqqûm?
t1: Is the hospitality (of Paradise) better or the tree of Zaqqum?
t2: Is that better as a hospitality, or the Tree of Ez-Zakkoum?
t3: Is this better as a welcome, or the tree of Zaqqum ?

ar: إِنَّا جَعَلْنَٰهَا فِتْنَةًۭ لِّلظَّٰلِمِينَ
en: We have surely made it a test for the wrongdoers.
t1: Undoubtedly, We have made this (tree) a torment for the wrongdoers.
t2: We have appointed it as a trial for the evildoers.
t3: Lo! We have appointed it a torment for wrong-doers.

ar: إِنَّهَا شَجَرَةٌۭ تَخْرُجُ فِىٓ أَصْلِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
en: Indeed, it is a tree that grows in the depths of Hell,
t1: Truly, this is a tree that springs out from the bottom of Hell.
t2: It is a tree that comes forth in the root of Hell;
t3: Lo! it is a tree that springeth in the heart of hell.

ar: طَلْعُهَا كَأَنَّهُۥ رُءُوسُ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينِ
en: bearing fruit like devils’ heads.
t1: The spikes of its fruit are as if heads of (ugly) satans.
t2: its spathes are as the heads of Satans,
t3: Its crop is as it were the heads of devils

ar: فَإِنَّهُمْ لَءَاكِلُونَ مِنْهَا فَمَالِـُٔونَ مِنْهَا ٱلْبُطُونَ
en: The evildoers will certainly ˹be left to˺ eat from it, filling up their bellies with it.
t1: So the inmates of Hell have to eat of it alone and have to fill their bellies with the same.
t2: and they eat of it, and of it fill their bellies,
t3: And lo! they verily must eat thereof, and fill (their) bellies therewith.

ar: ثُمَّ إِنَّ لَهُمْ عَلَيْهَا لَشَوْبًۭا مِّنْ حَمِيمٍۢ
en: Then on top of that they will be given a blend of boiling drink.
t1: Then for sure there will be scalding water mixed (with pus) for them after (eating, which will cut through their guts).
t2: then on top of it they have a brew of boiling water,
t3: And afterward, lo! thereupon they have a drink of boiling water

ar: ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَرْجِعَهُمْ لَإِلَى ٱلْجَحِيمِ
en: Then they will ultimately return to ˹their place in˺ Hell.
t1: Then (after eating) surely they will return to Hell (again).
t2: then their return is unto Hell.
t3: And afterward, lo! their return is surely unto hell.

ar: إِنَّهُمْ أَلْفَوْا۟ ءَابَآءَهُمْ ضَآلِّينَ
en: Indeed, they found their forefathers astray,
t1: Surely, they found their ancestors misguided.
t2: They found their fathers erring,
t3: They indeed found their fathers astray,

ar: فَهُمْ عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِمْ يُهْرَعُونَ
en: so they rushed in their footsteps!
t1: So they are made to rush on in their footsteps.
t2: and they run in their footsteps.
t3: But they make haste (to follow) in their footsteps.

ar: وَلَقَدْ ضَلَّ قَبْلَهُمْ أَكْثَرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
en: And surely most of the earlier generations had strayed before them,
t1: And in fact, most of the former people (also) lost the straight path.
t2: Before them erred most of the ancients,
t3: And verily most of the men of old went astray before them,

ar: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا فِيهِم مُّنذِرِينَ
en: although We had certainly sent warners among them.
t1: And surely, We sent the Warners amongst them as well.
t2: and We sent among them warners;
t3: And verily We sent among them warners.

ar: فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
en: See then what was the end of those who had been warned.
t1: So see how was the end of those who were warned,
t2: and behold, how was the end of them that were warned,
t3: Then see the nature of the consequence for those warned,

ar: إِلَّا عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
en: But not the chosen servants of Allah.
t1: Except for the chosen and exalted servants of Allah.
t2: except for God’s sincere servants.
t3: Save single-minded slaves of Allah.

ar: وَلَقَدْ نَادَىٰنَا نُوحٌۭ فَلَنِعْمَ ٱلْمُجِيبُونَ
en: Indeed, Noah cried out to Us, and how excellent are We in responding!
t1: And, verily, Nuh (Noah) cried to Us. So how excellent We are to respond to the prayers!
t2: Noah called to Us; and how excellent were the Answerers!
t3: And Noah verily prayed unto Us, and gracious was the Hearer of his prayer

ar: وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
en: We delivered him and his family from the great distress,
t1: And We delivered him and his family from the ordeal.
t2: And We delivered him and his people from the great distress,
t3: And We saved him and his household from the great distress,

ar: وَجَعَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُۥ هُمُ ٱلْبَاقِينَ
en: and made his descendants the sole survivors.
t1: And We made his offspring the only survivors.
t2: and We made his seed the survivors,
t3: And made his seed the survivors,

ar: وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
en: And We blessed him ˹with honourable mention˺ among later generations:
t1: And We made his virtuous remembrance endure amongst the successors (i.e., the Messengers and their people).
t2: and left for him among the later folk
t3: And left for him among the later folk (the salutation):

ar: سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ نُوحٍۢ فِى ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: “Peace be upon Noah among all peoples.”
t1: Peace be on Nuh (Noah) in all the worlds!
t2: ’Peace be upon Noah among all beings!’
t3: Peace be unto Noah among the peoples!

ar: إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
en: Indeed, this is how We reward the good-doers.
t1: Surely, We requite the pious the same way.
t2: Even so We recompense the good-doers;
t3: Lo! thus do We reward the good.

ar: إِنَّهُۥ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
en: ˹For˺ he was truly one of Our faithful servants.
t1: He was indeed of Our servants blessed with (perfect) faith.
t2: he was among Our believing servants.
t3: Lo! he is one of Our believing slaves.

ar: ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ
en: Then We drowned the others.
t1: Then We drowned the others.
t2: Then afterwards We drowned the rest.
t3: Then We did drown the others.

ar: ۞ وَإِنَّ مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ لَإِبْرَٰهِيمَ
en: And indeed, one of those who followed his way was Abraham.
t1: And verily, of his party was Ibrahim ([Abraham] as well, on him be peace).
t2: Of his party was also Abraham;
t3: And lo! of his persuasion verily was Abraham

ar: إِذْ جَآءَ رَبَّهُۥ بِقَلْبٍۢ سَلِيمٍ
en: ˹Remember˺ when he came to his Lord with a pure heart,
t1: When he appeared before his Lord with a purified and submissive heart,
t2: when he came unto his Lord with a pure heart,
t3: When he came unto his Lord with a whole heart;

ar: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَاذَا تَعْبُدُونَ
en: and said to his father and his people, “What are you worshipping?
t1: He said to his father (who was in fact his uncle, and he used to call him father, for he had brought him up) and his people: ‘What is it that you worship?
t2: when he said to his father and his folk, ’What do you serve?
t3: When he said unto his father and his folk: What is it that ye worship ?

ar: أَئِفْكًا ءَالِهَةًۭ دُونَ ٱللَّهِ تُرِيدُونَ
en: Is it false gods that you desire instead of Allah?
t1: Do you go for false gods besides Allah, inventing a false allegation?
t2: Is it a calumny, gods apart from God, that you desire?
t3: Is it a falsehood - gods beside Allah - that ye desire ?

ar: فَمَا ظَنُّكُم بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: What then do you expect from the Lord of all worlds?”
t1: Well! What do you think of the Lord of all the worlds?’
t2: What think you then of the Lord of all Being?’
t3: What then is your opinion of the Lord of the Worlds ?

ar: فَنَظَرَ نَظْرَةًۭ فِى ٱلنُّجُومِ
en: He later looked up to the stars ˹in contemplation˺,
t1: Then Ibrahim (Abraham) cast a look at the stars (to put them in doubt),
t2: And he cast a glance at the stars,
t3: And he glanced a glance at the stars

ar: فَقَالَ إِنِّى سَقِيمٌۭ
en: then said, “I am really sick.”
t1: And said: ‘I am not well (so cannot accompany you to the festival).’
t2: and he said, ’Surely I am sick.’
t3: Then said: Lo! I feel sick!

ar: فَتَوَلَّوْا۟ عَنْهُ مُدْبِرِينَ
en: So they turned their backs on him and went away.
t1: At that they turned their backs on him and left (for the festival).
t2: But they went away from him, turning their backs.
t3: And they turned their backs and went away from him.

ar: فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ ءَالِهَتِهِمْ فَقَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ
en: Then he ˹stealthily˺ advanced towards their gods, and said ˹mockingly˺, “Will you not eat ˹your offerings˺?
t1: Then Ibrahim (Abraham) went up to their gods (idols) quietly and said to them: ‘Do you not eat?
t2: Then he turned to their gods, and said, ’What do you eat?
t3: Then turned he to their gods and said: Will ye not eat ?

ar: مَا لَكُمْ لَا تَنطِقُونَ
en: What is wrong with you that you cannot speak?”
t1: What is the matter with you that you do not speak?’
t2: What ails you, that you speak not?’
t3: What aileth you that ye speak not ?

ar: فَرَاغَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضَرْبًۢا بِٱلْيَمِينِ
en: Then he swiftly turned on them, striking ˹them˺ with his right hand.
t1: Then Ibrahim (Abraham) began striking (and breaking) them with full force.
t2: And he turned upon them smiting them with his right hand.
t3: Then he attacked them, striking with his right hand.

ar: فَأَقْبَلُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِ يَزِفُّونَ
en: Later, his people came rushing towards him ˹furiously˺.
t1: Then the people came to him running (on returning from the festival).
t2: Then came the others to him hastening.
t3: And (his people) came toward him, hastening.

ar: قَالَ أَتَعْبُدُونَ مَا تَنْحِتُونَ
en: He argued, “How can you worship what you carve ˹with your own hands˺,
t1: Ibrahim (Abraham) said (to them): ‘Do you worship these (inanimate stones) which you yourselves carve out,
t2: He said, ’Do you serve what you hew,
t3: He said: Worship ye that which ye yourselves do carve

ar: وَٱللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
en: when it is Allah Who created you and whatever you do?”
t1: Whilst Allah has created you and (all) your doings?’
t2: and God created you and what you make?’
t3: When Allah hath created you and what ye make ?

ar: قَالُوا۟ ٱبْنُوا۟ لَهُۥ بُنْيَٰنًۭا فَأَلْقُوهُ فِى ٱلْجَحِيمِ
en: They said ˹to one another˺, “Build him a furnace and cast him into the blazing fire.”
t1: They said: ‘Raise for him a building (to burn him), then cast him into the blazing fire (in it).’
t2: They said, ’Build him a building, and cast him into the furnace!’
t3: They said: Build for him a building and fling him in the red- hotfire.

ar: فَأَرَادُوا۟ بِهِۦ كَيْدًۭا فَجَعَلْنَٰهُمُ ٱلْأَسْفَلِينَ
en: And so they sought to harm him, but We made them inferior.
t1: So they attempted to play a trick against Ibrahim (Abraham), but We humiliated them (when the fire eventually turned into a flower garden).
t2: They desired to outwit him; so We made them the lower ones.
t3: And they designed a snare for him, but We made them the undermost.

ar: وَقَالَ إِنِّى ذَاهِبٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ
en: He later said, “I am leaving ˹in obedience˺ to my Lord. He will guide me.
t1: Then Ibrahim (Abraham) said: ‘(Migrating,) I am going to my Lord. He will certainly guide me.’ (He migrated to Syria).
t2: He said, ’I am going to my Lord; He will guide me.
t3: And he said: Lo! I am going unto my Lord Who will guide me.

ar: رَبِّ هَبْ لِى مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
en: My Lord! Bless me with righteous offspring.”
t1: (Reaching the sacred land, he prayed:) ‘O my Lord, bless me with (a son,) one of the pious.’
t2: My Lord, give me one of the righteous.’
t3: My Lord! Vouchsafe me of the righteous.

ar: فَبَشَّرْنَٰهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ حَلِيمٍۢ
en: So We gave him good news of a forbearing son.
t1: So We gave him the good news of a very forbearing son (Isma‘il [Ishmael]).
t2: Then We gave him the good tidings of a prudent boy;
t3: So We gave him tidings of a gentle son.

ar: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعْىَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ فِى ٱلْمَنَامِ أَنِّىٓ أَذْبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ ۚ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ ۖ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
en: Then when the boy reached the age to work with him, Abraham said, “O my dear son! I have seen in a dream that I ˹must˺ sacrifice you. So tell me what you think.” He replied, “O my dear father! Do as you are commanded. Allah willing, you will find me steadfast.”
t1: Then when (Isma‘il [Ishmael]) reached (the age of) the ability to run about with him, Ibrahim (Abraham) said: ‘O my son, I have seen in a dream that I am sacrificing you. So think, what is your opinion?’ Isma‘il (Ishmael) said: ‘O my father, do that (immediately) which you are being commanded. If Allah wills, you will find me amongst the patient (and steadfast).’
t2: and when he had reached the age of running with him, he said, ’My son, I see in a dream that I shall sacrifice thee; consider, what thinkest thou?’ He said, ’My father, do as thou art bidden; thou shalt find me, God willing, one of the steadfast.’
t3: And when (his son) was old enough to walk with him, (Abraham) said: O my dear son, I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice thee. So look, what thinkest thou ? He said: O my father! Do that which thou art commanded. Allah willing, thou shalt find me of the steadfast.

ar: فَلَمَّآ أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُۥ لِلْجَبِينِ
en: Then when they submitted ˹to Allah’s Will˺, and Abraham laid him on the side of his forehead ˹for sacrifice˺,
t1: So when both submitted (to the will of Allah i.e., both surrendered to Allah’s command), and Ibrahim (Abraham) laid him down on his forehead—(the subsequent sight has not been described;)
t2: When they had surrendered, and he flung him upon his brow,
t3: Then, when they had both surrendered (to Allah), and he had flung him down upon his face,

ar: وَنَٰدَيْنَٰهُ أَن يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ
en: We called out to him, “O Abraham!
t1: And We called out to him: ‘O Ibrahim (Abraham)!
t2: We called unto him, ’Abraham,
t3: We called unto him: O Abraham!

ar: قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ ٱلرُّءْيَآ ۚ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
en: You have already fulfilled the vision.” Indeed, this is how We reward the good-doers.
t1: (How wonderfully) have you made your dream really true!’ Surely, We pay back the spiritually excellent the same way. (So you are blessed with the prominence of Our closest friend.)
t2: thou hast confirmed the vision; even so We recompense the good-doers.
t3: Thou hast already fulfilled the vision. Lo! thus do We reward the good.

ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْبَلَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلْمُبِينُ
en: That was truly a revealing test.
t1: It was by far a great open trial.
t2: This is indeed the manifest trial.’
t3: Lo! that verily was a clear test.

ar: وَفَدَيْنَٰهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍۢ
en: And We ransomed his son with a great sacrifice,
t1: And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.
t2: And We ransomed him with a mighty sacrifice,
t3: Then We ransomed him with a tremendous victim.

ar: وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
en: and blessed Abraham ˹with honourable mention˺ among later generations:
t1: And We preserved his virtuous remembrance (i.e., praise) amongst the succeeding generations.
t2: and left for him among the later folk
t3: And We left for him among the later folk (the salutation):

ar: سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
en: “Peace be upon Abraham.”
t1: Peace be upon Ibrahim (Abraham)!
t2: ’Peace be upon Abraham!’
t3: Peace be unto Abraham!

ar: كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
en: This is how We reward the good-doers.
t1: That is how We pay back those who are committed to spiritual excellence.
t2: Even so We recompense the good-doers;
t3: Thus do We reward the good.

ar: إِنَّهُۥ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
en: He was truly one of Our faithful servants.
t1: Surely, he was of Our servants with (perfect faith).
t2: he was among Our believing servants.
t3: Lo! he is one of Our believing slaves.

ar: وَبَشَّرْنَٰهُ بِإِسْحَٰقَ نَبِيًّۭا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
en: We ˹later˺ gave him good news of Isaac—a prophet, and one of the righteous.
t1: And (after Isma‘il [Ishmael]) We gave him the good news of Ishaq (Isaac). He was (also) a Prophet, one of the most pious.
t2: Then We gave him the good tidings of Isaac, a Prophet, one of the righteous.
t3: And we gave him tidings of the birth of Isaac, a prophet of the righteous.

ar: وَبَٰرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَىٰٓ إِسْحَٰقَ ۚ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا مُحْسِنٌۭ وَظَالِمٌۭ لِّنَفْسِهِۦ مُبِينٌۭ
en: We blessed him and Isaac as well. Some of their descendants did good, while others clearly wronged themselves.
t1: And We bestowed blessings on him and on Ishaq (Isaac). And amongst their descendants are both the virtuous as well as those who expressly wrong themselves.
t2: And We blessed him, and Isaac; and of their seed some are good-doers, and some manifest self-wrongers.
t3: And We blessed him and Isaac. And of their seed are some who do good, and some who plainly wrong themselves.

ar: وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ
en: And We certainly showed favour to Moses and Aaron,
t1: And surely, We blessed Musa (Moses) and Harun (Aaron) as well with Our favours.
t2: We also favoured Moses and Aaron,
t3: And We verily gave grace unto Moses and Aaron,

ar: وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُمَا وَقَوْمَهُمَا مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
en: and delivered them and their people from the great distress.
t1: And We delivered them and their people from the ordeal.
t2: and We delivered them and their people from the great distress.
t3: And saved them and their people from the great distress,

ar: وَنَصَرْنَٰهُمْ فَكَانُوا۟ هُمُ ٱلْغَٰلِبِينَ
en: We helped them so it was they who prevailed.
t1: And We helped them, so it was they who overmastered.
t2: And We helped them, so that they were the victors;
t3: And helped them so that they became the victors.

ar: وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُمَا ٱلْكِتَٰبَ ٱلْمُسْتَبِينَ
en: We gave them the clear Scripture,
t1: And We gave both of them the clear and enlightening Book (the Torah).
t2: and We gave them the Manifesting Book,
t3: And We gave them the clear Scripture

ar: وَهَدَيْنَٰهُمَا ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ
en: and guided them to the Straight Path.
t1: And We guided them both to the straight path.
t2: and guided them in the straight path,
t3: And showed them the right path.

ar: وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِمَا فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
en: And We blessed them ˹with honourable mention˺ among later generations:
t1: And We preserved their virtuous remembrance (also) amongst the succeeding generations.
t2: and left for them among the later folk
t3: And We left for them among the later folk (the salutation):

ar: سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ
en: “Peace be upon Moses and Aaron.”
t1: Peace be upon Musa (Moses) and Harun (Aaron)!
t2: ’Peace be upon Moses and, Aaron!’
t3: Peace be unto Moses and Aaron!

ar: إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
en: Indeed, this is how We reward the good-doers.
t1: That is how We pay back those who are committed to spiritual excellence.
t2: Even so We recompense the good-doers;
t3: Lo! thus do We reward the good.

ar: إِنَّهُمَا مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
en: They were truly ˹two˺ of Our faithful servants.
t1: Surely, both of them were of Our servants blessed with (perfect faith).
t2: they were among Our believing servants.
t3: Lo! they are two of Our believing slaves.

ar: وَإِنَّ إِلْيَاسَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
en: And Elias was indeed one of the messengers.
t1: And indeed, Ilyas (Elias too) was one of the Messengers.
t2: Elias too was one of the Envoys;
t3: And lo! Elias was of those sent (to warn),

ar: إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِۦٓ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
en: ˹Remember˺ when he said to his people, “Will you not fear ˹Allah˺?
t1: When he said to his people: ‘Do you not fear (Allah)?
t2: when he said to his people, ’Will you not be godfearing?
