t3: When he said unto his folk: Will ye not ward off (evil) ?

ar: أَتَدْعُونَ بَعْلًۭا وَتَذَرُونَ أَحْسَنَ ٱلْخَٰلِقِينَ
en: Do you call upon ˹the idol of˺ Ba’l and abandon the Best of Creators—
t1: Do you worship (the idol named) Ba‘l and turn away from the Best of creators,
t2: Do you call on Baal, and abandon the Best of creators?
t3: Will ye cry unto Baal and forsake the Best of creators,

ar: ٱللَّهَ رَبَّكُمْ وَرَبَّ ءَابَآئِكُمُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
en: Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers?”
t1: Allah, Who is your Lord and the Lord of your foregoing ancestors (as well)?’
t2: God, your Lord, and the Lord of your fathers, the ancients?’
t3: Allah, your Lord and Lord of your forefathers ?

ar: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَإِنَّهُمْ لَمُحْضَرُونَ
en: But they rejected him, so they will certainly be brought ˹for punishment˺.
t1: But they (the people of Ba‘lbek) gave lie to Ilyas (Elias), so they will (also) be brought (to the torment of Hell),
t2: But they cried him lies; so they will be among the arraigned,
t3: But they denied him, so they surely will be haled forth (to the doom)

ar: إِلَّا عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
en: But not the chosen servants of Allah.
t1: Except the chosen servants of Allah.
t2: except for God’s sincere servants;
t3: Save single-minded slaves of Allah.

ar: وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
en: We blessed him ˹with honourable mention˺ among later generations:
t1: And We preserved his virtuous remembrance (also) amongst the succeeding generations.
t2: and We left for him among the later folk
t3: And we left for him among the later folk (the salutation):

ar: سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰٓ إِلْ يَاسِينَ
en: “Peace be upon Elias.”
t1: Peace be upon Ilyas (Elias)!
t2: ’Peace be upon Elias!’
t3: Peace be unto Elias!

ar: إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
en: Indeed, this is how We reward the good-doers.
t1: That is how We pay back those who are committed to spiritual excellence.
t2: Even so We recompense the good-doers;
t3: Lo! thus do We reward the good.

ar: إِنَّهُۥ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
en: He was truly one of Our faithful servants.
t1: Surely, he was of Our servants blessed with (perfect faith).
t2: he was among Our believing servants.
t3: Lo! he is one of our believing slaves.

ar: وَإِنَّ لُوطًۭا لَّمِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
en: And Lot was indeed one of the messengers.
t1: And verily, Lut (Lot too) was one of the Messengers.
t2: Lot too was one of the Envoys;
t3: And lo! Lot verily was of those sent (to warn).

ar: إِذْ نَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ أَجْمَعِينَ
en: ˹Remember˺ when We delivered him and all of his family,
t1: When We delivered him and the whole of his family,
t2: when We delivered him and his people all together,
t3: When We saved him and his household, every one,

ar: إِلَّا عَجُوزًۭا فِى ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ
en: except an old woman, who was one of the doomed.
t1: Except that old woman who was of those who stayed behind;
t2: save an old woman among those that tarried;
t3: Save an old woman among those who stayed behind;

ar: ثُمَّ دَمَّرْنَا ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ
en: Then We ˹utterly˺ destroyed the rest.
t1: Then We destroyed the others.
t2: then We destroyed the others,
t3: Then We destroyed the others.

ar: وَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهِم مُّصْبِحِينَ
en: You ˹Meccans˺ certainly pass by their ruins day
t1: And surely, you pass by (the remains of their ruined towns whilst going from Mecca to Syria) in the morning,
t2: and you pass by them in the morning
t3: And lo! ye verily pass by (the ruin of) them in the morning

ar: وَبِٱلَّيْلِ ۗ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
en: and night. Will you not then understand?
t1: And at night as well. Do you not even then understand?
t2: and in the night; will you not understand?
t3: And at night-time; have ye then no sense ?

ar: وَإِنَّ يُونُسَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
en: And Jonah was indeed one of the messengers.
t1: And Yunus (Jonah too) was indeed one of the Messengers,
t2: Jonah too was one of the Envoys;
t3: And lo! Jonah verily was of those sent (to warn)

ar: إِذْ أَبَقَ إِلَى ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ
en: ˹Remember˺ when he fled to the overloaded ship.
t1: When he ran towards the full boat.
t2: when he ran away to the laden ship
t3: When he fled unto the laden ship,

ar: فَسَاهَمَ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُدْحَضِينَ
en: Then ˹to save it from sinking,˺ he drew straws ˹with other passengers˺. He lost ˹and was thrown overboard˺.
t1: Then (when it was caught into a whirlpool) they cast lots, and (in the draws) he came to be the loser (i.e., his name was drawn and those in the boat cast him overboard into the river).
t2: and cast lots, and was of the rebutted,
t3: And then drew lots and was of those rejected;

ar: فَٱلْتَقَمَهُ ٱلْحُوتُ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌۭ
en: Then the whale engulfed him while he was blameworthy.
t1: Then the fish swallowed him and he was a (self-condemning) repentant.
t2: then the whale swallowed him down, and he blameworthy.
t3: And the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy;

ar: فَلَوْلَآ أَنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسَبِّحِينَ
en: Had he not ˹constantly˺ glorified ˹Allah˺,
t1: Then if he had not been of those who glorify (Allah),
t2: Now had he not been of those that glorify God,
t3: And had he not been one of those who glorify (Allah)

ar: لَلَبِثَ فِى بَطْنِهِۦٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
en: he would have certainly remained in its belly until the Day of Resurrection.
t1: He would have stayed in the belly (of the fish) till the Day when people will be resurrected (from the graves).
t2: he would have tarried in its belly until the day they shall be raised;
t3: He would have tarried in its belly till the day when they are raised;

ar: ۞ فَنَبَذْنَٰهُ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ وَهُوَ سَقِيمٌۭ
en: But We cast him onto the open ˹shore˺, ˹totally˺ worn out,
t1: Then We cast him onto a wide plain (i.e., the beach) whilst he was sick.
t2: but We cast him upon the wilderness, and he was sick,
t3: Then We cast him on a desert shore while he was sick;

ar: وَأَنۢبَتْنَا عَلَيْهِ شَجَرَةًۭ مِّن يَقْطِينٍۢ
en: and caused a squash plant to grow over him.
t1: And We caused a creeping (gourd) plant to grow over him.
t2: and We caused to grow over him a tree of gourds.
t3: And We caused a tree of gourd to grow above him;

ar: وَأَرْسَلْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ مِا۟ئَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ
en: We ˹later˺ sent him ˹back˺ to ˹his city of˺ at least one hundred thousand people,
t1: And We sent him towards (the people of Nineveh in the land of Mosul,) a population of a hundred thousand or more.
t2: Then We sent him unto a hundred thousand, or more,
t3: And We sent him to a hundred thousand (folk) or more

ar: فَـَٔامَنُوا۟ فَمَتَّعْنَٰهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍۢ
en: who then believed ˹in him˺, so We allowed them enjoyment for a while.
t1: (Seeing the signs of torment,) they believed. So We granted them prosperity for a time.
t2: and they believed; so We gave them enjoyment for a while.
t3: And they believed, therefor We gave them comfort for a while.

ar: فَٱسْتَفْتِهِمْ أَلِرَبِّكَ ٱلْبَنَاتُ وَلَهُمُ ٱلْبَنُونَ
en: Ask them ˹O Prophet˺ if your Lord has daughters, while the pagans ˹prefer to˺ have sons.
t1: So ask these (disbelievers of Mecca): ‘Are there daughters for your Lord and sons for them?
t2: So ask them for a pronouncement -- Has thy Lord daughters, and they sons?
t3: Now ask them (O Muhammad): Hath thy Lord daughters whereas they have sons ?

ar: أَمْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ إِنَٰثًۭا وَهُمْ شَٰهِدُونَ
en: Or ˹ask them˺ if We created the angels as females right before their eyes.
t1: Did We create the angels as females and were they present (on the occasion)?’
t2: Or did We create the angels females, while they were witnesses?
t3: Or created We the angels females while they were present ?

ar: أَلَآ إِنَّهُم مِّنْ إِفْكِهِمْ لَيَقُولُونَ
en: Indeed, it is one of their ˹outrageous˺ fabrications to say,
t1: Listen! They assuredly say (this) out of their fabrications,
t2: Is it not of their own calumny that they say,
t3: Lo! it is of their falsehood that they say:

ar: وَلَدَ ٱللَّهُ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَٰذِبُونَ
en: “Allah has children.” They are simply liars.
t1: That Allah has begotten children and surely they are liars.
t2: ’God has begotten?’ They are truly liars.
t3: Allah hath begotten. Allah! verily they tell a lie.

ar: أَصْطَفَى ٱلْبَنَاتِ عَلَى ٱلْبَنِينَ
en: Has He chosen daughters over sons?
t1: Has He chosen daughters instead of sons? (The creed of the disbelievers of Mecca is being refuted in the language of their logic and mentality.)
t2: Has He chosen daughters above sons?
t3: (And again of their falsehood): He hath preferred daughters to sons.

ar: مَا لَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ
en: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
t1: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
t2: What ails you then, how you judge?
t3: What aileth you ? How judge ye ?

ar: أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
en: Will you not then be mindful?
t1: Do you not ponder?
t2: What, and will you not remember?
t3: Will ye not then reflect ?

ar: أَمْ لَكُمْ سُلْطَٰنٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
en: Or do you have ˹any˺ compelling proof?
t1: Do you have any clear proof (to establish your philosophy and ideology)?
t2: Or have you a clear authority?
t3: Or have ye a clear warrant ?

ar: فَأْتُوا۟ بِكِتَٰبِكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
en: Then bring ˹us˺ your scripture, if what you say is true!
t1: Produce your book if you are truthful.
t2: Bring your Book, if you speak truly!
t3: Then produce your writ, if ye are truthful.

ar: وَجَعَلُوا۟ بَيْنَهُۥ وَبَيْنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ نَسَبًۭا ۚ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمَتِ ٱلْجِنَّةُ إِنَّهُمْ لَمُحْضَرُونَ
en: They have also established a ˹marital˺ relationship between Him and the jinn. Yet the jinn ˹themselves˺ know well that such people will certainly be brought ˹for punishment˺.
t1: And they have fabricated a blood relationship between Allah and the jinn (as well), whereas the jinn know that they (too) will be made to appear (before the presence of Allah).
t2: They have set up a kinship between Him and the jinn; and the jinn know that they shall be arraigned.
t3: And they imagine kinship between him and the jinn, whereas the jinn know well that they will be brought before (Him).

ar: سُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
en: Glorified is Allah far above what they claim!
t1: Holy is Allah, Transcendent of what they utter.
t2: Glory be to God above that they describe,
t3: Glorified be Allah from that which they attribute (unto Him),

ar: إِلَّا عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
en: But not the chosen servants of Allah.
t1: But the chosen and exalted servants of Allah (do not say such things; they are not amongst them).
t2: except for God’s sincere servants.
t3: Save single-minded slaves of Allah.

ar: فَإِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ
en: Surely you ˹pagans˺ and whatever ˹idols˺ you worship
t1: So you and (the idols) which you worship,
t2: But as for you, and that you serve,
t3: Lo! verily, ye and that which ye worship,

ar: مَآ أَنتُمْ عَلَيْهِ بِفَٰتِنِينَ
en: can never lure ˹anyone˺ away from Him
t1: You all cannot misguide (anyone against Allah),
t2: you shall not tempt any against Him
t3: Ye cannot excite (anyone) against Him.

ar: إِلَّا مَنْ هُوَ صَالِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
en: except those ˹destined˺ to burn in Hell.
t1: Except the one who is bound to fall into Hell.
t2: except him who shall roast in Hell.
t3: Save him who is to burn in hell.

ar: وَمَا مِنَّآ إِلَّا لَهُۥ مَقَامٌۭ مَّعْلُومٌۭ
en: ˹The angels respond,˺ “There is not one of us without an assigned station ˹of worship˺.
t1: And (the angels say:) ‘Every one of us has an appointed station;
t2: None of us is there, but has a known station;
t3: There is not one of us but hath his known position.

ar: وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلصَّآفُّونَ
en: We are indeed the ones lined up in ranks ˹for Allah˺.
t1: And surely, we ourselves are those who remain standing in rows;
t2: we are the rangers,
t3: Lo! we, even we are they who set the ranks,

ar: وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلْمُسَبِّحُونَ
en: And we are indeed the ones ˹constantly˺ glorifying ˹His praise˺.”
t1: And surely, we ourselves remain engaged in glorifying (Allah).’
t2: we are they that give glory.
t3: Lo! we, even we are they who hymn His praise

ar: وَإِن كَانُوا۟ لَيَقُولُونَ
en: They certainly used to say,
t1: And no doubt, these people used to say:
t2: What though they would say,
t3: And indeed they used to say:

ar: لَوْ أَنَّ عِندَنَا ذِكْرًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
en: “If only we had a Reminder like ˹those of˺ earlier peoples,
t1: ‘If we (too) had some (Book) of direction and guidance from the bygone people,
t2: ’If only we had had a Reminder from the ancients,
t3: If we had but a reminder from the men of old

ar: لَكُنَّا عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
en: we would have truly been Allah’s devoted servants.”
t1: Then, certainly, we (too) would have been Allah’s exalted servants.’
t2: then were we God’s sincere servants.’
t3: We would be single-minded slaves of Allah.

ar: فَكَفَرُوا۟ بِهِۦ ۖ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ
en: But ˹now˺ they reject it, so they will soon know.
t1: But (now) they have rejected this (Qur’an). So they will soon come to know (their end).
t2: But they disbelieved in it; soon they shall know!
t3: Yet (now that it is come) they disbelieve therein; but they will come to know.

ar: وَلَقَدْ سَبَقَتْ كَلِمَتُنَا لِعِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
en: Our Word has already gone forth to Our servants, the messengers,
t1: And verily, Our command has been put into effect in respect of the servants whom We sent (i.e., the Messengers),
t2: Already Our Word has preceded to Our servants, the Envoys;
t3: And verily Our word went forth of old unto Our bondmen sent (to warn)

ar: إِنَّهُمْ لَهُمُ ٱلْمَنصُورُونَ
en: that they would surely be helped,
t1: That it is they who have been granted help,
t2: assuredly they shall be helped,
t3: That they verily would be helped,

ar: وَإِنَّ جُندَنَا لَهُمُ ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ
en: and that Our forces will certainly prevail.
t1: And that essentially it is only Our army that shall dominate.
t2: and Our host -- they are the victors.
t3: And that Our host, they verily would be the victors.

ar: فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍۢ
en: So turn away from the deniers for a while ˹O Prophet˺.
t1: So turn your attention away from them for a time.
t2: So turn thou from them for a while,
t3: So withdraw from them (O Muhammad) awhile,

ar: وَأَبْصِرْهُمْ فَسَوْفَ يُبْصِرُونَ
en: You will see ˹what will happen to˺ them, and they too will see!
t1: And keep watching them (constantly). So they will soon come to know (their end).
t2: and see them; soon they shall see!
t3: And watch, for they will (soon) see.

ar: أَفَبِعَذَابِنَا يَسْتَعْجِلُونَ
en: Do they ˹really˺ wish to hasten Our punishment?
t1: And do they want Our punishment to be hastened?
t2: What, do they seek to hasten Our chastisement?
t3: Would they hasten on Our doom ?

ar: فَإِذَا نَزَلَ بِسَاحَتِهِمْ فَسَآءَ صَبَاحُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
en: Yet when it descends upon them: how evil will that morning be for those who had been warned!
t1: But when that (torment) descends before them, how evil will be the morning of those who were warned!
t2: When it lights in their courtyard, how evil will be the morning of them that are warned!
t3: But when it cometh home to them, then it will be a hapless morn for those who have been warned.

ar: وَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍۢ
en: And turn away from them for a while.
t1: So turn your attention away from them for a while.
t2: So turn thou from them for a while,
t3: Withdraw from them awhile

ar: وَأَبْصِرْ فَسَوْفَ يُبْصِرُونَ
en: You will see, and they too will see!
t1: And keep watching them (constantly). So they will soon come to know (their end).
t2: and see; soon they shall see!
t3: And watch, for they will (soon) see.

ar: سُبْحَٰنَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ ٱلْعِزَّةِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
en: Glorified is your Lord—the Lord of Honour and Power—above what they claim!
t1: Holy is your Lord, the Lord of Honour, Transcendent above these (things) which they utter.
t2: Glory be to thy Lord, the Lord of Glory, above that they describe!
t3: Glorified be thy Lord, the Lord of Majesty, from that which they attribute (unto Him)

ar: وَسَلَٰمٌ عَلَى ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
en: Peace be upon the messengers.
t1: And peace be upon (all) the Messengers!
t2: And peace be upon the Envoys;
t3: And peace be unto those sent (to warn).

ar: وَٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: And praise be to Allah—Lord of all worlds.
t1: And all praise be to Allah alone, the Lord of all the worlds.
t2: and praise belongs to God, the Lord of all Being.
t3: And praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds!

ar: صٓ ۚ وَٱلْقُرْءَانِ ذِى ٱلذِّكْرِ
en: sãd. By the Quran, full of reminders!
t1: Sad. (Only Allah and the Messenger [blessings and peace be upon him] know the real meaning.) By the Holy Qur’an, full of direction and guidance.
t2: Sad. By the Koran, containing the Remembrance --
t3: Sad. By the renowned Qur’an,

ar: بَلِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ فِى عِزَّةٍۢ وَشِقَاقٍۢ
en: ˹This is the truth,˺ yet the disbelievers are ˹entrenched˺ in arrogance and opposition.
t1: But the disbelievers are in (the trouble of undue and unjust) conceit and arrogance, (suffering from) opposition and enmity (against Our Esteemed Prophet).
t2: nay, but the unbelievers glory in their schism.
t3: Nay, but those who disbelieve are in false pride and schism.

ar: كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن قَرْنٍۢ فَنَادَوا۟ وَّلَاتَ حِينَ مَنَاصٍۢ
en: ˹Imagine˺ how many peoples We destroyed before them, and they cried out when it was too late to escape.
t1: How many a community We have destroyed before them! And they started crying (on seeing the torment) when there was no time left for deliverance (and release).
t2: How many a generation We destroyed before them, and they called, but time was none to escape.
t3: How many a generation We destroyed before them, and they cried out when it was no longer the time for escape!

ar: وَعَجِبُوٓا۟ أَن جَآءَهُم مُّنذِرٌۭ مِّنْهُمْ ۖ وَقَالَ ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا سَٰحِرٌۭ كَذَّابٌ
en: Now, the pagans are astonished that a warner has come to them from among themselves. And the disbelievers say, “This is a magician, a total liar!
t1: And they wondered that a Warner had come to them from amongst themselves and the disbelievers said: ‘He is a magician, a great liar.
t2: Now they marvel that a warner has come to them from among them; and the unbelievers say, ’This is a lying sorcerer.
t3: And they marvel that a warner from among themselves hath come unto them, and the disbelievers say: This is a wizard, a charlatan.

ar: أَجَعَلَ ٱلْءَالِهَةَ إِلَٰهًۭا وَٰحِدًا ۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَشَىْءٌ عُجَابٌۭ
en: Has he reduced ˹all˺ the gods to One God? Indeed, this is something totally astonishing.”
t1: Has he turned all the gods into one God? That is indeed a very strange thing!’
t2: What, has he made the gods One God? This is indeed a marvellous thing.’
t3: Maketh he the gods One God ? Lo! that is an astounding thing.

ar: وَٱنطَلَقَ ٱلْمَلَأُ مِنْهُمْ أَنِ ٱمْشُوا۟ وَٱصْبِرُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ ءَالِهَتِكُمْ ۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَشَىْءٌۭ يُرَادُ
en: The chiefs among them went forth saying, “Carry on, and stand firm in devotion to your gods. Certainly this is just a scheme ˹for power˺.
t1: And their chiefs (stood up terminating their meeting with the Holy Prophet [blessings and peace be upon him] at Abu Talib’s house) and walked out saying (to the rest of the people): ‘You also walk out, and be firm-footed in (worshipping) your gods. There is for sure some motive (and purpose) behind it.
t2: And the Council of them depart, saying ’Go! Be steadfast to your gods; this is a thing to be desired.
t3: The chiefs among them go about, exhorting: Go and be staunch to your gods! Lo! this is a thing designed.

ar: مَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِى ٱلْمِلَّةِ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا ٱخْتِلَٰقٌ
en: We have never heard of this in the previous faith. This is nothing but a fabrication.
t1: We have not heard of this (belief in the Oneness of God) even amongst the last community (of Christianity or the religion of the Quraysh). This is but a fabricated lie.
t2: We have not heard of this in the last religion; this is surely an invention.
t3: We have not heard of this in later religion. This is naught but an invention.

ar: أَءُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلذِّكْرُ مِنۢ بَيْنِنَا ۚ بَلْ هُمْ فِى شَكٍّۢ مِّن ذِكْرِى ۖ بَل لَّمَّا يَذُوقُوا۟ عَذَابِ
en: Has the Reminder been revealed ˹only˺ to him out of ˹all of˺ us?” In fact, they are ˹only˺ in doubt of My ˹revealed˺ Reminder. In fact, ˹they do so because˺ they have not yet tasted My punishment.
t1: Has this admonition (the Qur’an) been sent down to him alone out of all of us?’ To be more precise, they are (caught) in doubt about My admonition. But in truth they have not yet tasted My torment.
t2: What, has the Remembrance been sent down on him out of us all?’ Nay, but they are in doubt of My Remembrance; nay, they have not yet tasted My chastisement.
t3: Hath the reminder been unto him (alone) among us ? Nay, but they are in doubt concerning My reminder; nay but they have not yet tasted My doom.

ar: أَمْ عِندَهُمْ خَزَآئِنُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْوَهَّابِ
en: Or ˹is it because˺ they possess the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord—the Almighty, the Giver ˹of all bounties˺.
t1: Do they have the treasures of the mercy of your Lord, Who is the Almighty, the Most Benevolent?
t2: Or have they the treasuries of thy Lord’s mercy, the All-mighty, the All-giving?
t3: Or are theirs the treasures of the mercy of thy Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower ?

ar: أَمْ لَهُم مُّلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ۖ فَلْيَرْتَقُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَسْبَٰبِ
en: Or ˹is it because˺ the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and everything in between belongs to them? Let them then climb their way ˹to heaven, if their claim is true˺.
t1: Or do they possess the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them? (If so,) then they should tie up ropes and climb up (to heaven).
t2: Or is theirs the kingdom of the heavens and earth and of what between them is? Why, then let them ascend the cords!
t3: Or is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them theirs ? Then let them ascend by ropes!

ar: جُندٌۭ مَّا هُنَالِكَ مَهْزُومٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْأَحْزَابِ
en: This is just another ˹enemy˺ force bound for defeat out there.
t1: They are just a worthless army of the armies (of the disbelievers) that is about to be badly defeated at this very place.
t2: A very host of parties is routed there!
t3: A defeated host are (all) the factions that are there.

ar: كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍۢ وَعَادٌۭ وَفِرْعَوْنُ ذُو ٱلْأَوْتَادِ
en: Before them, the people of Noah denied ˹the truth˺, as did ’ad, Pharaoh of the mighty structures,
t1: Before them the people of Nuh (Noah) and ‘Ad and (also) Pharaoh, the powerful king (who tortured with stakes), belied and disbelieved;
t2: Cried lies before them the people of Noah, and Ad, and Pharaoh, he of the tent-pegs,
t3: The folk of Noah before them denied (their messenger) and (so did the tribe of) A’ad, and Pharaoh firmly planted,

ar: وَثَمُودُ وَقَوْمُ لُوطٍۢ وَأَصْحَٰبُ لْـَٔيْكَةِ ۚ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلْأَحْزَابُ
en: Thamûd, the people of Lot, and the residents of the Forest. These were ˹all˺ enemy forces.
t1: And Thamud and the people of Lut (Lot) and the dwellers of (the Wood) al-Ayka (i.e., the people of Shu‘ayb) too (denied). These were the large armies.
t2: and Thamood, and the people of Lot, and the men of the Thicket - those were the parties;
t3: And (the tribe of) Thamud, and the folk of Lot, and the dwellers in the wood: these were the factions.

ar: إِن كُلٌّ إِلَّا كَذَّبَ ٱلرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ عِقَابِ
en: Each rejected their messenger, so My punishment was justified.
t1: Each (one of these) people rejected the Messengers and My torment became inevitable (for them).
t2: not one, that cried not lies to the Messengers, so My retribution was just.
t3: Not one of them but did deny the messengers, therefor My doom was justified,

ar: وَمَا يَنظُرُ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِلَّا صَيْحَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ مَّا لَهَا مِن فَوَاقٍۢ
en: These ˹pagans˺ are awaiting nothing but a single Blast that cannot be stopped.
t1: And all of them are waiting for a single mighty blast (shout) in which there will be no deferment.
t2: These are only awaiting for a single Cry, to which there is no delay.
t3: These wait for but one Shout, there will be no second thereto.

ar: وَقَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَا عَجِّل لَّنَا قِطَّنَا قَبْلَ يَوْمِ ٱلْحِسَابِ
en: They say ˹mockingly˺, “Our Lord! Hasten for us our share ˹of the punishment˺ before the Day of Reckoning.”
t1: And they say: ‘O our Lord, hasten to us our share even before the Day of Reckoning.’
t2: They say, ’Our Lord, hasten to us our share before the Day of Reckoning.’
t3: They say: Our Lord! Hasten on for us our fate before the Day of Reckoning.

ar: ٱصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَٱذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَا دَاوُۥدَ ذَا ٱلْأَيْدِ ۖ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌ
en: Be patient ˹O Prophet˺ with what they say. And remember Our servant, David, the man of strength. Indeed, he ˹constantly˺ turned ˹to Allah˺.
t1: (O My Esteemed Beloved!) Continue observing patience with what they say and remember Our servant Dawud (David), who had great power. Certainly, he was ever-turning (to Us in repentance).
t2: Bear patiently what they say, and remember Our servant David, the man of might; he was a penitent.
t3: Bear with what they say, and remember Our bondman David, lord of might, Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (toward Allah).

ar: إِنَّا سَخَّرْنَا ٱلْجِبَالَ مَعَهُۥ يُسَبِّحْنَ بِٱلْعَشِىِّ وَٱلْإِشْرَاقِ
en: We truly subjected the mountains to hymn ˹Our praises˺ along with him in the evening and after sunrise.
t1: Indeed, We put mountains under his command which (joining him) used to glorify Me evening and morning,
t2: With him We subjected the mountains to give glory at evening and sunrise,
t3: Lo! We subdued the hills to hymn the praises (of their Lord) with him at nightfall and sunrise,

ar: وَٱلطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةًۭ ۖ كُلٌّۭ لَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌۭ
en: And ˹We subjected˺ the birds, flocking together. All turned to him ˹echoing his hymns˺.
t1: And the birds as well that used to flock (in his presence); each would turn towards him (seeking to obey his commands).
t2: and the birds, duly mustered, every one to him reverting;
t3: And the birds assembled; all were turning unto Him.

ar: وَشَدَدْنَا مُلْكَهُۥ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ ٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَفَصْلَ ٱلْخِطَابِ
en: We strengthened his kingship, and gave him wisdom and sound judgment.
t1: And We strengthened and stabilized his state and rule, and blessed him with wisdom, insight and a decisive (and distinctive) oratory.
t2: We strengthened his kingdom, and gave him wisdom and speech decisive.
t3: We made his kingdom strong and gave him wisdom and decisive speech.

ar: ۞ وَهَلْ أَتَىٰكَ نَبَؤُا۟ ٱلْخَصْمِ إِذْ تَسَوَّرُوا۟ ٱلْمِحْرَابَ
en: Has the story of the two plaintiffs, who scaled the ˹wall of David’s˺ sanctuary, reached you ˹O Prophet˺?
t1: And has the news of the contenders reached you when they jumped over the wall and entered the chamber of worship (of Dawud [David])?
t2: Has the tiding of the dispute come to thee? When they scaled the Sanctuary,
t3: And hath the story of the litigants come unto thee ? How they climbed the wall into the royal chamber;

ar: إِذْ دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَىٰ دَاوُۥدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنْهُمْ ۖ قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ ۖ خَصْمَانِ بَغَىٰ بَعْضُنَا عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍۢ فَٱحْكُم بَيْنَنَا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَا تُشْطِطْ وَٱهْدِنَآ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ
en: When they came into David’s presence, he was startled by them. They said, “Have no fear. ˹We are merely˺ two in a dispute: one of us has wronged the other. So judge between us with truth—do not go beyond ˹it˺—and guide us to the right way.
t1: When they came inside to Dawud (David), he felt nervous. They said: ‘Do not feel upset. We are two parties in a dispute. One of us has wronged the other. So judge between us with truth and justice, and do not exceed limits, and lead us towards the right path.
t2: when they entered upon David, and he took fright at them; and they said, ’Fear not; two disputants we are -- one of us has injured the other; so judge between us justly, and transgress not, and guide us to the right path.’
t3: How they burst in upon David, and he was afraid of them. They said: Be not afraid! (We are) two litigants, one of whom hath wronged the other, therefor judge aright between us; be not unjust; and show us the fair way.

ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَآ أَخِى لَهُۥ تِسْعٌۭ وَتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةًۭ وَلِىَ نَعْجَةٌۭ وَٰحِدَةٌۭ فَقَالَ أَكْفِلْنِيهَا وَعَزَّنِى فِى ٱلْخِطَابِ
en: This is my brother. He has ninety-nine sheep while I have ˹only˺ one. ˹Still˺ he asked me to give it up to him, overwhelming me with ˹his˺ argument.”
t1: Surely, he is my brother; he has ninety-nine ewes and I have only one ewe. Yet he says: ‘Give it (also) to me,’ and he suppresses me in conversation (as well).
t2: ’Behold, this my brother has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe. So he said, "Give her into my charge"; and he overcame me in the argument.’
t3: Lo! this my brother hath ninety and nine ewes while I had one ewe; and he said: Entrust it to me, and he conquered me in speech.

ar: قَالَ لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعْجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِۦ ۖ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْخُلَطَآءِ لَيَبْغِى بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَقَلِيلٌۭ مَّا هُمْ ۗ وَظَنَّ دَاوُۥدُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّٰهُ فَٱسْتَغْفَرَ رَبَّهُۥ وَخَرَّ رَاكِعًۭا وَأَنَابَ ۩
en: David ˹eventually˺ ruled, “He has definitely wronged you in demanding ˹to add˺ your sheep to his. And certainly many partners wrong each other, except those who believe and do good—but how few are they!” Then David realized that We had tested him so he asked for his Lord’s forgiveness, fell down in prostration, and turned ˹to Him in repentance˺.
t1: Dawud (David) said: ‘He has done you a wrong in demanding your ewe to add to his own ewes, and it is true that most of the partners wrong one another except those who believe and do pious deeds, and such people are very few.’ And it occurred to Dawud (David) that We had put him to trial (through that dispute). So he prayed for forgiveness from his Lord and fell down prostrate and turned (to Allah) in repentance.
t2: Said he, ’Assuredly he has wronged thee in asking for thy ewe in addition to his sheep; and indeed many intermixers do injury one against the other, save those who believe, and do deeds of righteousness -- and how few they are!’ And David thought that We had only tried him; therefore he sought forgiveness of his Lord, and he fell down, bowing, and he repented.
t3: (David) said: He hath wronged thee in demanding thine ewe in addition to his ewes, and lo! many partners oppress one another, save such as believe and do good works, and they are few. And David guessed that We had tried him, and he sought forgiveness of his Lord, and he bowed himself and fell down prostrate and repented.

ar: فَغَفَرْنَا لَهُۥ ذَٰلِكَ ۖ وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلْفَىٰ وَحُسْنَ مَـَٔابٍۢ
en: So We forgave that for him. And he will indeed have ˹a status of˺ closeness to Us and an honourable destination!
t1: So We granted him forgiveness, and surely he enjoys special nearness in Our presence and an exalted position (in the Hereafter).
t2: Accordingly We forgave him that, and he has a near place in Our presence and a fair resort.
t3: So We forgave him that; and lo! he had access to Our presence and a happy journey’s end.

ar: يَٰدَاوُۥدُ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَٰكَ خَلِيفَةًۭ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱحْكُم بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ فَيُضِلَّكَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌۭ شَدِيدٌۢ بِمَا نَسُوا۟ يَوْمَ ٱلْحِسَابِ
en: ˹We instructed him:˺ “O David! We have surely made you an authority in the land, so judge between people with truth. And do not follow ˹your˺ desires or they will lead you astray from Allah’s Way. Surely those who go astray from Allah’s Way will suffer a severe punishment for neglecting the Day of Reckoning.”
t1: O Dawud (David)! Verily, We have made you (Our) vicegerent in the earth. So judge between the people (or rule) with truth and justice. And do not follow your desire, for this (pursuance of desire) shall turn you away from the path of Allah. Surely, those who turn away from the path of Allah, for them is severe punishment because they forget the Day of Reckoning.
t2: ’David, behold, We have appointed thee a viceroy in the earth; therefore judge between men justly, and follow not caprice, lest it lead thee astray from the way of God. Surely those who go astray from the way of God -- there awaits them a terrible chastisement, for that they have forgotten the Day of Reckoning.’
t3: (And it was said unto him): O David! Lo! We have set thee as a viceroy in the earth; therefor judge aright between mankind, and follow not desire that it beguile thee from the way of Allah. Lo! those who wander from the way of Allah have an awful doom, forasmuch as they forgot the Day of Reckoning.

ar: وَمَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا بَٰطِلًۭا ۚ ذَٰلِكَ ظَنُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ۚ فَوَيْلٌۭ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ
en: We have not created the heavens and earth and everything in between without purpose—as the disbelievers think. So woe to the disbelievers because of the Fire!
t1: And We have not created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them without any purpose and good reason. It is the view and concept of the disbelievers (that this is a purposeless creation that came about by chance). So for the disbelievers there is torment of the Fire of Hell.
t2: We have not created the heavens and earth, and what between them is, for vanity; such is the thought of the unbelievers, wherefore woe unto the unbelievers because of the Fire!
t3: And We created not the heaven and the earth and all that is between them in vain. That is the opinion of those who disbelieve. And woe unto those who disbelieve, from the Fire!

ar: أَمْ نَجْعَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ كَٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ أَمْ نَجْعَلُ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ كَٱلْفُجَّارِ
en: Or should We treat those who believe and do good like those who make mischief throughout the land? Or should We treat the righteous like the wicked?
t1: Shall We make those who believe and do constructive works like those who corrupt the earth with mischief and destructive works? Or shall We make the pious like the corrupt and wicked?
t2: Or shall We make those who believe and do righteous deeds as the workers of corruption in the earth, or shall We make the godfearing as the transgressors?
t3: Shall We treat those who believe and do good works as those who spread corruption in the earth; or shall We treat the pious as the wicked ?

ar: كِتَٰبٌ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَٰرَكٌۭ لِّيَدَّبَّرُوٓا۟ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ
en: ˹This is˺ a blessed Book which We have revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ so that they may contemplate its verses, and people of reason may be mindful.
t1: This is a Blessed Book that We have revealed to you so that the wise may ponder over its Verses and seek direction and guidance.
t2: A Book We have sent down to thee, Blessed, that men possessed of minds may ponder its signs and so remember.
t3: (This is) a Scripture that We have revealed unto thee, full of blessing, that they may ponder its revelations, and that men of understanding may reflect.

ar: وَوَهَبْنَا لِدَاوُۥدَ سُلَيْمَٰنَ ۚ نِعْمَ ٱلْعَبْدُ ۖ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌ
en: And We blessed David with Solomon—what an excellent servant ˹he was˺! Indeed, he ˹constantly˺ turned ˹to Allah˺.
t1: And We blessed Dawud (David) with (a son) Sulayman (Solomon). How excellent a servant was he! He is indeed oft-returning to Allah in repentance.
t2: And We gave unto David Solomon; how excellent a servant he was! He was a penitent.
t3: And We bestowed on David, Solomon. How excellent a slave! Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (toward Allah).

ar: إِذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بِٱلْعَشِىِّ ٱلصَّٰفِنَٰتُ ٱلْجِيَادُ
en: ˹Remember˺ when the well-trained, swift horses were paraded before him in the evening.
t1: When swift horses of a fine breed were presented to him in the evening,
t2: When in the evening were presented to him the standing steeds,
t3: When there were shown to him at eventide lightfooted coursers

ar: فَقَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ ٱلْخَيْرِ عَن ذِكْرِ رَبِّى حَتَّىٰ تَوَارَتْ بِٱلْحِجَابِ
en: He then proclaimed, “I am truly in love with ˹these˺ fine things out of remembrance for Allah,” until they went out of sight.
t1: He said (remorsefully): ‘I have cherished love for wealth (i.e., horses) more than the love for the remembrance of my Lord until (the sun) disappeared behind the veil (of night).’
t2: he said, ’Lo, I have loved the love of good things better than the remembrance of my Lord, until the sun was bidden behind the veil.
t3: And he said: Lo! I have preferred the good things (of the world) to the remembrance of my Lord; till they were taken out of sight behind the curtain.

ar: رُدُّوهَا عَلَىَّ ۖ فَطَفِقَ مَسْحًۢا بِٱلسُّوقِ وَٱلْأَعْنَاقِ
en: ˹He ordered,˺ “Bring them back to me!” Then he began to rub down their legs and necks.
t1: He said: ‘Bring them (horses) back to me.’ So he cut away their legs and necks (with a sword, and thus he slaughtered his love for nearness to Allah).
t2: Return them to me!’ And he began to stroke their shanks and necks.
t3: (Then he said): Bring them back to me, and fell to slashing (with his sword their) legs and necks.

ar: وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا سُلَيْمَٰنَ وَأَلْقَيْنَا عَلَىٰ كُرْسِيِّهِۦ جَسَدًۭا ثُمَّ أَنَابَ
en: And indeed, We tested Solomon, placing a ˹deformed˺ body on his throne, then he turned ˹to Allah in repentance˺.
t1: And indeed, We (also) put Sulayman (Solomon) to trial, and placed an (unusually created) body on his throne. Then he regained (the rule).
t2: Certainly We tried Solomon, and We cast upon his throne a mere body; then he repented.
t3: And verily We tried Solomon, and set upon his throne a (mere) body. Then did he repent.

ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱغْفِرْ لِى وَهَبْ لِى مُلْكًۭا لَّا يَنۢبَغِى لِأَحَدٍۢ مِّنۢ بَعْدِىٓ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْوَهَّابُ
en: He prayed, “My Lord! Forgive me, and grant me an authority that will never be matched by anyone after me. You are indeed the Giver ˹of all bounties˺.”
t1: He submitted: ‘O my Lord, forgive me, and bestow on me such a reign that no one may have after me. Surely, You are Most Benevolent.’
t2: He said, ’My Lord, forgive me, and give me a kingdom such as may not befall anyone after me; surely Thou art the All-giver.’
t3: He said: My Lord! Forgive me and bestow on me sovereignty such as shall not belong to any after me. Lo! Thou art the Bestower.

ar: فَسَخَّرْنَا لَهُ ٱلرِّيحَ تَجْرِى بِأَمْرِهِۦ رُخَآءً حَيْثُ أَصَابَ
en: So We subjected to him the wind, blowing gently at his command to wherever he pleased.
t1: Then We caused the wind to obey him. It used to blow gently under his command wherever he would desire (it) to go.
t2: So We subjected to him the wind, that ran at his commandment, softly, wherever he might light on,
t3: So We made the wind subservient unto him, setting fair by his command whithersoever he intended.

ar: وَٱلشَّيَٰطِينَ كُلَّ بَنَّآءٍۢ وَغَوَّاصٍۢ
en: And ˹We subjected to him˺ every builder and diver of the jinn,
t1: And all the jinn (and devils were also subdued to him) and every architect and diver (too),
t2: and the Satans, every builder and diver
t3: And the unruly, every builder and diver (made We subservient),

ar: وَءَاخَرِينَ مُقَرَّنِينَ فِى ٱلْأَصْفَادِ
en: and others bound together in chains.
t1: And (also) other jinn bound in chains.
t2: and others also, coupled in fetters:
t3: And others linked together in chains,

ar: هَٰذَا عَطَآؤُنَا فَٱمْنُنْ أَوْ أَمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍۢ
en: ˹Allah said,˺ “This is Our gift, so give or withhold ˹as you wish˺, never to be called to account.”
t1: (Allah said:) ‘This is Our bestowal. (Whether you) confer (it) on others or hold back (to you), no account will be asked for (in both the cases).’
t2: ’This is Our gift; bestow or withhold without reckoning.’
t3: (Saying): This is Our gift, so bestow thou, or withhold, without reckoning.

ar: وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلْفَىٰ وَحُسْنَ مَـَٔابٍۢ
en: And he will indeed have ˹a status of˺ closeness to Us and an honourable destination!
t1: And surely, he enjoys exclusive nearness in Our presence and an exalted position in the Hereafter.
t2: And he had a near place in Our presence and a fair resort.
t3: And lo! he hath favour with Us, and a happy journey’s end.

ar: وَٱذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَآ أَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَسَّنِىَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ بِنُصْبٍۢ وَعَذَابٍ
en: And remember Our servant Job, when he cried out to his Lord, “Satan has afflicted me with distress and suffering.”
t1: And mention Our servant Ayyub (Job) when he cried to his Lord: ‘Satan has afflicted me with great torture and suffering.’
t2: Remember also Our servant Job; when he called to his Lord, ’Behold, Satan has visited me with weariness and chastisement.’
t3: And make mention (O Muhammad) of Our bondman Job, when he cried unto his Lord (saying): Lo! the devil doth afflict me with distress and torment.

ar: ٱرْكُضْ بِرِجْلِكَ ۖ هَٰذَا مُغْتَسَلٌۢ بَارِدٌۭ وَشَرَابٌۭ
en: ˹We responded,˺ “Stomp your foot: ˹now˺ here is a cool ˹and refreshing˺ spring for washing and drinking.”
t1: (Allah said:) ‘Strike the ground with your foot. Here is a spring (of cool water) to bathe and drink.’
t2: ’Stamp thy foot! This is a laving-place cool, and a drink.’
t3: (And it was said unto him): Strike the ground with thy foot. This (spring) is a cool bath and a refreshing drink.

ar: وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥٓ أَهْلَهُۥ وَمِثْلَهُم مَّعَهُمْ رَحْمَةًۭ مِّنَّا وَذِكْرَىٰ لِأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ
en: And We gave him back his family, twice as many, as a mercy from Us and a lesson for people of reason.
t1: And We gave him his family, and as many more (members of family) along with them, as a special mercy from Us and as advice for the wise.
t2: And We gave to him his family, and the like of them with them, as a mercy from us, and a reminder unto men possessed of minds;
t3: And We bestowed on him (again) his household and therewith the like thereof, a mercy from Us, and a memorial for men of understanding.

ar: وَخُذْ بِيَدِكَ ضِغْثًۭا فَٱضْرِب بِّهِۦ وَلَا تَحْنَثْ ۗ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَٰهُ صَابِرًۭا ۚ نِّعْمَ ٱلْعَبْدُ ۖ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌۭ
en: ˹And We said to him,˺ “Take in your hand a bundle of grass, and strike ˹your wife˺ with it, and do not break your oath.” We truly found him patient. What an excellent servant ˹he was˺! Indeed, he ˹constantly˺ turned ˹to Allah˺.
t1: (O Ayyub [Job]!) Take a broom of (one hundred) twigs in your hand, and strike (your wife once) with that (to fulfil your oath), and do not break your oath. Surely, We found him steadfast. How excellent a servant was (Ayyub [Job])! Surely, he was oft-returning (to Us) in repentance.
t2: and, ’Take in thy hand a bundle of rushes, and strike therewith, and do not fail in thy oath.’ Surely We found him a steadfast man. How excellent a servant he was! He was a penitent.
t3: And (it was said unto him): Take in thine hand a branch and smite therewith, and break not thine oath. Lo! We found him steadfast, how excellent a slave! Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (to his Lord).

ar: وَٱذْكُرْ عِبَٰدَنَآ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ أُو۟لِى ٱلْأَيْدِى وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرِ
en: And remember Our servants: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—the men of strength and insight.
t1: And mention Our servants Ibrahim (Abraham) and Ishaq (Isaac) and Ya‘qub (Jacob), who wielded great power and possessed vision.
t2: Remember also Our servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob -- men of might they and of vision.
t3: And make mention of Our bondmen, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, men of parts and vision.

ar: إِنَّآ أَخْلَصْنَٰهُم بِخَالِصَةٍۢ ذِكْرَى ٱلدَّارِ
en: We truly chose them for the honour of proclaiming the Hereafter.
t1: Surely, We chose them for an exclusive (characteristic of) the remembrance of the home in the Hereafter.
t2: Assuredly We purified them with a quality most pure, the remembrance of the Abode,
t3: Lo! We purified them with a pure thought, remembrance of the Home (of the Hereafter).

ar: وَإِنَّهُمْ عِندَنَا لَمِنَ ٱلْمُصْطَفَيْنَ ٱلْأَخْيَارِ
en: And in Our sight they are truly among the chosen and the finest.
t1: And verily, in Our Sight they were of the chosen, exalted (and) most liked servants.
t2: and in Our sight they are of the chosen, the excellent.
t3: Lo! in Our sight they are verily of the elect, the excellent.

ar: وَٱذْكُرْ إِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَٱلْيَسَعَ وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ ۖ وَكُلٌّۭ مِّنَ ٱلْأَخْيَارِ
en: Also remember Ishmael, Elisha, and Ⱬul-Kifl. All are among the best.
t1: And (also) mention Isma‘il (Ishmael) and al-Yasa‘ (Isaiah) and Dhu al-Kifl (Ezekiel). And all of them were of the chosen ones.
t2: Remember also Our servants Ishmael, Elisha, and Dhul Kifl; each is among the excellent.
t3: And make mention of Ishmael and Elisha and Dhu’l-Kifl. All are of the chosen.

ar: هَٰذَا ذِكْرٌۭ ۚ وَإِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مَـَٔابٍۢ
en: This is ˹all˺ a reminder. And the righteous will certainly have an honourable destination:
t1: This is the direction and guidance (which is cited in the first Verse of this Sura). And surely, for the Godfearing there is a blessed abode.
t2: This is a Remembrance; and for the godfearing is a fair resort,
t3: This is a reminder. And lo! for those who ward off (evil) is a happy journey’s end,

ar: جَنَّٰتِ عَدْنٍۢ مُّفَتَّحَةًۭ لَّهُمُ ٱلْأَبْوَٰبُ
en: the Gardens of Eternity, whose gates will be open for them.
t1: (They are) the Gardens of Eden to live in forever. Their doors will be opened for them.
t2: Gardens of Eden, whereof the gates are open to them,
t3: Gardens of Eden, whereof the gates are opened for them,

ar: مُتَّكِـِٔينَ فِيهَا يَدْعُونَ فِيهَا بِفَٰكِهَةٍۢ كَثِيرَةٍۢ وَشَرَابٍۢ
en: There they will recline, calling for abundant fruit and drink.
t1: There, reclining on cushions, they will be sitting (on couches), calling (at intervals) for plenteous fine fruits and (delicious) drinks.
t2: wherein they recline, and wherein they call for fruits abundant, and sweet potions,
t3: Wherein, reclining, they call for plenteous fruit and cool drink (that is) therein.

ar: ۞ وَعِندَهُمْ قَٰصِرَٰتُ ٱلطَّرْفِ أَتْرَابٌ
en: And with them will be maidens of modest gaze and equal age.
t1: And beside them will be pure women (houris) with gazes lowered (i.e., chaste) and of equal age.
t2: and with them maidens restraining their glances of equal age.
t3: And with them are those of modest gaze, companions.

ar: هَٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِيَوْمِ ٱلْحِسَابِ
en: This is what you are promised for the Day of Reckoning.
t1: These are the blessings which you are promised for the Day of Reckoning.
t2: ’This is what you were promised for the Day of Reckoning;
t3: This it is that ye are promised for the Day of Reckoning.

ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَرِزْقُنَا مَا لَهُۥ مِن نَّفَادٍ
en: This is indeed Our provision that will never end.
t1: Surely, this is Our provision which is never to exhaust.
t2: this is Our provision, unto which there is no end.’
t3: Lo! this in truth is Our provision, which will never waste away.

ar: هَٰذَا ۚ وَإِنَّ لِلطَّٰغِينَ لَشَرَّ مَـَٔابٍۢ
en: That is that. And the transgressors will certainly have the worst destination:
t1: This (is for the believers), and surely for the defiant there is an extremely evil abode.
t2: All this; but for the insolent awaits an ill resort,
t3: This (is for the righteous). And lo! for the transgressors there with be an evil journey’s end,

ar: جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَوْنَهَا فَبِئْسَ ٱلْمِهَادُ
en: Hell, where they will burn. What an evil place to rest!
t1: (That is) Hell which they will enter, and that is extremely evil bedding.
t2: Gehenna, wherein they are roasted - an evil cradling!
t3: Hell, where they will burn, an evil resting-place.

ar: هَٰذَا فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌۭ وَغَسَّاقٌۭ
en: Let them then taste this: boiling water and ˹oozing˺ pus,
t1: This (is punishment) so they should taste it: boiling water and pus.
t2: All this; so let them taste it - boiling water and pus,
t3: Here is a boiling and an ice-cold draught, so let them taste it,

ar: وَءَاخَرُ مِن شَكْلِهِۦٓ أَزْوَٰجٌ
en: and other torments of the same sort!
t1: And there is also a variety of (torments of) similar nature.
t2: and other torments of the like kind coupled together.
t3: And other (torment) of the kind in pairs (the two extremes)!

ar: هَٰذَا فَوْجٌۭ مُّقْتَحِمٌۭ مَّعَكُمْ ۖ لَا مَرْحَبًۢا بِهِمْ ۚ إِنَّهُمْ صَالُوا۟ ٱلنَّارِ
en: ˹The misleaders will say to one another,˺ “Here is a crowd ˹of followers˺ being thrown in with us. They are not welcome, ˹for˺ they ˹too˺ will burn in the Fire.”
t1: (The Guards of Hell or the inmates of Hell already there will say:) ‘This is an(other) army which is rushing into Hell along with you. There is no welcome for them. Surely, they (too) are about to enter Hell.’
t2: ’This is a troop rushing in with you; there is no Welcome for them; they shall roast in the Fire.’
t3: Here is an army rushing blindly with you. (Those who are already in the Fire say): No word of welcome for them. Lo! they will roast at the Fire.

ar: قَالُوا۟ بَلْ أَنتُمْ لَا مَرْحَبًۢا بِكُمْ ۖ أَنتُمْ قَدَّمْتُمُوهُ لَنَا ۖ فَبِئْسَ ٱلْقَرَارُ
en: The followers will respond, “No! You are not welcome! You brought this upon us. What an evil place for settlement!”
t1: They (the arrivals) will say: ‘In fact, it is you; may there be no reception for you! It is but you who brought us this (disbelief and torment). So (this) is an evil resting place.’
t2: They say, ’No, it is you have no Welcome; you forwarded it for us; how evil a stablishment!’
t3: They say: Nay, but you (misleaders), for you there is no word of welcome. Ye prepared this for us (by your misleading). Now hapless is the plight.

ar: قَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَا مَن قَدَّمَ لَنَا هَٰذَا فَزِدْهُ عَذَابًۭا ضِعْفًۭا فِى ٱلنَّارِ
en: Adding, “Our Lord! Whoever brought this upon us, double their punishment in the Fire.”
t1: They will say: ‘O our Lord, the one who brought for us this (disbelief or torment), increase his torment in Hell twofold.’
t2: They say, ’Our Lord, whoso forwarded this for us, give him a double chastisement in the Fire!’
t3: They say: Our Lord! Whoever did prepare this for us, oh, give him double portion of the Fire!

ar: وَقَالُوا۟ مَا لَنَا لَا نَرَىٰ رِجَالًۭا كُنَّا نَعُدُّهُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَشْرَارِ
en: The tyrants will ask ˹one another˺, “But why do we not see those we considered to be lowly?
t1: And they will say: ‘What is the matter with us that we do not see (those) persons (here) we used to count amongst the evil people?’
t2: They say, ’How is it with us, that we do not see men here that we counted among the wicked?
t3: And they say: What aileth us that we behold not men whom we were wont to count among the wicked ?

ar: أَتَّخَذْنَٰهُمْ سِخْرِيًّا أَمْ زَاغَتْ عَنْهُمُ ٱلْأَبْصَٰرُ
en: Were we wrong in mocking them ˹in the world˺? Or do our eyes ˹just˺ fail to see them ˹in the Fire˺?”
t1: Did we use to scoff at them (unjustly) or did our eyes miss (to recognize) them? (These were the sold-to-God divines like ‘Ammar, Khabab, Suhayb, Bilal and Salman, [may Allah be well pleased with all of them.])
t2: What, did we take them for a laughing-stock? Or have our eyes swerved away from them?’
t3: Did we take them (wrongly) for a laughing-stock, or have our eyes missed them ?

ar: إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ لَحَقٌّۭ تَخَاصُمُ أَهْلِ ٱلنَّارِ
en: This dispute between the residents of the Fire will certainly come to pass.
t1: Surely, this mutual dispute of the inmates of Hell is true.
t2: Surely that is true -- the disputing of the inhabitants of the Fire.
t3: Lo! that is very truth: the wrangling of the dwellers in the Fire.

ar: قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ مُنذِرٌۭ ۖ وَمَا مِنْ إِلَٰهٍ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ ٱلْوَٰحِدُ ٱلْقَهَّارُ
en: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I am only a warner. And there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Allah—the One, the Supreme.
t1: Say: ‘I am only a Warner and there is no God except Allah, the One, the All-Dominant,
t2: Say: ’I am only a warner. There is not any god but God, the One, the Omnipotent,
t3: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): I am only a warner, and there is no God save Allah, the One, the Absolute,

ar: رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْغَفَّٰرُ
en: ˹He is the˺ Lord of the heavens and the earth and everything in between—the Almighty, Most Forgiving.”
t1: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and (all) what is between the two, the Almighty, Most Forgiving.’
t2: Lord of the heavens and earth, and of what between them is, the All-mighty, the All-forgiving.’
t3: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, the Mighty, the Pardoning.

ar: قُلْ هُوَ نَبَؤٌا۟ عَظِيمٌ
en: Say, “This ˹Quran˺ is momentous news,
t1: Say: ‘That (Day of Rising) is the tremendous piece of news.
t2: Say: ’It is a mighty tiding
t3: Say: It is tremendous tidings

ar: أَنتُمْ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضُونَ
en: from which you ˹pagans˺ are turning away.”
t1: You have turned your faces away from it.
t2: from which you are turning away.
t3: Whence ye turn away!

ar: مَا كَانَ لِىَ مِنْ عِلْمٍۭ بِٱلْمَلَإِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰٓ إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ
en: ˹And say,˺ “I had no knowledge of the highest assembly ˹in heaven˺ when they differed ˹concerning Adam˺.
t1: I did not know of the Supreme Assembly (of angels on my own) when they were holding discussions (about the creation of Adam).
t2: I had no knowledge of the High Council when they disputed.
t3: I had no knowledge of the Highest Chiefs when they disputed;

ar: إِن يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ إِلَّآ أَنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ نَذِيرٌۭ مُّبِينٌ
en: What is revealed to me is that I am only sent with a clear warning.”
t1: The only Revelation that is sent to me (from Allah) is that I am but a clear and straight Warner.’
t2: This alone is revealed to me, that I am only a clear warner.’
t3: It is revealed unto me only that I may be a plain warner.

ar: إِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى خَٰلِقٌۢ بَشَرًۭا مِّن طِينٍۢ
en: ˹Remember, O  Prophet˺ when your Lord said to the angels, “I am going to create a human being from clay.
t1: (Recall) when your Lord said to the angels: ‘I am about to create a human organism from (moist) clay.
t2: When thy Lord said to the angels, ’See, I am creating a mortal of a clay.
t3: When thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to create a mortal out of mire,

ar: فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُۥ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِى فَقَعُوا۟ لَهُۥ سَٰجِدِينَ
en: So when I have fashioned him and had a spirit of My Own ˹creation˺ breathed into him, fall down in prostration to him.”
t1: Then when I have perfected its (visible body) and blown into its (invisible) self My Own (illumining) spirit, fall down prostrate before him (in his honour).’
t2: When I have shaped him, and breathed My spirit in him, fall you down, bowing before him!’
t3: And when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My Spirit, then fall down before him prostrate,

ar: فَسَجَدَ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ
en: So the angels prostrated all together—
t1: So all the angels fell down together prostrating themselves before him,
t2: Then the angels bowed themselves all together,
t3: The angels fell down prostrate, every one,

ar: إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ ٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
en: but not Iblis, becoming unfaithful.
t1: Except Iblis. He showed arrogance (against the dignity of the Prophet) and became one of the disbelievers.
t2: save Iblis; he waxed proud, and was one of the unbelievers.
t3: Saving Iblis; he was scornful and became one of the disbelievers.

ar: قَالَ يَٰٓإِبْلِيسُ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَن تَسْجُدَ لِمَا خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَىَّ ۖ أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ أَمْ كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلْعَالِينَ
en: Allah asked, “O Iblis! What prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My Own Hands? Did you ˹just˺ become proud? Or have you always been arrogant?”
t1: (Allah) said: ‘O Iblis, what has prevented you from falling down prostrate before this (exalted person) whom I have created with My Own (Benevolent) Hand? Did you show arrogance (to him), or were you (presuming yourself) high ranking?’
t2: Said He, ’Iblis, what prevented thee to bow thyself before that I created with My own hands? Hast thou waxed proud, or art thou of the lofty ones?’
t3: He said: O Iblis! What hindereth thee from falling prostrate before that which I have created with both My hands ? Art thou too proud or art thou of the high exalted ?

ar: قَالَ أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْهُ ۖ خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍۢ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍۢ
en: He replied, “I am better than he is: You created me from fire and him from clay.”
t1: (Comparing himself with the Prophet,) he said: ‘I am better than he. You have created me from fire and You have created him from clay.’
t2: Said he, ’I am better than he; Thou createdst me of tire, and him Thou createdst of clay.’
t3: He said: I am better than him. Thou createdst me of fire, whilst him Thou didst create of clay.

ar: قَالَ فَٱخْرُجْ مِنْهَا فَإِنَّكَ رَجِيمٌۭ
en: Allah commanded, “Then get out of Paradise, for you are truly cursed.
t1: Allah said: ‘So get out from here (for the sin of insolence against the Prophet). Surely, you are rejected.
t2: Said He, ’Then go thou forth hence; thou art accursed.
t3: He said: Go forth from hence, for lo! thou art outcast,

ar: وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ لَعْنَتِىٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ
en: And surely upon you is My condemnation until the Day of Judgment.”
t1: And surely, My curse is on you till the Day of Resurrection.’
t2: Upon thee shall rest My curse, till the Day of Doom.’
t3: And lo! My curse is on thee till the Day of Judgment.

ar: قَالَ رَبِّ فَأَنظِرْنِىٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
en: Satan appealed, “My Lord! Then delay my end until the Day of their resurrection.”
t1: He said: ‘O Lord, then give me respite (to remain alive) till the Day when they are raised alive from the graves.’
t2: Said he, ’My Lord, respite me till the day they shall be raised.’
t3: He said: My Lord! Reprieve me till the day when they are raised.

ar: قَالَ فَإِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنظَرِينَ
en: Allah said, “You will be delayed
t1: Allah said: ‘(Be off;) you are surely of those who are granted respite,
t2: Said He, ’Thou art among the ones that are respited
t3: He said: Lo! thou art of those reprieved

ar: إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْوَقْتِ ٱلْمَعْلُومِ
en: until the appointed Day.”
t1: Till the Day of the time which is appointed (and known).’
t2: until the day of the known time.’
t3: Until the day of the time appointed.

ar: قَالَ فَبِعِزَّتِكَ لَأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
en: Satan said, “By Your Glory! I will certainly mislead them all,
t1: He said: ‘By Your Honour, I shall certainly turn all of them away from the straight path with persistence,
t2: Said he, ’Now, by Thy glory, I shall pervert them all together,
t3: He said: Then, by Thy might, I surely will beguile them every one,

ar: إِلَّا عِبَادَكَ مِنْهُمُ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
en: except Your chosen servants among them.”
t1: Except those of Your servants who are chosen and exalted ones.’
t2: excepting those Thy servants among them that are sincere.’
t3: Save Thy single-minded slaves among them.

ar: قَالَ فَٱلْحَقُّ وَٱلْحَقَّ أَقُولُ
en: Allah concluded, “The truth is—and I ˹only˺ say the truth—:
t1: Allah said: ‘So the truth is (this), and the truth I say,
t2: Said He, ’This is the truth, and the truth I say;
t3: He said: The Truth is, and the Truth I speak,

ar: لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكَ وَمِمَّن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
en: I will surely fill up Hell with you and whoever follows you from among them, all together.”
t1: That I will fill Hell with you and with all those who will follow your (denigrating mindset).’
t2: I shall assuredly fill Gehenna with thee, and with whosoever of them follows thee, all together.’
t3: That I shall fill hell with thee and with such of them as follow thee, together.

ar: قُلْ مَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍۢ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلْمُتَكَلِّفِينَ
en: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹Quran˺, nor do I pretend to be someone I am not.
t1: Say: ‘I do not ask you for any reward for this (preaching of the truth), nor am I of those who pretend.
t2: Say: ’I ask of you no wage for it, neither am I of those who take things upon themselves.
t3: Say (O Muhammad, unto mankind): I ask of you no fee for this, and I am no simulating.

ar: إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌۭ لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: It is only a reminder to the whole world.
t1: This (Qur’an) is only direction and guidance for the whole world.
t2: It is nothing but a reminder unto all beings,
t3: Lo! it is naught else than a reminder for all peoples

ar: وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ نَبَأَهُۥ بَعْدَ حِينٍۭ
en: And you will certainly know its truth before long.”
t1: And you will yourselves come to know its truth after a while.’
t2: and you shall surely know its tiding after a while.’
t3: And ye will come in time to know the truth thereof.

ar: تَنزِيلُ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ
en: The revelation of this Book is from Allah—the Almighty, All-Wise.
t1: The revelation of this Book is from Allah, the Lord of Honour, All-Wise.
t2: The sending down of the Book is from God the All-mighty, the All-wise.
t3: The revelation of the Scripture is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.

ar: إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ بِٱلْحَقِّ فَٱعْبُدِ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصًۭا لَّهُ ٱلدِّينَ
en: Indeed, We have sent down the Book to you ˹O Prophet˺ in truth, so worship Allah ˹alone˺, being sincerely devoted to Him.
t1: Surely, We have revealed (this) Book to you with the truth. So worship Allah for His sake alone in sincere obedience.
t2: We have sent down to thee the Book with the truth; so worship God, making thy religion His sincerely.
t3: Lo! We have revealed the Scripture unto thee (Muhammad) with truth; so worship Allah, making religion pure for Him (only).

ar: أَلَا لِلَّهِ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْخَالِصُ ۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ أَوْلِيَآءَ مَا نَعْبُدُهُمْ إِلَّا لِيُقَرِّبُونَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ زُلْفَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ فِى مَا هُمْ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَنْ هُوَ كَٰذِبٌۭ كَفَّارٌۭ
en: Indeed, sincere devotion is due ˹only˺ to Allah. As for those who take other lords besides Him, ˹saying,˺ “We worship them only so they may bring us closer to Allah,” surely Allah will judge between all regarding what they differed about. Allah certainly does not guide whoever persists in lying and disbelief.
t1: (Say to the people:) ‘Listen! Sincere obedience and worship is only Allah’s due.’ And those (disbelievers) who have taken (idols as) helpers other than Allah (say in false justification of their idol-worship:) ‘We worship them only that they may bring us near to Allah.’ Surely, Allah will judge between them concerning the matter in which they differ. Certainly, Allah does not give guidance to the one who is a liar and highly ungrateful.
t2: Belongs not sincere religion to God? And those who take protectors, apart from Him -- ’We only serve them that they may bring us nigh in nearness to God’ -- surely God shall judge between them touching that whereon they are at variance. Surely God guides not him who is a liar, unthankful.
t3: Surely pure religion is for Allah only. And those who choose protecting friends beside Him (say): We worship them only that they may bring us near unto Allah. Lo! Allah will judge between them concerning that wherein they differ. Lo! Allah guideth not him who is a liar, an ingrate.

ar: لَّوْ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدًۭا لَّٱصْطَفَىٰ مِمَّا يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ ۚ سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ ۖ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْوَٰحِدُ ٱلْقَهَّارُ
en: Had it been Allah’s Will to have offspring, He could have chosen whatever He willed of His creation. Glory be to Him! He is Allah—the One, the Supreme.
t1: Had Allah willed to beget children (for Himself), He would have chosen whom He liked out of His Creation. Glory be to Him, He is Allah, the One, the All-Dominant.
t2: Had God desired to take to Him a son, He would have chosen whatever He willed of that He has created. Glory be to Him! He is God, the One, the Omnipotent.
t3: If Allah had willed to choose a son, He could have chosen what He would of that which He hath created. Be He Glorified! He is Allah, the One, the Absolute.

ar: خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ بِٱلْحَقِّ ۖ يُكَوِّرُ ٱلَّيْلَ عَلَى ٱلنَّهَارِ وَيُكَوِّرُ ٱلنَّهَارَ عَلَى ٱلَّيْلِ ۖ وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ ۖ كُلٌّۭ يَجْرِى لِأَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّى ۗ أَلَا هُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْغَفَّٰرُ
en: He created the heavens and the earth for a purpose. He wraps the night around the day, and wraps the day around the night. And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each orbiting for an appointed term. He is truly the Almighty, Most Forgiving.
t1: He created the heavens and the earth with a decreed celestial order and planning. He causes the night to overlap the day and the day to overlap the night. And He is the One Who has subjected the sun and the moon (to a system). Each (star and planet) rotates in its orbit till an appointed time. Beware! He is the One Who is All-Dominant (over the entire system), the Most Forgiving.
t2: He created the heavens and the earth in truth, wrapping night about the day, and wrapping the day about the night; and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each of them running to a stated term. Is not He the All-mighty, the All-forgiving?
t3: He hath created the heavens and the earth with truth. He maketh night to succeed day, and He maketh day to succeed night, and He constraineth the sun and the moon to give service, each running on for an appointed term. Is not He the Mighty, the Forgiver ?

ar: خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍۢ وَٰحِدَةٍۢ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَأَنزَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ ثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَزْوَٰجٍۢ ۚ يَخْلُقُكُمْ فِى بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمْ خَلْقًۭا مِّنۢ بَعْدِ خَلْقٍۢ فِى ظُلُمَٰتٍۢ ثَلَٰثٍۢ ۚ ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ لَهُ ٱلْمُلْكُ ۖ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُصْرَفُونَ
en: He created you ˹all˺ from a single soul, That is Allah—your Lord! All authority belongs to Him. There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. How can you then be turned away?
t1: He has created all of you from a single life cell, and then made from it a similar pair. And then He brought about for you eight living animals in pairs. He shapes you in the wombs of your mothers from one creative phase into the next in sequence and (completes this process) in three (germinal) layers. This is Allah, your Lord, to Whom belongs all Power and Authority. There is no God except He. Where then are you deviated (and disoriented after knowing these concealed realities of creation)?
t2: He created you of a single soul, then from it He appointed its mate; and He sent down to you of the cattle eight couples. He creates you in your mothers’ wombs creation after creation in threefold shadows. That then is God, your Lord; to Him belongs the Kingdom; there is no god but He; so how are you turned about?
t3: He created you from one being, then from that (being) He made its mate; and He hath provided for you of cattle eight kinds. He created you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in a threefold gloom. Such is Allah, your Lord. His is the Sovereignty. There is no God save Him. How then are ye turned away ?

ar: إِن تَكْفُرُوا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِىٌّ عَنكُمْ ۖ وَلَا يَرْضَىٰ لِعِبَادِهِ ٱلْكُفْرَ ۖ وَإِن تَشْكُرُوا۟ يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ ۗ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌۭ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ ۗ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُم مَّرْجِعُكُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمٌۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
en: If you disbelieve, then ˹know that˺ Allah is truly not in need of you, nor does He approve of disbelief from His servants. But if you become grateful ˹through faith˺, He will appreciate that from you. No soul burdened with sin will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. He certainly knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart.
t1: If you disbelieve, then surely Allah is Self-Sufficient and He does not like disbelief (and ingratitude) for His servants, and if you give thanks, (so) He likes that for you. And no bearer of burden will bear the burden of any other. Then you have to return to your Lord. Then He will inform you of the deeds which you used to do. Surely, He knows best the secrets of the hearts.
t2: If you are unthankful, God is independent of you, yet He approves not unthankfulness in His servants; but if you are thankful, He will approve it in you. And no soul laden bears the load of another. Then to your Lord shall you return, and He will tell you what you have been doing. He knows the thoughts within the breasts.
t3: If ye are thankless, yet Allah is Independent of you, though He is not pleased with thanklessness for His bondmen; and if ye are thankful He is pleased therewith for you. No laden soul will bear another’s load. Then unto your Lord is your return; and He will tell you what ye used to do. Lo! He knoweth what is in the breasts (of men).

ar: ۞ وَإِذَا مَسَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ ضُرٌّۭ دَعَا رَبَّهُۥ مُنِيبًا إِلَيْهِ ثُمَّ إِذَا خَوَّلَهُۥ نِعْمَةًۭ مِّنْهُ نَسِىَ مَا كَانَ يَدْعُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِ مِن قَبْلُ وَجَعَلَ لِلَّهِ أَندَادًۭا لِّيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ ۚ قُلْ تَمَتَّعْ بِكُفْرِكَ قَلِيلًا ۖ إِنَّكَ مِنْ أَصْحَٰبِ ٱلنَّارِ
en: When one is touched with hardship, they cry out to their Lord, turning to Him ˹alone˺. But as soon as He showers them with blessings from Him, they ˹totally˺ forget the One they had cried to earlier, and set up equals to Allah to mislead ˹others˺ from His Way. Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Enjoy your disbelief for a little while! You will certainly be one of the inmates of the Fire.”
t1: And when some suffering afflicts man, he turns to his Lord and cries out. Then when (Allah) grants him some blessing from Himself, he forgets that (suffering) which he used to beseech relief from. And (then) he sets up (idols) as partners with Allah to make (others also) lose His way. Say: ‘(O disbeliever,) profit a little (worldly gain) from your disbelief; you are certainly of the inmates of Hell.
t2: When some affliction visits a man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to him; then when He confers on him a blessing from Him he forgets that he was calling to before and sets up compeers to God, to lead astray from His way. Say: ’Enjoy thy unbelief a little; thou shalt be among the inhabitants of the Fire.’
t3: And when some hurt toucheth man, he crieth unto his Lord, turning unto Him (repentant). Then, when He granteth him a boon from Him he forgetteth that for which he cried unto Him before, and setteth up rivals to Allah that he may beguile (men) from his way. Say (O Muhammad, unto such an one): Take pleasure in thy disbelief a while. Lo! thou art of the owners of the Fire.

ar: أَمَّنْ هُوَ قَٰنِتٌ ءَانَآءَ ٱلَّيْلِ سَاجِدًۭا وَقَآئِمًۭا يَحْذَرُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ وَيَرْجُوا۟ رَحْمَةَ رَبِّهِۦ ۗ قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِى ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ ۗ إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ
en: ˹Are they better˺ or those who worship ˹their Lord˺ devoutly in the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of their Lord? Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Are those who know equal to those who do not know?” None will be mindful ˹of this˺ except people of reason.
t1: Well! (Is this polytheist better or) that (believer) who worships during the hours of the night standing and in prostration, lives in fear of the Hereafter and expects mercy from his Lord?’ Say: ‘Can those who have knowledge and those who do not be alike?’ So only the wise do receive the admonition.
t2: Or is he who is obedient in the watches of the night, bowing himself and standing, he being afraid of the world to come and hoping for the mercy of his Lord . . ? Say: ’Are they equal -- those who know and those who know not?’ Only men possessed of minds remember.
t3: Is he who payeth adoration in the watches of the night, prostrate and standing, bewaring of the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, (to be accounted equal with a disbeliever) ? Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Are those who know equal with those who know not ? But only men of understanding will pay heed.

ar: قُلْ يَٰعِبَادِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱتَّقُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ ۚ لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا۟ فِى هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةٌۭ ۗ وَأَرْضُ ٱللَّهِ وَٰسِعَةٌ ۗ إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى ٱلصَّٰبِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍۢ
en: Say ˹O Prophet, that Allah says˺, “O My servants who believe! Be mindful of your Lord. Those who do good in this world will have a good reward. And Allah’s earth is spacious. Only those who endure patiently will be given their reward without limit.”
t1: (O Beloved,) say (on My behalf), ‘O My servants, you who have believed, adopt Godwariness; it is for the men of spiritual excellence in this world that there is excellent reward. And Allah’s earth is vast. So the steadfast will certainly be given their reward without measure.’
t2: Say: ’My servants who believe, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world good, and God’s earth is wide. Surely the patient will be paid their wages in full without reckoning.’
t3: Say: O My bondmen who believe! Observe your duty to your Lord. For those who do good in this world there is good, and Allah’s earth is spacious. Verily the steadfast will be paid their wages without stint.

ar: قُلْ إِنِّىٓ أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصًۭا لَّهُ ٱلدِّينَ
en: Say, “I am commanded to worship Allah, being sincerely devoted to Him ˹alone˺.
t1: Say: ‘I have been commanded to worship Allah in sincerest obedience and devotion to Him alone.’
t2: Say: ’I have been commanded to serve God making my religion His sincerely;
t3: Say (O Muhammad): Lo! I am commanded to worship Allah, making religion pure for Him (only).

ar: وَأُمِرْتُ لِأَنْ أَكُونَ أَوَّلَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ
en: And I am commanded to be the first of those who submit ˹to His Will˺.”
t1: And I was (also) commanded to become the first Muslim of all (His creation).
t2: and I have been commanded to be the first of those that surrender.’
t3: And I am commanded to be the first of those who are muslims (surrender unto Him).

ar: قُلْ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ إِنْ عَصَيْتُ رَبِّى عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍۢ
en: Say, “I truly fear—if I were to disobey my Lord—the torment of a tremendous Day.”
t1: Say: ‘If I disobeyed My Lord, I would fear the torment of a Terrible Day.’
t2: Say: ’Truly I fear, if I should rebel against my Lord, the chastisement of a dreadful day.’
t3: Say: Lo! if I should disobey my Lord, I fear the doom of a tremendous Day.

ar: قُلِ ٱللَّهَ أَعْبُدُ مُخْلِصًۭا لَّهُۥ دِينِى
en: Say, “It is ˹only˺ Allah that I worship, being sincere in my devotion to Him.
t1: Say: ‘I worship Allah alone making obedience purely for Him.
t2: Say: ’God I serve, making my religion His sincerely;
t3: Say: Allah I worship, making my religion pure for Him (only).

ar: فَٱعْبُدُوا۟ مَا شِئْتُم مِّن دُونِهِۦ ۗ قُلْ إِنَّ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ وَأَهْلِيهِمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ ۗ أَلَا ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلْخُسْرَانُ ٱلْمُبِينُ
en: Worship then whatever ˹gods˺ you want instead of Him.” Say, “The ˹true˺ losers are those who will lose themselves and their families on Judgment Day. That is indeed the clearest loss.”
t1: So worship what you like besides Allah.’ Say: ‘Surely, losers are only those who will bring loss to their own souls and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Remember! That truly is the manifest loss.
t2: so serve what you will apart from Him.’ Say: ’Surely the losers are they who lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection; is not that the manifest loss?
t3: Then worship what ye will beside Him. Say: The losers will be those who lose themselves and their housefolk on the Day of Resurrection. Ah, that will be the manifest loss!

ar: لَهُم مِّن فَوْقِهِمْ ظُلَلٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ وَمِن تَحْتِهِمْ ظُلَلٌۭ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ يُخَوِّفُ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦ عِبَادَهُۥ ۚ يَٰعِبَادِ فَٱتَّقُونِ
en: They will have layers of fire above and below them. That is what Allah warns His servants with. So fear Me, O  My servants!
t1: For them there will be clouds of fire (as covers) over them and pavements of fire beneath them too. This is (the torment) with which Allah warns His servants.’ O My servants! Always fear Me.
t2: Above them they shall have overshadowings. of the Fire, and underneath them overshadowings; that it is wherewith God frightens His servants: "O My servants, so fear you Me!"’
t3: They have an awning of fire above them and beneath them a dais (of fire). With this doth Allah appal His bondmen. O My bondmen, therefor fear Me!

ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱجْتَنَبُوا۟ ٱلطَّٰغُوتَ أَن يَعْبُدُوهَا وَأَنَابُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ لَهُمُ ٱلْبُشْرَىٰ ۚ فَبَشِّرْ عِبَادِ
en: And those who shun the worship of false gods, turning to Allah ˹alone˺, will have good news. So give good news to My servants ˹O Prophet˺—
t1: And those who kept off from idol-worship and turned to Allah, for them is good news. So give glad tidings to My servants.
t2: Those who eschew the serving of idols and turn penitent to God, for them is good tidings! So give thou good tidings to My servants
t3: And those who put away false gods lest they should worship them and turn to Allah in repentance, for them there are glad tidings. Therefor give good tidings (O Muhammad) to My bondmen

ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَمِعُونَ ٱلْقَوْلَ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ أَحْسَنَهُۥٓ ۚ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ ۖ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمْ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ
en: those who listen to what is said and follow the best of it. These are the ones ˹rightly˺ guided by Allah, and these are ˹truly˺ the people of reason.
t1: Those who listen attentively to what is said, then follow the best in it, it is they whom Allah has given guidance, and it is they who have wisdom.
t2: who give ear to the Word and follow the fairest of it. Those are they whom God has guided; those -- they are men possessed of minds.
t3: Who hear advice and follow the best thereof. Such are those whom Allah guideth, and such are men of understanding.

ar: أَفَمَنْ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ كَلِمَةُ ٱلْعَذَابِ أَفَأَنتَ تُنقِذُ مَن فِى ٱلنَّارِ
en: What about those against whom the decree of torment has been justified? Is it you ˹O Prophet˺ who will then save those bound for the Fire?
t1: But can you save him for whom the command of torment has become due and who has become the inmate of Hell (for ever)?
t2: He against whom the word of chastisement is realized -- shalt thou deliver him out of the Fire?
t3: Is he on whom the word of doom is fulfilled (to be helped), and canst thou (O Muhammad) rescue him who is in the Fire ?

ar: لَٰكِنِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْا۟ رَبَّهُمْ لَهُمْ غُرَفٌۭ مِّن فَوْقِهَا غُرَفٌۭ مَّبْنِيَّةٌۭ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ ۖ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ ۖ لَا يُخْلِفُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمِيعَادَ
en: But those mindful of their Lord will have ˹elevated˺ mansions, built one above the other, under which rivers flow. ˹That is˺ the promise of Allah. ˹And˺ Allah never fails in ˹His˺ promise.
t1: But for those who fear their Lord are lofty palaces (in Paradise) with lofty mansions built over and rivers flowing beneath. This is Allah’s promise. Allah does not go against His promise.
t2: But those who fear their Lord -- for them await lofty chambers, above which are built lofty chambers, underneath which rivers flow -- God’s promise; God fails not the tryst.
t3: But those who keep their duty to their Lord, for them are lofty halls with lofty halls above them, built (for them), beneath which rivers flow. (It is) a promise of Allah. Allah faileth not His promise.

ar: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ فَسَلَكَهُۥ يَنَٰبِيعَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ يُخْرِجُ بِهِۦ زَرْعًۭا مُّخْتَلِفًا أَلْوَٰنُهُۥ ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَرَىٰهُ مُصْفَرًّۭا ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُۥ حُطَٰمًا ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَذِكْرَىٰ لِأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ
