ar: وَلَمَّا جَآءَ عِيسَىٰ بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ قَالَ قَدْ جِئْتُكُم بِٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَلِأُبَيِّنَ لَكُم بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِى تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ ۖ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
en: When Jesus came with clear proofs, he declared, “I have come to you with wisdom, and to clarify to you some of what you differ about. So fear Allah, and obey me.
t1: And when ‘Isa (Jesus) came with evident signs, he said: ‘Surely, I have come to you with wisdom and understanding, and (with the purpose) that I may make clear to you some of the matters on which you disagree. So fear Allah and obey me.
t2: And when Jesus came with the clear signs he said, ’I have come to you with wisdom, and that I may make clear to you some of that whereon you are at variance; so fear you God and obey you me.
t3: When Jesus came with clear proofs (of Allah’s Sovereignty), he said: I have come unto you with wisdom, and to make plain some of that concerning which ye differ. So keep your duty to Allah, and obey me.

ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ رَبِّى وَرَبُّكُمْ فَٱعْبُدُوهُ ۚ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطٌۭ مُّسْتَقِيمٌۭ
en: Surely Allah ˹alone˺ is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him ˹alone˺. This is the Straight Path.”
t1: Surely, Allah is the One Who is your Lord and my Lord (as well). So worship Him alone. That is the only straight path.’
t2: Assuredly God is my Lord and your Lord; therefore serve Him; this is a straight path.’
t3: Lo! Allah, He is my Lord and your Lord. So worship Him. This is a right path.

ar: فَٱخْتَلَفَ ٱلْأَحْزَابُ مِنۢ بَيْنِهِمْ ۖ فَوَيْلٌۭ لِّلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ
en: Yet their ˹various˺ groups have differed among themselves ˹about him˺, so woe to the wrongdoers when they face the torment of a painful Day!
t1: Then various sects cropped up amongst them. So those who did wrong, woe to them on account of the torment of a grievous Day!
t2: But the parties among them fell into variance; so woe unto those who did evil, because of the chastisement of a painful day.
t3: But the factions among them differed. Then woe unto those who do wrong from the doom of a painful day.

ar: هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّا ٱلسَّاعَةَ أَن تَأْتِيَهُم بَغْتَةًۭ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
en: Are they waiting for the Hour to take them by surprise when they least expect ˹it˺?
t1: What are they waiting for (save) the Hour that should seize them all of a sudden whilst they have no awareness of it?
t2: Are they looking for aught but the Hour, that it shall come upon them suddenly, when they are not aware?
t3: Await they aught save the Hour, that it shall come upon them suddenly, when they know not ?

ar: ٱلْأَخِلَّآءُ يَوْمَئِذٍۭ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ إِلَّا ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ
en: Close friends will be enemies to one another on that Day, except the righteous,
t1: On that Day, all friends and acquaintances will become enemies to one another except the pious. (Only their friendship and nearness [wilaya] will prove fruitful.)
t2: Friends on that day shall be foes to one another, but the god-fearing.
t3: Friends on that day will be foes one to another, save those who kept their duty (to Allah).

ar: يَٰعِبَادِ لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ وَلَآ أَنتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ
en: ˹who will be told,˺ “O My servants! There is no fear for you Today, nor will you grieve—
t1: (It will be said to them:) ‘O My (intimate) servants, there is no fear for you this Day, nor shall you grieve.’
t2: ’O My servants, today no fear is on you, neither do you sorrow’ --
t3: O My slaves! For you there is no fear this day, nor is it ye who grieve;

ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَكَانُوا۟ مُسْلِمِينَ
en: ˹those˺ who believed in Our signs and ˹fully˺ submitted ˹to Us˺.
t1: (It is) they who believed in Our Revelations and were always obedient (to Us).
t2: even those who believed in Our signs, and had surrendered themselves
t3: (Ye) who believed Our revelations and were self-surrendered,

ar: ٱدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْجَنَّةَ أَنتُمْ وَأَزْوَٰجُكُمْ تُحْبَرُونَ
en: Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, rejoicing.”
t1: Enter Paradise, you and your intimate companions* (all); you will be honoured (with blessings, comforts and the pleasures of Paradise).
t2: ’Enter Paradise, you and your wives, walking with joy!’
t3: Enter the Garden, ye and your wives, to be made glad.

ar: يُطَافُ عَلَيْهِم بِصِحَافٍۢ مِّن ذَهَبٍۢ وَأَكْوَابٍۢ ۖ وَفِيهَا مَا تَشْتَهِيهِ ٱلْأَنفُسُ وَتَلَذُّ ٱلْأَعْيُنُ ۖ وَأَنتُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
en: Golden trays and cups will be passed around to them. There will be whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in. And you will be there forever.
t1: The plates and drinking cups made of gold will be passed around amongst them, and all those things which the hearts will long for, and (that which) will cool the eyes will be available there. And you will dwell there forever.
t2: There shall be passed around them platters of gold, and cups, therein being whatever the souls desire, and the eyes delight in. ’And therein, you shall dwell forever.
t3: Therein are brought round for them trays of gold and goblets, and therein is all that souls desire and eyes find sweet. And ye are immortal therein.

ar: وَتِلْكَ ٱلْجَنَّةُ ٱلَّتِىٓ أُورِثْتُمُوهَا بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
en: That is the Paradise which you will be awarded for what you used to do.
t1: And, (O Godfearing folk,) this is the Paradise of which you have been made the owners, a recompense of those (works) which you used to do.
t2: This is the Paradise that you have been given for an inheritance for the things that you were doing.
t3: This is the Garden which ye are made to inherit because of what ye used to do.

ar: لَكُمْ فِيهَا فَٰكِهَةٌۭ كَثِيرَةٌۭ مِّنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ
en: There you will have abundant fruit to eat from.
t1: There are abundant fruits in it for you to eat.
t2: Therein you have abundant fruits, whereof you may eat.’
t3: Therein for you is fruit in plenty whence to eat.

ar: إِنَّ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ فِى عَذَابِ جَهَنَّمَ خَٰلِدُونَ
en: Indeed, the wicked will be in the torment of Hell forever.
t1: Indeed, the sinners will live forever in the torment of Hell,
t2: But the evildoers dwell forever in the chastisement of Gehenna
t3: Lo! the guilty are immortal in hell’s torment.

ar: لَا يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ وَهُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ
en: It will never be lightened for them, and there they will be overwhelmed with despair.
t1: Which will never be decreased for them, and they will be lying there in endless despair.
t2: that is not abated for them and therein they are sore confounded.
t3: It is not relaxed for them, and they despair therein.

ar: وَمَا ظَلَمْنَٰهُمْ وَلَٰكِن كَانُوا۟ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
en: We did not wrong them, but it was they who were the wrongdoers.
t1: And We have not wronged them, but they were themselves the wrongdoers.
t2: We never wronged them, but they themselves did the wrong.
t3: We wronged them not, but they it was who did the wrong.

ar: وَنَادَوْا۟ يَٰمَٰلِكُ لِيَقْضِ عَلَيْنَا رَبُّكَ ۖ قَالَ إِنَّكُم مَّٰكِثُونَ
en: They will cry, “O Malik! Let your Lord finish us off.” He will answer, “You are definitely here to stay.”
t1: And they will cry out (to the guard of Hell): ‘O master, (better it is if) your Lord causes us to die.’ He will say: ‘(Now) you will live (in the same plight) forever.’
t2: And they shall call, ’O Malik, let thy Lord have done with us!’ He will say, ’You will surely tarry.’
t3: And they cry: O master! Let thy Lord make an end of us. He saith: Lo! here ye must remain.

ar: لَقَدْ جِئْنَٰكُم بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ لِلْحَقِّ كَٰرِهُونَ
en: We certainly brought the truth to you, but most of you were resentful of the truth.
t1: Surely, We brought you the truth, but most of you disliked the truth.
t2: ’We brought you the truth, but most of you were averse to the truth.’
t3: We verily brought the Truth unto you, but ye were, most of you, averse to the Truth.

ar: أَمْ أَبْرَمُوٓا۟ أَمْرًۭا فَإِنَّا مُبْرِمُونَ
en: Or have they mastered some ˹evil˺ plan? Then We ˹too˺ are surely planning.
t1: Have they (the disbelievers of Mecca) finalized (any scheme against the Messenger [blessings and peace be upon him])? So We (too) are going to take the ultimate decision.
t2: Or have they contrived some matter? We too are contriving.
t3: Or do they determine any thing (against the Prophet) ? Lo! We (also) are determining.

ar: أَمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّا لَا نَسْمَعُ سِرَّهُمْ وَنَجْوَىٰهُم ۚ بَلَىٰ وَرُسُلُنَا لَدَيْهِمْ يَكْتُبُونَ
en: Or do they think that We do not hear their ˹evil˺ thoughts and secret talks? Yes ˹We do˺! And Our messenger-angels are in their presence, recording ˹it all˺.
t1: Do they think that We do not hear their secret talk and whisperings? Why not? (We do listen.) And the angels sent by Us also remain with them, writing.
t2: Or do they think We hear not their secret and what they conspire together? Yes indeed, and Our messengers are present with them writing it down.
t3: Or deem they that We cannot hear their secret thoughts and private confidences ? Nay, but Our envoys, present with them, do record.

ar: قُلْ إِن كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ وَلَدٌۭ فَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلْعَٰبِدِينَ
en: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “If the Most Compassionate ˹really˺ had offspring, I would be the first worshipper.”
t1: Say: ‘If (supposing the impossible) the Most Kind (Lord) had a son (or children), I would have been the first one to worship (him).’
t2: Say: ’If the All-merciful has a son, then I am the first to serve him.
t3: Say (O Muhammad): If the Beneficent One hath a son, then, I shall be first among the worshippers. (But there is no son).

ar: سُبْحَٰنَ رَبِّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَرْشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
en: Glorified is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, far above what they claim.
t1: The Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, Glory be to Him, Transcendent above all what they ascribe (to Him).
t2: Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above that they describe.’
t3: Glorified be the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, from that which they ascribe (unto Him)!

ar: فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُوا۟ وَيَلْعَبُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ يُلَٰقُوا۟ يَوْمَهُمُ ٱلَّذِى يُوعَدُونَ
en: So let them indulge ˹in falsehood˺ and amuse ˹themselves˺ until they face their Day, which they have been warned of.
t1: So leave them. Let them remain indulged in vain talk and absurd sport until they meet the Day which they are promised.
t2: Then leave them alone to plunge and play, until they encounter that day of theirs which they are promised.
t3: So let them flounder (in their talk) and play until they meet the Day which they are promised.

ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِلَٰهٌۭ وَفِى ٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَٰهٌۭ ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
en: It is He Who is ˹the only˺ God in the heavens and ˹the only˺ God on the earth. For He is the All-Wise, All-Knowing.
t1: And He is the One Who is God in the heaven and God in the earth (as well) and He is Most Wise, All-Knowing.
t2: And it is He who in heaven is God and in earth is God; He is the All-wise, the All-knowing.
t3: And He it is Who in the heaven is God, and in the earth God. He is the Wise, the Knower.

ar: وَتَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِى لَهُۥ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَعِندَهُۥ عِلْمُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
en: And Blessed is the One to Whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and everything in between! With Him ˹alone˺ is the knowledge of the Hour. And to Him you will ˹all˺ be returned.
t1: And Most Blessed is He to Whom belongs the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and (also of all) that is between them. And He has the knowledge of the Last Hour (as well), and you will be returned to Him alone.
t2: Glory be to Him, to whom belongs the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and all that between them is; with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you shall be returned.
t3: And blessed be He unto Whom belongeth the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, and with Whom is knowledge of the Hour, and unto Whom ye will be returned.

ar: وَلَا يَمْلِكُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةَ إِلَّا مَن شَهِدَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ
en: ˹But˺ those ˹objects of worship˺ they invoke besides Him have no power to intercede, except those who testify to the truth knowingly.
t1: And those whom they (the disbelievers) worship instead of Allah have no power to intercede. But, (on the contrary, they do have the power of intercession) who bear witness to the truth, and they also know it (with certitude).
t2: Those they call upon, apart from Him, have no power of intercession, save such as have testified to the truth, and that knowingly.
t3: And those unto whom they cry instead of Him possess no power of intercession, saving him who beareth witness unto the Truth knowingly.

ar: وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُم مَّنْ خَلَقَهُمْ لَيَقُولُنَّ ٱللَّهُ ۖ فَأَنَّىٰ يُؤْفَكُونَ
en: If you ask them ˹O Prophet˺ who created them, they will certainly say, “Allah!” How can they then be deluded ˹from the truth˺?
t1: And if you ask them: ‘Who has created them?’ they will certainly say: ‘Allah.’ Then where are they wandering disorientated?
t2: If thou askest them, ’Who created you?’ they will say, ’God.’ How then are they perverted?
t3: And if thou ask them who created them, they will surely say: Allah. How then are they turned away ?

ar: وَقِيلِهِۦ يَٰرَبِّ إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ قَوْمٌۭ لَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ
en: ˹Allah is Aware of˺ the Prophet’s cry: “O my Lord! Indeed, these are a people who persist in disbelief.”
t1: And by his (Esteemed Messenger’s) saying: ‘O Lord, surely, they are a people who (somehow) do not tend to believe.’
t2: And for his saying, ’My Lord, surely these are a people who believe not’ --
t3: And he saith: O my Lord! Lo! these are a folk who believe not.

ar: فَٱصْفَحْ عَنْهُمْ وَقُلْ سَلَٰمٌۭ ۚ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ
en: So bear with them and respond with peace. They will soon come to know.
t1: So, (O My Beloved,) turn your face away from them and say (like this: ‘Alright, our greeting is:) Peace!’ Then soon they will come to know (their end).
t2: yet pardon them, and say, ’Peace!’ Soon they will know.
t3: Then bear with them (O Muhammad) and say: Peace. But they will come to know.

ar: حمٓ
en: ha-Mĩm.
t1: Ha-Mim. (Only Allah and the Messenger [blessings and peace be upon him] know the real meaning.)
t2: Ha Mim
t3: Ha. Mim.

ar: وَٱلْكِتَٰبِ ٱلْمُبِينِ
en: By the clear Book!
t1: By this Light-Giving Book,
t2: By the Clear Book.
t3: By the Scripture that maketh plain

ar: إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ فِى لَيْلَةٍۢ مُّبَٰرَكَةٍ ۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ
en: Indeed, We sent it down on a blessed night, for We always warn ˹against evil˺.
t1: Surely, We have sent it down in a blessed night. Surely, We are the Warner.
t2: We have sent it down in a blessed night (We are ever warning)
t3: Lo! We revealed it on a blessed night - Lo! We are ever warning -

ar: فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ
en: On that night every matter of wisdom is ordained
t1: In this (night) judgment is given on all matters of wisdom (separately),
t2: therein every wise bidding
t3: Whereon every wise command is made clear

ar: أَمْرًۭا مِّنْ عِندِنَآ ۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ
en: by a command from Us, for We have always sent ˹messengers˺
t1: By Our command; surely, it is We Who send.
t2: determined as a bidding from Us, (We are ever sending)
t3: As a command from Our presence - Lo! We are ever sending -

ar: رَحْمَةًۭ مِّن رَّبِّكَ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
en: as a mercy from your Lord. He ˹alone˺ is truly the All-Hearing, All-Knowing—
t1: (It) is mercy from your Lord. Verily, He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing,
t2: as a mercy from thy Lord (surely He is the All-hearing, the All-knowing)
t3: A mercy from thy Lord. Lo! He, even He is the Hearer, the Knower,

ar: رَبِّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ ۖ إِن كُنتُم مُّوقِنِينَ
en: the Lord of the heavens and the earth and everything in between, if only you had sure faith.
t1: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, provided you have faith with certitude.
t2: Lord of the heavens and earth, and all that between them is if you have faith.
t3: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, if ye would be sure.

ar: لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ يُحْىِۦ وَيُمِيتُ ۖ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ ءَابَآئِكُمُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
en: There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. He ˹alone˺ gives life and causes death. ˹He is˺ your Lord, and the Lord of your forefathers.
t1: There is no God but He. He is the One Who gives life and causes death. He is your Lord and the Lord of your fathers (as well).
t2: There is no god but He; He gives life and makes to die; your Lord and the Lord of your fathers, the ancients.
t3: There is no God save Him. He quickeneth and giveth death; your Lord and Lord of your forefathers.

ar: بَلْ هُمْ فِى شَكٍّۢ يَلْعَبُونَ
en: In fact, they are in doubt, amusing themselves.
t1: Yet they are in doubt, busy playing.
t2: Nay, but they are in doubt, playing.
t3: Nay, but they play in doubt.

ar: فَٱرْتَقِبْ يَوْمَ تَأْتِى ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِدُخَانٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
en: Wait then ˹O Prophet˺ for the day ˹when˺ the sky will be veiled in haze, clearly visible,
t1: So wait for the Day when the sky will cause a clear smoke to appear,
t2: So be on the watch for a day when heaven shall bring a manifest smoke
t3: But watch thou (O Muhammad) for the day when the sky will produce visible smoke

ar: يَغْشَى ٱلنَّاسَ ۖ هَٰذَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌۭ
en: overwhelming the people. ˹They will cry,˺ “This is a painful torment.
t1: Which will envelop people (i.e., will encompass everything). That will be a painful torment.
t2: covering the people; this is a painful chastisement.
t3: That will envelop the people. This will be a painful torment.

ar: رَّبَّنَا ٱكْشِفْ عَنَّا ٱلْعَذَابَ إِنَّا مُؤْمِنُونَ
en: Our Lord! Remove ˹this˺ torment from us, ˹and˺ we will certainly believe.”
t1: (They will then say:) ‘O our Lord! Remove this torment from us. Surely, we believe.’
t2: ’O our Lord, remove Thou from us the chastisement; we are believers.’
t3: (Then they will say): Our Lord relieve us of the torment. Lo! we are believers.

ar: أَنَّىٰ لَهُمُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ وَقَدْ جَآءَهُمْ رَسُولٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
en: How can they be reminded when a messenger has already come to them, making things clear,
t1: How can their acceptance of the admonition now be (of any use), whereas there came to them a Messenger with a clear exposition?
t2: How should they have the Reminder, seeing a clear Messenger already came to them,
t3: How can there be remembrance for them, when a messenger making plain (the Truth) had already come unto them,

ar: ثُمَّ تَوَلَّوْا۟ عَنْهُ وَقَالُوا۟ مُعَلَّمٌۭ مَّجْنُونٌ
en: then they turned away from him, saying, “A madman, taught by others!”?
t1: But they turned their faces from him and (denigrating) they said: ‘(He) is a tutored madman.’
t2: then they turned away from him and said, ’A man tutored, possessed!’
t3: And they had turned away from him and said: One taught (by others), a madman ?

ar: إِنَّا كَاشِفُوا۟ ٱلْعَذَابِ قَلِيلًا ۚ إِنَّكُمْ عَآئِدُونَ
en: Indeed, We will remove ˹that˺ torment for a while, and you ˹Meccans˺ will return ˹to disbelief˺.
t1: Indeed, We remove the torment a little (but) you will certainly reiterate (the same disbelief).
t2: ’Behold, We are removing the chastisement a little; behold, you revert!’
t3: Lo! We withdraw the torment a little. Lo! ye return (to disbelief).

ar: يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ ٱلْبَطْشَةَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰٓ إِنَّا مُنتَقِمُونَ
en: ˹Then˺ on the Day We will deal ˹you˺ the fiercest blow, We will surely inflict punishment.
t1: The Day when We will seize with the Greatest Seizure, (that Day) We shall certainly exact revenge.
t2: Upon the day when We shall assault most mightily, then We shall take Our vengeance.
t3: On the day when We shall seize them with the greater seizure, (then) in truth We shall punish.

ar: ۞ وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَجَآءَهُمْ رَسُولٌۭ كَرِيمٌ
en: Indeed, before them We tested Pharaoh’s people: a noble messenger came to them,
t1: And in fact, We put to trial the people of Pharaoh (also) before them and the exalted Messenger (Musa [Moses]) came to them.
t2: Already before them We tried the people of Pharaoh, and a noble Messenger came unto them,
t3: And verily We tried before them Pharaoh’s folk, when there came unto them a noble messenger,

ar: أَنْ أَدُّوٓا۟ إِلَىَّ عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ ۖ إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌۭ
en: ˹proclaiming,˺ “Hand over the servants of Allah to me. I am truly a trustworthy messenger to you.
t1: (He said:) ‘Hand over to me the servants of Allah (the Children of Israel). Verily, I am a trusted Messenger for your guidance and leadership.
t2: saying, ’Deliver to me God’s servants; I am for you a faithful Messenger,
t3: Saying: Give up to me the slaves of Allah. Lo! I am a faithful messenger unto you.

ar: وَأَن لَّا تَعْلُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ۖ إِنِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم بِسُلْطَٰنٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
en: And do not be arrogant with Allah. I have certainly come to you with a compelling proof.
t1: And do not rebel against Allah. I have come to you with the enlightening proof.
t2: and, ’Rise not up against God; behold, I come to you with a clear authority,
t3: And saying: Be not proud against Allah. Lo! I bring you a clear warrant.

ar: وَإِنِّى عُذْتُ بِرَبِّى وَرَبِّكُمْ أَن تَرْجُمُونِ
en: And indeed, I seek refuge with my Lord and your Lord so you do not stone me ˹to death˺.
t1: And I have indeed sought the protection of my Lord and your Lord lest you should stone me.
t2: and I take refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you should stone me.
t3: And lo! I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord lest ye stone me to death.

ar: وَإِن لَّمْ تُؤْمِنُوا۟ لِى فَٱعْتَزِلُونِ
en: ˹But˺ if you do not believe me, then let me be.”
t1: And if you do not believe in me, then keep away from me.’
t2: ’But if so be that you believe me not, go you apart from me!’
t3: And if ye put no faith in me, then let me go.

ar: فَدَعَا رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ قَوْمٌۭ مُّجْرِمُونَ
en: Ultimately, he cried out to his Lord, “These are a wicked people!”
t1: Then he prayed to his Lord: ‘Surely, they are a sinful people.’
t2: And he called to his Lord, saying, ’These are a sinful people.’
t3: And he cried unto his Lord, (saying): These are guilty folk.

ar: فَأَسْرِ بِعِبَادِى لَيْلًا إِنَّكُم مُّتَّبَعُونَ
en: ˹Allah responded,˺ “Leave with My servants at night, for you will surely be pursued.
t1: (Allah said:) ‘Then set out with My servants by night. You shall certainly be chased.
t2: ’Then set thou forth with My servants in a watch of the night; surely you will be followed.
t3: Then (his Lord commanded): Take away My slaves by night. Lo! ye will be followed,

ar: وَٱتْرُكِ ٱلْبَحْرَ رَهْوًا ۖ إِنَّهُمْ جُندٌۭ مُّغْرَقُونَ
en: And leave the sea parted, for they are certainly an army bound to drown.”
t1: And (after you pass through) leave the river still and split open. Surely, they are an army who will be drowned.’
t2: And leave the sea becalmed; they are a drowned host.’
t3: And leave the sea behind at rest, for lo! they are a drowned host.

ar: كَمْ تَرَكُوا۟ مِن جَنَّٰتٍۢ وَعُيُونٍۢ
en: ˹Imagine˺ how many gardens and springs the tyrants left behind,
t1: How many a garden and spring they left behind!
t2: They left how many gardens and fountains,
t3: How many were the gardens and the watersprings that they left behind,

ar: وَزُرُوعٍۢ وَمَقَامٍۢ كَرِيمٍۢ
en: as well as ˹various˺ crops and splendid residences,
t1: And green crops and magnificent buildings!
t2: sown fields, and how noble a station,
t3: And the cornlands and the goodly sites

ar: وَنَعْمَةٍۢ كَانُوا۟ فِيهَا فَٰكِهِينَ
en: and luxuries which they fully enjoyed.
t1: And blessings (and comforts) in which they used to luxuriate!
t2: and what prosperity they had rejoiced in!
t3: And pleasant things wherein they took delight!

ar: كَذَٰلِكَ ۖ وَأَوْرَثْنَٰهَا قَوْمًا ءَاخَرِينَ
en: So it was. And We awarded it ˹all˺ to another people.
t1: So it happened! We made another people the inheritors of all that.
t2: Even so; and We bequeathed them upon another people.
t3: Even so (it was), and We made it an inheritance for other folk;

ar: فَمَا بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ مُنظَرِينَ
en: Neither heaven nor earth wept over them, nor was their fate delayed.
t1: Then neither the heaven nor the earth wept over them, nor were they given respite.
t2: Neither heaven nor earth wept for them, nor were they respited;
t3: And the heaven and the earth wept not for them, nor were they reprieved.

ar: وَلَقَدْ نَجَّيْنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ مِنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْمُهِينِ
en: And We certainly delivered the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment
t1: And verily, We delivered the Children of Israel from a humiliating suffering,
t2: and We delivered the Children of Israel from the humbling chastisement,
t3: And We delivered the Children of Israel from the shameful doom;

ar: مِن فِرْعَوْنَ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَالِيًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ
en: of Pharaoh. He was truly a tyrant, a transgressor.
t1: From Pharaoh. Indeed, he was of the most rebellious transgressors.
t2: from Pharaoh; surely he was a high One, of the prodigals;
t3: (We delivered them) from Pharaoh. Lo! he was a tyrant of the wanton ones.

ar: وَلَقَدِ ٱخْتَرْنَٰهُمْ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عَلَى ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: And indeed, We chose the Israelites knowingly above the others.
t1: And surely, We chose them (the Children of Israel) above (their contemporary civilizations of) the world on the basis of knowledge.
t2: and We chose them, out of a knowledge, above all beings,
t3: And We chose them, purposely, above (all) creatures.

ar: وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُم مِّنَ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ مَا فِيهِ بَلَٰٓؤٌۭا۟ مُّبِينٌ
en: And We showed them signs in which there was a clear test.
t1: And We bestowed upon them signs containing an obvious favour (and a clear trial).
t2: and gave them signs wherein there was a manifest trial.
t3: And We gave them portents wherein was a clear trial.

ar: إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ لَيَقُولُونَ
en: Indeed, these ˹Meccans˺ say,
t1: Surely, they say:
t2: These men do say,
t3: Lo! these, forsooth, are saying:

ar: إِنْ هِىَ إِلَّا مَوْتَتُنَا ٱلْأُولَىٰ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُنشَرِينَ
en: “There is nothing beyond our first death, and we will never be resurrected.
t1: ‘There is nothing after our first death and we shall not be raised up (again).
t2: ’There is nothing but our first death; we shall not be revived.
t3: There is naught but our first death, and we shall not be raised again.

ar: فَأْتُوا۟ بِـَٔابَآئِنَآ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
en: Bring ˹back˺ our forefathers, if what you say is true.”
t1: So bring back our ancestors (alive) if you are truthful.’
t2: Bring us our fathers, if you speak truly!’
t3: Bring back our fathers, if ye speak the truth!

ar: أَهُمْ خَيْرٌ أَمْ قَوْمُ تُبَّعٍۢ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ ۚ أَهْلَكْنَٰهُمْ ۖ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ مُجْرِمِينَ
en: Are they superior to the people of Tubba’ and those before them? We destroyed them ˹all˺, ˹for˺ they were truly wicked.
t1: Well, are they better or the people of Tubba‘ (the people of As‘ad Abu Kurib al-Himyari, the King of Yemen) and those who were before them? We destroyed (all of) them. Surely, they were people given to evildoing.
t2: Are they better, or the people of Tubba’ and those before them whom We destroyed? They were surely sinners.
t3: Are they better, or the folk of Tubb’a and those before them ? We destroyed them, for surely they were guilty.

ar: وَمَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَٰعِبِينَ
en: We did not create the heavens and the earth and everything in between for sport.
t1: And We have not created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them merely in sport.
t2: We created not the heavens and earth, and all that between them is, in play;
t3: And We created not the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, in play.

ar: مَا خَلَقْنَٰهُمَآ إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
en: We only created them for a purpose, but most of these ˹pagans˺ do not know.
t1: We have created them both with (the purpose and reason) of truth. But most of them do not know.
t2: We created them not save in truth; but most of them know it not.
t3: We created them not save with truth; but most of them know not.

ar: إِنَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْفَصْلِ مِيقَٰتُهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
en: Surely the Day of ˹Final˺ Decision is the time appointed for all—
t1: Surely, the Day of Judgment is the appointed time for all of them;
t2: Surely the Day of Decision shall be their appointed time, all together,
t3: Assuredly the Day of Decision is the term for all of them,

ar: يَوْمَ لَا يُغْنِى مَوْلًى عَن مَّوْلًۭى شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ
en: the Day no kith or kin will be of benefit to another whatsoever, nor will they be helped,
t1: The Day when a friend shall not avail a friend at all, nor will they be helped,
t2: the day a master shall avail nothing a client, and they shall not be helped,
t3: A day when friend can in naught avail friend, nor can they be helped,

ar: إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَ ٱللَّهُ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
en: except those shown mercy by Allah. He is truly the Almighty, Most Merciful.
t1: Except those to whom Allah has shown mercy. (They will intercede for one another.) Surely, He is Almighty, Ever-Merciful.
t2: save him upon whom God has mercy; He is the All-mighty, the All-compassionate.
t3: Save him on whom Allah hath mercy. Lo! He is the Mighty, the Merciful.

ar: إِنَّ شَجَرَتَ ٱلزَّقُّومِ
en: Surely ˹the fruit of˺ the tree of Zaqqûm
t1: Indeed, the tree bearing thorny fruit,
t2: Lo, the Tree of Ez-Zakkoum
t3: Lo! the tree of Zaqqum,

ar: طَعَامُ ٱلْأَثِيمِ
en: will be the food of the evildoer.
t1: Will be the food of the major sinners.
t2: is the food of the guilty,
t3: The food of the sinner!

ar: كَٱلْمُهْلِ يَغْلِى فِى ٱلْبُطُونِ
en: Like molten metal, it will boil in the bellies
t1: It will boil in the bellies like molten copper,
t2: like molten copper, bubbling in the belly
t3: Like molten brass, it seetheth in their bellies

ar: كَغَلْىِ ٱلْحَمِيمِ
en: like the boiling of hot water.
t1: Like the seething of simmering water.
t2: as boiling water bubbles.
t3: As the seething of boiling water.

ar: خُذُوهُ فَٱعْتِلُوهُ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
en: ˹It will be said,˺ “Seize them and drag them into the depths of the Hellfire.
t1: (It will be commanded:) ‘Seize him and drag him forcefully to the midst of Hell,
t2: ’Take him, and thrust him into the midst of Hell,
t3: (And it will be said): Take him and drag him to the midst of hell,

ar: ثُمَّ صُبُّوا۟ فَوْقَ رَأْسِهِۦ مِنْ عَذَابِ ٱلْحَمِيمِ
en: Then pour over their heads the torment of boiling water.”
t1: Then torment him by pouring boiling water over his head.
t2: then pour over his head the chastisement of boiling water!’
t3: Then pour upon his head the torment of boiling water.

ar: ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْكَرِيمُ
en: ˹The wicked will be told,˺ “Taste this. You mighty, noble one!
t1: Taste it! Yes, you it is, the respectable and venerable (in your notion and claim).
t2: ’Taste! Surely thou art the mighty, the noble.
t3: (Saying): Taste! Lo! thou wast forsooth the mighty, the noble!

ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَا مَا كُنتُم بِهِۦ تَمْتَرُونَ
en: This is truly what you ˹all˺ used to doubt.”
t1: Certainly, this is the very Hell you used to doubt.’
t2: This is that concerning which you were doubting.’
t3: Lo! this is that whereof ye used to doubt.

ar: إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِى مَقَامٍ أَمِينٍۢ
en: Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure place,
t1: Assuredly, the Godfearing will be in a place of calm and peace,
t2: Surely the godfearing shall be in a station secure
t3: Lo! those who kept their duty will be in a place secured.

ar: فِى جَنَّٰتٍۢ وَعُيُونٍۢ
en: amid Gardens and springs,
t1: Amid gardens and springs,
t2: among gardens and fountains,
t3: Amid gardens and watersprings,

ar: يَلْبَسُونَ مِن سُندُسٍۢ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍۢ مُّتَقَٰبِلِينَ
en: dressed in fine silk and rich brocade, facing one another.
t1: Dressed in fine silk and heavy brocade, facing one another.
t2: robed in silk and brocade, set face to face.
t3: Attired in silk and silk embroidery, facing one another.

ar: كَذَٰلِكَ وَزَوَّجْنَٰهُم بِحُورٍ عِينٍۢ
en: So it will be. And We will pair them to maidens with gorgeous eyes.
t1: So will it happen! And We shall marry them to fair maidens having lovely wide eyes.
t2: Even so; and We shall espouse them to wide-eyed houris,
t3: Even so (it will be). And We shall wed them unto fair ones with wide, lovely eyes.

ar: يَدْعُونَ فِيهَا بِكُلِّ فَٰكِهَةٍ ءَامِنِينَ
en: There they will call for every fruit in serenity.
t1: (Sitting) there, they will call calmly for every kind of fruit.
t2: therein calling for every fruit, secure.
t3: They call therein for every fruit in safety.

ar: لَا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ إِلَّا ٱلْمَوْتَةَ ٱلْأُولَىٰ ۖ وَوَقَىٰهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
en: There they will never taste death, beyond the first death. And He will protect them from the punishment of the Hellfire—
t1: There (in Paradise) they will not taste death except the first death (which would have passed). And Allah will save them from the torment of Hell.
t2: They shall not taste therein of death, save the first death, And He shall guard them against the chastisement of Hell --
t3: They taste not death therein, save the first death. And He hath saved them from the doom of hell,

ar: فَضْلًۭا مِّن رَّبِّكَ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
en: as ˹an act of˺ grace from your Lord. That is ˹truly˺ the ultimate triumph.
t1: It is a bounty of your Lord (i.e., your Lord will bestow through your mediation alone). That is but a great success.
t2: a bounty from thy Lord; that is the mighty triumph.
t3: A bounty from thy Lord. That is the supreme triumph.

ar: فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَٰهُ بِلِسَانِكَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
en: Indeed, We have made this ˹Quran˺ easy in your own language ˹O Prophet˺ so perhaps they will be mindful.
t1: So We have made this (Qur’an) easy in your own tongue so that they may take advice.
t2: Now We have made it easy by thy tongue, that haply they may remember.
t3: And We have made (this Scripture) easy in thy language only that they may heed.

ar: فَٱرْتَقِبْ إِنَّهُم مُّرْتَقِبُونَ
en: Wait then! They too are certainly waiting.
t1: So wait. Certainly, they (too) are waiting. (You will see Our revenge and their evil end, and they will see your glory and My favours to the believers through your mediation.)
t2: So be on the watch; they too are on the watch.
t3: Wait then (O Muhammad). Lo! they (too) are waiting.

ar: حمٓ
en: ha-Mĩm.
t1: Ha-Mim. (Only Allah and the Messenger [blessings and peace be upon him] know the real meaning.)
t2: Ha Mim
t3: Ha. Mim.

ar: تَنزِيلُ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ
en: The revelation of this Book is from Allah—the Almighty, All-Wise.
t1: The revelation of (this) Book is from Allah, Almighty, Most Wise.
t2: The sending down of the Book is from God, the All-mighty, the All-wise.
t3: The revelation of the Scripture is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.

ar: إِنَّ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
en: Surely in ˹the creation of˺ the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers.
t1: Indeed, there are signs for the believers in the heavens and the earth.
t2: Surely in the heavens and earth there are signs for the believers;
t3: Lo! in the heavens and the earth are portents for believers.

ar: وَفِى خَلْقِكُمْ وَمَا يَبُثُّ مِن دَآبَّةٍ ءَايَٰتٌۭ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يُوقِنُونَ
en: And in your own creation, and whatever living beings He dispersed, are signs for people of sure faith.
t1: And in your (own) creation, and in the animals which He scatters, there are signs for those who believe with certitude.
t2: and in your creation, and the crawling things He scatters abroad, there are signs for a people having sure faith,
t3: And in your creation, and all the beasts that He scattereth in the earth, are portents for a folk whose faith is sure.

ar: وَٱخْتِلَٰفِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ وَمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مِن رِّزْقٍۢ فَأَحْيَا بِهِ ٱلْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَتَصْرِيفِ ٱلرِّيَٰحِ ءَايَٰتٌۭ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَعْقِلُونَ
en: And ˹in˺ the alternation of the day and the night, the provision sent down from the skies by Allah—reviving the earth after its death—and the shifting of the winds, are signs for people of understanding.
t1: And in the alternation of night and day, and in that provision (of rain) which Allah sends down from the sky, and by that gives life to the earth after its death, and (in the same way) in the changing of the wind direction, there are signs for those who apply reason.
t2: and in the alternation of night and day, and the provision God sends down from heaven, and therewith revives the earth after it is dead, and the turning about of the winds, there are signs for a people who understand.
t3: And the difference of night and day and the provision that Allah sendeth down from the sky and thereby quickeneth the earth after her death, and the ordering of the winds, are portents for a people who have sense.

ar: تِلْكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱللَّهِ نَتْلُوهَا عَلَيْكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ ۖ فَبِأَىِّ حَدِيثٍۭ بَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ وَءَايَٰتِهِۦ يُؤْمِنُونَ
en: These are Allah’s revelations which We recite to you ˹O Prophet˺ in truth. So what message will they believe in after ˹denying˺ Allah and His revelations?
t1: These are the Revelations of Allah which We recite to you with absolute truth. Then what will they believe in after Allah and His Revelations?
t2: Those are the signs of God that We recite to thee in truth; in what manner of discourse then, after God and His signs, will they believe?
t3: These are the portents of Allah which We recite unto thee (Muhammad) with truth. Then in what fact, after Allah and His portents, will they believe ?

ar: وَيْلٌۭ لِّكُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ أَثِيمٍۢ
en: Woe to every sinful liar.
t1: Woe to every liar given to fabricating false allegations (and) every dreadful evildoer,
t2: Woe to every guilty impostor
t3: Woe unto each sinful liar,

ar: يَسْمَعُ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُصِرُّ مُسْتَكْبِرًۭا كَأَن لَّمْ يَسْمَعْهَا ۖ فَبَشِّرْهُ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍۢ
en: They hear Allah’s revelations recited to them, then persist ˹in denial˺ arrogantly as if they did not hear them. So give them good news of a painful punishment.
t1: The one who listens to the Revelations of Allah that are recited to him, then insists (on his disbelief) arrogantly as if he did not hear them, give him the news of a grievous torment!
t2: who hears the signs of God being recited to him, then perseveres in waxing proud, as if he has not heard them; so give him the good tidings of a painful chastisement.
t3: Who heareth the revelations of Allah recited unto him, and then continueth in pride as though he heard them not. Give him tidings of a painful doom.

ar: وَإِذَا عَلِمَ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَا شَيْـًٔا ٱتَّخَذَهَا هُزُوًا ۚ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌۭ مُّهِينٌۭ
en: And whenever they learn anything of Our revelations, they make a mockery of it. It is they who will suffer a humiliating punishment.
t1: And when he learns about any thing of Our Verses (of the Qur’an), he makes it a joke. It is they for whom there is humiliating torment.
t2: And when he knows anything of Our signs, he takes them in mockery; those for them awaits a humbling chastisement.
t3: And when he knoweth aught of Our revelations he maketh it a jest. For such there is a shameful doom.

ar: مِّن وَرَآئِهِمْ جَهَنَّمُ ۖ وَلَا يُغْنِى عَنْهُم مَّا كَسَبُوا۟ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَا مَا ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْلِيَآءَ ۖ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
en: Awaiting them is Hell. Their ˹worldly˺ gains will not be of any benefit to them whatsoever, nor will those protectors they have taken besides Allah. And they will suffer a tremendous punishment.
t1: Beyond (their current term of life), there is Hell. And (the worldly riches) which they have earned will be of no use to them. Nor will those idols be (of any benefit) that they have made guardians instead of Allah. And there is a very severe torment for them.
t2: Behind them Gehenna; and that they have earned shall not avail them aught, nor those they took as protectors, apart from God; for them awaits a mighty chastisement.
t3: Beyond them there is hell, and that which they have earned will naught avail them, nor those whom they have chosen for protecting friends beside Allah. Theirs will be an awful doom.

ar: هَٰذَا هُدًۭى ۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌۭ مِّن رِّجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ
en: This ˹Quran˺ is ˹true˺ guidance. And those who deny their Lord’s revelations will suffer the ˹worst˺ torment of agonizing pain.
t1: This (Qur’an) is guidance. And for those who disbelieved in the Revelations of Allah is an extremely grievous torment in store.
t2: This is guidance; and those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord, there awaits them a painful chastisement of wrath.
t3: This is guidance. And those who disbelieve the revelations of their Lord, for them there is a painful doom of wrath.

ar: ۞ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى سَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلْبَحْرَ لِتَجْرِىَ ٱلْفُلْكُ فِيهِ بِأَمْرِهِۦ وَلِتَبْتَغُوا۟ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
en: Allah is the One Who has subjected the sea for you so that ships may sail upon it by His command, and that you may seek His bounty, and that perhaps you will be grateful.
t1: Allah is the One Who has placed the sea under your control so that ships and vessels may sail in it by His command, so that you may look for His bounty (i.e., sustenance through the sea routes as well), and that you may become grateful (to Him).
t2: God is He who has subjected to you the sea, that the ships may run on it at His commandment, and that you may seek His bounty; haply so you will be thankful.
t3: Allah it is Who hath made the sea of service unto you that the ships may run thereon by His command, and that ye may seek of His bounty, and that haply ye may be thankful;

ar: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا مِّنْهُ ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
en: He ˹also˺ subjected for you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth—all by His grace. Surely in this are signs for people who reflect.
t1: And He has made subservient to you, out of His will, whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, all of it (under a system). Surely, there are signs in it for those who ponder.
t2: And He has subjected to you what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, all together, from Him. Surely in that are signs for a people who reflect.
t3: And hath made of service unto you whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth; it is all from Him. Lo! herein verily are portents for a people who reflect.

ar: قُل لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ يَغْفِرُوا۟ لِلَّذِينَ لَا يَرْجُونَ أَيَّامَ ٱللَّهِ لِيَجْزِىَ قَوْمًۢا بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ
en: ˹O Prophet!˺ Tell the believers to forgive those who do not fear Allah’s days ˹of torment˺, so that He will reward each group for what they used to commit.
t1: Say to the believers to disregard those who neither hope for nor fear (the coming of) the Days of Allah, so that He may give them full reward of those (deeds) which they used to earn.
t2: Say unto those who believe, that they forgive those who do not look for the days of God, that He may recompense a people for that they have been earning.
t3: Tell those who believe to forgive those who hope not for the days of Allah; in order that He may requite folk what they used to earn.

ar: مَنْ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا فَلِنَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَنْ أَسَآءَ فَعَلَيْهَا ۖ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ تُرْجَعُونَ
en: Whoever does good, it is to their own benefit. And whoever does evil, it is to their own loss. Then to your Lord you will ˹all˺ be returned.
t1: Whoever does a righteous work does it for (the benefit of) his own soul, and whoever commits some evil act, then he alone is to face (suffering caused by it). Then all of you will be returned to your Lord.
t2: Whoso does righteousness, it is to his own gain, and whoso does evil, it is to his own loss; then to your Lord you shall be returned.
t3: Whoso doeth right, it is for his soul, and whoso doeth wrong, it is against it. And afterward unto your Lord ye will be brought back.

ar: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْحُكْمَ وَٱلنُّبُوَّةَ وَرَزَقْنَٰهُم مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَفَضَّلْنَٰهُمْ عَلَى ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: Indeed, We gave the Children of Israel the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood; granted them good, lawful provisions; and favoured them above the others.
t1: And surely, We gave to the Children of Israel the Book, the reign and Prophethood, and provided them with sustenance of pure things. And We exalted them above (their contemporary) worlds (i.e., the nations and civilizations of that age).
t2: Indeed, We gave the Children of Israel the Book, the Judgment, and the Prophethood, and We provided them with good things, and We preferred them above all beings.
t3: And verily we gave the Children of Israel the Scripture and the Command and the Prophethood, and provided them with good things and favoured them above (all) peoples;

ar: وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُم بَيِّنَٰتٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْأَمْرِ ۖ فَمَا ٱخْتَلَفُوٓا۟ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْعِلْمُ بَغْيًۢا بَيْنَهُمْ ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقْضِى بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فِيمَا كَانُوا۟ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ
en: We ˹also˺ gave them clear commandments regarding ˹their˺ faith. But it was not until knowledge came to them that they differed out of mutual envy. Surely your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Judgment regarding their differences.
t1: And We gave them clear proofs of religion (and Prophethood). But they disagreed (about it) after the knowledge (of raising the Prophet Muhammad [blessings and peace be upon him]) had come to them, merely because of their mutual jealousy, spite and antagonism. Surely, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Rising concerning the matter in which they used to disagree.
t2: We gave them clear signs of the Command; so they differed not, except after the knowledge had come to them, being insolent one to another. Surely thy Lord will decide between them on the Day of Resurrection touching their differences.
t3: And gave them plain commandments. And they differed not until after the knowledge came unto them, through rivalry among themselves. Lo! thy Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ.

ar: ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَٰكَ عَلَىٰ شَرِيعَةٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْأَمْرِ فَٱتَّبِعْهَا وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَآءَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
en: Now We have set you ˹O Prophet˺ on the ˹clear˺ Way of faith. So follow it, and do not follow the desires of those who do not know ˹the truth˺.
t1: Then We set you on the open path of Shariah (Islamic law). So follow it persistently. And do not yield to the desires of those who are simply unaware (of the glory, dignity and trueness of your Din [Religion]).
t2: Then We set thee upon an open way of the Command; therefore follow it, and follow not the caprices of those who do not know.
t3: And now have We set thee (O Muhammad) on a clear road of (Our) commandment; so follow it, and follow not the whims of those who know not.

ar: إِنَّهُمْ لَن يُغْنُوا۟ عَنكَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيْـًۭٔا ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ بَعْضٍۢ ۖ وَٱللَّهُ وَلِىُّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ
en: They certainly can be of no benefit to you against Allah whatsoever. Surely the wrongdoers are patrons of each other, whereas Allah is the Patron of the righteous.
t1: Surely, these people will not be of any help to you at all (despite promises) from Allah (for crucial time of hardships coming in the way of Islam). And in truth, the wrongdoers (in the world) are friends and helpers only to one another and Allah is the Friend and Helper of the Godfearing.
t2: Surely they will not avail thee aught against God. Surely the evildoers are friends one of the other; God is the friend of the godfearing.
t3: Lo! they can avail thee naught against Allah. And lo! as for the wrong-doers, some of them are friends of others; and Allah is the Friend of those who ward off (evil).

ar: هَٰذَا بَصَٰٓئِرُ لِلنَّاسِ وَهُدًۭى وَرَحْمَةٌۭ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يُوقِنُونَ
en: This ˹Quran˺ is an insight for humanity—a guide and mercy for people of sure faith.
t1: This (Qur’an) contains proofs, which provide vision and lessons of warning to the people, and is guidance and mercy for those who believe with certitude.
t2: This is clear proofs for men, and a guidance, and a mercy to a people having sure faith.
t3: This is clear indication for mankind, and a guidance and a mercy for a folk whose faith is sure.

ar: أَمْ حَسِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱجْتَرَحُوا۟ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ أَن نَّجْعَلَهُمْ كَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ سَوَآءًۭ مَّحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ ۚ سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ
en: Or do those who commit evil deeds ˹simply˺ think that We will make them equal—in their life and after their death—to those who believe and do good? How wrong is their judgment!
t1: Do those who have earned evil deeds think that We shall make them resemble those who believe and do good deeds (so as) to make their life and death alike? The claim, which they (the disbelievers) make, is the worst evil.
t2: Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We shall make them as those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal their living and their dying? How ill they judge!
t3: Or do those who commit ill-deeds suppose that We shall make them as those who believe and do good works, the same in life and death ? Bad is their judgment!

ar: وَخَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلِتُجْزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفْسٍۭ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ
en: For Allah created the heavens and the earth for a purpose, so that every soul may be paid back for what it has committed. And none will be wronged.
t1: And Allah created the heavens and the earth with (a strategy based on) truth, in order that every soul is rewarded for the deeds that it earns and they will not be wronged.
t2: God created the heavens and the earth in truth, and that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned; they shall not be wronged.
t3: And Allah hath created the heavens and the earth with truth, and that every soul may be repaid what it hath earned. And they will not be wronged.

ar: أَفَرَءَيْتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍۢ وَخَتَمَ عَلَىٰ سَمْعِهِۦ وَقَلْبِهِۦ وَجَعَلَ عَلَىٰ بَصَرِهِۦ غِشَٰوَةًۭ فَمَن يَهْدِيهِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
en: Have you seen ˹O Prophet˺ those who have taken their own desires as their god? ˹And so˺ Allah left them to stray knowingly, sealed their hearing and hearts, and placed a cover on their sight. Who then can guide them after Allah? Will you ˹all˺ not then be mindful?
t1: Have you seen him who has made his desire his god and Allah has held him astray despite his knowledge and has sealed his ears and his heart and has blindfolded his eyes? Then who can guide him after Allah? So do you not accept advice?
t2: Hast thou seen him who has taken his caprice to be his god, and God has led him astray out of a knowledge, and set a seal upon his hearing and his heart, and laid a covering on his eyes? Who shall guide him after God? What, will you not remember?
t3: Hast thou seen him who maketh his desire his god, and Allah sendeth him astray purposely, and sealeth up his hearing and his heart, and setteth on his sight a covering ? Then who will lead him after Allah (hath condemned him) ? Will ye not then heed ?

ar: وَقَالُوا۟ مَا هِىَ إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا ٱلدُّنْيَا نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيَا وَمَا يُهْلِكُنَآ إِلَّا ٱلدَّهْرُ ۚ وَمَا لَهُم بِذَٰلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ ۖ إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ
en: And they argue, “There is nothing beyond our worldly life. We die; others are born. And nothing destroys us but ˹the passage of˺ time.” Yet they have no knowledge ˹in support˺ of this ˹claim˺. They only speculate.
t1: And they say: ‘There is nothing (else) except our worldly life. We die and live here (only). And nothing kills us except (circumstances and occurrences of) time (i.e., they deny Allah and the Hereafter absolutely). And they simply do not have any knowledge of this (reality). They follow only their speculation and assumption.
t2: They say, ’There is nothing but our present life; we die, and we live, and nothing but Time destroys us.’ Of that they have no knowledge; they merely conjecture.
t3: And they say: There is naught but our life of the world; we die and we live, and naught destroyeth us save time; when they have no knowledge whatsoever of (all) that; they do but guess.

ar: وَإِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتُنَا بَيِّنَٰتٍۢ مَّا كَانَ حُجَّتَهُمْ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوا۟ ٱئْتُوا۟ بِـَٔابَآئِنَآ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
en: And whenever Our clear revelations are recited to them, their only argument is to say: “Bring our forefathers back, if what you say is true!”
t1: And when Our clear Verses are recited to them, they do not have any plea except to say: ‘Bring back our fathers (raised alive) if you are truthful.’
t2: And when Our signs are recited to them, clear signs, their only argument is that they say, ’Bring us our fathers, if you speak truly.’
t3: And when Our clear revelations are recited unto them their only argument is that they say: Bring (back) our fathers. then, if ye are truthful.

ar: قُلِ ٱللَّهُ يُحْيِيكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يَجْمَعُكُمْ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
en: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “˹It is˺ Allah ˹Who˺ gives you life, then causes you to die, then will gather you ˹all˺ on the Day of Judgment, about which there is no doubt. But most people do not know.”
t1: Say: ‘Allah is the One Who gives you life, and He is the One Who causes you to die. Then He will gather all of you towards the Day of Resurrection about which there is no doubt. But most people do not know.’
t2: Say: ’God gives you life, then makes you die, then He shall gather you to the Day of Resurrection, wherein is no doubt, but most men do not know.’
t3: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Allah giveth life to you, then causeth you to die, then gathereth you unto the Day of Resurrection whereof there is no doubt. But most of mankind know not.

ar: وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۚ وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ يَخْسَرُ ٱلْمُبْطِلُونَ
en: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. On the Day the Hour will be established, the people of falsehood will then be in ˹total˺ loss.
t1: And the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah alone. And the Day when the Last Hour comes, then (all) the disbelievers will run into serious loss.
t2: And unto Allah belongeth the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth; and on the day when the Hour riseth, on that day those who follow falsehood will be lost.
t3: And unto Allah belongeth the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth; and on the day when the Hour riseth, on that day those who follow falsehood will be lost.

ar: وَتَرَىٰ كُلَّ أُمَّةٍۢ جَاثِيَةًۭ ۚ كُلُّ أُمَّةٍۢ تُدْعَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ كِتَٰبِهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
en: And you will see every faith-community on its knees. Every community will be summoned to its record ˹of deeds˺. ˹They all will be told,˺ “This Day you will be rewarded for what you used to do.
t1: And you will see every party (of the disbelievers and beliers) sitting, fallen on their knees. Every community will be called to its book (of deeds): ‘You will be rewarded Today for the deeds that you used to do.
t2: And thou shalt see every nation hobbling on their knees, every nation being summoned unto its Book: ’Today you shall be recompensed for that you were doing.
t3: And thou wilt see each nation crouching, each nation summoned to its record. (And it will be said unto them): This day ye are requited what ye used to do.

ar: هَٰذَا كِتَٰبُنَا يَنطِقُ عَلَيْكُم بِٱلْحَقِّ ۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا نَسْتَنسِخُ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
en: This record of Ours speaks the truth about you. Indeed, We always had your deeds recorded ˹by the angels˺.”
t1: This is Our record that will speak about you with absolute truth. Verily, We used to (preserve) by getting transcribed what you used to do.’
t2: This is Our Book, that speaks against you the truth; We have been registering all that you were doing.’
t3: This Our Book pronounceth against you with truth. Lo! We have caused (all) that ye did to be recorded.

ar: فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَيُدْخِلُهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ فِى رَحْمَتِهِۦ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْمُبِينُ
en: As for those who believed and did good, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is ˹truly˺ the absolute triumph.
t1: So those who believe and do good deeds, their Lord will admit them to His mercy. That is nothing but an evident success.
t2: And as for those who have believed and done deeds of righteousness, their Lord shall admit them into His mercy; that is the manifest triumph.
t3: Then, as for those who believed and did good works, their Lord will bring them in unto His mercy. That is the evident triumph.

ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَفَلَمْ تَكُنْ ءَايَٰتِى تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ فَٱسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ وَكُنتُمْ قَوْمًۭا مُّجْرِمِينَ
en: And as for those who disbelieved, ˹they will be told,˺ “Were My revelations not recited to you, yet you acted arrogantly and were a wicked people?
t1: And those who disbelieved (it will be said to them:) ‘Were My Verses not recited to you? But you showed arrogance and you were the evildoers.’
t2: But as for those who have disbelieved: ’Were not My signs recited to you, and you waxed proud, and were a sinful people?
t3: And as for those who disbelieved (it will be said unto them): Were not Our revelations recited unto you ? But ye were scornful and became a guilty folk.

ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ إِنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّۭ وَٱلسَّاعَةُ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهَا قُلْتُم مَّا نَدْرِى مَا ٱلسَّاعَةُ إِن نَّظُنُّ إِلَّا ظَنًّۭا وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُسْتَيْقِنِينَ
en: And whenever it was said ˹to you˺, ‘Surely Allah’s promise ˹of judgment˺ is true and there is no doubt about the Hour,’ you said ˹mockingly˺, ‘We do not know what the Hour is! We think it is no more than speculation, and we are not convinced ˹that it will ever come˺.’”
t1: And when it was said: ‘The promise of Allah is true, and there is no doubt about (the coming of) the Last Hour,’ you used to say: ‘We do not know what the Last Hour is; we regard it nothing but a conjecture; nor do we have any faith in it.’
t2: And when it was said, "God’s promise is true, and the Hour, there is no doubt of it," you said; "We know not what the Hour may be; we have only a surmise, and are by no means certain."
t3: And when it was said: Lo! Allah’s promise is the truth, and there is no doubt of the Hour’s coming, ye said: We know not what the Hour is. We deem it naught but a conjecture, and we are by no means convinced.

ar: وَبَدَا لَهُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتُ مَا عَمِلُوا۟ وَحَاقَ بِهِم مَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ
en: And the evil ˹consequences˺ of their deeds will unfold before them, and they will be overwhelmed by what they used to ridicule.
t1: And all their evil works which they used to do will be exposed, and that (torment) which they used to make fun of will beset them.
t2: And the evil deeds that they have done shall appear to them, and they shall be encompassed by that they mocked at.
t3: And the evils of what they did will appear unto them, and that which they used to deride will befall them.

ar: وَقِيلَ ٱلْيَوْمَ نَنسَىٰكُمْ كَمَا نَسِيتُمْ لِقَآءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هَٰذَا وَمَأْوَىٰكُمُ ٱلنَّارُ وَمَا لَكُم مِّن نَّٰصِرِينَ
en: It will be said, “This Day We will neglect you as you neglected the meeting of this Day of yours! Your home will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers.
t1: And it will be said (to them): ‘Today We forget you as you forgot your Meeting on this Day. And Hell is your abode and there will be no helper for you.
t2: And it shall be said, ’Today We do forget you, even as you forgot the encounter of this your day; and your refuge is the Fire, and you shall have no helpers.
t3: And it will be said: This day We forget you, even as ye forgot the meeting of this your day; and your habitation is the Fire, and there is none to help you.

ar: ذَٰلِكُم بِأَنَّكُمُ ٱتَّخَذْتُمْ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ هُزُوًۭا وَغَرَّتْكُمُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا ۚ فَٱلْيَوْمَ لَا يُخْرَجُونَ مِنْهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ
en: This is because you made a mockery of Allah’s revelations, and were deluded by ˹your˺ worldly life.” So ˹from˺ that Day ˹on˺ they will not be taken out of the Fire, nor will they be allowed to appease ˹their Lord˺.
t1: That (is) so because you made fun of Allah’s Revelations, and the worldly life deceived you.’ So Today neither will they be taken out of that (Hell), nor will there be accepted from them any attempt to seek (Allah’s) pleasure by means of repentance.
t2: That is for that you took God’s signs in mockery, and the present life deluded you.’ So today they shall not be brought forth from it, nor will they be suffered to make amends.
t3: This, forasmuch as ye made the revelations of Allah a jest, and the life of the world beguiled you. Therefor this day they come not forth from thence, nor can they make amends.

ar: فَلِلَّهِ ٱلْحَمْدُ رَبِّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَرَبِّ ٱلْأَرْضِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: So all praise is for Allah—Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of all worlds.
t1: So all praise belongs to Allah alone, Who is the Lord of the heavens and the Master of the earth (and also) the Sustainer of all the worlds.
t2: So to God belongs praise, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, Lord of all Being.
t3: Then praise be to Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, the Lord of the Worlds.

ar: وَلَهُ ٱلْكِبْرِيَآءُ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
en: To Him belongs ˹all˺ Majesty in the heavens and the earth. And He is the Almighty, All-Wise.
t1: And all Greatness (i.e., Eminence) in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him alone, and He is the One Who is Almighty, Most Wise.
t2: His is the Domination an the heavens and the earth; He is the All-mighty, the All-wise.
t3: And unto Him (alone) belongeth Majesty in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.

ar: حمٓ
en: ha-Mĩm.
t1: Ha-Mim. (Only Allah and the Messenger [blessings and peace be upon him] know the real meaning.)
t2: Ha Mim
t3: Ha. Mim.

ar: تَنزِيلُ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ
en: The revelation of this Book is from Allah—the Almighty, All-Wise.
t1: The revelation of this Book is from Allah, Almighty, Most Wise.
t2: The sending down of the Book is from God, the All-mighty, the All-wise.
t3: The revelation of the Scripture is from Allah the Mighty, the Wise.

ar: مَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَأَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى ۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ عَمَّآ أُنذِرُوا۟ مُعْرِضُونَ
en: We only created the heavens and the earth and everything in between for a purpose and an appointed term. Yet the disbelievers are turning away from what they have been warned about.
t1: We have not created the heavens and the earth and (the creation) that is between them but with wisdom and (the fixing of) an appointed term. And those who have disbelieved turn away from what they have been warned of.
t2: We have not created the heavens and the earth, and what between them is, save with the truth and a stated term; but the unbelievers are turning away from that they were warned of.
t3: We created not the heavens and the earth and all that is between them save with truth, and for a term appointed. But those who disbelieve turn away from that whereof they are warned.

ar: قُلْ أَرَءَيْتُم مَّا تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَرُونِى مَاذَا خَلَقُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ أَمْ لَهُمْ شِرْكٌۭ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ ۖ ٱئْتُونِى بِكِتَٰبٍۢ مِّن قَبْلِ هَٰذَآ أَوْ أَثَٰرَةٍۢ مِّنْ عِلْمٍ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
en: Ask ˹them, O  Prophet˺, “Have you considered whatever ˹idols˺ you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created on earth! Or do they have a share in ˹the creation of˺ the heavens? Bring me a scripture ˹revealed˺ before this ˹Quran˺ or a shred of knowledge, if what you say is true.”
t1: Say: ‘Tell me of the (idols) you worship instead of Allah; show me what they have created in the earth, or (bring it forth if) they have a partnership in (the creation of) the heavens. Bring me (as a proof) any Book (revealed) before this (Qur’an), or some remnant of knowledge (transmitted from the bygone people), if you are truthful.’
t2: Say: ’Have you considered that you call upon apart from God? Show me what they have created of the earth; or have they a partnership in the heavens? Bring me a Book before this, or some remnant of a knowledge, if you speak truly.’
t3: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Have ye thought on all that ye invoke beside Allah ? Show me what they have created of the earth. Or have they any portion in the heavens ? Bring me a scripture before this (Scripture), or some vestige of knowledge (in support of what ye say), if ye are truthful.

ar: وَمَنْ أَضَلُّ مِمَّن يَدْعُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَن لَّا يَسْتَجِيبُ لَهُۥٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ وَهُمْ عَن دُعَآئِهِمْ غَٰفِلُونَ
en: And who could be more astray than those who call upon others besides Allah—˹others˺ that cannot respond to them until the Day of Judgment, and are ˹even˺ unaware of their calls?
t1: And who can be more in error than someone who worships such (idols) apart from Allah as cannot answer (his question) till the Day of Resurrection? And those (idols) have no consciousness of their prayer and worship.
t2: And who is further astray than he who calls, apart from God, upon such a one as shall not answer him till the Day of Resurrection? Such as are heedless of their calling,
t3: And who is further astray than those who, instead of Allah, pray unto such as hear not their prayer until the Day of Resurrection, and are unconscious of their prayer,

ar: وَإِذَا حُشِرَ ٱلنَّاسُ كَانُوا۟ لَهُمْ أَعْدَآءًۭ وَكَانُوا۟ بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ كَٰفِرِينَ
en: And when ˹such˺ people will be gathered together, those ˹gods˺ will be their enemies and will disown their worship.
t1: And when mankind shall be gathered (on the Day of Resurrection), those (false gods) will be their enemies and will deny their worship (for their own absolution).
t2: and when mankind are mustered, shall be enemies to them, and shall deny their service.
t3: And when mankind are gathered (to the Judgment) will become enemies for them, and will become deniers of having been worshipped.

ar: وَإِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتُنَا بَيِّنَٰتٍۢ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لِلْحَقِّ لَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ هَٰذَا سِحْرٌۭ مُّبِينٌ
en: Whenever Our clear revelations are recited to them, the disbelievers say of the truth when it has come to them, “This is pure magic.”
t1: And when Our clear Verses are recited to them, (then) the disbelievers say about the truth (the Qur’an) whilst it has come to them: ‘This is obvious magic.’
t2: And when Our signs are recited to them, clear signs, the unbelievers say to the truth when it has come to them, ’This is manifest sorcery.’
t3: And when Our clear revelations are recited unto them, those who disbelieve say of the Truth when it reacheth them: This is mere magic.

ar: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ ٱفْتَرَىٰهُ ۖ قُلْ إِنِ ٱفْتَرَيْتُهُۥ فَلَا تَمْلِكُونَ لِى مِنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيْـًٔا ۖ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ ۖ كَفَىٰ بِهِۦ شَهِيدًۢا بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَكُمْ ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
en: Or do they say, “He has fabricated this ˹Quran˺!”? Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “If I have done so, then there is nothing whatsoever you can do to save me from Allah. He knows best what ˹slurs˺ you indulge about it. Sufficient is He as a Witness between you and me. And He is the All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
t1: Do they say that (the Messenger) has fabricated it (the Qur’an)? Say: ‘If I have concocted it, then you have no authority to save me from (the torment of) Allah. And He knows best the (words) you utter about this (Qur’an) as mockery. He (Allah) is Sufficient as witness between me and you. And He is Most Forgiving, Ever-Merciful.’
t2: Or do they say, ’He has forged it’? Say: ’If I have forged it, you have no power to help me against God. He knows very well what you are pressing upon; He suffices as a witness between me and you; He is the All-forgiving, the All-compassionate.’
t3: Or say they: He hath invented it ? Say (O Muhammad): If I have invented it, still ye have no power to support me against Allah. He is Best Aware of what ye say among yourselves concerning it. He sufficeth for a witness between me and you. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.

ar: قُلْ مَا كُنتُ بِدْعًۭا مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ وَمَآ أَدْرِى مَا يُفْعَلُ بِى وَلَا بِكُمْ ۖ إِنْ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا مَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
en: Say, “I am not the first messenger ever sent, nor do I know what will happen to me or you. I only follow what is revealed to me. And I am only sent with a clear warning.”
t1: Say: ‘I am not the first Messenger (sent to mankind that no precedent of Messengership exists before me). Nor do I know of my own accord (i.e., purely by means of my own mental faculty and self-application) what will be done to me or what will be done to you. (My knowledge is nothing except that) I follow that revelation alone which is sent to me. (It is this that provides me knowledge about everything.) And I am simply a clear Warner (on the basis of this knowledge obtained through revelation).
t2: Say: ’I am not an innovation among the Messengers, and I know not what shall be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me; I am only a clear warner.’
t3: Say: I am no new thing among the messengers (of Allah), nor know I what will be done with me or with you. I do but follow that which is inspired in me, and I am but a plain warner.

ar: قُلْ أَرَءَيْتُمْ إِن كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ وَكَفَرْتُم بِهِۦ وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌۭ مِّنۢ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ عَلَىٰ مِثْلِهِۦ فَـَٔامَنَ وَٱسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
en: Ask ˹them, O  Prophet˺, “Consider if this ˹Quran˺ is ˹truly˺ from Allah and you deny it, and a witness from the Children of Israel attests to it and then believes, whereas you act arrogantly. Surely Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.”
t1: Say: ‘Tell me, if this (Qur’an) is from Allah and you deny it and a witness from the Children of Israel (also) bears testimony to the mention of (the revelation of) such a Book (in the Revealed Books revealed earlier), then he believes (in it as well), but (despite that) you show arrogance (then what will be your fate?) Surely, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.’
t2: Say: ’Have you considered? If it be from God, and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from among the Children of Israel hears witness to its like, and believes, and you wax proud, God guides not the people of the evildoers.
t3: Bethink you: If it is from Allah and ye disbelieve therein, and a witness of the Children of Israel hath already testified to the like thereof and hath believed, and ye are too proud (what plight is yours) ? Lo! Allah guideth not wrong-doing folk.

ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَوْ كَانَ خَيْرًۭا مَّا سَبَقُونَآ إِلَيْهِ ۚ وَإِذْ لَمْ يَهْتَدُوا۟ بِهِۦ فَسَيَقُولُونَ هَٰذَآ إِفْكٌۭ قَدِيمٌۭ
en: The disbelievers say of the believers, “Had it been ˹something˺ good, they would not have beaten us to it.” Now since they reject its guidance, they will say, “˹This is˺ an ancient fabrication!”
t1: And the disbelievers said to the believers: ‘Had it (the Din of Muhammad [blessings and peace be upon him]) been a better (religion), these people would not have advanced towards it taking the lead over us. (We would have accepted it before anyone else.)’ And when they (the disbelievers) have not taken guidance from it (themselves), now they say: ‘This is an old lie (and a fabrication).’
t2: The unbelievers say, as regards the believers, ’If it had been aught good, they had not outstripped us to it.’ And since they are not guided by it, certainly they will say, ’This is an old calumny!’
t3: And those who disbelieve say of those who believe: If it had been (any) good, they would not have been before us in attaining it. And since they will not be guided by it, they say: This is an ancient lie;

ar: وَمِن قَبْلِهِۦ كِتَٰبُ مُوسَىٰٓ إِمَامًۭا وَرَحْمَةًۭ ۚ وَهَٰذَا كِتَٰبٌۭ مُّصَدِّقٌۭ لِّسَانًا عَرَبِيًّۭا لِّيُنذِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ
en: And before this ˹Quran˺ the Book of Moses was ˹revealed as˺ a guide and mercy. And this Book is a confirmation, in the Arabic tongue, to warn those who do wrong, and as good news to those who do good.
t1: And before it was the Book of Musa (Moses [the Torah]), a guide and mercy. And this Book confirms that. It is in the Arabic language to warn the wrongdoers and give good news to the pious.
t2: Yet before it was the Book of Moses for a model and a mercy; and this is a Book confirming, in Arabic tongue, to warn the evildoers, and good tidings to the good-doers.
t3: When before it there was the Scripture of Moses, an example and a mercy; and this is a confirming Scripture in the Arabic language, that it may warn those who do wrong and bring good tidings for the righteous.

ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَقَٰمُوا۟ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ
en: Surely those who say, “Our Lord is Allah,” and then remain steadfast—there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve.
t1: Surely, those who say: ‘Allah is our Lord,’ then hold fast (to it) have nothing to fear, nor shall they grieve.
t2: Surely those who say, ’Our Lord is God’ and then go straight, no fear shall be on them, neither shall they sorrow.
t3: Lo! those who say: Our Lord is Allah, and thereafter walk aright, there shall no fear come upon them neither shall they grieve.

ar: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا جَزَآءًۢ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
en: It is they who will be the residents of Paradise, staying there forever, as a reward for what they used to do.
t1: They it is, the people of Paradise, who will live in it forever. This is the reward of the deeds they used to do.
t2: Those are the inhabitants of Paradise, therein dwelling forever, as a recompense for that they have been doing.
t3: Such are rightful owners of the Garden, immortal therein, as a reward for what they used to do.

ar: وَوَصَّيْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيْهِ إِحْسَٰنًا ۖ حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُۥ كُرْهًۭا وَوَضَعَتْهُ كُرْهًۭا ۖ وَحَمْلُهُۥ وَفِصَٰلُهُۥ ثَلَٰثُونَ شَهْرًا ۚ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَبَلَغَ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةًۭ قَالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِىٓ أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَىَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَىَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَٰلِحًۭا تَرْضَىٰهُ وَأَصْلِحْ لِى فِى ذُرِّيَّتِىٓ ۖ إِنِّى تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَإِنِّى مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ
en: We have commanded people to honour their parents. Their mothers bore them in hardship and delivered them in hardship. Their ˹period of˺ bearing and weaning is thirty months. In time, when the child reaches their prime at the age of forty, they pray, “My Lord! Inspire me to ˹always˺ be thankful for Your favours which You blessed me and my parents with, and to do good deeds that please You. And instil righteousness in my offspring. I truly repent to You, and I truly submit ˹to Your Will˺.”
t1: And We have commanded man to be benevolent towards his parents. His mother bears him (in the womb) with pain and gives birth to him with pain. And bearing him (in the womb) and weaning of him (i.e., the period of pregnancy and feeding) is (spread over) thirty months. Till, when he attains to manhood and then reaches (the age of) forty years, he says: ‘O my Lord, bestow on me the ability to give You thanks for the favour which You have done to me and my parents, and that I may do such deeds as may please You, and endow me and my children with virtue and piety. Assuredly I turn to You, and certainly I am of those who obey You in submissiveness.’
t2: We have charged man, that he be kind to his parents; his mother bore him painfully, and painfully she gave birth to him; his bearing and his weaning are thirty months. Until, when he is fully grown, and reaches forty years, he says, ’O my Lord, dispose me that I may be thankful for Thy blessing wherewith Thou hast blessed me and my father and mother, and that I may do righteousness well-pleasing to Thee; and make me righteous also in my seed. Behold, I repent to Thee, and am among those that surrender.’
t3: And We have commended unto man kindness toward parents. His mother beareth him with reluctance, and bringeth him forth with reluctance, and the bearing of him and the weaning of him is thirty months, till, when he attaineth full strength and reacheth forty years, he saith: My Lord! Arouse me that I may give thanks for the favour wherewith Thou hast favoured me and my parents, and that I may do right acceptable unto Thee. And be gracious unto me in the matter of my seed. Lo! I have turned unto Thee repentant, and lo! I am of those who surrender (unto Thee).

ar: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهُمْ أَحْسَنَ مَا عَمِلُوا۟ وَنَتَجَاوَزُ عَن سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمْ فِىٓ أَصْحَٰبِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ۖ وَعْدَ ٱلصِّدْقِ ٱلَّذِى كَانُوا۟ يُوعَدُونَ
en: It is from these ˹people˺ that We will accept the good they did, and overlook their misdeeds—along with the residents of Paradise, ˹in fulfilment of˺ the true promise they have been given.
t1: It is they whose good works We accept and overlook their omissions. (It is) they (who) are the people of Paradise. This is the true promise which is being made to them.
t2: Those are they from whom We shall accept the best of what they have done, and We shall pass over their evil deeds. They are among the inhabitants of Paradise -- the promise of the very truth, which they were promised.
t3: Those are they from whom We accept the best of what they do, and overlook their evil deeds. (They are) among the owners of the Garden. This is the true promise which they were promised (in the world).

ar: وَٱلَّذِى قَالَ لِوَٰلِدَيْهِ أُفٍّۢ لَّكُمَآ أَتَعِدَانِنِىٓ أَنْ أُخْرَجَ وَقَدْ خَلَتِ ٱلْقُرُونُ مِن قَبْلِى وَهُمَا يَسْتَغِيثَانِ ٱللَّهَ وَيْلَكَ ءَامِنْ إِنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّۭ فَيَقُولُ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّآ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
en: But some scold their parents, “Enough with you! Are you warning me that I will be brought forth ˹from the grave˺, while many generations had already perished before me ˹for good˺?” The parents cry to Allah for help, ˹and warn their child,˺ “Pity you. Have faith! Surely Allah’s promise is true.” But the deniers insist, “This is nothing but ancient fables.”
t1: And he who says to his parents: ‘Fie on you! Do you promise me that I shall be brought forth (from the grave and given life once more) when generations have passed away before me?’ Now both (the parents) pray to Allah for help (and say to the son:) ‘Woe to you, (O son!) Accept faith. Surely, Allah’s promise is true.’ But he says (in reply): ‘These (words) are nothing but the fiction of the bygone people.’
t2: But he who says to his father and his mother, ’Fie upon you! Do you promise me that I shall be brought forth, when already generations have passed away before me?’ while they call upon God for succour -- ’Woe upon thee! Believe; surely God’s promise is true’; then he says, ’This is naught but the fairy-tales of the ancients’ --
t3: And whoso saith unto his parents: Fie upon you both! Do ye threaten me that I shall be brought forth (again) when generations before me have passed away ?
