So He knew (the al-Hudaybiya treaty as a preamble to the truth of the dream) which you did not know, and gave you an immediate victory (the victory of Khaybar even before the victory of Mecca, soon after returning from al-Hudaybiya. The next year He bestowed the victory of Mecca and entry to the Sacred Mosque.)
t2: God has indeed fulfilled the vision He vouchsafed to His Messenger truly: ’You shall enter the Holy Mosque, if God wills, in security, your heads shaved, your hair cut short, not fearing.’ He knew what you knew not, and appointed ere that a nigh victory.
t3: Allah hath fulfilled the vision for His messenger in very truth. Ye shall indeed enter the Inviolable Place of Worship, if Allah will, secure, (having your hair) shaven and cut, not fearing. But He knoweth that which ye know not, and hath given you a near victory beforehand.

ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُۥ بِٱلْهُدَىٰ وَدِينِ ٱلْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلدِّينِ كُلِّهِۦ ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَهِيدًۭا
en: He is the One Who has sent His Messenger with ˹right˺ guidance and the religion of truth, making it prevail over all others. And sufficient is Allah as a Witness.
t1: He is the One Who sent His Messenger (blessings and peace be upon him) with guidance and the Din (Religion) of truth to make it prevail over all other religions. And Allah is Sufficient as a witness (to the truthfulness and veracity of the Messenger [blessings and peace be upon him]).
t2: It is He who has sent His Messenger with the guidance and the religion of truth, that He may uplift it above every religion. God suffices as a witness.
t3: He it is Who hath sent His messenger with the guidance and the religion of truth, that He may cause it to prevail over all religion. And Allah sufficeth as a Witness.

ar: مُّحَمَّدٌۭ رَّسُولُ ٱللَّهِ ۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ مَعَهُۥٓ أَشِدَّآءُ عَلَى ٱلْكُفَّارِ رُحَمَآءُ بَيْنَهُمْ ۖ تَرَىٰهُمْ رُكَّعًۭا سُجَّدًۭا يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًۭا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضْوَٰنًۭا ۖ سِيمَاهُمْ فِى وُجُوهِهِم مِّنْ أَثَرِ ٱلسُّجُودِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ مَثَلُهُمْ فِى ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ ۚ وَمَثَلُهُمْ فِى ٱلْإِنجِيلِ كَزَرْعٍ أَخْرَجَ شَطْـَٔهُۥ فَـَٔازَرَهُۥ فَٱسْتَغْلَظَ فَٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَىٰ سُوقِهِۦ يُعْجِبُ ٱلزُّرَّاعَ لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ ٱلْكُفَّارَ ۗ وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ مِنْهُم مَّغْفِرَةًۭ وَأَجْرًا عَظِيمًۢا
en: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. And those with him are firm with the disbelievers To those of them who believe and do good, Allah has promised forgiveness and a great reward.
t1: Muhammad (blessings and peace be upon him) is the Messenger of Allah. And those with him are hard and tough against the disbelievers but kind-hearted and merciful amongst themselves. You see them excessively bowing and prostrating themselves. They simply seek Allah’s grace and pleasure. Their mark is an impression of prostrations on their faces (prominent on the foreheads as light). These traits of theirs are (mentioned) in the Torah and the (same) qualities are also (described) in the Injil (the Gospel). These (Companions) are like a cultivated crop (of Our Esteemed Beloved) which (first of all) brought forth its thin shoot, then made it powerful and strong, and then it thickened and stood straight on its stalk. (And when it flourished, bloomed and danced,) it delighted and charmed the cultivators. (Allah has, likewise, made the Companions of His Beloved strong, grown up trees of faith,) so that by means of them He would inflame the hearts of the disbelievers (that burn in the jealousy of the Holy Prophet Muhammad [blessings and peace be upon him]). Those who believe and do pious works, Allah has promised them forgiveness and an immense reward.
t2: Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and those who are with him are hard against the unbelievers, merciful one to another. Thou seest them bowing, prostrating, seeking bounty from God and good pleasure. Their mark is on their faces, the trace of prostration. That is their likeness in the Torah, and their likeness in the Gospel: as a seed that puts forth its shoot, and strengthens it, and it grows stout and rises straight upon its stalk, pleasing the sowers, that through them He may enrage the unbelievers. God has promised those of them who believe and do deeds of righteousness forgiveness and a mighty wage.
t3: Muhammad is the messenger of Allah. And those with him are hard against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. Thou (O Muhammad) seest them bowing and falling prostrate (in worship), seeking bounty from Allah and (His) acceptance. The mark of them is on their foreheads from the traces of prostration. Such is their likeness in the Torah and their likeness in the Gospel - like as sown corn that sendeth forth its shoot and strengtheneth it and riseth firm upon its stalk, delighting the sowers - that He may enrage the disbelievers wiith (the sight of) them. Allah hath promised, unto such of them as believe and do good works, forgiveness and immense reward.

ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تُقَدِّمُوا۟ بَيْنَ يَدَىِ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ ۖ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌۭ
en: O believers! Do not proceed ˹in any matter˺ before ˹a decree from˺ Allah and His Messenger. And fear Allah. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
t1: O believers! Do not step ahead of Allah and His Messenger ([blessings and peace be upon him] in any matter) and keep fearing Allah (lest some discourtesy should occur displeasing the Messenger [blessings and peace be upon him]). Surely, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
t2: O believers, advance not before God and His Messenger; and fear God. God is All-hearing, All-knowing.
t3: O ye who believe! Be not forward in the presence of Allah and His messenger, and keep your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is Hearer, Knower.

ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَرْفَعُوٓا۟ أَصْوَٰتَكُمْ فَوْقَ صَوْتِ ٱلنَّبِىِّ وَلَا تَجْهَرُوا۟ لَهُۥ بِٱلْقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ أَن تَحْبَطَ أَعْمَٰلُكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ لَا تَشْعُرُونَ
en: O believers! Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, nor speak loudly to him as you do to one another, or your deeds will become void while you are unaware.
t1: O believers! Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet (blessings and peace be upon him), and (also) do not speak to him so loud as you are loud when you speak to one another (lest) all your actions should come to nothing (including your faith), and you are not even aware (that your faith and all pious works have been wrecked).
t2: O believers, raise not your voices above the Prophet’s voice, and be not loud in your speech to him, as you are loud one to another, lest your works fail while you are not aware.
t3: O ye who believe! Lift not up your voices above the voice of the Prophet, nor shout when speaking to him as ye shout one to another, lest your works be rendered vain while ye perceive not.

ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أَصْوَٰتَهُمْ عِندَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱمْتَحَنَ ٱللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ ۚ لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌۭ وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ
en: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of Allah’s Messenger are the ones whose hearts Allah has refined for righteousness. They will have forgiveness and a great reward.
t1: Assuredly, those who keep their voices low in the presence of Allah’s Messenger (out of profound veneration and submissiveness), it is they whose hearts Allah has chosen for Godwariness and permeated with sincerity. For them alone is forgiveness and an immense reward.
t2: Surely those who lower their voices in the presence of God’s Messenger, those are they whose hearts God has tested for godfearing; they shall have forgiveness and a mighty wage.
t3: Lo! they who subdue their voices in the presence of the messenger of Allah, those are they whose hearts Allah hath proven unto righteousness. Theirs will be forgiveness and immense reward.

ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنَادُونَكَ مِن وَرَآءِ ٱلْحُجُرَٰتِ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ
en: Indeed, most of those who call out to you ˹O Prophet˺ from outside ˹your˺ private quarters have no understanding ˹of manners˺.
t1: Verily, those who call out to you from outside your apartments, most of them do not have the understanding (of your exalted station and incomparable status and polite manners of veneration that are due to you).
t2: Surely those who call unto thee from behind the apartments, the most of them do not understand.
t3: Lo! those who call thee from behind the private apartments, most of them have no sense.

ar: وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ صَبَرُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ تَخْرُجَ إِلَيْهِمْ لَكَانَ خَيْرًۭا لَّهُمْ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
en: Had they been patient until you could come out to them, it would have certainly been better for them. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
t1: And if they had only been patient till you had come out to them, it would have been better for them. And Allah is Most Forgiving, Ever-Merciful.
t2: And if they had patience, until thou comest out to them, that would be better for them; and God is All-forgiving, All-compassionate.
t3: And if they had had patience till thou camest forth unto them, it had been better for them. And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.

ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِن جَآءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌۢ بِنَبَإٍۢ فَتَبَيَّنُوٓا۟ أَن تُصِيبُوا۟ قَوْمًۢا بِجَهَٰلَةٍۢ فَتُصْبِحُوا۟ عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلْتُمْ نَٰدِمِينَ
en: O believers, if an evildoer brings you any news, verify ˹it˺ so you do not harm people unknowingly, becoming regretful for what you have done.
t1: O believers! If some wicked person brings you any news, inquire thoroughly into its truth (lest) you should cause (undue) harm to a people unknowingly, and later feel regret for what you have done.
t2: O believers, if an ungodly man comes to you with a tiding, make clear, lest you afflict a people unwittingly, and then repent of what you have done.
t3: O ye who believe! If an evil-liver bring you tidings, verify it, lest ye smite some folk in ignorance and afterward repent of what ye did.

ar: وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ فِيكُمْ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ لَوْ يُطِيعُكُمْ فِى كَثِيرٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْأَمْرِ لَعَنِتُّمْ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إِلَيْكُمُ ٱلْإِيمَٰنَ وَزَيَّنَهُۥ فِى قُلُوبِكُمْ وَكَرَّهَ إِلَيْكُمُ ٱلْكُفْرَ وَٱلْفُسُوقَ وَٱلْعِصْيَانَ ۚ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلرَّٰشِدُونَ
en: And keep in mind that Allah’s Messenger is ˹still˺ in your midst. If he were to yield to you in many matters, you would surely suffer ˹the consequences˺. But Allah has endeared faith to you, making it appealing in your hearts. And He has made disbelief, rebelliousness, and disobedience detestable to you. Those are the ones rightly guided.
t1: And remember that the Messenger of Allah (blessings and peace be upon him) is amongst you. If he accepted what you say in most of the matters, you would be in serious trouble. But Allah has blessed you with the love of faith and has embelished it in your hearts and has made you hate disbelief, disobedience and sins. Such are they that follow the path of Din (Religion) resolutely and steadfastly.
t2: And know that the Messenger of God is among you. If he obeyed you in much of the affair, you would suffer; but God has endeared to you belief, decking it fair in your hearts, and He has made detestable to you unbelief and ungodliness and disobedience. Those -- they are the right-minded,
t3: And know that the messenger of Allah is among you. If he were to obey you in much of the government, ye would surely be in trouble; but Allah hath endeared the faith to you and hath beautified it in your hearts, and hath made disbelief and lewdness and rebellion hateful unto you. Such are they who are the rightly guided.

ar: فَضْلًۭا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَنِعْمَةًۭ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌۭ
en: ˹This is˺ a bounty and a blessing from Allah. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
t1: (It) is due to Allah’s bounty and favour (i.e., the raising of the untaught Messenger and his presence amongst you). And Allah is All-Knowing, Most Wise.
t2: by God’s favour and blessing; God is All-knowing, All-wise.
t3: (It is) a bounty and a grace from Allah; and Allah is Knower, Wise.

ar: وَإِن طَآئِفَتَانِ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ٱقْتَتَلُوا۟ فَأَصْلِحُوا۟ بَيْنَهُمَا ۖ فَإِنۢ بَغَتْ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا عَلَى ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ فَقَٰتِلُوا۟ ٱلَّتِى تَبْغِى حَتَّىٰ تَفِىٓءَ إِلَىٰٓ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ فَإِن فَآءَتْ فَأَصْلِحُوا۟ بَيْنَهُمَا بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَأَقْسِطُوٓا۟ ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُقْسِطِينَ
en: And if two groups of believers fight each other, then make peace between them. But if one of them transgresses against the other, then fight against the transgressing group until they ˹are willing to˺ submit to the rule of Allah. If they do so, then make peace between both ˹groups˺ in all fairness and act justly. Surely Allah loves those who uphold justice.
t1: And if two parties of the Muslims fight, make them reconcile. Then if either of these (parties) commits injustice and aggression against the other, fight against (the party) that is committing aggression till it returns to Allah’s command (of establishing peace). When they revert and submit, make peace between them with equity. And put justice to work. Surely, Allah loves those who do justice.
t2: If two parties of the believers fight, put things right between them; then, if one of them is insolent against the other, fight the insolent one till it reverts to God’s commandment. If it reverts, set things right between them equitably, and be just. Surely God loves the just.
t3: And if two parties of believers fall to fighting, then make peace between them. And if one party of them doeth wrong to the other, fight ye that which doeth wrong till it return unto the ordinance of Allah; then, if it return, make peace between them justly, and act equitably. Lo! Allah loveth the equitable.

ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِخْوَةٌۭ فَأَصْلِحُوا۟ بَيْنَ أَخَوَيْكُمْ ۚ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ
en: The believers are but one brotherhood, so make peace between your brothers. And be mindful of Allah so you may be shown mercy.
t1: The truth is that (all) believers are brothers (to one another). So make peace between your two brothers and always fear Allah, so that you may be shown mercy.
t2: The believers indeed are brothers; so set things right between your two brothers, and fear God; haply so you will find mercy.
t3: The believers are naught else than brothers. Therefore make peace between your brethren and observe your duty to Allah that haply ye may obtain mercy.

ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌۭ مِّن قَوْمٍ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونُوا۟ خَيْرًۭا مِّنْهُمْ وَلَا نِسَآءٌۭ مِّن نِّسَآءٍ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُنَّ خَيْرًۭا مِّنْهُنَّ ۖ وَلَا تَلْمِزُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَلَا تَنَابَزُوا۟ بِٱلْأَلْقَٰبِ ۖ بِئْسَ ٱلِٱسْمُ ٱلْفُسُوقُ بَعْدَ ٱلْإِيمَٰنِ ۚ وَمَن لَّمْ يَتُبْ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
en: O believers! Do not let some ˹men˺ ridicule others, they may be better than them, nor let ˹some˺ women ridicule other women, they may be better than them. Do not defame one another, nor call each other by offensive nicknames. How evil it is to act rebelliously after having faith! And whoever does not repent, it is they who are the ˹true˺ wrongdoers.
t1: O believers! Let no community ridicule another community. It is likely that they may be better than those (who ridicule). Nor should women make fun of other women. It is likely that they may be better than those (who make fun). And do not offend or find fault with one another, nor call each other names. Calling someone wicked or indecent after (he embraces) faith is an extremely evil name. And those who do not turn to Allah in repentance, it is they who are the wrongdoers.
t2: O believers, let not any people scoff at another people who may be better than they; neither let women scoff at women who may be better than themselves. And find not fault with one another, neither revile one another by nicknames. An evil name is ungodliness after belief. And whoso repents not, those -- they are the evildoers.
t3: O ye who believe! Let not a folk deride a folk who may be better than they (are), not let women (deride) women who may be better than they are; neither defame one another, nor insult one another by nicknames. Bad is the name of lewdness after faith. And whoso turneth not in repentance, such are evil-doers.

ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱجْتَنِبُوا۟ كَثِيرًۭا مِّنَ ٱلظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ ٱلظَّنِّ إِثْمٌۭ ۖ وَلَا تَجَسَّسُوا۟ وَلَا يَغْتَب بَّعْضُكُم بَعْضًا ۚ أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتًۭا فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ ۚ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ تَوَّابٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
en: O  believers! Avoid many suspicions, ˹for˺ indeed, some suspicions are sinful. And do not spy, nor backbite one another. Would any of you like to eat the flesh of their dead brother? You would despise that! And fear Allah. Surely Allah is ˹the˺ Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful.
t1: O believers! Avoid most conjectures. Indeed, some conjectures are sins (liable to punishment in the Hereafter). And spy not (on someone’s unknown matters or secrets), nor backbite one another. Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would hate it. And fear Allah (in all such matters). Indeed, Allah is Ever-Returning, Ever-Merciful.
t2: O believers, eschew much suspicion; some suspicion is a sin. And do not spy, neither backbite one another; would any of you like to eat the flesh of his brother dead? You would abominate it. And fear you God; assuredly God turns, and He is All-compassionate.
t3: O ye who believe! Shun much suspicion; for lo! some suspicion is a crime. And spy not, neither backbite one another. Would one of you love to eat the flesh of his dead brother ? Ye abhor that (so abhor the other)! And keep your duty (to Allah). Lo! Allah is Relenting, Merciful.

ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍۢ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلْنَٰكُمْ شُعُوبًۭا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓا۟ ۚ إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتْقَىٰكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌۭ
en: O humanity! Indeed, We created you from a male and a female, and made you into peoples and tribes so that you may ˹get to˺ know one another. Surely the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous among you. Allah is truly All-Knowing, All-Aware.
t1: O people! We created you from a male and a female, and (divided) you into (large) peoples and tribes, so that you might recognize one another. Surely, the most honourable amongst you in the sight of Allah is he who fears Allah the most. Certainly, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.
t2: O mankind, We have created you male and female, and appointed you races and tribes, that you may know one another. Surely the noblest among you in the sight of God is the most godfearing of you. God is All-knowing, All-aware.
t3: O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct. Lo! Allah is Knower, Aware.

ar: ۞ قَالَتِ ٱلْأَعْرَابُ ءَامَنَّا ۖ قُل لَّمْ تُؤْمِنُوا۟ وَلَٰكِن قُولُوٓا۟ أَسْلَمْنَا وَلَمَّا يَدْخُلِ ٱلْإِيمَٰنُ فِى قُلُوبِكُمْ ۖ وَإِن تُطِيعُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ لَا يَلِتْكُم مِّنْ أَعْمَٰلِكُمْ شَيْـًٔا ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌ
en: ˹Some of˺ the nomadic Arabs say, “We believe.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “You have not believed. But say, ‘We have submitted,’ for faith has not yet entered your hearts. But if you obey Allah and His Messenger ˹wholeheartedly˺, He will not discount anything from ˹the reward of˺ your deeds. Allah is truly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
t1: The Bedouins say: ‘We have believed.’ Say: ‘You have not believed. Rather say: We have accepted Islam. And the belief has not yet gone into your hearts. If you obey Allah and His Messenger (blessings and peace be upon him), He will not decrease anything (in reward) for your deeds. Surely, Allah is Most Forgiving, Ever-Merciful.’
t2: The Bedouins say, ’We believe.’ Say: ’You do not believe; rather say, "We surrender"; for belief has not yet entered your hearts. If you obey God and His Messenger, He will not diminish you anything of your works. God is All-forgiving, All-compassionate.’
t3: The wandering Arabs say: We believe. Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Ye believe not, but rather say "We submit," for the faith hath not yet entered into your hearts. Yet, if ye obey Allah and His messenger, He will not withhold from you aught of (the reward of) your deeds. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.

ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْتَابُوا۟ وَجَٰهَدُوا۟ بِأَمْوَٰلِهِمْ وَأَنفُسِهِمْ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلصَّٰدِقُونَ
en: The ˹true˺ believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger—never doubting—and strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. They are the ones true in faith.
t1: The true believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger (blessings and peace be upon him) and then never have any doubt, and who fight in the way of Allah with their material as well as human resources. It is they who are true (in their claim to believe).
t2: The believers are those who believe in God and His Messenger, then have not doubted, and have struggled with their possessions and their selves in the way of God; those -- they are the truthful ones.
t3: The (true) believers are those only who believe in Allah and His messenger and afterward doubt not, but strive with their wealth and their lives for the cause of Allah. Such are the sincere.

ar: قُلْ أَتُعَلِّمُونَ ٱللَّهَ بِدِينِكُمْ وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌۭ
en: Say, “Do you inform Allah of your faith, when Allah ˹already˺ knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.”
t1: Say: ‘Are you trying to show off to Allah your Din (Religion) whilst Allah knows all that is in the heavens and in the earth? And Allah is Well Aware of everything.’
t2: Say: ’What, would you teach God what your religion is, and God knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth? And God has knowledge of everything.’
t3: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Would ye teach Allah your religion, when Allah knoweth all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth, and Allah is Aware of all things ?

ar: يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ أَسْلَمُوا۟ ۖ قُل لَّا تَمُنُّوا۟ عَلَىَّ إِسْلَٰمَكُم ۖ بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ هَدَىٰكُمْ لِلْإِيمَٰنِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
en: They regard their acceptance of Islam as a favour to you. Tell ˹them, O  Prophet˺, “Do not regard your Islam as a favour to me. Rather, it is Allah Who has done you a favour by guiding you to the faith, if ˹indeed˺ you are faithful.
t1: These people are showing off to you that they have done a favour to you by embracing Islam. Say: ‘Do not show off your Islam as a favour to me. Instead, Allah is the One Who favours you by guiding you to faith, provided you are true (to belief).’
t2: They count it as a favour to thee that they have surrendered! Say: ’Do not count your surrendering as a favour to me; nay, but rather God confers a favour upon you, in that He has guided you to belief, if it be that you are truthful.
t3: They make it a favour unto thee (Muhammad) that they have surrendered (unto Him). Say: Deem not your Surrender a favour unto me; but Allah doth confer a favour on you, inasmuch as He hath led you to the Faith, if ye are earnest.

ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
en: Surely Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and earth. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.”
t1: Surely, Allah knows all the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and Allah monitors best whatever you do.
t2: God knows the Unseen of the heavens and of the earth; and God sees the things you do.’
t3: Lo! Allah knoweth the Unseen of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Seer of what ye do.

ar: قٓ ۚ وَٱلْقُرْءَانِ ٱلْمَجِيدِ
en: Qãf. By the glorious Quran!
t1: Qaf. (Only Allah and the Messenger [blessings and peace be upon him] know the real meaning.) By the Glorious Qur’an,
t2: Qaf. By the glorious Koran!
t3: Qaf. By the Glorious Qur’an,

ar: بَلْ عَجِبُوٓا۟ أَن جَآءَهُم مُّنذِرٌۭ مِّنْهُمْ فَقَالَ ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا شَىْءٌ عَجِيبٌ
en: ˹All will be resurrected,˺ yet the deniers are astonished that a warner has come to them from among themselves ˹warning of resurrection˺. So the disbelievers say, “This is an astonishing thing!
t1: But they wondered that a Warner had come to them from amongst themselves. So the disbelievers say: ‘This is strange!
t2: Nay, but they marvel that a warner has come to them from among them; and the unbelievers say, ’This is a marvellous thing!
t3: Nay, but they marvel that a warner of their own hath come unto them; and the disbelievers say: This is a strange thing:

ar: أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًۭا ۖ ذَٰلِكَ رَجْعٌۢ بَعِيدٌۭ
en: ˹Will we be returned to life,˺ when we are dead and reduced to dust? Such a return is impossible.”
t1: Is it that when we are dead and have become dust (then we shall become alive again)? This return is far (from understanding and perception).’
t2: What, when we are dead and become dust? That is a far returning!’
t3: When we are dead and have become dust (shall we be brought back again) ? That would be a far return!

ar: قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنقُصُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ ۖ وَعِندَنَا كِتَٰبٌ حَفِيظٌۢ
en: We certainly know what the earth consumes of them ˹after their death˺, and with us is a well-preserved Record.
t1: Definitely, We know how much the earth (eats up and) consumes their (bodies), and We have a Book wherein everything is preserved.
t2: We know what the earth diminishes of them; with Us is a book recording.
t3: We know that which the earth taketh of them, and with Us is a recording Book.

ar: بَلْ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ لَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ فَهُمْ فِىٓ أَمْرٍۢ مَّرِيجٍ
en: In fact, they reject the truth when it has come to them, so they are in a confused state.
t1: But (strange and far from understanding is this that) they denied the truth (i.e., the Messenger and the Qur’an) when it came to them. So they have themselves stepped into anxiety and confusion.
t2: Nay, but they cried lies to the truth when it came to them, and so they are in a case confused.
t3: Nay, but they have denied the truth when it came unto them, therefor they are now in troubled case.

ar: أَفَلَمْ يَنظُرُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَوْقَهُمْ كَيْفَ بَنَيْنَٰهَا وَزَيَّنَّٰهَا وَمَا لَهَا مِن فُرُوجٍۢ
en: Have they not then looked at the sky above them: how We built it and adorned it ˹with stars˺, leaving it flawless?
t1: Have they not looked at the sky above them how We made it and (how) We adorned it, and there is no crack in it?
t2: What, have they not beheld heaven above them, how We have built it, and decked it out fair, and it has no cracks?
t3: Have they not then observed the sky above them, how We have constructed it and beautified it, and how there are no rifts therein ?

ar: وَٱلْأَرْضَ مَدَدْنَٰهَا وَأَلْقَيْنَا فِيهَا رَوَٰسِىَ وَأَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍۭ بَهِيجٍۢ
en: As for the earth, We spread it out and placed upon it firm mountains, and produced in it every type of pleasant plant—
t1: And (in the same way) We spread out the earth and We placed in it heavy mountains and produced in it every kind of beautiful plants.
t2: And the earth -- We stretched it forth, and cast on it firm mountains, and We caused to grow therein of every joyous kind
t3: And the earth have We spread out, and have flung firm hills therein, and have caused of every lovely kind to grow thereon,

ar: تَبْصِرَةًۭ وَذِكْرَىٰ لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍۢ مُّنِيبٍۢ
en: ˹all as˺ an insight and a reminder to every servant who turns ˹to Allah˺.
t1: All that is (a source of) insight, direction and guidance for every servant who turns (to Allah in repentance).
t2: for an insight and a reminder to every penitent servant.
t3: A vision and a reminder for every penitent slave.

ar: وَنَزَّلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ مُّبَٰرَكًۭا فَأَنۢبَتْنَا بِهِۦ جَنَّٰتٍۢ وَحَبَّ ٱلْحَصِيدِ
en: And We send down blessed rain from the sky, bringing forth gardens and grains for harvest,
t1: And We showered blessed water from the sky and then produced with it gardens and (also) the grain of harvests,
t2: And We sent down out of heaven water blessed, and caused to grow thereby gardens and grain of harvest
t3: And We send down from the sky blessed water whereby We give growth unto gardens and the grain of crops,

ar: وَٱلنَّخْلَ بَاسِقَٰتٍۢ لَّهَا طَلْعٌۭ نَّضِيدٌۭ
en: and towering palm trees ˹loaded˺ with clustered fruit,
t1: And date-palms soaring high with layers of spathes.
t2: and tall palm-trees with spathes compact,
t3: And lofty date-palms with ranged clusters,

ar: رِّزْقًۭا لِّلْعِبَادِ ۖ وَأَحْيَيْنَا بِهِۦ بَلْدَةًۭ مَّيْتًۭا ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلْخُرُوجُ
en: ˹as˺ a provision for ˹Our˺ servants. And with this ˹rain˺ We revive a lifeless land. Similar is the emergence ˹from the graves˺.
t1: (This all is done as) sustenance for the servants, and We gave life with this (water) to the dead earth. In like manner is (your) coming forth from the graves.
t2: a provision for the servants, and thereby We revived a land that was dead. Even so is the coming forth.
t3: Provision (made) for men; and therewith We quicken a dead land. Even so will be the resurrection of the dead.

ar: كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍۢ وَأَصْحَٰبُ ٱلرَّسِّ وَثَمُودُ
en: Before them, the people of Noah denied ˹the truth,˺ as did the people of the Water-pit, Thamûd,
t1: Before these (disbelievers of Mecca), the people of Nuh (Noah) and the people of the blind well (al-Rass in al-Yamama) and Thamud (the people of Salih, in the town of al-Hijr near Tabuk on the Medina-Syria road),
t2: Cried lies before them the people of Noah and the men of Er-Rass, and Thamood,
t3: The folk of Noah denied (the truth) before them, and (so did) the dwellers at Ar-Rass and (the tribe of) Thamud,

ar: وَعَادٌۭ وَفِرْعَوْنُ وَإِخْوَٰنُ لُوطٍۢ
en: ’Ȃd, Pharaoh, the kinfolk of Lot,
t1: And ‘Ad (the people of Hud in Ahqaf valley of Yemen situated between Oman and the al-Mahra) and Pharaoh (the ruler of Egypt) and the people of Lut [Lot] (living in Sodom and ‘Amura [Gomorrah] in Palestine),
t2: and Ad and Pharaoh, the brothers of Lot,
t3: And (the tribe of) A’ad, and Pharaoh, and the brethren of Lot,

ar: وَأَصْحَٰبُ ٱلْأَيْكَةِ وَقَوْمُ تُبَّعٍۢ ۚ كُلٌّۭ كَذَّبَ ٱلرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ وَعِيدِ
en: the residents of the Forest, Each rejected ˹their˺ messenger, so My warning was fulfilled.
t1: And the inhabitants of al-Ayka (the wood in Madyan, the people of Shu‘ayb), and the people of Tubba‘ (the people of As‘ad Abu Kurib al-Himyari, the King of Yemen)—(in sum) all (of them) rejected the Messengers. So My promise of punishment (against them) proved true.
t2: the men of the Thicket, the people of Tubba’. Every one cried lies to the Messengers, and My threat came true.
t3: And the dwellers in the wood, and the folk of Tubb’a: every one denied their messengers, therefor My threat took effect.

ar: أَفَعَيِينَا بِٱلْخَلْقِ ٱلْأَوَّلِ ۚ بَلْ هُمْ فِى لَبْسٍۢ مِّنْ خَلْقٍۢ جَدِيدٍۢ
en: Were We incapable of creating ˹them˺ the first time? In fact, they are in doubt about ˹their˺ re-creation.
t1: So are We tired by the first creation? (Nay!) In fact, it is they who are in doubt about the new creation.
t2: What, were We wearied by the first creation? No indeed; but they are in uncertainty as to the new creation.
t3: Were We then worn out by the first creation ? Yet they are in doubt about a new creation.

ar: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِۦ نَفْسُهُۥ ۖ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
en: Indeed, ˹it is˺ We ˹Who˺ created humankind and ˹fully˺ know what their souls whisper to them, and We are closer to them than ˹their˺ jugular vein.
t1: And assuredly, We created man and We know (also) the doubts which his (ill-commanding) self puts (into his heart and mind). And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.
t2: We indeed created man; and We know what his soul whispers within him, and We are nearer to him than the jugular vein.
t3: We verily created man and We know what his soul whispereth to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.

ar: إِذْ يَتَلَقَّى ٱلْمُتَلَقِّيَانِ عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ قَعِيدٌۭ
en: As the two recording-angels—˹one˺ sitting to the right, and ˹the other to˺ the left—note ˹everything˺,
t1: When the two receivers receive (the recording angels write down his every communication and work), sitting on the right and on the left,
t2: When the two angels meet together, sitting one on the right, and one on the left,
t3: When the two Receivers receive (him), seated on the right hand and on the left,

ar: مَّا يَلْفِظُ مِن قَوْلٍ إِلَّا لَدَيْهِ رَقِيبٌ عَتِيدٌۭ
en: not a word does a person utter without having a ˹vigilant˺ observer ready ˹to write it down˺.
t1: Not a word does he utter but a watcher is there beside him ready (to write it).
t2: not a word he utters, but by him is an observer ready.
t3: He uttereth no word but there is with him an observer ready.

ar: وَجَآءَتْ سَكْرَةُ ٱلْمَوْتِ بِٱلْحَقِّ ۖ ذَٰلِكَ مَا كُنتَ مِنْهُ تَحِيدُ
en: ˹Ultimately,˺ with the throes of death will come the truth. This is what you were trying to escape!
t1: And the stupor of death comes with the truth. (O man,) that is what you were running away from!
t2: And death’s agony comes in truth; that is what thou wast shunning!
t3: And the agony of death cometh in truth. (And it is said unto him): This is that which thou wast wont to shun.

ar: وَنُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ يَوْمُ ٱلْوَعِيدِ
en: And the Trumpet will be blown. This is the Day ˹you were˺ warned of.
t1: And the Trumpet will be blown. It is (this torment) the Day of Warning.
t2: And the Trumpet shall be blown; that is the Day of the Threat.
t3: And the trumpet is blown. This is the threatened Day.

ar: وَجَآءَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍۢ مَّعَهَا سَآئِقٌۭ وَشَهِيدٌۭ
en: Each soul will come forth with an angel to drive it and another to testify.
t1: And every soul will appear (before Our presence), one (angel) forcing it forward and (the other) a witness (to its actions).
t2: And every soul shall come, and with it a driver and a witness.
t3: And every soul cometh, along with it a driver and a witness.

ar: لَّقَدْ كُنتَ فِى غَفْلَةٍۢ مِّنْ هَٰذَا فَكَشَفْنَا عَنكَ غِطَآءَكَ فَبَصَرُكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌۭ
en: ˹It will be said to the denier,˺ “You were totally heedless of this. Now We have lifted this veil of yours, so Today your sight is sharp!”
t1: The truth is that you were negligent of this (Day), so We have removed your veil (of negligence) and Today your sight is sharp.
t2: ’Thou wast heedless of this; therefore We have now removed from thee thy covering, and so thy sight today is piercing.’
t3: (And unto the evil-doer it is said): Thou wast in heedlessness of this. Now We have removed from thee thy covering, and piercing is thy sight this day.

ar: وَقَالَ قَرِينُهُۥ هَٰذَا مَا لَدَىَّ عَتِيدٌ
en: And one’s accompanying-angel will say, “Here is the record ready with me.”
t1: And his close companion (angel) will say: ‘That is what I have ready (for you).’
t2: And his comrade shall say, ’This is what I have, made ready.’
t3: And (unto the evil-doer) his comrade saith: This is that which I have ready (as testimony).

ar: أَلْقِيَا فِى جَهَنَّمَ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ عَنِيدٍۢ
en: ˹It will be said to both angels,˺ “Throw into Hell every stubborn disbeliever,
t1: (It will be commanded:) ‘Both of you hurl into Hell every (such) ungrateful rebel,
t2: ’Cast, you twain, into Gehenna every froward unbeliever,
t3: (And it is said): Do ye twain hurl to hell each rebel ingrate,

ar: مَّنَّاعٍۢ لِّلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍۢ مُّرِيبٍ
en: withholder of good, transgressor, and doubter,
t1: That hinders from good, exceeds the limits, doubts and puts into doubt,
t2: every hinderer of the good, transgressor, disquieter,
t3: Hinderer of good, transgressor, doubter,

ar: ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَأَلْقِيَاهُ فِى ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلشَّدِيدِ
en: who set up another god with Allah. So cast them into the severe punishment.”
t1: That had set up another god besides Allah. So hurl him into a fierce torment.’
t2: who set up with God another god; therefore, you twain, cast him into the terrible chastisement.’
t3: Who setteth up another god along with Allah. Do ye twain hurl him to the dreadful doom.

ar: ۞ قَالَ قَرِينُهُۥ رَبَّنَا مَآ أَطْغَيْتُهُۥ وَلَٰكِن كَانَ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۭ بَعِيدٍۢ
en: One’s ˹devilish˺ associate will say, “Our Lord! I did not make them transgress. Rather, they were far astray ˹on their own˺.”
t1: (Now) his (other) companion (Satan) will say: ‘O our Lord, I did not misguide him. In fact, he was himself suffering from misguidance of extreme degree.’
t2: And his comrade shall say, ’Our Lord, I made him not insolent, but he was in far error.’
t3: His comrade saith: Our Lord! I did not cause him to rebel, but he was (himself) far gone in error.

ar: قَالَ لَا تَخْتَصِمُوا۟ لَدَىَّ وَقَدْ قَدَّمْتُ إِلَيْكُم بِٱلْوَعِيدِ
en: Allah will respond, “Do not dispute in My presence, since I had already given you a warning.
t1: Allah will say: ‘Do not dispute in My presence whilst I have already sent you the warning (of punishment).
t2: He shall say, ’Dispute not before Me! For I sent you beforehand -- the threat.
t3: He saith: Contend not in My presence, when I had already proffered unto you the warning.

ar: مَا يُبَدَّلُ ٱلْقَوْلُ لَدَىَّ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ بِظَلَّٰمٍۢ لِّلْعَبِيدِ
en: My Word cannot be changed, nor am I unjust to ˹My˺ creation.”
t1: The command is never changed in My presence. Nor do I wrong the servants.’
t2: The Word is not changed with Me; I wrong not My servants.’
t3: The sentence that cometh from Me cannot be changed, and I am in no wise a tyrant unto the slaves.

ar: يَوْمَ نَقُولُ لِجَهَنَّمَ هَلِ ٱمْتَلَأْتِ وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِن مَّزِيدٍۢ
en: ˹Beware of˺ the Day We will ask Hell, “Are you full ˹yet˺?” And it will respond, “Are there any more?”
t1: That Day We shall ask Hell: ‘Are you filled up?’ And it will say: ‘Is there any more?’
t2: Upon the day We shall say unto Gehenna, ’Art thou filled?’ And it shall say, ’Are there any more to come?’
t3: On the day when We say unto hell: Art thou filled ? and it saith: Can there be more to come ?

ar: وَأُزْلِفَتِ ٱلْجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ
en: And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous, not far off.
t1: And Paradise will be brought close to the pious; it will not be distant at all.
t2: And Paradise shall be brought forward to the godfearing, not afar:
t3: And the Garden is brought nigh for those who kept from evil, no longer distant.

ar: هَٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍۢ
en: ˹And it will be said to them,˺ “This is what you were promised, for whoever ˹constantly˺ turned ˹to Allah˺ and kept up ˹His commandments˺—
t1: (And it will be said to them:) ‘This is what you were promised; (it is meant) for everyone who turns to Allah in repentance and who guards (his Din [Religion] and faith),
t2: ’This is that you were promised; it is for every mindful penitent.’
t3: (And it is said): This is that which ye were promised. (It is) for every penitent and heedful one,

ar: مَّنْ خَشِىَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَجَآءَ بِقَلْبٍۢ مُّنِيبٍ
en: who were in awe of the Most Compassionate without seeing ˹Him˺, and have come with a heart turning ˹only to Him˺.
t1: Who fears the Most Kind (Lord) unseen, and comes (before the presence of Allah) with a heart turned in repentance.
t2: Whosoever fears the All-merciful in the Unseen, and comes with a penitent heart:
t3: Who feareth the Beneficent in secret and cometh with a contrite heart.

ar: ٱدْخُلُوهَا بِسَلَٰمٍۢ ۖ ذَٰلِكَ يَوْمُ ٱلْخُلُودِ
en: Enter it in peace. This is the Day of eternal life!”
t1: Enter it in peace; this is the Day of Eternity.’
t2: ’Enter it in peace! This is the Day of Eternity.’
t3: Enter it in peace. This is the day of immortality.

ar: لَهُم مَّا يَشَآءُونَ فِيهَا وَلَدَيْنَا مَزِيدٌۭ
en: There they will have whatever they desire, and with Us is ˹even˺ more.
t1: All those blessings which they will long for will be there for them in that (Paradise), and there is still another blessing with Us (or much more; so the lovers will be enchanted).
t2: Therein they shall have whatever they will; and with Us there is yet more.
t3: There they have all that they desire, and there is more with Us.

ar: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْنٍ هُمْ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُم بَطْشًۭا فَنَقَّبُوا۟ فِى ٱلْبِلَٰدِ هَلْ مِن مَّحِيصٍ
en: ˹Imagine˺ how many peoples We destroyed before them, who were far mightier than them. Then ˹when the torment came,˺ they ˹desperately˺ sought refuge in the land. ˹But˺ was there any escape?
t1: And how many generations We destroyed before them (the disbelievers and idolaters of Mecca) who were far stronger in power and might than they! So they searched the cities (of the world) to run away somewhere for refuge (from death or torment).
t2: How many a generation We destroyed before them that was stronger in valour than they, then they searched about in the land; was there any asylum?
t3: And how many a generation We destroyed before them, who were mightier than these in prowess so that they overran the lands! Had they any place of refuge (when the judgment came) ?

ar: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَذِكْرَىٰ لِمَن كَانَ لَهُۥ قَلْبٌ أَوْ أَلْقَى ٱلسَّمْعَ وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌۭ
en: Surely in this is a reminder for whoever has a ˹mindful˺ heart and lends an attentive ear.
t1: There is indeed sure warning and admonition in it for him who has a heart (vigilant and awake, far from negligence,) or listens with active attention (i.e., focuses attention having no contact with anyone other than Allah) and is in a state of (spiritual) vision (i.e., remains lost in the effulgent disclosures of Allah’s absolute beauty).
t2: Surely in that there is a reminder to him who has a heart, or will give ear with a present mind.
t3: Lo! therein verily is a reminder for him who hath a heart, or giveth ear with full intelligence.

ar: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِى سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍۢ وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِن لُّغُوبٍۢ
en: Indeed, We created the heavens and the earth and everything in between in six Days,
t1: And surely, We have created the heavens and the earth and that (universe) which is between the two in six periods and no fatigue has touched Us.
t2: We created the heavens and the earth, and what between them is, in six days, and no weariness touched Us.
t3: And verily We created the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, in six Days, and naught of weariness touched Us.

ar: فَٱصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ ٱلْغُرُوبِ
en: So be patient ˹O Prophet˺ with what they say. And glorify the praises of your Lord before sunrise and before sunset.
t1: So be patient with what they say and glorify your Lord with praise before sunrise and before sunset.
t2: So be thou patient under what they say, and proclaim thy Lord’s praise before the rising of the sun, and before its setting,
t3: Therefor (O Muhammad) bear with what they say, and hymn the praise of thy Lord before the rising and before the setting of the sun;

ar: وَمِنَ ٱلَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَأَدْبَٰرَ ٱلسُّجُودِ
en: And glorify Him during part of the night and after the prayers.
t1: And also glorify Him during some hours of the night and after the Prayers as well.
t2: and proclaim thy Lord’s praise in the night, and at the ends of the prostrations.
t3: And in the night-time hymn His praise, and after the (prescribed) prostrations.

ar: وَٱسْتَمِعْ يَوْمَ يُنَادِ ٱلْمُنَادِ مِن مَّكَانٍۢ قَرِيبٍۢ
en: And listen! On the Day the caller will call out from a near place,
t1: And listen attentively (of the Day) when a caller will call from a near place,
t2: And listen thou for the day when the caller shall call from a near place.
t3: And listen on the day when the crier crieth from a near place,

ar: يَوْمَ يَسْمَعُونَ ٱلصَّيْحَةَ بِٱلْحَقِّ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ يَوْمُ ٱلْخُرُوجِ
en: the Day all will hear the ˹mighty˺ Blast in ˹all˺ truth, that will be the Day of emergence ˹from the graves˺.
t1: The Day when people will assuredly hear a mighty roar. That will be the Day of coming out from the graves.
t2: On the day they hear the Cry in truth, that is the day of coming forth.
t3: The day when they will hear the (Awful) Cry in truth. That is the day of coming forth (from the graves).

ar: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْىِۦ وَنُمِيتُ وَإِلَيْنَا ٱلْمَصِيرُ
en: It is certainly We Who give life and cause death. And to Us is the final return.
t1: Surely, it is We Who give life, and it is We Who cause death, and to Us is the return.
t2: It is We who give life, and make to die, and to Us is the homecoming.
t3: Lo! We it is Who quicken and give death, and unto Us is the journeying.

ar: يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ ٱلْأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ سِرَاعًۭا ۚ ذَٰلِكَ حَشْرٌ عَلَيْنَا يَسِيرٌۭ
en: ˹Beware of˺ the Day the earth will split open, letting them rush forth. That will be an easy gathering for Us.
t1: The Day when the earth will split apart from above them, they will come out in haste. This raising them alive (i.e., gathering the people once again) is quite easy for Us.
t2: Upon the day when the earth is split asunder from about them as they hasten forth; that is a mustering easy for Us.
t3: On the day when the earth splitteth asunder from them, hastening forth (they come). That is a gathering easy for Us (to make).

ar: نَّحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ ۖ وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيْهِم بِجَبَّارٍۢ ۖ فَذَكِّرْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ مَن يَخَافُ وَعِيدِ
en: We know best what they say. And you ˹O Prophet˺ are not ˹there˺ to compel them ˹to believe˺. So remind with the Quran ˹only˺ those who fear My warning.
t1: We know best what they say, and you are not the one to coerce them. So advise by means of the Qur’an anyone who fears My threat of punishment.
t2: We know very well what they say; thou art not a tyrant over them. Therefore remind by the Koran him who fears My threat.
t3: We are Best Aware of what they say, and thou (O Muhammad) art in no wise a compeller over them. But warn by the Qur’an him who feareth My threat.

ar: وَٱلذَّٰرِيَٰتِ ذَرْوًۭا
en: By the winds scattering ˹dust˺,
t1: By the winds that blow and scatter,
t2: By the swift scatterers
t3: By those that winnow with a winnowing

ar: فَٱلْحَٰمِلَٰتِ وِقْرًۭا
en: and ˹the clouds˺ loaded with rain,
t1: And by the clouds that carry a heavy load (of water),
t2: and the burden-bearers
t3: And those that bear the burden (of the rain)

ar: فَٱلْجَٰرِيَٰتِ يُسْرًۭا
en: and ˹the ships˺ gliding with ease,
t1: And by the vessels that float with elegance,
t2: and the smooth runners
t3: And those that glide with ease (upon the sea)

ar: فَٱلْمُقَسِّمَٰتِ أَمْرًا
en: and ˹the angels˺ administering affairs by ˹Allah’s˺ command!
t1: And by the angels that distribute work,
t2: and the partitioners,
t3: And those who distribute (blessings) by command,

ar: إِنَّمَا تُوعَدُونَ لَصَادِقٌۭ
en: Indeed, what you are promised is true.
t1: Surely the promise (of the Hereafter) being made to you is absolutely true.
t2: surely that you are promised is true,
t3: Lo! that wherewith ye are threatened is indeed true,

ar: وَإِنَّ ٱلدِّينَ لَوَٰقِعٌۭ
en: And the Judgment will certainly come to pass.
t1: And surely, the reward and the punishment (of actions) are bound to take place.
t2: and surely the Doom is about to fall!
t3: And lo! the judgment will indeed befall.

ar: وَٱلسَّمَآءِ ذَاتِ ٱلْحُبُكِ
en: ˹And˺ by the heavens in their marvellous design!
t1: And by the heaven with its galaxies and orbits (of stars and planets),
t2: By heaven with all its tracks
t3: By the heaven full of paths,

ar: إِنَّكُمْ لَفِى قَوْلٍۢ مُّخْتَلِفٍۢ
en: Surely you are ˹lost˺ in conflicting views ˹regarding the truth˺.
t1: Certainly you are (caught) in inconsistent statements.
t2: surely you speak at variance,
t3: Lo! ye, forsooth, are of various opinion (concerning the truth).

ar: يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ مَنْ أُفِكَ
en: Only those ˹destined to be˺ deluded are turned away from it.
t1: He alone who is turned away (from the knowledge of pre-eternity) turns away (from the Holy Messenger [blessings and peace be upon him] and the Qur’an).
t2: and perverted therefrom are some.
t3: He is made to turn away from it who is (himself) averse.

ar: قُتِلَ ٱلْخَرَّٰصُونَ
en: Condemned are the liars—
t1: Ruined are those who tell lies out of assumption and conjecture,
t2: Perish the conjecturers
t3: Accursed be the conjecturers

ar: ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ فِى غَمْرَةٍۢ سَاهُونَ
en: those who are ˹steeped˺ in ignorance, totally heedless.
t1: Those who are oblivious (of the Hereafter) due to negligence and ignorance.
t2: who are dazed in perplexity
t3: Who are careless in an abyss!

ar: يَسْـَٔلُونَ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ
en: They ask ˹mockingly˺, “When is this Day of Judgment?”
t1: They ask: ‘When is the Day of Requital?’
t2: asking, ’When shall be the Day of Doom?’
t3: They ask: When is the Day of Judgment ?

ar: يَوْمَ هُمْ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ
en: ˹It is˺ the Day they will be tormented over the Fire.
t1: (Say:) ‘The Day (when) they will be roasted in the Fire of Hell.’
t2: Upon the day when they shall be tried at the Fire:
t3: (It is) the day when they will be tormented at the Fire,

ar: ذُوقُوا۟ فِتْنَتَكُمْ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى كُنتُم بِهِۦ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ
en: ˹They will be told,˺ “Taste your torment! This is what you sought to hasten.”
t1: (It will be said to them:) ‘Relish your punishment. It is this punishment which you seek to hasten.’
t2: ’Taste your trial! This is that you were seeking to hasten.’
t3: (And it will be said unto them): Taste your torment (which ye inflicted). This is what ye sought to hasten.

ar: إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِى جَنَّٰتٍۢ وَعُيُونٍ
en: Indeed, the righteous will be amid Gardens and springs,
t1: Surely, the pious will be (rejoicing) in gardens and springs,
t2: Surely the godfearing shall be among gardens and fountains
t3: Lo! those who keep from evil will dwell amid gardens and watersprings,

ar: ءَاخِذِينَ مَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ ۚ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَبْلَ ذَٰلِكَ مُحْسِنِينَ
en: ˹joyfully˺ receiving what their Lord will grant them. Before this ˹reward˺ they were truly good-doers ˹in the world˺:
t1: Receiving those blessings (in ecstatic delight) which their Lord will be giving them (with munificence and benevolence). Surely, it is they who were people of spiritual excellence (in their life) before this.
t2: taking whatsoever their Lord has given them; they were good-doers before that.
t3: Taking that which their Lord giveth them; for lo! aforetime they were doers of good;

ar: كَانُوا۟ قَلِيلًۭا مِّنَ ٱلَّيْلِ مَا يَهْجَعُونَ
en: they used to sleep only little in the night,
t1: They used to sleep at night only for a short while,
t2: Little of the night would they slumber,
t3: They used to sleep but little of the night,

ar: وَبِٱلْأَسْحَارِ هُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ
en: and pray for forgiveness before dawn.
t1: And used to (get up and) seek forgiveness in the later part of the night.
t2: and in the mornings they would ask for forgiveness;
t3: And ere the dawning of each day would seek forgiveness,

ar: وَفِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ حَقٌّۭ لِّلسَّآئِلِ وَٱلْمَحْرُومِ
en: And in their wealth there was a rightful share ˹fulfilled˺ for the beggar and the poor.
t1: And in their wealth was appointed a due share for the beggars and the destitute (i.e., all the needy).
t2: and the beggar and the outcast had a share in their wealth.
t3: And in their wealth the beggar and the outcast had due share.

ar: وَفِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ءَايَٰتٌۭ لِّلْمُوقِنِينَ
en: There are ˹countless˺ signs on earth for those with sure faith,
t1: And there are many signs in the earth for the people with the truth of certitude (i.e., people of perfect certitude),
t2: In the earth are signs for those having sure faith;
t3: And in the earth are portents for those whose faith is sure.

ar: وَفِىٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ ۚ أَفَلَا تُبْصِرُونَ
en: as there are within yourselves. Can you not see?
t1: And in your selves (as well). So do you not notice?
t2: and in your selves; what, do you not see?
t3: And (also) in yourselves. Can ye then not see ?

ar: وَفِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ رِزْقُكُمْ وَمَا تُوعَدُونَ
en: In heaven is your sustenance and whatever you are promised.
t1: And (also) there is sustenance for you in the heaven and (all that too) which you are promised.
t2: And in heaven is your provision, and that you are promised.
t3: And in the heaven is your providence and that which ye are promised;

ar: فَوَرَبِّ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ إِنَّهُۥ لَحَقٌّۭ مِّثْلَ مَآ أَنَّكُمْ تَنطِقُونَ
en: Then by the Lord of heaven and earth! ˹All˺ this is certainly as true as ˹the fact that˺ you can speak!
t1: So, by the Lord of heavens and the earth, this (promise of Ours) is true just as is your speech. (You firmly believe in what you utter.)
t2: So by the Lord of heaven and earth, it is as surely true as that you have speech.
t3: And by the Lord of the heavens and the earth, it is the truth, even as (it is true) that ye speak.

ar: هَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ
en: Has the story of Abraham’s honoured guests reached you ˹O Prophet˺?
t1: Has the news of the venerable guests of Ibrahim (Abraham) come to you?
t2: Hast thou received the story of the honoured guests of Abraham?
t3: Hath the story of Abraham’s honoured guests reached thee (O Muhammad) ?

ar: إِذْ دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًۭا ۖ قَالَ سَلَٰمٌۭ قَوْمٌۭ مُّنكَرُونَ
en: ˹Remember˺ when they entered his presence and greeted ˹him with˺, “Peace!” He replied, “Peace ˹be upon you˺!” ˹Then he said to himself,˺ “˹These are˺ an unfamiliar people.”
t1: When those (angels) came to him, they wished him peace. Ibrahim (Abraham) also said (in reply): ‘Peace (be upon you)!’ (and thought in his mind that) they were strangers.
t2: When they entered unto him, saying ’Peace!’ he said ’Peace! You are a people unknown to me.’
t3: When they came in unto him and said: Peace! he answered, Peace! (and thought): Folk unknown (to me).

ar: فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِۦ فَجَآءَ بِعِجْلٍۢ سَمِينٍۢ
en: Then he slipped off to his family and brought a fat ˹roasted˺ calf,
t1: Then he went to his home in haste and brought a healthy, roasted calf.
t2: Then he turned to his household and brought a fattened calf,
t3: Then he went apart unto his housefolk so that they brought a fatted calf;

ar: فَقَرَّبَهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ
en: and placed it before them, asking, “Will you not eat?”
t1: Then he presented it to them and said: ‘Will you not eat?’
t2: and he laid it before them saying, ’Will you not eat?’
t3: And he set it before them, saying: Will ye not eat ?

ar: فَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةًۭ ۖ قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ ۖ وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ عَلِيمٍۢ
en: ˹They did not eat,˺ so he grew fearful of them.
t1: Then he felt somewhat concerned about them (when they did not eat). They (the angels) said: ‘Do not worry,’ then they gave him the news about a son possessing knowledge and wisdom (Ishaq [Isaac]).
t2: Then he conceived a fear of them. They said, ’Be not afraid!’ And they gave him good tidings of a cunning boy.
t3: Then he conceived a fear of them. They said: Fear not! and gave him tidings of (the birth of) a wise son.

ar: فَأَقْبَلَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُهُۥ فِى صَرَّةٍۢ فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌۭ
en: Then his wife came forward with a cry, clasping her forehead ˹in astonishment˺, exclaiming, “˹A baby from˺ a barren, old woman!”
t1: Then his wife (Sara) came with a voice laden with wonder and frustration, patted her forehead in astonishment and said: ‘(Will) an old and barren woman (give birth to a child)?’
t2: Then came forward his wife, clamouring, and she smote her face, and said, ’An old woman, barren!’
t3: Then his wife came forward, making moan, and smote her face, and cried: A barren old woman!

ar: قَالُوا۟ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
en: They replied, “Such has your Lord decreed. He is truly the All-Wise, All-Knowing.”
t1: The (angels) said: ‘It will happen exactly as your Lord has said; surely, He is Most Wise, All-Knowing.’
t2: They said, ’So says thy Lord; He is the All-wise, the All-knowing.’
t3: They said: Even so saith thy Lord. Lo! He is the Wise, the Knower.

ar: ۞ قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكُمْ أَيُّهَا ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
en: ˹Later,˺ Abraham asked, “What is your mission, O  messengers?”
t1: Ibrahim (Abraham) said: ‘O deputed angels, what is your intent (for coming, apart from this good news)?’
t2: Said he, ’And what is your business, envoys?’
t3: (Abraham) said: And (afterward) what is your errand, O ye sent (from Allah) ?

ar: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّآ أُرْسِلْنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍۢ مُّجْرِمِينَ
en: They replied, “We have actually been sent to a wicked people,
t1: They said: ‘We have been sent to the evildoing people (the people of Lut [Lot]),
t2: They said, ’We have been sent to a people of sinners,
t3: They said: Lo! we are sent unto a guilty folk,

ar: لِنُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهِمْ حِجَارَةًۭ مِّن طِينٍۢ
en: to send upon them stones of ˹baked˺ clay,
t1: So that we may rain on them THE the stones of baked clay,
t2: to loose upon them stones of clay
t3: That we may send upon them stones of clay,

ar: مُّسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ
en: marked by your Lord for the transgressors.”
t1: (The stones) that have been marked from your Lord for those who transgress.’
t2: marked with thy Lord for the prodigal.
t3: Marked by thy Lord for (the destruction of) the wanton.

ar: فَأَخْرَجْنَا مَن كَانَ فِيهَا مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
en: Then ˹before the torment˺ We evacuated the believers from the city.
t1: Then We moved everyone who was of the believers in it out (from the town of the people of Lut [Lot]).
t2: So We brought forth such believers as were in it,
t3: Then we brought forth such believers as were there.

ar: فَمَا وَجَدْنَا فِيهَا غَيْرَ بَيْتٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ
en: But We only found one family that had submitted ˹to Allah˺.
t1: So We did not find in that town (any house) of the Muslims except one (in which were the Prophet Lut [Lot] and his two daughters).
t2: but We found not therein except one house of those that have surrendered themselves.
t3: But We found there but one house of those surrendered (to Allah).

ar: وَتَرَكْنَا فِيهَآ ءَايَةًۭ لِّلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلْأَلِيمَ
en: And We have left a sign there ˹as a lesson˺ for those who fear the painful punishment.
t1: And We made in that (town) a sign to subsist (as a lesson of warning) for those who fear the grievous torment.
t2: And therein We left a sign to those who fear the painful chastisement.
t3: And We left behind therein a portent for those who fear a painful doom.

ar: وَفِى مُوسَىٰٓ إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ بِسُلْطَٰنٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
en: And in ˹the story of˺ Moses ˹was another lesson,˺ when We sent him to Pharaoh with compelling proof,
t1: And (there are signs) in (the incident of) Musa (Moses) as well when We sent him to Pharaoh with clear proof.
t2: And also in Moses, when We sent him unto Pharaoh, with a clear authority,
t3: And in Moses (too, there is a portent) when We sent him unto Pharaoh with clear warrant,

ar: فَتَوَلَّىٰ بِرُكْنِهِۦ وَقَالَ سَٰحِرٌ أَوْ مَجْنُونٌۭ
en: but Pharaoh was carried away by his power, saying ˹of Moses˺, “A magician or a madman!”
t1: He turned away along with his cabinet members and said: ‘(Here is) a magician or a madman.’
t2: but he turned his back, with his court, saying, ’A sorcerer, or a man possessed!’
t3: But he withdrew (confiding) in his might, and said: A wizard or a madman.

ar: فَأَخَذْنَٰهُ وَجُنُودَهُۥ فَنَبَذْنَٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌۭ
en: So We seized him and his soldiers, casting them into the sea while he was blameworthy.
t1: Then We seized him and his army (with torment), and drowned them (all) in the river. And he was but the perpetrator of condemnable works.
t2: So We seized him and his hosts, and We cast them into the sea, and he blameworthy.
t3: So We seized him and his hosts and flung them in the sea, for he was reprobate.

ar: وَفِى عَادٍ إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلرِّيحَ ٱلْعَقِيمَ
en: And in ˹the story of˺ ’ad ˹was another lesson,˺ when We sent against them the devastating wind.
t1: And there is (a sign) in (the destruction of) the people of ‘Ad too when We sent upon them a wind devoid of any good and blessing.
t2: And also in Ad, when We loosed against them the withering wind
t3: And in (the tribe of) A’ad (there is a portent) when we sent the fatal wind against them.

ar: مَا تَذَرُ مِن شَىْءٍ أَتَتْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا جَعَلَتْهُ كَٱلرَّمِيمِ
en: There was nothing it came upon that it did not reduce to ashes.
t1: Whatever it passed over, it did not leave without turning it to dust.
t2: that left nothing it came upon, but made it as stuff decayed.
t3: It spared naught that it reached, but made it (all) as dust.

ar: وَفِى ثَمُودَ إِذْ قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَمَتَّعُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍۢ
en: And in ˹the story of˺ Thamûd ˹was another lesson,˺ when they were told, “Enjoy yourselves ˹only˺ for a ˹short˺ while.”
t1: And also there is (a sign of warning) in the (destruction of) the people of Thamud when they were told: ‘Take benefit for an appointed term.’
t2: And also in Thamood, when it was said to them, ’Take your enjoyment for a while!’
t3: And in (the tribe of) Thamud (there is a portent) when it was told them: Take your ease awhile.

ar: فَعَتَوْا۟ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ ٱلصَّٰعِقَةُ وَهُمْ يَنظُرُونَ
en: Still they persisted in defying the commands of their Lord, so they were overtaken by a ˹mighty˺ blast while they were looking on.
t1: But they disobeyed the command of their Lord. So a horrifying thunder seized them, and they could only stare at it stunned.
t2: Then they turned in disdain from the commandment of their Lord, and the thunderbolt took them and they themselves beholding
t3: But they rebelled against their Lord’s decree, and so the thunderbolt overtook them even while they gazed;

ar: فَمَا ٱسْتَطَٰعُوا۟ مِن قِيَامٍۢ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ مُنتَصِرِينَ
en: Then they were not able to rise up, nor were they helped.
t1: Then they could neither gather strength to stand, nor take revenge (on Us).
t2: and they were not able to stand upright, and were not helped.
t3: And they were unable to rise up, nor could they help themselves.

ar: وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍۢ مِّن قَبْلُ ۖ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًۭا فَٰسِقِينَ
en: And the people of Noah ˹had also been destroyed˺ earlier. They were truly a rebellious people.
t1: And (We also destroyed) the people of Nuh (Noah) before this. Surely, they were a people extremely disobedient.
t2: And the people of Noah before; surely they were an ungodly people.
t3: And the folk of Noah aforetime. Lo! they were licentious folk.

ar: وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بَنَيْنَٰهَا بِأَيْي۟دٍۢ وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ
en: We built the universe with ˹great˺ might, and We are certainly expanding ˹it˺.
t1: And We built the heavenly universe with great might. And surely, We are expanding (this universe) more and more.
t2: And heaven -- We built it with might, and We extend it wide.
t3: We have built the heaven with might, and We it is Who make the vast extent (thereof).

ar: وَٱلْأَرْضَ فَرَشْنَٰهَا فَنِعْمَ ٱلْمَٰهِدُونَ
en: As for the earth, We spread it out. How superbly did We smooth it out!
t1: And We alone made (the surface of the) earth a (livable) floor. So how graciously We make up and spread out!
t2: And the earth -- We spread it forth; O excellent Smoothers!
t3: And the earth have We laid out, how gracious is the Spreader (thereof)!

ar: وَمِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقْنَا زَوْجَيْنِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ
en: And We created pairs of all things so perhaps you would be mindful.
t1: And of everything We have created two pairs so that you may concentrate and understand.
t2: And of everything created We two kinds; haply you will remember
t3: And all things We have created by pairs, that haply ye may reflect.

ar: فَفِرُّوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ۖ إِنِّى لَكُم مِّنْهُ نَذِيرٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
en: So ˹proclaim, O  Prophet˺: “Flee to Allah! I am truly sent by Him with a clear warning to you.
t1: So run towards Allah. Surely, I am a clear Warner to you from Him.
t2: Therefore flee unto God! I am a clear warner from Him to you.
t3: Therefor flee unto Allah; lo! I am a plain warner unto you from him.

ar: وَلَا تَجْعَلُوا۟ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ ۖ إِنِّى لَكُم مِّنْهُ نَذِيرٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
en: And do not set up another god with Allah. I am truly sent by Him with a clear warning to you.”
t1: And do not set up any god apart from Allah. Surely, I am a clear Warner to you from Him.
t2: And set not up with God another god; I am a clear warner from Him to you.
t3: And set not any other god along with Allah; lo! I am a plain warner unto you from Him.

ar: كَذَٰلِكَ مَآ أَتَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا قَالُوا۟ سَاحِرٌ أَوْ مَجْنُونٌ
en: Similarly, no messenger came to those before them without being told: “A magician or a madman!”
t1: Likewise, no Messenger came to those before them, but they said the same: ‘(This is) a magician or a madman.’
t2: Even so not a Messenger came to those before them but they said, ’A sorcerer, or a man possessed!’
t3: Even so there came no messenger unto those before them but they said: A wizard or a madman!

ar: أَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِهِۦ ۚ بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌۭ طَاغُونَ
en: Have they passed this ˹cliché˺ down to one another? In fact, they have ˹all˺ been a transgressing people.
t1: Were they transmitting this advice to one another? In truth, they were (all) a disobedient and rebellious people.
t2: What, have they bequeathed it one to another? Nay, but they are an insolent people.
t3: Have they handed down (the saying) as an heirloom one unto another ? Nay, but they are froward folk.

ar: فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ فَمَآ أَنتَ بِمَلُومٍۢ
en: So ˹now˺ turn away from them ˹O Prophet˺, for you will not be blamed.
t1: So turn away your kind and caring looks from them. There is no blame on you (for their disbelief).
t2: So turn thou from them; thou wilt not be reproached.
t3: So withdraw from them (O Muhammad), for thou art in no wise blameworthy,

ar: وَذَكِّرْ فَإِنَّ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ تَنفَعُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
en: But ˹continue to˺ remind. For certainly reminders benefit the believers.
t1: And keep giving direction and guidance, for direction and guidance surely benefits the believers.
t2: And remind; the Reminder profits the believers.
t3: And warn, for warning profiteth believers.

ar: وَمَا خَلَقْتُ ٱلْجِنَّ وَٱلْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ
en: I did not create jinn and humans except to worship Me.
t1: And I created the jinn and human beings solely to adopt My servitude.
t2: I have not created jinn and mankind except to serve Me.
t3: I created the jinn and humankind only that they might worship Me.

ar: مَآ أُرِيدُ مِنْهُم مِّن رِّزْقٍۢ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَن يُطْعِمُونِ
en: I seek no provision from them, nor do I need them to feed Me.
t1: I do not ask for any sustenance (i.e., earning) from them, nor do I require that they should feed Me.
t2: I desire of them no provision, neither do I desire that they should feed Me.
t3: I seek no livelihood from them, nor do I ask that they should feed

ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلرَّزَّاقُ ذُو ٱلْقُوَّةِ ٱلْمَتِينُ
en: Indeed, Allah ˹alone˺ is the Supreme Provider—Lord of all Power, Ever Mighty.
t1: Truly, Allah alone is the Sustainer of everyone, the Lord of Great Might, the Most Strong. (He does not need anyone’s help and assistance.)
t2: Surely God is the All-provider, the Possessor of Strength, the Ever-Sure.
t3: Lo! Allah! He it is that giveth livelihood, the Lord of unbreakable might.

ar: فَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ ذَنُوبًۭا مِّثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصْحَٰبِهِمْ فَلَا يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ
en: The wrongdoers will certainly have a share ˹of the torment˺ like that of their predecessors. So do not let them ask Me to hasten ˹it˺.
t1: So there is a fixed share of the torment for these wrongdoers (too) like the share of the torment of their companions (who have passed before). So let them not ask Me to hasten (it).
t2: The evildoers shall have their portion, like the portion of their fellows; so let them not hasten Me!
t3: And lo! for those who (now) do wrong there is an evil day like unto the evil day (which came for) their likes (of old); so let them not ask Me to hasten on (that day).

ar: فَوَيْلٌۭ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن يَوْمِهِمُ ٱلَّذِى يُوعَدُونَ
en: Woe then to the disbelievers when they face their Day which they are warned of!
t1: So a terrible destruction awaits the disbelievers on that Day of theirs which they have been promised.
t2: So woe to the unbelievers, for that day of theirs that they are promised.
t3: And woe unto those who disbelieve, from (that) their day which they are promised.

ar: وَٱلطُّورِ
en: By Mount Ṭûr!
t1: By (the Mountain) Tur,
t2: By the Mount
t3: By the Mount,

ar: وَكِتَٰبٍۢ مَّسْطُورٍۢ
en: And by the Book written
t1: And by the Book inscribed,
t2: and a Book inscribed
t3: And a Scripture inscribed

ar: فِى رَقٍّۢ مَّنشُورٍۢ
en: on open pages ˹for all to read˺!
t1: (Which is) on an Unfolded Scroll,
t2: in a parchment unrolled,
t3: On fine parchment unrolled,

ar: وَٱلْبَيْتِ ٱلْمَعْمُورِ
en: And by the ˹Sacred˺ House frequently visited!
t1: And by the House populated (by the angels i.e., the Ka‘ba in heaven),
t2: by the House inhabited
t3: And the House frequented,

ar: وَٱلسَّقْفِ ٱلْمَرْفُوعِ
en: And by the canopy raised ˹high˺!
t1: And by the Lofty Roof (i.e., the High Heaven or the Most Exalted Throne),
t2: and the roof uplifted
t3: And the roof exalted,

ar: وَٱلْبَحْرِ ٱلْمَسْجُورِ
en: And by the seas set on fire!
t1: And by the swelling sea!
t2: and the sea swarming,
t3: And the sea kept filled,

ar: إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّكَ لَوَٰقِعٌۭ
en: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will come to pass—
t1: Surely, the torment of your Lord will do take place.
t2: surely thy Lord’s chastisement is about to fall;
t3: Lo! the doom of thy Lord will surely come to pass;

ar: مَّا لَهُۥ مِن دَافِعٍۢ
en: none will avert it—
t1: No one can avert it.
t2: there is none to avert it.
t3: There is none that can ward it off.

ar: يَوْمَ تَمُورُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ مَوْرًۭا
en: on the Day the heavens will be shaken violently,
t1: The Day when the heaven will shake with a terrible tremor,
t2: Upon the day when heaven spins dizzily
t3: On the day when the heaven will heave with (awful) heaving,

ar: وَتَسِيرُ ٱلْجِبَالُ سَيْرًۭا
en: and the mountains will be blown away entirely.
t1: And the mountains (leaving their locations) will fly fast (like clouds) and scatter (like dust particles),
t2: and the mountains are in motion,
t3: And the mountains move away with (awful) movement,

ar: فَوَيْلٌۭ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
en: Then woe on that Day to the deniers—
t1: So on that Day, woe to those who belie,
t2: woe that day unto those that cry lies,
t3: Then woe that day unto the deniers

ar: ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ فِى خَوْضٍۢ يَلْعَبُونَ
en: those who amuse themselves with falsehood!
t1: Those who are playing a game of negligence, rapt in falsehood (i.e., absurdity).
t2: such as play at plunging,
t3: Who play in talk of grave matters;

ar: يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلَىٰ نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا
en: ˹It is˺ the Day they will be fiercely shoved into the Fire of Hell.
t1: The Day when they will be forcefully pushed towards the Fire of Hell,
t2: the day when they shall be pitched into the fire of Gehenna:
t3: The day when they are thrust with a (disdainful) thrust, into the fire of hell

ar: هَٰذِهِ ٱلنَّارُ ٱلَّتِى كُنتُم بِهَا تُكَذِّبُونَ
en: ˹They will be told,˺ “This is the Fire which you used to deny.
t1: (It will be said to them:) ‘This is the Fire of Hell you used to belie.
t2: ’This is the fire that you cried lies to!
t3: (And it is said unto them): This is the Fire which ye were wont to deny.

ar: أَفَسِحْرٌ هَٰذَآ أَمْ أَنتُمْ لَا تُبْصِرُونَ
en: Is this magic, or do you not see?
t1: So is it magic, or do you not see?
t2: What, is this magic, or is it you that do not see?
t3: Is this magic, or do ye not see ?

ar: ٱصْلَوْهَا فَٱصْبِرُوٓا۟ أَوْ لَا تَصْبِرُوا۟ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ ۖ إِنَّمَا تُجْزَوْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
en: Burn in it! It is the same whether you endure ˹it˺ patiently or not. You are only rewarded for what you used to do.”
t1: Enter it. Then it is all the same for you whether you observe patience, or you do not observe patience. You will be paid only for those deeds which you used to do.’
t2: Roast in it! And bear you patiently, or bear not patiently, equal it is to you; you are only being recompensed for that you were working.’
t3: Endure the heat thereof, and whether ye are patient of it or impatient of it is all one for you. Ye are only being paid for what ye used to do.

ar: إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِى جَنَّٰتٍۢ وَنَعِيمٍۢ
en: Indeed, the righteous will be in Gardens and bliss,
t1: Surely, the Godfearing will be in the Gardens and Bliss.
t2: Surely the godfearing shall be in gardens and bliss,
t3: Lo! those who kept their duty dwell in gardens and delight,

ar: فَٰكِهِينَ بِمَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ وَوَقَىٰهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
en: enjoying whatever their Lord will have granted them. And their Lord will have protected them from the torment of the Hellfire.
t1: They will be delighted at (the bestowals) their Lord will have blessed them with. And their Lord will keep them safe from the punishment of Hell.
t2: rejoicing in that their Lord has given them; and their Lord shall guard them against the chastisement of Hell.
t3: Happy because of what their Lord hath given them, and (because) their Lord hath warded off from them the torment of hell-fire.

ar: كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ هَنِيٓـًٔۢا بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
en: ˹They will be told,˺ “Eat and drink happily for what you used to do.”
t1: (It will be said to them:) ‘Relish food and drink as a reward for the (pious) deeds which you used to do.’
t2: ’Eat and drink, with wholesome appetite, for that you were working.
t3: (And it is said unto them): Eat and drink in health (as a reward) for what ye used to do,

ar: مُتَّكِـِٔينَ عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍۢ مَّصْفُوفَةٍۢ ۖ وَزَوَّجْنَٰهُم بِحُورٍ عِينٍۢ
en: They will be reclining on thrones, ˹neatly˺ lined up ˹facing each other˺. And We will pair them to maidens with gorgeous eyes.
t1: They will be reclining (sitting) on couches arranged in rows, and We will marry them to maidens with fair colour (and) fascinating eyes.
t2: Reclining upon couches ranged in rows; and We shall espouse them to wide-eyed houris.
t3: Reclining on ranged couches. And we wed them unto fair ones with wide, lovely eyes.

ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُم بِإِيمَٰنٍ أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَمَآ أَلَتْنَٰهُم مِّنْ عَمَلِهِم مِّن شَىْءٍۢ ۚ كُلُّ ٱمْرِئٍۭ بِمَا كَسَبَ رَهِينٌۭ
en: As for those who believe and whose descendants follow them in faith, We will elevate their descendants to their rank, never discounting anything ˹of the reward˺ of their deeds. Every person will reap only what they sowed.
t1: And those who believe and whose children follow them in faith, We shall also unite their children with them (in the ranks of Paradise even if their actions would not fall in that grade. It would be in the honour of their pious fathers). And We shall also not reduce in anyway the reward of the actions of their (pious fathers. Besides this,) everyone will be held in (reward and punishment for) his own works.
t2: And those who believed, and their seed followed them in belief, We shall join their seed with them, and We shall not defraud them of aught of their work; every man shall be pledged for what he earned.
t3: And they who believe and whose seed follow them in faith, We cause their seed to join them (there), and We deprive them of nought of their (life’s) work. Every man is a pledge for that which he hath earned.

ar: وَأَمْدَدْنَٰهُم بِفَٰكِهَةٍۢ وَلَحْمٍۢ مِّمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ
en: And We will ˹continually˺ provide them with whatever fruit or meat they desire.
t1: And We will keep giving them fruit and meat more and more as they desire.
t2: And We shall succour them with fruits and flesh such as they desire
t3: And We provide them with fruit and meat such as they desire.

ar: يَتَنَٰزَعُونَ فِيهَا كَأْسًۭا لَّا لَغْوٌۭ فِيهَا وَلَا تَأْثِيمٌۭ
en: They will pass around to each other a drink ˹of pure wine,˺ which leads to no idle talk or sinfulness.
t1: There, they will take the cups (of holy drink) by grabbing. This (holy drink of Paradise) will be free of foolish talk and sinful acts.
t2: while they pass therein a cup one to another wherein is no idle talk, no cause of sin,
t3: There they pass from hand to hand a cup wherein is neither vanity nor cause of sin.

ar: ۞ وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ غِلْمَانٌۭ لَّهُمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ لُؤْلُؤٌۭ مَّكْنُونٌۭ
en: And they will be waited on by their youthful servants like spotless pearls.
t1: And (the serving) youths will go round them as if they were pearls kept hidden in covers.
t2: and there go round them youths, their own, as if they were hidden pearls.
t3: And there go round, waiting on them menservants of their own, as they were hidden pearls.

ar: وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍۢ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
en: They will turn to one another inquisitively.
t1: And they will turn to one another, enquiring well-being.
t2: They advance one upon another, asking each other questions.
t3: And some of them draw near unto others, questioning,

ar: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا كُنَّا قَبْلُ فِىٓ أَهْلِنَا مُشْفِقِينَ
en: They will say, “Before ˹this reward˺ we used to be in awe ˹of Allah˺ in the midst of our people.
t1: They will say: ‘Surely before this, we used to live in fear (of Allah’s torment) in our homes.
t2: They say, ’We were before among our people, ever going in fear,
t3: Saying: Lo! of old, when we were with our families, we were ever anxious;

ar: فَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا وَوَقَىٰنَا عَذَابَ ٱلسَّمُومِ
en: So Allah has graced us and protected us from the torment of ˹Hell’s˺ scorching heat.
t1: So Allah has been Gracious to favour us and has saved us from the punishment of the Fire of Hell.
t2: and God was gracious to us, and guarded us against the chastisement of the burning wind;
t3: But Allah hath been gracious unto us and hath preserved us from the torment of the breath of Fire.

ar: إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبْلُ نَدْعُوهُ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْبَرُّ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
en: Indeed, we used to call upon Him ˹alone˺ before. He is truly the Most Kind, Most Merciful.”
t1: Indeed, we used to worship Him alone beforehand. Surely, He is Most Gracious, Ever-Merciful.’
t2: we were before ever calling upon Him; surely He is the All-benign, the All-compassionate.’
t3: Lo! we used to pray unto Him of old. Lo! He is the Benign, the Merciful.

ar: فَذَكِّرْ فَمَآ أَنتَ بِنِعْمَتِ رَبِّكَ بِكَاهِنٍۢ وَلَا مَجْنُونٍ
en: So ˹continue to˺ remind ˹all, O  Prophet˺. For you, by the grace of your Lord, are not a fortune-teller or a madman.
t1: So, (O Esteemed Beloved,) continue to admonish (them). By the grace and blessing of your Lord, you are neither a soothsayer (the one who gives news through the jinn) nor a madman.
t2: Therefore remind! by thy Lord’s blessing thou art not a soothsayer neither possessed.
t3: Therefor warn (men, O Muhammad). By the grace of Allah thou art neither soothsayer nor madman.

ar: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ شَاعِرٌۭ نَّتَرَبَّصُ بِهِۦ رَيْبَ ٱلْمَنُونِ
en: Or do they say, “˹He is˺ a poet, for whom we ˹eagerly˺ await an ill-fate!”?
t1: Do the disbelievers say: ‘(He is) a poet for whom we look forward to some temporal disasters’?
t2: Or do they say, ’He is a poet for whom we await Fate’s uncertainty’?
t3: Or say they: (he is) a poet, (one) for whom we may expect the accident of time ?

ar: قُلْ تَرَبَّصُوا۟ فَإِنِّى مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْمُتَرَبِّصِينَ
