en: Or are you asking them for a reward ˹for the message˺ so that they are overburdened by debt?
t1: Do you ask them for any reward (for preaching the faith in Messengership) that they are weighed down with (the burden of) paying the recompense?
t2: Or askest thou them for a wage, and so they are weighed down with debt?
t3: Or dost thou (Muhammad) ask a fee from them so that they are heavily taxed ?

ar: أَمْ عِندَهُمُ ٱلْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ
en: Or do they have access to ˹the Record in˺ the unseen, so they copy it ˹for all to see˺?
t1: Do they have the knowledge of the unseen that they write down (their judgments on the basis of that)?
t2: Or is the Unseen in their keeping, and so they are writing it down?
t3: Or is the Unseen theirs that they can write (thereof) ?

ar: فَٱصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ ٱلْحُوتِ إِذْ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌۭ
en: So be patient with your Lord’s decree, and do not be like ˹Jonah,˺ the Man of the Whale, who cried out ˹to Allah˺, in total distress.
t1: So be steadfast in waiting for the command of your Lord, and do not (take it to your heart) like (Yunus [Jonah], the Messenger with) fish episode, when he cried out (to Allah) in a state pent up with rage and grief (against his community).
t2: So be thou patient under the judgment of thy Lord, and be not as the Man of the Fish, when he called, choking inwardly.
t3: But wait thou for thy Lord’s decree, and be not like him of the fish, who cried out in despair.

ar: لَّوْلَآ أَن تَدَٰرَكَهُۥ نِعْمَةٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦ لَنُبِذَ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌۭ
en: Had he not been shown grace by his Lord, he would have certainly been cast onto the open ˹shore˺, still blameworthy.
t1: Had the mercy and blessing of his Lord not helped him, he would certainly have been thrown in the barren field, blamed. (But Allah saved him from that.)
t2: Had there not overtaken him a blessing from his Lord he would have been cast upon the wilderness, being condemned.
t3: Had it not been that favour from his Lord had reached him he surely had been cast into the wilderness while he was reprobate.

ar: فَٱجْتَبَٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَجَعَلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
en: Then his Lord chose him, making him one of the righteous.
t1: Then his Lord exalted him and (placed him) amongst the perfectly pious (blessing him with His exceptional nearness).
t2: But his Lord had chosen him, and He placed him among the righteous.
t3: But his Lord chose him and placed him among the righteous.

ar: وَإِن يَكَادُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأَبْصَٰرِهِمْ لَمَّا سَمِعُوا۟ ٱلذِّكْرَ وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُۥ لَمَجْنُونٌۭ
en: The disbelievers would almost cut you down with their eyes when they hear ˹you recite˺ the Reminder, and say, “He is certainly a madman.”
t1: And indeed, when the disbelievers listen to the Qur’an, it seems as if they wish to damage you with their (jealously evil) looks and say: ‘He is insane.’
t2: The unbelievers wellnigh strike thee down with their glances, when they hear the Reminder, and they say, ’Surely he is a man possessed!’
t3: And lo! those who disbelieve would fain disconcert thee with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and they say: Lo! he is indeed mad;

ar: وَمَا هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌۭ لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: But it is simply a reminder to the whole world.
t1: And it (the Qur’an) is direction and guidance for all the worlds.
t2: And it is nothing but a Reminder unto all beings.
t3: When it is naught else than a Reminder to creation.

ar: ٱلْحَآقَّةُ
en: The Inevitable Hour!
t1: The surely Inevitable Hour!
t2: The Indubitable!
t3: The Reality!

ar: مَا ٱلْحَآقَّةُ
en: What is the Inevitable Hour?
t1: What is the surely Inevitable Hour?
t2: What is the Indubitable?
t3: What is the Reality ?

ar: وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا ٱلْحَآقَّةُ
en: And what will make you realize what the Inevitable Hour is?
t1: And what has made you alert what (calamity) surely is the Inevitable Hour?
t2: And what will teach thee what is the Indubitable?
t3: Ah, what will convey unto thee what the reality is!

ar: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ وَعَادٌۢ بِٱلْقَارِعَةِ
en: ˹Both˺ Thamûd and ’Ȃd denied the Striking Disaster.
t1: Thamud and ‘Ad rejected the (calamity of a) Shattering Gravitational Collision (of all the existent cosmic bodies).
t2: Thamood and Ad cried lies to the Clatterer.
t3: (The tribes of) Thamud and A’ad disbelieved in the judgment to come.

ar: فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا۟ بِٱلطَّاغِيَةِ
en: As for Thamûd, they were destroyed by an overwhelming blast.
t1: So, as for the people of Thamud, they were destroyed by the extremely violent, Deafening Blast.
t2: As for Thamood, they were destroyed by the Screamer;
t3: As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the lightning.

ar: وَأَمَّا عَادٌۭ فَأُهْلِكُوا۟ بِرِيحٍۢ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍۢ
en: And as for ’Ȃd, they were destroyed by a furious, bitter wind
t1: And as for the people of ‘Ad, they (too) were destroyed by a violently cold, roaring gale.
t2: and as for Ad, they were destroyed by a wind clamorous,
t3: And as for A’ad, they were destroyed by a fierce roaring wind,

ar: سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍۢ وَثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًۭا فَتَرَى ٱلْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍۢ
en: which Allah unleashed on them non-stop for seven nights and eight days, so that you would have seen its people lying dead like trunks of uprooted palm trees.
t1: Allah made that (gale) seize them for consecutive seven nights and eight days. So, you could see them lying dead (during that time as if) they were hollow roots of the uprooted palm trees.
t2: violent that He compelled against them seven nights and eight days, uninterruptedly, and thou mightest see the people laid prostrate in it as if they were the stumps of fallen down palm-trees.
t3: Which He imposed on them for seven long nights and eight long days so that thou mightest have seen men lying overthrown, as they were hollow trunks of palm-trees.

ar: فَهَلْ تَرَىٰ لَهُم مِّنۢ بَاقِيَةٍۢ
en: Do you see any of them left alive?
t1: So do you see any of them surviving?
t2: Now dost thou see any remnant of them?
t3: Canst thou (O Muhammad) see any remnant of them ?

ar: وَجَآءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَن قَبْلَهُۥ وَٱلْمُؤْتَفِكَٰتُ بِٱلْخَاطِئَةِ
en: Also, Pharaoh and those before him, and ˹the people of˺ the overturned cities ˹of Lot˺ indulged in sin,
t1: And Pharaoh and those before him and (the dwellers of) the overthrown towns (of the community of Lut [Lot]) committed grave sins.
t2: Pharaoh likewise, and those before him, and the Subverted Cities -- they committed error,
t3: And Pharaoh and those before him, and the communities that were destroyed, brought error,

ar: فَعَصَوْا۟ رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَهُمْ أَخْذَةًۭ رَّابِيَةً
en: each disobeying their Lord’s messenger, so He seized them with a crushing grip.
t1: So they (also) disobeyed the Messenger of their Lord. And Allah seized them with a mighty seizure.
t2: and they rebelled against the Messenger of their Lord, and He seized them with a surpassing grip.
t3: And they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, therefor did He grip them with a tightening grip.

ar: إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَا ٱلْمَآءُ حَمَلْنَٰكُمْ فِى ٱلْجَارِيَةِ
en: Indeed, when the floodwater had overflowed, We carried you in the floating Ark ˹with Noah˺,
t1: Indeed, when the water (of the Deluge) overflowed the limit, We carried you in the floating Ark,
t2: Lo, when the waters rose, We bore you in the running ship
t3: Lo! when the waters rose, We carried you upon the ship

ar: لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةًۭ وَتَعِيَهَآ أُذُنٌۭ وَٰعِيَةٌۭ
en: so that We may make this a reminder to you, and that attentive ears may grasp it.
t1: So that We make this (episode a reminding) lesson of warning for you and that the retentive ears may retain it.
t2: that We might make it a reminder for you and for heeding ears to hold.
t3: That We might make it a memorial for you, and that remembering ears (that heard the story) might remember.

ar: فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌۭ وَٰحِدَةٌۭ
en: At last, when the Trumpet will be blown with one blast,
t1: Then when the Trumpet will be blown once,
t2: So, when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast
t3: And when the trumpet shall sound one blast

ar: وَحُمِلَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ
en: and the earth and mountains will be lifted up and crushed with one blow,
t1: And the earth and mountains will be removed (from their places), they will then be crushed to sand particles in a single crash.
t2: and the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with a single blow,
t3: And the earth with the mountains shall be lifted up and crushed with one crash,

ar: فَيَوْمَئِذٍۢ وَقَعَتِ ٱلْوَاقِعَةُ
en: on that Day the Inevitable Event will have come to pass.
t1: Then that will be the Hour when the surely Inevitable (calamity) will occur.
t2: then, on that day, the Terror shall come to pass,
t3: Then, on that day will the Event befall.

ar: وَٱنشَقَّتِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ فَهِىَ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ وَاهِيَةٌۭ
en: The sky will then be so torn that it will be frail,
t1: And (all) the heavenly bodies will split apart and this universe will come to comprise (black) holes (by means of a force which coordinates and keeps the system going).*
t2: and heaven shall be split, for upon that day it shall be very frail,
t3: And the heaven will split asunder, for that day it will be frail.

ar: وَٱلْمَلَكُ عَلَىٰٓ أَرْجَآئِهَا ۚ وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ ثَمَٰنِيَةٌۭ
en: with the angels on its sides. On that Day eight ˹mighty angels˺ will bear the Throne of your Lord above them.
t1: And the angels will be standing on its edges and above them that Day, and eight (angels or parties of angels) will be carrying the Throne of your Lord.
t2: and the angels shall stand upon its borders, and upon that day eight shall carry above them the Throne of thy Lord.
t3: And the angels will be on the sides thereof, and eight will uphold the Throne of thy Lord that day, above them.

ar: يَوْمَئِذٍۢ تُعْرَضُونَ لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌۭ
en: You will then be presented ˹before Him for judgment˺, and none of your secrets will stay hidden.
t1: That Day you will be made to appear (for reckoning). Nothing of your secrets will remain hidden.
t2: On that day you shall be exposed, not one secret of yours concealed.
t3: On that day ye will be exposed; not a secret of you will be hidden.

ar: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِيَمِينِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ هَآؤُمُ ٱقْرَءُوا۟ كِتَٰبِيَهْ
en: As for those given their records in their right hand, they will cry ˹happily˺, “Here ˹everyone˺! Read my record!
t1: So the one who will be given his record in the right hand will say (pleased): ‘Come and read my record.
t2: Then as for him who is given his book in his right hand, he shall say, ’Here, take and read my book!
t3: Then, as for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: Take, read my book!

ar: إِنِّى ظَنَنتُ أَنِّى مُلَٰقٍ حِسَابِيَهْ
en: I surely knew I would face my reckoning.”
t1: I firmly believed that I would find my account (easy).’
t2: Certainly I thought that I should encounter my reckoning.’
t3: Surely I knew that I should have to meet my reckoning.

ar: فَهُوَ فِى عِيشَةٍۢ رَّاضِيَةٍۢ
en: They will be in a life of bliss,
t1: So he will live a pleasant life,
t2: So he shall be in a pleasing life
t3: Then he will be in blissful state

ar: فِى جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍۢ
en: in an elevated Garden,
t1: In an elevated lofty Paradise,
t2: in a lofty Garden,
t3: In a high garden

ar: قُطُوفُهَا دَانِيَةٌۭ
en: whose fruit will hang within reach.
t1: The clusters of its fruits hanging low (due to abundance).
t2: its clusters nigh to gather.
t3: Whereof the clusters are in easy reach.

ar: كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ هَنِيٓـًٔۢا بِمَآ أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِى ٱلْأَيَّامِ ٱلْخَالِيَةِ
en: ˹They will be told,˺ “Eat and drink joyfully for what you did in the days gone by.”
t1: (It will be said to them:) ‘Eat and drink rejoicing, in recompense of (your deeds) that you had sent forward during the days of your past (life).’
t2: ’Eat and drink with wholesome appetite for that you did long ago, in the days gone by.’
t3: (And it will be said unto those therein): Eat and drink at ease for that which ye sent on before you in past days.

ar: وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِشِمَالِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيْتَنِى لَمْ أُوتَ كِتَٰبِيَهْ
en: And as for those given their record in their left hand, they will cry ˹bitterly˺, “I wish I had not been given my record,
t1: And as for him who will be given his record in his left hand, he will say: ‘Would that I had not been given my record!
t2: But as for him who is given his book in his left hand, he shall say, ’Would that I had not been given my book
t3: But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say: Oh, would that I had not been given my book

ar: وَلَمْ أَدْرِ مَا حِسَابِيَهْ
en: nor known anything of my reckoning!
t1: And would that I had not known about my account!
t2: and not known my reckoning!
t3: And knew not what my reckoning!

ar: يَٰلَيْتَهَا كَانَتِ ٱلْقَاضِيَةَ
en: I wish death was the end!
t1: Alas! Would that (death) had settled my affair once and for all!
t2: Would it had been the end!
t3: Oh, would that it had been death!

ar: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنِّى مَالِيَهْ ۜ
en: My wealth has not benefited me!
t1: Today my wealth has not been able to keep (the torment) away from me even a little.
t2: My wealth has not availed me,
t3: My wealth hath not availed me,

ar: هَلَكَ عَنِّى سُلْطَٰنِيَهْ
en: My authority has been stripped from me.”
t1: My power and domain have (also) gone from me.’
t2: my authority is gone from me.’
t3: My power hath gone from me.

ar: خُذُوهُ فَغُلُّوهُ
en: ˹It will be said,˺ “Seize and shackle them,
t1: (It will be commanded:) ‘Seize him and put him in neck-fetter.
t2: ’Take him, and fetter him,
t3: (It will be said): Take him and fetter him

ar: ثُمَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ
en: then burn them in Hell,
t1: Then cast him into Hell.
t2: and then roast him in Hell,
t3: And then expose him to hell-fire

ar: ثُمَّ فِى سِلْسِلَةٍۢ ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ ذِرَاعًۭا فَٱسْلُكُوهُ
en: then tie them up with chains seventy arms long.
t1: Then bind him tightly in a seventy yard long chain.
t2: then in a chain of seventy cubits’ length insert him!
t3: And then insert him in a chain whereof the length is seventy cubits.

ar: إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
en: For they never had faith in Allah, the Greatest,
t1: Verily, he did not believe in Allah, the Lord of Majesty.
t2: Behold, he never believed in God the All-mighty,
t3: Lo! He used not to believe in Allah the Tremendous,

ar: وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ
en: nor encouraged the feeding of the poor.
t1: Nor did he urge the feeding of the poor.
t2: and he never urged the feeding of the needy;
t3: And urged not on the feeding of the wretched.

ar: فَلَيْسَ لَهُ ٱلْيَوْمَ هَٰهُنَا حَمِيمٌۭ
en: So this Day they will have no close friend here,
t1: So Today he does not have any warm friend.
t2: therefore he today has not here one loyal friend,
t3: Therefor hath he no lover here this day,

ar: وَلَا طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍۢ
en: nor any food except ˹oozing˺ pus,
t1: Nor has he anything to eat except filthy pus,
t2: neither any food saving foul pus,
t3: Nor any food save filth

ar: لَّا يَأْكُلُهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱلْخَٰطِـُٔونَ
en: which none will eat except the evildoers.”
t1: That no one will eat except the sinners.’
t2: that none excepting the sinners eat.’
t3: Which none but sinners eat.

ar: فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُونَ
en: Now, I do swear by whatever you see,
t1: So I swear by the things that you see,
t2: No! I swear by that you see
t3: But nay! I swear by all that ye see

ar: وَمَا لَا تُبْصِرُونَ
en: and whatever you cannot see!
t1: And by those things that you do not see.
t2: and by that you do not see,
t3: And all that ye see not

ar: إِنَّهُۥ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍۢ كَرِيمٍۢ
en: Indeed, this ˹Quran˺ is the recitation of a noble Messenger.
t1: Assuredly, this (Qur’an) is the (God-sent) commandment of the Exalted and Glorious Messenger ([blessings and peace be upon him] which he expounds as a Messenger and as a Vicegerent).
t2: it is the speech of a noble Messenger.
t3: That it is indeed the speech of an illustrious messenger.

ar: وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَاعِرٍۢ ۚ قَلِيلًۭا مَّا تُؤْمِنُونَ
en: It is not the prose of a poet ˹as you claim˺, ˹yet˺ you hardly have any faith.
t1: And it is not the poetry of a poet (composed with literary expertise). You have but little faith.
t2: It is not the speech of a poet (little do you believe)
t3: It is not poet’s speech - little is it that ye believe!

ar: وَلَا بِقَوْلِ كَاهِنٍۢ ۚ قَلِيلًۭا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ
en: Nor is it the mumbling of a fortune-teller, ˹yet˺ you are hardly mindful.
t1: Nor is it the word of a fortune-teller (designed by skilful guesswork). You take but little advice.
t2: nor the speech of a soothsayer (little do you remember).
t3: Nor diviner’s speech - little is it that ye remember!

ar: تَنزِيلٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: ˹It is˺ a revelation from the Lord of all worlds.
t1: (This) is sent down by the Lord of all the worlds.
t2: A sending down from the Lord of all Being.
t3: It is a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds.

ar: وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنَا بَعْضَ ٱلْأَقَاوِيلِ
en: Had the Messenger made up something in Our Name,
t1: And had he ascribed to Us even a (single) fabricated thing,
t2: Had he invented against Us any sayings,
t3: And if he had invented false sayings concerning Us,

ar: لَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُ بِٱلْيَمِينِ
en: We would have certainly seized him by his right hand,
t1: We would have seized him with full force and might,
t2: We would have seized him by the right hand,
t3: We assuredly had taken him by the right hand

ar: ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنَا مِنْهُ ٱلْوَتِينَ
en: then severed his aorta,
t1: Then certainly We would have cut his life artery,
t2: then We would surely have cut his life-vein
t3: And then severed his life-artery,

ar: فَمَا مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَٰجِزِينَ
en: and none of you could have shielded him ˹from Us˺!
t1: Then no one of you could have held (Us) back from it.
t2: and not one of you could have defended him.
t3: And not one of you could have held Us off from him.

ar: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَتَذْكِرَةٌۭ لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ
en: Indeed, this ˹Quran˺ is a reminder to those mindful ˹of Allah˺.
t1: So no doubt this (Qur’an) is direction and guidance for the Godfearing.
t2: Surely it is a Reminder to the godfearing;
t3: And lo! it is a warrant unto those who ward off (evil).

ar: وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنكُم مُّكَذِّبِينَ
en: And We certainly know that some of you will persist in denial,
t1: And surely, We know that some of you are the beliers (of this open truth).
t2: but We know that some of you will cry lies.
t3: And lo! We know that some among you will deny (it).

ar: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
en: and it will surely be a source of regret for the disbelievers.
t1: And surely, this is (a cause of) bitter regret for the disbelievers.
t2: Surely it is a sorrow to the unbelievers;
t3: And lo! it is indeed an anguish for the disbelievers.

ar: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَحَقُّ ٱلْيَقِينِ
en: And indeed, this ˹Quran˺ is the absolute truth.
t1: And undeniably, it is the truth of Absolute Certitude.
t2: yet indeed it is the truth of certainty.
t3: And lo! it is absolute truth.

ar: فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
en: So glorify the Name of your Lord, the Greatest.
t1: So, (O Esteemed Beloved,) glorify your Lord, Most Magnificent, with persistence.
t2: Then magnify the Name of thy Lord, the All-mighty.
t3: So glorify the name of thy Tremendous Lord.

ar: سَأَلَ سَآئِلٌۢ بِعَذَابٍۢ وَاقِعٍۢ
en: A challenger has demanded a punishment bound to come
t1: A questioner asked for the torment which is sure to come about,
t2: A questioner asked of a chastisement about to fall
t3: A questioner questioned concerning the doom about to fall

ar: لِّلْكَٰفِرِينَ لَيْسَ لَهُۥ دَافِعٌۭ
en: for the disbelievers—to be averted by none—
t1: Upon the disbelievers, which no one can repel.
t2: for the unbelievers, which none may avert,
t3: Upon the disbelievers, which none can repel,

ar: مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ذِى ٱلْمَعَارِجِ
en: from Allah, Lord of pathways of ˹heavenly˺ ascent,
t1: (That will befall) from Allah, Who is the Lord of the Ascending Steps to Heaven (and of the higher ranks and grades of spiritual hierarchy).
t2: from God, the Lord of the Stairways.
t3: From Allah, Lord of the Ascending Stairways

ar: تَعْرُجُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ إِلَيْهِ فِى يَوْمٍۢ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُۥ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍۢ
en: ˹through which˺ the angels and the ˹holy˺ spirit
t1: The angels and al-Ruh al-Amin (the Spirit) rise towards His (Throne) in a Day which measures fifty thousand years (according to the worldly scale).*
t2: To Him the angels and the Spirit mount up, in a day whereof the measure is fifty thousand years.
t3: (Whereby) the angels and the Spirit ascend unto Him in a Day whereof the span is fifty thousand years.

ar: فَٱصْبِرْ صَبْرًۭا جَمِيلًا
en: So endure ˹this denial, O  Prophet,˺ with beautiful patience.
t1: So, (O Beloved,) observe patience (on the assertions of the disbelievers) without regrets.
t2: So be thou patient with a sweet patience;
t3: But be patient (O Muhammad) with a patience fair to see.

ar: إِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَهُۥ بَعِيدًۭا
en: They truly see this ˹Day˺ as impossible,
t1: Surely, they imagine that (Day) to be far off,
t2: behold, they see it as if far off;
t3: Lo! they behold it afar off

ar: وَنَرَىٰهُ قَرِيبًۭا
en: but We see it as inevitable.
t1: But We see it very near.
t2: but We see it is nigh.
t3: While we behold it nigh:

ar: يَوْمَ تَكُونُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ كَٱلْمُهْلِ
en: On that Day the sky will be like molten brass
t1: On that Day the sky will become like molten copper,
t2: Upon the day when heaven shall be as molten copper
t3: The day when the sky will become as molten copper,

ar: وَتَكُونُ ٱلْجِبَالُ كَٱلْعِهْنِ
en: and the mountains like ˹tufts of˺ wool.
t1: And the mountains like (flakes of) coloured wool,
t2: and the mountains shall be as plucked wool-tufts,
t3: And the hills become as flakes of wool,

ar: وَلَا يَسْـَٔلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيمًۭا
en: And no close friend will ask ˹about˺ their friends,
t1: And no friend will enquire after his friend,
t2: no loyal friend shall question loyal friend,
t3: And no familiar friend will ask a question of his friend

ar: يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ ۚ يَوَدُّ ٱلْمُجْرِمُ لَوْ يَفْتَدِى مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِئِذٍۭ بِبَنِيهِ
en: ˹although˺ they will be made to see each other. The wicked will wish to ransom themselves from the punishment of that Day by their children,
t1: (Though) they will be shown (to one another). The sinner would desire to ransom himself from the torment of that Day by his children,
t2: as they are given sight of them. The sinner will wish that he might ransom himself from the chastisement of that day even by his sons,
t3: Though they will be given sight of them. The guilty man will long to be able to ransom himself from the punishment of that day at the price of his children

ar: وَصَٰحِبَتِهِۦ وَأَخِيهِ
en: their spouses, their siblings,
t1: And (by giving) his wife and his brother,
t2: his companion wife, his brother,
t3: And his spouse and his brother

ar: وَفَصِيلَتِهِ ٱلَّتِى تُـْٔوِيهِ
en: their clan that sheltered them,
t1: And (all) his family who used to provide him shelter,
t2: his kin who sheltered him,
t3: And his kin that harboured him

ar: وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ
en: and everyone on earth altogether, just to save themselves.
t1: And all the people on earth (as recompense for himself), so that this (atonement) may save him from (Allah’s torment).
t2: and whosoever is in the earth, all together, so that then it might deliver him.
t3: And all that are in the earth, if then it might deliver him.

ar: كَلَّآ ۖ إِنَّهَا لَظَىٰ
en: But no! There will certainly be a raging Flame
t1: But no! By no means! Surely, that is a Flaming Fire,
t2: Nay, verily it is a furnace
t3: But nay! for lo! it is the fire of hell

ar: نَزَّاعَةًۭ لِّلشَّوَىٰ
en: ripping off scalps.
t1: Stripping off the skin of all the limbs and the scalp.
t2: snatching away the scalp,
t3: Eager to roast;

ar: تَدْعُوا۟ مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
en: It will summon whoever turned their backs ˹on Allah˺ and turned away ˹from the truth˺,
t1: It is calling him who turned his back (on the truth) and turned away,
t2: calling him who drew back and turned away,
t3: It calleth him who turned and fled (from truth),

ar: وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعَىٰٓ
en: and gathered and hoarded ˹wealth˺.
t1: And (he who) accumulated wealth and then held it (from distribution).
t2: who amassed and hoarded.
t3: And hoarded (wealth) and withheld it.

ar: ۞ إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعًا
en: Indeed, humankind was created impatient:
t1: Surely, man has been created impatient and greedy.
t2: Surely man was created fretful,
t3: Lo! man was created anxious,

ar: إِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ جَزُوعًۭا
en: distressed when touched with evil,
t1: He gets upset and worried when some hardship (or financial loss) afflicts him,
t2: when evil visits him, impatient,
t3: Fretful when evil befalleth him

ar: وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلْخَيْرُ مَنُوعًا
en: and withholding when touched with good—
t1: But becomes miserly when he receives good fortune (or affluence),
t2: when good visits him, grudging,
t3: And, when good befalleth him, grudging;

ar: إِلَّا ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ
en: except those who pray,
t1: Except for those who offer Prayer,
t2: save those that pray
t3: Save worshippers.

ar: ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَىٰ صَلَاتِهِمْ دَآئِمُونَ
en: consistently performing their prayers;
t1: And are constant in their Prayer,
t2: and continue at their prayers,
t3: Who are constant at their worship

ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ حَقٌّۭ مَّعْلُومٌۭ
en: and who give the rightful share of their wealth
t1: And those (who are committed to sacrifice and) in whose wealth there is a fixed share,
t2: those in whose wealth is a right known
t3: And in whose wealth there is a right acknowledged

ar: لِّلسَّآئِلِ وَٱلْمَحْرُومِ
en: to the beggar and the poor;
t1: Of one who begs and of one who is needy but does not beg,
t2: for the beggar and the outcast,
t3: For the beggar and the destitute;

ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُصَدِّقُونَ بِيَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ
en: and who ˹firmly˺ believe in the Day of Judgment;
t1: And those who affirm the Day of Requital,
t2: who confirm the Day of Doom
t3: And those who believe in the Day of Judgment,

ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم مِّنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّهِم مُّشْفِقُونَ
en: and those who fear the punishment of their Lord—
t1: And those who fear the torment of their Lord;
t2: and go in fear of the chastisement of their Lord
t3: And those who are fearful of their Lord’s doom -

ar: إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّهِمْ غَيْرُ مَأْمُونٍۢ
en: ˹knowing that˺ none should feel secure from their Lord’s punishment—
t1: Surely, the torment of their Lord is not a thing which should not be feared;
t2: (from their Lord’s chastisement none feels secure)
t3: Lo! the doom of their Lord is that before which none can feel secure -

ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَٰفِظُونَ
en: and those who guard their chastity
t1: And those who safeguard their private parts,
t2: and guard their private parts
t3: And those who preserve their chastity

ar: إِلَّا عَلَىٰٓ أَزْوَٰجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ
en: except with their wives or those ˹bondwomen˺ in their possession, for then they are free from blame,
t1: Except from their wives or the female slaves they possess. So (in this) there is no blame on them.
t2: save from their wives and what their right hands own, then not being blameworthy
t3: Save with their wives and those whom their right hands possess, for thus they are not blameworthy;

ar: فَمَنِ ٱبْتَغَىٰ وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْعَادُونَ
en: but whoever seeks beyond that are the transgressors.
t1: But he who looks for more than that, then it is they who transgress the limits.
t2: (but whoso seeks after more than that, they are the transgressors),
t3: But whoso seeketh more than that, those are they who are transgressors;

ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَمَٰنَٰتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ رَٰعُونَ
en: ˹The faithful are˺ also those who are true to their trusts and covenants;
t1: And those who safeguard their trusts and promises,
t2: and who preserve their trusts and their covenant,
t3: And those who keep their pledges and their covenant,

ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِشَهَٰدَٰتِهِمْ قَآئِمُونَ
en: and who are honest in their testimony;
t1: And those who stand firm on their testimonies,
t2: and perform their witnessings,
t3: And those who stand by their testimony

ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَىٰ صَلَاتِهِمْ يُحَافِظُونَ
en: and who are ˹properly˺ observant of their prayers.
t1: And those who safeguard their Prayers,
t2: and who observe their prayers.
t3: And those who are attentive at their worship.

ar: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ فِى جَنَّٰتٍۢ مُّكْرَمُونَ
en: These will be in Gardens, held in honour.
t1: It is they who will enjoy great honour and respect in the Gardens.
t2: Those shall be in Gardens, high-honoured.
t3: These will dwell in Gardens, honoured.

ar: فَمَالِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ قِبَلَكَ مُهْطِعِينَ
en: So what is the matter with the disbelievers that they rush ˹head-long˺ towards you ˹O Prophet˺,
t1: So what is the matter with the disbelievers that they are coming towards you running,
t2: What ails the unbelievers, running with outstretched necks
t3: What aileth those who disbelieve, that they keep staring toward thee (O Muhammad), open-eyed,

ar: عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ عِزِينَ
en: from the right and the left, in groups ˹to mock you˺?
t1: From the right as well as the left, in groups?
t2: towards thee on the right hand and on the left hand in knots?
t3: On the right and on the left, in groups ?

ar: أَيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِئٍۢ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُدْخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍۢ
en: Does every one of them expect to be admitted into a Garden of Bliss?
t1: Does every one of them hope that he may be admitted to the Garden of Bliss (without faith and deeds)?
t2: What, is every man of them eager to be admitted to a Garden of Bliss?
t3: Doth every man among them hope to enter the Garden of Delight ?

ar: كَلَّآ ۖ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰهُم مِّمَّا يَعْلَمُونَ
en: But no! Indeed, they ˹already˺ know what We created them from.
t1: Certainly not! Surely, We have created them from a substance which they (also) know.
t2: Not so; for We have created them of what they know.
t3: Nay, verily. Lo! We created them from what they know.

ar: فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْمَشَٰرِقِ وَٱلْمَغَٰرِبِ إِنَّا لَقَٰدِرُونَ
en: So, I do swear by the Lord of ˹all˺ the points of sunrise and sunset that We are truly capable
t1: So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests that surely We have Absolute Power,
t2: No! I swear by the Lord of the Easts and Wests, surely We are able
t3: But nay! I swear by the Lord of the rising-places and the setting- places of the planets that We verily are Able

ar: عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّبَدِّلَ خَيْرًۭا مِّنْهُمْ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ
en: of replacing them with ˹others˺ better than them, and We cannot be prevented ˹from doing so˺.
t1: To replace them with people better than them and We are not at all incapable (of doing it).
t2: to substitute a better than they; We shall not be outstripped.
t3: To replace them by (others) better than them. And we are not to be outrun.

ar: فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُوا۟ وَيَلْعَبُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ يُلَٰقُوا۟ يَوْمَهُمُ ٱلَّذِى يُوعَدُونَ
en: So let them indulge ˹in falsehood˺ and amuse ˹themselves˺ until they face their Day, which they have been threatened with—
t1: So leave them occupied with their absurd talk and pastime until they meet that Day of theirs which they have been promised.
t2: Then leave them alone to plunge and play until they encounter that day of theirs which they are promised,
t3: So let them chat and play until they meet their Day which they are promised,

ar: يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلْأَجْدَاثِ سِرَاعًۭا كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَىٰ نُصُبٍۢ يُوفِضُونَ
en: the Day they will come forth from the graves swiftly, as if racing to an idol ˹for a blessing˺,
t1: The Day when they will come forth from their graves in haste as if they are running towards the temples of their idols.
t2: the day they shall come forth from the tombs hastily, as if they were hurrying unto a waymark,
t3: The day when they come forth from the graves in haste, as racing to a goal,

ar: خَٰشِعَةً أَبْصَٰرُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌۭ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمُ ٱلَّذِى كَانُوا۟ يُوعَدُونَ
en: with eyes downcast, utterly covered with disgrace. That is the Day they have ˹always˺ been warned of.
t1: (Their plight) will be that their eyes will be cast down (with shame and fear) and disgrace enveloping them. It is this Day which they were promised.
t2: humbled their eyes, overspreading them abasement. That is the day which they were promised.
t3: With eyes aghast, abasement stupefying them: Such is the Day which they are promised.

ar: إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦٓ أَنْ أَنذِرْ قَوْمَكَ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌۭ
en: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people ˹saying to him˺, “Warn your people before a painful punishment comes to them.”
t1: Surely, We sent Nuh (Noah) to his people: ‘Warn your people before a painful torment comes upon them.’
t2: We sent Noah to his people, saying, ’Warn thy people, ere there come on them a painful chastisement.’
t3: Lo! We sent Noah unto his people (saying): Warn thy people ere the painful doom come unto them.

ar: قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ إِنِّى لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌۭ مُّبِينٌ
en: Noah proclaimed, “O my people! I am truly sent to you with a clear warning:
t1: He said: ‘O my people! Indeed, I am a clear Warner to you,
t2: He said, ’O my people, I am unto you a clear warner,
t3: He said: O my people! Lo! I am a plain warner unto you

ar: أَنِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ
en: worship Allah ˹alone˺, fear Him, and obey me.
t1: That you must worship Allah and fear Him and obey me.
t2: saying, "Serve God, and fear Him, and obey you me,
t3: (Bidding you): Serve Allah and keep your duty unto Him and obey me,

ar: يَغْفِرْ لَكُم مِّن ذُنُوبِكُمْ وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّى ۚ إِنَّ أَجَلَ ٱللَّهِ إِذَا جَآءَ لَا يُؤَخَّرُ ۖ لَوْ كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
en: He will forgive your sins, and delay your end until the appointed time. Indeed, when the time set by Allah comes, it cannot be delayed, if only you knew!”
t1: He will forgive your sins and will give you respite till an appointed term. Surely, when (the appointed) time of Allah comes, then respite is not given if only you knew.’
t2: nd He will forgive you your sins, and defer you to a stated term; God’s term, when it comes, cannot be deferred, did you but know."’
t3: That He may forgive you somewhat of your sins and respite you to an appointed term. Lo! the term of Allah, when it cometh, cannot be delayed, if ye but knew.

ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى دَعَوْتُ قَوْمِى لَيْلًۭا وَنَهَارًۭا
en: He cried, “My Lord! I have surely called my people day and night,
t1: Nuh (Noah) submitted: ‘O my Lord! Indeed, I kept calling my people night and day,
t2: He said; ’My Lord, I have called my people by night and by day,
t3: He said: My Lord! Lo! I have called unto my people night and day

ar: فَلَمْ يَزِدْهُمْ دُعَآءِىٓ إِلَّا فِرَارًۭا
en: but my calls only made them run farther away.
t1: But my calling did no good except making them flee away.
t2: but my calling has only increased them in flight.
t3: But all my calling doth but add to their repugnance;

ar: وَإِنِّى كُلَّمَا دَعَوْتُهُمْ لِتَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ جَعَلُوٓا۟ أَصَٰبِعَهُمْ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ وَٱسْتَغْشَوْا۟ ثِيَابَهُمْ وَأَصَرُّوا۟ وَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ ٱسْتِكْبَارًۭا
en: And whenever I invite them to be forgiven by You, they press their fingers into their ears, cover themselves with their clothes, persist ˹in denial˺, and act very arrogantly.
t1: And every time I called them (towards faith) so that You might forgive them, they only thrust their fingers into their ears and wrapped their clothes over themselves and stuck obstinately (to disbelief) and behaved most arrogantly.
t2: And whenever I called them, that Thou mightest forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, and wrapped them in their garments, and persisted, and waxed very proud.
t3: And lo! whenever I call unto them that Thou mayst pardon them they thrust their fingers in their ears and cover themselves with their garments and persist (in their refusal) and magnify themselves in pride.

ar: ثُمَّ إِنِّى دَعَوْتُهُمْ جِهَارًۭا
en: Then I certainly called them openly,
t1: Then I called them aloud.
t2: Then indeed I called them openly;
t3: And lo! I have called unto them aloud,

ar: ثُمَّ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَنتُ لَهُمْ وَأَسْرَرْتُ لَهُمْ إِسْرَارًۭا
en: then I surely preached to them publicly and privately,
t1: Then I advised them publicly and privately and secretly (as well).
t2: then indeed I spoke publicly unto them, and I spoke unto them secretly,
t3: And lo! I have made public proclamation unto them, and I have appealed to them in private.

ar: فَقُلْتُ ٱسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ غَفَّارًۭا
en: saying, ‘Seek your Lord’s forgiveness, ˹for˺ He is truly Most Forgiving.
t1: Then I said: ‘Seek forgiveness from your Lord. Surely, He is Most Forgiving.
t2: and I said, "Ask you forgiveness of your Lord; surely He is ever All-forgiving,
t3: And I have said: Seek pardon of your Lord. Lo! He was ever Forgiving.

ar: يُرْسِلِ ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيْكُم مِّدْرَارًۭا
en: He will shower you with abundant rain,
t1: He will send down on you torrents of rain,
t2: and He will loose heaven upon you in torrents
t3: He will let loose the sky for you in plenteous rain,

ar: وَيُمْدِدْكُم بِأَمْوَٰلٍۢ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجْعَل لَّكُمْ جَنَّٰتٍۢ وَيَجْعَل لَّكُمْ أَنْهَٰرًۭا
en: supply you with wealth and children, and give you gardens as well as rivers.
t1: And will help you with wealth and sons and will grow for you gardens and will make streams flow for you.
t2: and will succour you with wealth and sons, and will appoint for you gardens, and will appoint for you rivers.
t3: And will help you with wealth and sons, and will assign unto you Gardens and will assign unto you rivers.

ar: مَّا لَكُمْ لَا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَارًۭا
en: What is the matter with you that you are not in awe of the Majesty of Allah,
t1: What is the matter with you that you do not have faith in, or the gnosis of, Allah’s Majesty,
t2: What ails you, that you look not for majesty in God,
t3: What aileth you that ye hope not toward Allah for dignity

ar: وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ أَطْوَارًا
en: when He truly created you in stages ˹of development˺?
t1: Whereas He has created you through diverse conditions?
t2: seeing He created you by stages?
t3: When He created you by (divers) stages ?

ar: أَلَمْ تَرَوْا۟ كَيْفَ خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَمَٰوَٰتٍۢ طِبَاقًۭا
en: Do you not see how Allah created seven heavens, one above the other,
t1: Have you not seen how Allah has created seven (or many) heavenly spheres corresponding to one another (layer upon layer)?
t2: Have you not regarded how God created seven heavens one upon another,
t3: See ye not how Allah hath created seven heavens in harmony,

ar: وَجَعَلَ ٱلْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًۭا وَجَعَلَ ٱلشَّمْسَ سِرَاجًۭا
en: placing the moon within them as a ˹reflected˺ light, and the sun as a ˹radiant˺ lamp?
t1: And He brightened in them the moon and made the sun a radiant lamp (i.e., the source of light and heat).
t2: and set the moon therein for a light and the sun for a lamp?
t3: And hath made the moon a light therein, and made the sun a lamp ?

ar: وَٱللَّهُ أَنۢبَتَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًۭا
en: Allah ˹alone˺ caused you to grow from the earth like a plant.
t1: And Allah has caused you to grow like vegetation from the earth.*
t2: And God caused you to grow out of the earth,
t3: And Allah hath caused you to grow as a growth from the earth,

ar: ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًۭا
en: Then He will return you to it, and then simply bring you forth ˹again˺.
t1: Then He will return you into the same (earth) and will then bring you forth (from the same again).
t2: then He shall return you into it, and bring you forth.
t3: And afterward He maketh you return thereto, and He will bring you forth again, a (new) forthbringing.

ar: وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ بِسَاطًۭا
en: And Allah ˹alone˺ spread out the earth for you
t1: And Allah has made the earth a vast expanse for you,
t2: And God has laid the earth for you as a carpet,
t3: And Allah hath made the earth a wide expanse for you

ar: لِّتَسْلُكُوا۟ مِنْهَا سُبُلًۭا فِجَاجًۭا
en: to walk along its spacious pathways.’”
t1: So that you may move around through its broad ways.’
t2: that thereof you may thread ways, ravines."
t3: That ye may thread the valley-ways thereof.

ar: قَالَ نُوحٌۭ رَّبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِى وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ مَن لَّمْ يَزِدْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَوَلَدُهُۥٓ إِلَّا خَسَارًۭا
en: ˹Eventually,˺ Noah cried, “My Lord! They have certainly persisted in disobeying me, and followed ˹instead˺ those ˹elite˺ whose ˹abundant˺ wealth and children only increase them in loss,
t1: Nuh (Noah) submitted: ‘O my Lord! They have disobeyed me and kept following that (class of the rebellious rich) whose wealth and children have not increased for them anything but loss.
t2: Noah said, ’My Lord, they have rebelled against me, and followed him whose wealth and children increase him only in loss,
t3: Noah said: My Lord! Lo! they have disobeyed me and followed one whose wealth and children increase him in naught save ruin;

ar: وَمَكَرُوا۟ مَكْرًۭا كُبَّارًۭا
en: and who have devised a tremendous plot,
t1: And they kept perpetrating huge frauds (to keep the common man in error).
t2: and have devised a mighty device
t3: And they have plotted a mighty plot,

ar: وَقَالُوا۟ لَا تَذَرُنَّ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّۭا وَلَا سُوَاعًۭا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْرًۭا
en: urging ˹their followers˺, ‘Do not abandon your idols—especially Wadd, Suwa’, Yaghûth, Ya’ûq, and Nasr.’
t1: And they kept saying: Do not turn away from your gods and never abandon (the idols named as) Wadd, Suwa‘, Yaghuth, Ya‘uq and Nasr (as well).
t2: and have said, "Do not leave your gods, and do not leave Wadd, nor Suwa’, Yaghuth, Ya’uq, neither Nasr."
t3: And they have said: Forsake not your gods. Forsake not Wadd, nor Suwa’, nor Yaghuth and Ya’uq and Nasr.

ar: وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا۟ كَثِيرًۭا ۖ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلَٰلًۭا
en: Those ˹elite˺ have already led many astray. So ˹O Lord˺, only allow the wrongdoers to stray farther away.”
t1: And truly, they have misled many people. So, (O my Lord,) do not increase these wrongdoers (in anything) except misguidance.’
t2: And they have led many astray. Increase Thou not the evildoers save in error!’
t3: And they have led many astray, and Thou increasest the wrong-doers in naught save error.

ar: مِّمَّا خَطِيٓـَٰٔتِهِمْ أُغْرِقُوا۟ فَأُدْخِلُوا۟ نَارًۭا فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا۟ لَهُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَنصَارًۭا
en: So because of their sins, they were drowned, then admitted into the Fire. And they found none to help them against Allah.
t1: (In the end) they were drowned due to their sins and then flung into Fire. So they could not find any helper for themselves against Allah.
t2: And because of their transgressions they were drowned, and admitted into a Fire, for they found not, apart from God, any to help them.
t3: Because of their sins they were drowned, then made to enter a Fire. And they found they had no helpers in place of Allah.

ar: وَقَالَ نُوحٌۭ رَّبِّ لَا تَذَرْ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ دَيَّارًا
en: Noah had prayed, “My Lord! Do not leave a single disbeliever on earth.
t1: And Nuh (Noah) submitted: ‘O my Lord! Do not leave even a single disbeliever living on earth.
t2: And Noah said, ’My Lord, leave not upon the earth of the unbelievers even one.
t3: And Noah said: My Lord! Leave not one of the disbelievers in the land.

ar: إِنَّكَ إِن تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا۟ عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوٓا۟ إِلَّا فَاجِرًۭا كَفَّارًۭا
en: For if You spare ˹any of˺ them, they will certainly mislead Your servants, and give birth only to ˹wicked˺ sinners, staunch disbelievers.
t1: Surely, if You leave them (alive), they will keep leading your servants astray and will beget none but the most wicked and extremely disbelieving children.
t2: Surely, if Thou leavest them, they will lead Thy servants astray, and will beget none but unbelieving libertines.
t3: If Thou shouldst leave them, they will mislead Thy slaves and will beget none save lewd ingrates.

ar: رَّبِّ ٱغْفِرْ لِى وَلِوَٰلِدَىَّ وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيْتِىَ مُؤْمِنًۭا وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارًۢا
en: My Lord! Forgive me, my parents, and whoever enters my house in faith, and ˹all˺ believing men and women. And increase the wrongdoers only in destruction.”
t1: O my Lord! Forgive me and my parents and everyone who enters my home as a believer and (all) the believing men and the believing women, and do not increase anything for the wrongdoers except destruction.’
t2: My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whosoever enters my house as a believer, and the believers, men and women alike; and do Thou not increase the evildoers save in ruin!’
t3: My Lord! Forgive me and my parents and him who entereth my house believing, and believing men and believing women, and increase not the wrong-doers in aught save ruin.

ar: قُلْ أُوحِىَ إِلَىَّ أَنَّهُ ٱسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْجِنِّ فَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا سَمِعْنَا قُرْءَانًا عَجَبًۭا
en: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened ˹to the Quran,˺ and said ˹to their fellow jinn˺: ‘Indeed, we have heard a wondrous recitation.
t1: Say: ‘It has been revealed to me that a party of the jinn listened to (my recitation) carefully and then (went back to their people and) said: Surely, we have heard a wonderful Qur’an.
t2: Say: ’It has been revealed to me that a company of the jinn gave ear, then they said, "We have indeed heard a Koran wonderful,
t3: Say (O Muhammad): It is revealed unto me that a company of the Jinn gave ear, and they said: Lo! we have heard a marvellous Qur’an,

ar: يَهْدِىٓ إِلَى ٱلرُّشْدِ فَـَٔامَنَّا بِهِۦ ۖ وَلَن نُّشْرِكَ بِرَبِّنَآ أَحَدًۭا
en: It leads to Right Guidance so we believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord ˹in worship˺.
t1: It shows the path of guidance. So we have believed in it and will never set up any partner with our Lord.
t2: guiding to rectitude. We believe in it, and we will not associate with our Lord anyone.
t3: Which guideth unto righteousness, so we believe in it and we ascribe no partner unto our Lord.

ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ تَعَٰلَىٰ جَدُّ رَبِّنَا مَا ٱتَّخَذَ صَٰحِبَةًۭ وَلَا وَلَدًۭا
en: ˹Now, we believe that˺ our Lord—Exalted is His Majesty—has neither taken a mate nor offspring,
t1: And that exalted is the Glory of our Lord. He has taken for Himself neither any wife nor any children.
t2: He -- exalted be our Lord’s majesty! has not taken to Himself either consort or a son.
t3: And (we believe) that He - exalted be the glory of our Lord! - hath taken neither wife nor son,

ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ كَانَ يَقُولُ سَفِيهُنَا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ شَطَطًۭا
en: and that the foolish of us used to utter ˹outrageous˺ falsehoods about Allah.
t1: And that only a fool from amongst us used to utter things about Allah far from the truth, crossing bounds.
t2: The fool among us spoke against God outrage,
t3: And that the foolish one among us used to speak concerning Allah an atrocious lie.

ar: وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن تَقُولَ ٱلْإِنسُ وَٱلْجِنُّ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًۭا
en: We certainly thought that humans and jinn would never speak lies about Allah.
t1: And that we thought that man and jinn would never tell a lie against Allah.
t2: and we had thought that men and jinn would never speak against God a lie.
t3: And lo! we had supposed that humankind and jinn would not speak a lie concerning Allah -

ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ كَانَ رِجَالٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْإِنسِ يَعُوذُونَ بِرِجَالٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْجِنِّ فَزَادُوهُمْ رَهَقًۭا
en: And some men used to seek refuge with some jinn—so they increased each other in wickedness.
t1: And that some of the men used to take shelter with some of the jinn. So they increased defiance amongst the jinn.
t2: But there were certain men of mankind who would take refuge with certain men of the jinn, and they increased them in vileness,
t3: And indeed (O Muhammad) individuals of humankind used to invoke the protection of individuals of the jinn, so that they increased them in revolt against Allah);

ar: وَأَنَّهُمْ ظَنُّوا۟ كَمَا ظَنَنتُمْ أَن لَّن يَبْعَثَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدًۭا
en: And those ˹humans˺ thought, just like you ˹jinn˺, that Allah would not resurrect anyone ˹for judgment˺.
t1: And, (O party of jinn,) those men also thought just as you thought that Allah would never raise up anyone (after death).
t2: and they thought, even as you also thought, that God would never raise up anyone.
t3: And indeed they supposed, even as ye suppose, that Allah would not raise anyone (from the dead) -

ar: وَأَنَّا لَمَسْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ فَوَجَدْنَٰهَا مُلِئَتْ حَرَسًۭا شَدِيدًۭا وَشُهُبًۭا
en: ˹Earlier˺ we tried to reach heaven ˹for news˺, only to find it filled with stern guards and shooting stars.
t1: And that we touched the heavens and found them filled with high-alert guards and stars shining and burning (like brands).
t2: And we stretched towards heaven, but we found it filled with terrible guards and meteors.
t3: And (the Jinn who had listened to the Qur’an said): We had sought the heaven but had found it filled with strong warders and meteors.

ar: وَأَنَّا كُنَّا نَقْعُدُ مِنْهَا مَقَٰعِدَ لِلسَّمْعِ ۖ فَمَن يَسْتَمِعِ ٱلْءَانَ يَجِدْ لَهُۥ شِهَابًۭا رَّصَدًۭا
en: We used to take up positions there for eavesdropping, but whoever dares eavesdrop now will find a flare lying in wait for them.
t1: And that we used to sit on certain seats (in the heavens previously, to listen to the news), but if someone now seeks to listen, then he will find a flame of fire (waiting) for him in ambush.
t2: We would sit there on seats to hear; but any listening now finds a meteor in wait for him.
t3: And we used to sit on places (high) therein to listen. But he who listeneth now findeth a flame in wait for him;

ar: وَأَنَّا لَا نَدْرِىٓ أَشَرٌّ أُرِيدَ بِمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ أَمْ أَرَادَ بِهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ رَشَدًۭا
en: Now, we have no clue whether evil is intended for those on earth, or their Lord intends for them what is right.
t1: And that we do not know whether some evil has been intended (by our restriction) in respect of those people who are in the earth, or their Lord intends some good for them.
t2: And so we know not whether evil is intended for those in the earth, or whether their Lord intends for them rectitude.
t3: And we know not whether harm is boded unto all who are in the earth, or whether their Lord intendeth guidance for them.

ar: وَأَنَّا مِنَّا ٱلصَّٰلِحُونَ وَمِنَّا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ ۖ كُنَّا طَرَآئِقَ قِدَدًۭا
en: Among us are those who are righteous and those who are less so. We have been of different factions.
t1: And that amongst us are some who are pious and there are also some (evil) exceptions amongst us. We were (following) different ways.
t2: And some of us are the righteous, and some of us are otherwise; we are sects differing.
t3: And among us there are righteous folk and among us there are far from that. We are sects having different rules.

ar: وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن نُّعْجِزَ ٱللَّهَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَن نُّعْجِزَهُۥ هَرَبًۭا
en: ˹Now,˺ we truly know that we cannot frustrate Allah on earth, nor can we escape from Him ˹into heaven˺.
t1: And we have ascertained that we can by no means come in the way of Allah (whilst living) in the earth, nor can we thwart Him by escaping (from the earth).
t2: Indeed, we thought that we should never be able to frustrate God in the earth, neither be able to frustrate Him by flight.
t3: And we know that we cannot escape from Allah in the earth, nor can we escape by flight.

ar: وَأَنَّا لَمَّا سَمِعْنَا ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ ۖ فَمَن يُؤْمِنۢ بِرَبِّهِۦ فَلَا يَخَافُ بَخْسًۭا وَلَا رَهَقًۭا
en: When we heard the guidance ˹of the Quran˺, we ˹readily˺ believed in it. For whoever believes in their Lord will have no fear of being denied ˹a reward˺ or wronged.
t1: And that when we listened to (the Book of) Guidance, we believed in it. Then he who believes in his Lord fears neither loss nor injustice.
t2: When we heard the guidance, we believed in it; and whosoever believes in his Lord, he shall fear neither paltriness nor vileness.
t3: And when we heard the guidance, we believed therein, and whoso believeth in his Lord, he feareth neither loss nor oppression.

ar: وَأَنَّا مِنَّا ٱلْمُسْلِمُونَ وَمِنَّا ٱلْقَٰسِطُونَ ۖ فَمَنْ أَسْلَمَ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ تَحَرَّوْا۟ رَشَدًۭا
en: And among us are those who have submitted ˹to Allah˺ and those who are deviant. So ˹as for˺ those who submitted, it is they who have attained Right Guidance.
t1: And that (some) of us are obedient and (some) of us are wrongdoers as well. So he who becomes obedient, it is they who seek righteousness.
t2: And some of us have surrendered, and some of us have deviated. Those who have surrendered sought rectitude;
t3: And there are among us some who have surrendered (to Allah) and there are among us some who are unjust. And whoso hath surrendered to Allah, such have taken the right path purposefully.

ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلْقَٰسِطُونَ فَكَانُوا۟ لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَبًۭا
en: And as for the deviant, they will be fuel for Hell.’”
t1: And as for the wrongdoers, they will be the fuel of Hell.’
t2: but as for those who have deviated, they have become firewood for Gehenna!"’
t3: And as for those who are unjust, they are firewood for hell.

ar: وَأَلَّوِ ٱسْتَقَٰمُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلطَّرِيقَةِ لَأَسْقَيْنَٰهُم مَّآءً غَدَقًۭا
en: Had the deniers followed the Right Way, We would have certainly granted them abundant rain to drink—
t1: And this (Revelation has also come to me) that if they had remained firm on the right path (the path of truth, the path of the remembrance of Allah), then We would have provided them with abundant water,
t2: Would they but go straight on the way, We would give them to drink of water copious,
t3: If they (the idolaters) tread the right path, We shall give them to drink of water in abundance

ar: لِّنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ ۚ وَمَن يُعْرِضْ عَن ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِۦ يَسْلُكْهُ عَذَابًۭا صَعَدًۭا
en: as a test for them. And whoever turns away from the remembrance of their Lord will be admitted by Him into an overwhelming punishment.
t1: So that We put them to trial by this blessing. And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, He will cause him to enter a severe torment.
t2: that We might try them therein. And whosoever turns away from the Remembrance of his Lord, He will thrust him into chastisement rigorous.
t3: That We may test them thereby, and whoso turneth away from the remembrance of his Lord; He will thrust him into ever-growing torment.

ar: وَأَنَّ ٱلْمَسَٰجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلَا تَدْعُوا۟ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ أَحَدًۭا
en: The places of worship are ˹only˺ for Allah, so do not invoke anyone besides Him.
t1: And that mosques are (specified) for Allah alone. So never worship anyone else besides Allah.
t2: The places of worship belong to God; so call not, along with God, upon anyone.
t3: And the places of worship are only for Allah, so pray not unto anyone along with Allah.

ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ لَمَّا قَامَ عَبْدُ ٱللَّهِ يَدْعُوهُ كَادُوا۟ يَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِ لِبَدًۭا
en: Yet when the servant of Allah stood up calling upon Him ˹alone˺, the pagans almost swarmed over him.
t1: And that when the servant of Allah (Muhammad [blessings and peace be upon him]) stood up to worship Him, they thronged around him (to listen to his recitation).
t2: When the servant of God stood calling on Him, they were wellnigh upon him in swarms.
t3: And when the slave of Allah stood up in prayer to Him, they crowded on him, almost stifling.

ar: قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَدْعُوا۟ رَبِّى وَلَآ أُشْرِكُ بِهِۦٓ أَحَدًۭا
en: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I call only upon my Lord, associating none with Him ˹in worship˺.”
t1: Say: ‘I worship only my Lord and do not associate any partner with Him.’
t2: Say: ’I call only upon my Lord, and I do not associate with Him anyone.
t3: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): I pray unto Allah only, and ascribe unto Him no partner.

ar: قُلْ إِنِّى لَآ أَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّۭا وَلَا رَشَدًۭا
en: Say, “It is not in my power to harm or benefit you.”
t1: Say: ‘I do not possess any power to do you harm (i.e., make you disbelieve) or to do you good (i.e., make you believe. So Allah is the real Lord. I am a mediator and means).’
t2: Say: ’Surely I possess no power over you, either for hurt or for rectitude.’
t3: Say: Lo! I control not hurt nor benefit for you.

ar: قُلْ إِنِّى لَن يُجِيرَنِى مِنَ ٱللَّهِ أَحَدٌۭ وَلَنْ أَجِدَ مِن دُونِهِۦ مُلْتَحَدًا
en: Say, “No one can protect me from Allah ˹if I were to disobey Him˺, nor can I find any refuge other than Him.
t1: Say: ‘Neither can anyone shelter me from a torment (against the command) of Allah, nor can I ever find refuge apart from Him.
t2: Say: ’From God shall protect me not anyone, and I shall find, apart from Him, no refuge,
t3: Say: Lo! none can protect me from Allah, nor can I find any refuge beside Him

ar: إِلَّا بَلَٰغًۭا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِسَٰلَٰتِهِۦ ۚ وَمَن يَعْصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدًا
en: ˹My duty is˺ only to convey ˹the truth˺ from Allah and ˹deliver˺ His messages.” And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger will certainly be in the Fire of Hell, to stay there for ever and ever.
t1: But (my responsibility is) to communicate from Allah His commands and messages. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger (blessings and peace be upon him), surely there is for him the Fire of Hell in which they will live forever.’
t2: excepting a Deliverance from God and His Messages. And whoso rebels against God and His messenger, for him there awaits the Fire of Gehenna; therein they shall dwell forever.’
t3: (Mine is) but conveyance (of the Truth) from Allah, and His messages; and whoso disobeyeth Allah and His messenger, lo! his is fire of hell, wherein such dwell for ever.

ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا رَأَوْا۟ مَا يُوعَدُونَ فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَضْعَفُ نَاصِرًۭا وَأَقَلُّ عَدَدًۭا
en: Only when they see what they have been threatened with will they know who is weaker in helpers and inferior in manpower.
t1: Until, when they will see that torment which is being promised to them, (then) they will come to know who is weaker in helpers and fewer in numbers.
t2: Until, when they see that which they are promised, then they will know who is weaker in helpers and fewer in numbers.
t3: Till (the day) when they shall behold that which they are promised (they may doubt); but then they will know (for certain) who is weaker in allies and less in multitude.

ar: قُلْ إِنْ أَدْرِىٓ أَقَرِيبٌۭ مَّا تُوعَدُونَ أَمْ يَجْعَلُ لَهُۥ رَبِّىٓ أَمَدًا
en: Say, “I do not know if what you are promised is near or my Lord has set a distant time for it.
t1: Say: ‘I do not know whether that (Day of Rising) which is being promised to you is near, or my Lord has appointed a longer term for that.’
t2: Say: ’I do not know whether that which you are promised is nigh, or whether my Lord will appoint for it a space;
t3: Say (O Muhammad, unto the disbelievers): I know not whether that which ye are promised is nigh, or if my Lord hath set a distant term for it.

ar: عَٰلِمُ ٱلْغَيْبِ فَلَا يُظْهِرُ عَلَىٰ غَيْبِهِۦٓ أَحَدًا
en: ˹He is the˺ Knower of the unseen, disclosing none of it to anyone,
t1: (He is) the Knower of the unseen. So He does not inform any (common man) of His unseen,
t2: Knower He of the Unseen, and He discloses not His Unseen to anyone,
t3: (He is) the Knower of the Unseen, and He revealeth unto none His secret,

ar: إِلَّا مَنِ ٱرْتَضَىٰ مِن رَّسُولٍۢ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَسْلُكُ مِنۢ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِۦ رَصَدًۭا
en: except messengers of His choice. Then He appoints angel-guards before and behind them
t1: Except for His Messengers with whom He is well-pleased (and reveals to them alone the unseen because that is an exclusive trait of Prophethood and a Messenger’s miracle as well). So indeed He appoints protectors at both front and rear of him (the Messenger, for the security of the knowledge of the unseen),
t2: save only to such a Messenger as He is well-pleased with; then He despatches before him and behind him watchers,
t3: Save unto every messenger whom He hath chosen, and then He maketh a guard to go before him and a guard behind him

ar: لِّيَعْلَمَ أَن قَدْ أَبْلَغُوا۟ رِسَٰلَٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ وَأَحَاطَ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ وَأَحْصَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ عَدَدًۢا
en: to ensure that the messengers fully deliver the messages of their Lord—though He ˹already˺ knows all about them, and keeps account of everything.”
t1: So that Allah may bring to light that surely they (the Messengers) have communicated the messages of their Lord, and Allah has (already) encompassed what they have (of Allah’s injunctions and the knowledge of the unseen) and He has kept count of everything.
t2: that He may know they have delivered the Messages of their Lord; and He encompasses all that is with them, and He has numbered everything in numbers.’
t3: That He may know that they have indeed conveyed the messages of their Lord. He surroundeth all their doings, and He keepeth count of all things.

ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمُزَّمِّلُ
en: O you wrapped ˹in your clothes˺!
t1: O mantled (Beloved!)
t2: O thou enwrapped in thy robes,
t3: O thou wrapped up in thy raiment!

ar: قُمِ ٱلَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا
en: Stand all night ˹in prayer˺ except a little—
t1: Rise and stand (in Prayer) at night but (for) a short while,
t2: keep vigil the night, except a little
t3: Keep vigil the night long, save a little -

ar: نِّصْفَهُۥٓ أَوِ ٱنقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا
en: ˹pray˺ half the night, or a little less,
t1: Half the night or decrease it a little,
t2: (a half of it, or diminish a little,
t3: A half thereof, or abate a little thereof

ar: أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَرْتِيلًا
en: or a little more—and recite the Quran ˹properly˺ in a measured way.
t1: Or increase a little more to it. And recite the Qur’an with most pleasant pauses.
t2: or add a little), and chant the Koran very distinctly;
t3: Or add (a little) thereto - and chant the Qur’an in measure,

ar: إِنَّا سَنُلْقِى عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًۭا ثَقِيلًا
en: ˹For˺ We will soon send upon you a weighty revelation.
t1: Soon We shall send down to you a burdensome command.
t2: Behold, We shall cast upon thee a weighty word;
t3: For we shall charge thee with a word of weight.

ar: إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ ٱلَّيْلِ هِىَ أَشَدُّ وَطْـًۭٔا وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلًا
en: Indeed, worship in the night is more impactful and suitable for recitation.
t1: No doubt rising at night strictly subdues (the ill-commanding self), and makes the tongue deliver straight and clear speech (with the concentration of head and heart).
t2: surely the first part of the night is heavier in tread, more upright in speech,
t3: Lo! the vigil of the night is (a time) when impression is more keen and speech more certain.

ar: إِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ سَبْحًۭا طَوِيلًۭا
en: For during the day you are over-occupied ˹with worldly duties˺.
t1: Of course, there are many commitments for you during the day.
t2: surely in the day thou hast long business.
t3: Lo! thou hast by day a chain of business.

ar: وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًۭا
en: ˹Always˺ remember the Name of your Lord, and devote yourself to Him wholeheartedly.
t1: And continue remembering the Name of your Lord, devoted completely to Him alone (in your heart and soul), broken away from everyone else.
t2: And remember the Name of thy Lord, and devote thyself unto Him very devoutly.
t3: So remember the name of thy Lord and devote thyself with a complete devotion -

ar: رَّبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ وَٱلْمَغْرِبِ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَٱتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًۭا
en: ˹He is the˺ Lord of the east and the west. There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him, so take Him ˹alone˺ as a Trustee of Affairs.
t1: He is the Lord of the east and the west. There is no God but He. So take Him alone as (your) Guardian.
t2: Lord of the East and the West; there is no god but He; so take Him for a Guardian.
t3: Lord of the East and the West; there is no God save Him; so choose thou Him alone for thy defender -

ar: وَٱصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَٱهْجُرْهُمْ هَجْرًۭا جَمِيلًۭا
en: Be patient ˹O Prophet˺ with what they say, and depart from them courteously.
t1: And observe patience with what they (disbelievers) utter and turn aside from them in a fine manner.
t2: And bear thou patiently what they say, and forsake them graciously.
t3: And bear with patience what they utter, and part from them with a fair leave-taking.

ar: وَذَرْنِى وَٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ أُو۟لِى ٱلنَّعْمَةِ وَمَهِّلْهُمْ قَلِيلًا
en: And leave to Me the deniers—the people of luxury—and bear with them for a little while.
t1: And leave Me (to deal) with the denying rich money-mongers (to take revenge). And give them a little respite (so that their evil deeds may cross the limit).
t2: Leave Me to those who cry lies, those prosperous ones, and respite them a little,
t3: Leave Me to deal with the deniers, lords of ease and comfort (in this life); and do thou respite them awhile.

ar: إِنَّ لَدَيْنَآ أَنكَالًۭا وَجَحِيمًۭا
en: ˹For˺ We certainly have shackles, a ˹raging˺ Fire,
t1: Surely, We have heavy shackles and the Blazing Fire (of Hell),
t2: for with Us there are fetters, and a furnace,
t3: Lo! with Us are heavy fetters and a raging fire,

ar: وَطَعَامًۭا ذَا غُصَّةٍۢ وَعَذَابًا أَلِيمًۭا
en: choking food, and a painful punishment ˹in store for them˺
t1: And food that chokes the throat and most painful torment.
t2: and food that chokes, and a painful chastisement,
t3: And food which choketh (the partaker), and a painful doom

ar: يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ وَكَانَتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ كَثِيبًۭا مَّهِيلًا
en: on the Day the earth and mountains will shake ˹violently˺, and mountains will be ˹reduced to˺ dunes of shifting sand.
t1: The Day when the earth and the mountains shall shake violently and mountains will turn into heaps of flying away sand.
t2: upon the day when the earth and the mountains shall quake and the mountains become a slipping heap of sand.
t3: On the day when the earth and the hills rock, and the hills become a heap of running sand.

ar: إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَآ إِلَيْكُمْ رَسُولًۭا شَٰهِدًا عَلَيْكُمْ كَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَآ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولًۭا
en: Indeed, We have sent to you a messenger as a witness over you, just as We sent a messenger to Pharaoh.
t1: Surely, We have sent towards you a Messenger (blessings and peace be upon him) who bears witness to you (seeing thoroughly your states of being) as We sent a Messenger towards Pharaoh.
t2: Surely We have sent unto you a Messenger as a witness over you, even as We sent to Pharaoh a Messenger,
t3: Lo! We have sent unto you a messenger as witness against you, even as We sent unto Pharaoh a messenger.

ar: فَعَصَىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ ٱلرَّسُولَ فَأَخَذْنَٰهُ أَخْذًۭا وَبِيلًۭا
en: But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a stern grip.
t1: So Pharaoh disobeyed that Messenger, and We seized him with a devastating seizure.
t2: but Pharaoh rebelled against the Messenger, so We seized him remorselessly.
t3: But Pharaoh rebelled against the messenger, whereupon We seized him with no gentle grip.

ar: فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إِن كَفَرْتُمْ يَوْمًۭا يَجْعَلُ ٱلْوِلْدَٰنَ شِيبًا
en: If you ˹pagans˺ persist in disbelief, then how will you guard yourselves against ˹the horrors of˺ a Day which will turn children’s hair grey?
t1: If you continue disbelieving, then how will you save yourselves from (the torment of) that Day which will turn the children old,
t2: If therefore you disbelieve, how will you guard yourselves against a day that shall make the children grey-headed?
t3: Then how, if ye disbelieve, will ye protect yourselves upon the day which will turn children grey,

ar: ٱلسَّمَآءُ مُنفَطِرٌۢ بِهِۦ ۚ كَانَ وَعْدُهُۥ مَفْعُولًا
en: It will ˹even˺ cause the sky to split apart. His promise ˹of judgment˺ must be fulfilled.
t1: (The Day) by whose severity the heaven will be split apart? His promise is bound to be fulfilled.
t2: Whereby heaven shall be split, and its promise shall be performed.
t3: The very heaven being then rent asunder. His promise is to be fulfilled.

ar: إِنَّ هَٰذِهِۦ تَذْكِرَةٌۭ ۖ فَمَن شَآءَ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ سَبِيلًا
en: Surely this is a reminder. So let whoever wills take the ˹Right˺ Way to their Lord.
t1: Verily, this (Qur’an) is an admonition. So let him who desires adopt the way to reach his Lord.
t2: Surely this is a Reminder; so let him who will take unto his Lord a way.
t3: Lo! This is a Reminder. Let him who will, then, choose a way unto his Lord.

ar: ۞ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَىِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُۥ وَثُلُثَهُۥ وَطَآئِفَةٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مَعَكَ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ ۚ عَلِمَ أَن لَّن تُحْصُوهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ ۖ فَٱقْرَءُوا۟ مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنَ ٱلْقُرْءَانِ ۚ عَلِمَ أَن سَيَكُونُ مِنكُم مَّرْضَىٰ ۙ وَءَاخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ ۙ وَءَاخَرُونَ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ فَٱقْرَءُوا۟ مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنْهُ ۚ وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَقْرِضُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًۭا ۚ وَمَا تُقَدِّمُوا۟ لِأَنفُسِكُم مِّنْ خَيْرٍۢ تَجِدُوهُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْرًۭا وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْرًۭا ۚ وَٱسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۢ
en: Surely your Lord knows that you ˹O Prophet˺ stand ˹in prayer˺ for nearly two-thirds of the night, or ˹sometimes˺ half of it, or a third, as do some of those with you. Allah ˹alone˺ keeps a ˹precise˺ measure of the day and night. He knows that you ˹believers˺ are unable to endure this, and has turned to you in mercy. And seek Allah’s forgiveness. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
t1: Surely, your Lord knows that you stand (for prayer sometimes) about two-thirds of the night and (sometimes) half the night and (sometimes) a third of the night, and (also) a party of those who are with you (join in standing up for Prayer). And Allah is the One Who keeps the true measure (of increasing or decreasing) the night and the day. He knows that you just do not have the power to encompass it so He granted you forgiveness (by reducing the toil). So recite the Qur’an as much as is easy for you. He knows that (some of) you will be ill and (some) others will be travelling in the land to look for Allah’s bounty and (still some) others will be fighting in the way of Allah. So recite as much as is easy for you. And establish Prayer and pay Zakat (the Alms-due) and lend Allah a goodly loan. And whatever good you will send forward for yourselves, you will find it in the presence of Allah much better and in reward still greater. And keep seeking forgiveness from Allah. Allah is Most Forgiving, Ever-Merciful.
t2: Thy Lord knows that thou keepest vigil nearly two-thirds of the night, or a half of it, or a third of it, and a party of those with thee; and God determines the night and the day. He knows that you will not number it, and He has turned towards you. Therefore recite of the Koran so much as is feasible. He knows that some of you are sick, and others journeying in the land, seeking the bounty of God, and others fighting in the way of God. So recite of it so much as is feasible. And perform the prayer, and pay the alms, and lend to God a good loan. Whatever good you shall forward to your souls’ account, you shall find it with God as better, and mightier a wage. And ask God’s forgiveness; God is All-forgiving, All-compassionate.
t3: Lo! thy Lord knoweth how thou keepest vigil sometimes nearly two- thirds of the night, or (sometimes) half or a third thereof, as do a party of those with thee. Allah measureth the night and the day. He knoweth that ye count it not, and turneth unto you in mercy. Recite, then, of the Qur’an that which is easy for you. He knoweth that there are sick folk among you, while others travel in the land in search of Allah’s bounty, and others (still) are fighting for the cause of Allah. So recite of it that which is easy (for you), and establish worship and pay the poor-due, and (so) lend unto Allah a goodly loan. Whatsoever good ye send before you for your souls, ye will find it with Allah, better and greater in the recompense. And seek forgiveness of Allah. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.

ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمُدَّثِّرُ
en: O you covered up ˹in your clothes˺!
t1: O enwrapped (Beloved!)
t2: O thou shrouded in thy mantle,
t3: O thou enveloped in thy cloak,

ar: قُمْ فَأَنذِرْ
en: Arise and warn ˹all˺.
t1: Rise and give warning (to the people).
t2: arise, and warn!
t3: Arise and warn!

ar: وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ
en: Revere your Lord ˹alone˺.
t1: And glorify the Greatnesss (and Majesty) of your Lord.
t2: Thy Lord magnify
t3: Thy Lord magnify,

ar: وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ
en: Purify your garments.
t1: And (always) keep your (visible and spiritual) attire purified and cleansed (as before).
t2: thy robes purify
t3: Thy raiment purify,

ar: وَٱلرُّجْزَ فَٱهْجُرْ
en: ˹Continue to˺ shun idols.
t1: And keep away from the idols (and sins as usual).
t2: and defilement flee!
t3: Pollution shun!

ar: وَلَا تَمْنُن تَسْتَكْثِرُ
en: Do not do a favour expecting more ˹in return˺.
t1: And do not do a favour (to anyone with the purpose of) seeking more from him.
t2: Give not, thinking to gain greater
t3: And show not favour, seeking wordly gain!

ar: وَلِرَبِّكَ فَٱصْبِرْ
en: And persevere for ˹the sake of˺ your Lord.
t1: And observe patience for the sake of your Lord.
t2: and be patient unto thy Lord.
t3: For the sake of thy Lord, be patient!

ar: فَإِذَا نُقِرَ فِى ٱلنَّاقُورِ
en: ˹For˺ when the Trumpet will be sounded,
t1: Then when the Trumpet will be blown (a second time),
t2: For when the Trump is sounded
t3: For when the trumpet shall sound,

ar: فَذَٰلِكَ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ
en: that will ˹truly˺ be a difficult Day—
t1: So that Day (the Day of Resurrection) will be an extremely hard day,
t2: that day will be a harsh day,
t3: Surely that day will be a day of anguish,

ar: عَلَى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍۢ
en: far from easy for the disbelievers.
t1: Not at all easy for the disbelievers.
t2: for the unbelievers not easy.
t3: Not of ease, for disbelievers.

ar: ذَرْنِى وَمَنْ خَلَقْتُ وَحِيدًۭا
en: And leave to me ˹O Prophet˺ the one I created all by Myself,
t1: Leave Me (to take revenge) on him whom I have created alone,
t2: Leave Me with him whom I created alone,
t3: Leave Me (to deal) with him whom I created lonely,

ar: وَجَعَلْتُ لَهُۥ مَالًۭا مَّمْدُودًۭا
en: and granted him abundant wealth,
t1: And I provided him wealth in abundance,
t2: and appointed for him ample wealth
t3: And then bestowed upon him ample means,

ar: وَبَنِينَ شُهُودًۭا
en: and children always by his side,
t1: And (gave) him sons remaining present (before him),
t2: and sons standing before him,
t3: And sons abiding in his presence

ar: وَمَهَّدتُّ لَهُۥ تَمْهِيدًۭا
en: and made life very easy for him.
t1: And granted him affluence (in sources of luxury).
t2: and made all things smooth for him;
t3: And made (life) smooth for him.

ar: ثُمَّ يَطْمَعُ أَنْ أَزِيدَ
en: Yet he is hungry for more.
t1: Yet he desires that I should give him more.
t2: then he is eager that I should do more.
t3: Yet he desireth that I should give more.

ar: كَلَّآ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ لِءَايَٰتِنَا عَنِيدًۭا
en: But no! ˹For˺ he has been truly stubborn with Our revelations.
t1: No way! He has certainly been inimical to Our Revelations.
t2: Nay! He is forward unto Our signs;
t3: Nay! For lo! he hath been stubborn to Our revelations.

ar: سَأُرْهِقُهُۥ صَعُودًا
en: I will make his fate unbearable,
t1: Soon I shall afflict him with (the punishment of) a severe toil.
t2: and I shall constrain him to a hard ascent.
t3: On him I shall impose a fearful doom.

ar: إِنَّهُۥ فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ
en: for he contemplated and determined ˹a degrading label for the Quran˺.
t1: Surely, he reflected and devised a plot.
t2: Lo! He reflected, and determined --
t3: For lo! he did consider; then he planned -

ar: فَقُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ
en: May he be condemned! How evil was what he determined!
t1: So let (Allah’s) curse be on him! How he plotted!
t2: death seize him, how he determined!
t3: (Self-)destroyed is he, how he planned!

ar: ثُمَّ قُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ
en: May he be condemned even more! How evil was what he determined!
t1: Let again (Allah’s) curse be on him! How he plotted!
t2: Again, death seize him, how he determined!
t3: Again (self-)destroyed is he, how he planned! -

ar: ثُمَّ نَظَرَ
en: Then he re-contemplated ˹in frustration˺,
t1: Then he pondered (over his scheme again).
t2: Then he beheld,
t3: Then looked he,

ar: ثُمَّ عَبَسَ وَبَسَرَ
en: then frowned and scowled,
t1: Then he frowned and twisted his face.
t2: then he frowned, and scowled,
t3: Then frowned he and showed displeasure.

ar: ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ
en: then turned his back ˹on the truth˺ and acted arrogantly,
t1: Then he turned back (from the truth) and showed arrogance.
t2: then he retreated, and waxed proud.
t3: Then turned he away in pride

ar: فَقَالَ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحْرٌۭ يُؤْثَرُ
en: saying, “This ˹Quran˺ is nothing but magic from the ancients.
t1: Then he said: ‘This (Qur’an) is nothing but magic which is being transmitted from the past (magicians).
t2: He said, ’This is naught but a trumped-up sorcery;
t3: And said: This is naught else than magic from of old;

ar: إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا قَوْلُ ٱلْبَشَرِ
en: This is no more than the word of a man.”
t1: This (Qur’an) is nothing (else) but the words of a human being.’
t2: ’this is nothing but mortal speech.’
t3: This is naught else than speech of mortal man.

ar: سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ
en: Soon I will burn him in Hell!
t1: I will soon cast him into Hell.
t2: I shall surely roast him in Sakar;
t3: Him shall I fling unto the burning.

ar: وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا سَقَرُ
en: And what will make you realize what Hell is?
t1: And who has told you what Saqar (the Fire of Hell) is?
t2: and what will teach thee what is Sakar?
t3: - Ah, what will convey unto thee what that burning is! -

ar: لَا تُبْقِى وَلَا تَذَرُ
en: It does not let anyone live or die,
t1: That (is the Fire which) does not spare, nor does it leave out.
t2: It spares not, neither leaves alone
t3: It leaveth naught; it spareth naught

ar: لَوَّاحَةٌۭ لِّلْبَشَرِ
en: scorching the skin.
t1: (That) scorches the skin and blackens it.
t2: scorching the flesh;
t3: It shrivelleth the man.

ar: عَلَيْهَا تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ
en: It is overseen by nineteen ˹keepers˺.
t1: There are nineteen (angels appointed as guards) over it.
t2: over it are nineteen.
t3: Above it are nineteen.

ar: وَمَا جَعَلْنَآ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلنَّارِ إِلَّا مَلَٰٓئِكَةًۭ ۙ وَمَا جَعَلْنَا عِدَّتَهُمْ إِلَّا فِتْنَةًۭ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَيَزْدَادَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِيمَٰنًۭا ۙ وَلَا يَرْتَابَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ۙ وَلِيَقُولَ ٱلَّذِينَ فِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌۭ وَٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلًۭا ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ ۚ وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۚ وَمَا هِىَ إِلَّا ذِكْرَىٰ لِلْبَشَرِ
en: We have appointed only ˹stern˺ angels as wardens of the Fire.
